title: release: published Story graph pulls TWO providers of re-frame.adapter.reagent (stock reagent direct + reagent-slim via xray) - settle at the dependency boundary BEFORE story-v*
description:
FILED 2026-09-09 13:2x AUSEST from the rf2-pv7p decision pass (tip de042b5455). Found by the
Codex review of the rf2-pv7p dossier; verified at source before filing. BLOCKS rf2-pv7p's
third tag (story-v*) and nothing earlier.

THE DEFECT. The PUBLISHED Story dependency graph contains TWO providers of the single
canonical namespace re-frame.adapter.reagent:

  tools/story/deps.edn:16   day8/re-frame2-reagent   (direct runtime dep)
  tools/story/deps.edn:67   day8/re-frame2-xray
    -> tools/xray/deps.edn:81   day8/reagent-slim    (runtime dep of xray, NO exclusion)

At publication time .github/scripts/transform-reagent-slim-ns.sh renames the slim adapter
onto the canonical path: it moves src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs to
src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs (script lines 55-56) and rewrites the ns form (line 80).
That is the same file the stock day8/re-frame2-reagent artefact ships. So a consumer whose
only tool coordinate is day8/re-frame2-story gets both jars, both carrying
re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs, and which one wins is classpath order.

THE ASSUMPTION IT VIOLATES is stated verbatim in .github/workflows/release.yml:562-568:
"downstream apps depend on EXACTLY ONE of {day8/re-frame2-reagent, day8/reagent-slim} so
the adapter ns is single-source per app." Story's published graph makes that false.

WHY NO GATE CATCHES IT. In the source checkout slim sits at re-frame.adapter.reagent-slim,
so the monorepo build never sees a clash and the collision is invisible in-tree. Downstream,
a COMPLETE pom and a GREEN clojure -P are both entirely consistent with the collision --
resolution proves the GAVs exist, not that they provide disjoint namespaces. The two
implementations do identify themselves differently at runtime
(implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:197 vs
implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:124).

STATUS: source-derived, NOT reproduced at runtime. First job is to confirm or refute it with
a packaged consumer, not to start fixing.

WHAT TO DO. Settle the adapter choice at the DEPENDENCY BOUNDARY and prove the resulting
consumer graph before story-v* is cut. Do not let classpath order pick an adapter. Do NOT
turn this into an adapter re-architecture, and do NOT assume an untested exclusion preserves
both Story's and Xray's contracts -- Xray renders through re-frame.substrate.adapter and
declares slim as its default transitive adapter deliberately (see the comment at
tools/xray/deps.edn:77-81), so removing it needs a stated replacement, not a silent drop.

ACTIONABLE NOW, independent of the Clojars chain: this is a deps.edn / packaging question
that needs no published artefact and no verified group. It does not wait on rf2-uelji,
rf2-fo4ng or rf2-kmqx3.

URGENCY: P1 because the act it guards is IRREVERSIBLE -- Clojars has no yank, and a story-v*
tag cut over this graph publishes three permanent jars whose adapter provider is ambiguous.

The `All required checks passed` aggregator was present and SUCCESS and was NOT subtracted from the band.

## THE DEFECT WAS FILED SOURCE-DERIVED AND IS NOW CONFIRMED AGAINST A PACKAGED CONSUMER

The worker did not take the bead's word for it. It built both adapter jars from the REAL `transform-reagent-slim-ns.sh` output, installed them into a local Maven repo modelling the published poms, and resolved a consumer whose only tool coordinate is `day8/re-frame2-story`:

    PROVIDERS_FOUND= 2
      provider[0] kind=:rf.adapter/reagent
      provider[1] kind=:rf.adapter/reagent-slim

The only non-manifest entry the two jars share is exactly `re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs`.

**THE WINNER FLIPS ON THE CONSUMER'S OWN UNRELATED CHOICES**, which is the part that makes this a real bug rather than an untidiness. Ordering is by dependency DEPTH, so plain Story gets stock Reagent (depth 1, direct) — but a consumer who also pins `day8/reagent-slim` directly gets the SLIM adapter winning at the canonical namespace while Story's shell is built against stock `reagent.core`.

## THE GATES COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT, AND TWO OF THEM ACTIVELY REQUIRE THE COLLISION

`clojure -Stree` exits **0** and prints a healthy tree over the colliding graph, in BOTH consumer shapes; a complete pom is equally consistent with it. Worse, the two release preflights REQUIRE both providers into the poms — `preflight-xray-package.sh` derives its required set from every `:local/root`, which includes slim. The discriminator that worked was the runtime `:kind` self-identification off a real classpath. Recording this because the instruments that look authoritative here are the ones that cannot see it.

## THE FIX

`tools/story/deps.edn` excludes `day8/reagent-slim` from its Xray edge. Xray's own `deps.edn` is UNTOUCHED, so standalone Xray keeps slim as its default; Story's stated replacement is its own `day8/re-frame2-reagent`. The exclusion applies to `:local/root` too, so the in-tree graph now matches the published one — no tested-tree/published divergence. Verified Xray's sources require neither `reagent2.*` nor the adapter namespace, line-oriented AND flattened/comment-stripped, with a control that bit.

## A SECOND CHANGE WAS FORCED, AND IT IS NOT A FLOOR MOVE

`verify-version-lockstep.sh` structurally forbade ANY extra key on a tools `:local/root` coordinate: its file-text match included the closing brace, while its converse pass compares against a NORMALISED one-key form. Both failure directions were measured before it was touched. The file-text match now matches the `<lib> {:local/root "<path>"` prefix. The lib-to-path pairing is still pinned exactly as before — and it is what the release rewrite itself keys off — so this narrows the pattern without lowering what it asserts. Sabotage confirmed it still bites: breaking the pairing reds the gate at exit 1 in both directions, blob hash restored identically.

## GATES

`verify-version-lockstep.sh` 0 (post-rebase); `--self-test` 0 at 21/21; `tools/story clojure -M:test` 0 at 1914 tests / 7047 assertions; `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` 0; four script unit-test files 0 at 395 assertions. All captured from the worker's own `.exit` files, never a pipe.

`examples_compile` is armed but CANNOT observe this diff — `shadow-cljs.edn` uses explicit `:source-paths` and never consumes `tools/story/deps.edn`. The worker said so rather than quoting the arming as coverage. It also declined to link the shared `node_modules`, and the mayor's tree was verified intact at 103 entries / 27 `.bin`.

## RESIDUAL, SPLIT OUT RATHER THAN ABSORBED

A consumer using Story AND pinning `day8/reagent-slim` directly still resolves two providers, because Story's direct `day8/re-frame2-reagent` dep is irreducible. That is PRE-EXISTING rather than caused by this change, and settling it is the adapter re-architecture this bead rules out. Separately, nothing would catch a regression if someone deleted the exclusion — filed as its own bead. The worker correctly refused to add the assertion under this bead's authority.

title: False HTTP issuance status: replacement inherits the prior request's abort
description:
Merged-PR audit #9944 (f2b9a278c8a65e21ac211300855c67c54989e0fb), source rf2-y8doi.18. The narrowed issuance record still falsely marks a healthy replacement request ERROR when it supersedes an in-flight request with the same request-id (ordinary debounce/search behavior).
Producer evidence at this merge: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:471-475 calls registry/supersede! synchronously while issuing the NEW request. registry.cljc:599-605 calls the OLD handle abort-fn synchronously; transport.cljc:728-775 emits :rf.http/aborted with :reason :request-id-superseded and the SAME request-id. emit-error! uses the currently active issuing handler scope, so that old-attempt abort can land in the NEW issuing bundle. The PR premise that only body-prep failures can reach that bundle is false.
Consumer: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc http-row-for-this-record? compares request-id only, then common-record accepts the abort as failure/cancel-cause. HTTP adapter converts only :ok to :issued. The new request therefore becomes :error with :cancel-cause :request-id-superseded and displays the old attempt failure.
Executed JVM projection probe from the guarded audit worktree: a runtime-shaped handled/new fx plus the synchronous prior abort returns {:status :error :cancel-cause :request-id-superseded}. Expected :issued assertion exits 1; controls pass (no abort -> :issued; actual same-id request-prep failure -> :error). Source resource URL proves the probe loaded audit-sep17-monitor. Artifact ai/gate-http-audit-sep17-monitor-9944-1.log, exit file alongside. This is a projection probe supported by traced producer code, not a live HTTP integration run.
Required correction: within the existing issuance-only design, attribute only genuinely supported same-attempt failures and do not attach the previous request cancellation to the replacement. Keep the real synchronous body-prep failure case. Add regression coverage for same-id replacement and anonymous issuance beside an unrelated same-bundle cancellation. A cross-buffer completion join or new public API is unnecessary; the separately deferred rf2-6ooch is not this defect. Update the false only-body-prep premise where needed. No exact OPEN Bead records this correction; rf2-st7j0 concerns correlation filtering, a different bug.

title: xray: Settings precedence: `configure!` clobbers persisted Settings, `init!` never loads them, boot replays an unclamped width
description:
Filed from the senior-developer review wave over Xray (epic rf2-y8doi, tree reviewed at trunk 9555881fe3, 2026-09-17), item C5 of the triage shortlist. Mike's instruction for the wave: "Have an agent with a senior developer persona review the xray codebase. Create beads for any actionable insights. Ensure that the spec is up to date."

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md; paste it into any dispatch preamble unchanged)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

Mike's restatement for this wave (2026-09-17): "The posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece. But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer. We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a minimal, ergonomic API and excellent tools, and low friction. For each review, remember that we don't want to over-engineer. We just want to create a library which has excellent ergonomics for creating SPAs. We don't need to litigate every last, fine detail and drown in the minutiae."

## The item, verbatim from the triage shortlist

### C5. Settings precedence: `configure!` clobbers persisted Settings, `init!` never loads them, boot replays an unclamped width  [size: M] [from: rf2-y8doi.4#1, rf2-y8doi.3#2, rf2-y8doi.10#1(c)]

- Why it matters: a host using `(configure! {:rf.xray/settings …})` on the preload path loses the user's saved Settings on every boot (the documented order `defaults < configure! < persisted` is delivered inverted); a `(xray/init! …)` host never sees persisted Settings at all; `(configure! {:keybinding-enabled? false})` is a no-op on the preload path; and a width dragged on a wide monitor replays unclamped on a narrower one and can squeeze the host app to zero width.
- What to do: replace the `reset!` in `configure!`'s `:rf.xray/settings` branch (config.cljc:1837-1838) with the three-way merge `load-settings-from-storage!` performs (defaults < seed < persisted) and re-run `settings-effects/apply-all!`; make `keybinding-enabled?` reactive (a flip calls `detach!`/`attach!`) so 015:477-480's "before the preload" clause can go; have `init!` call `load-settings-from-storage!` + `apply-all!`; clamp in `apply-panel-width!` with `config/clamp-panel-width-px` against `js/window.innerWidth` and write the clamped value back through `update-setting!`; reconcile the contradictory comments config.cljc:1469-1471 vs mount.cljs:1304-1307. Rewrite config_test.clj:561-574 to call the real chain (`load-settings-from-storage!` against a stubbed storage) instead of composing `#'merge-known-sections` by hand — the .10 lead.
- Files (fence): tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/config.cljc, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/effects.cljs, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs (comment only), tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/persistence_cljs_test.cljs, tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/effects_cljs_test.cljs, tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/config_test.clj

Node lane; config_test.clj on JVM.

- Re-verified: no — .4 cites the two contradictory comments and the test pinning the impossible order; .3 cites the single clamp call site (registry.cljs:614, drag path only). Sufficient.

found it — init!'s new apply-all! call broke three rows in preload_decoupling_cljs_test.cljs that stub
a listener-only document — and the resolvers' own docstring already promised nil. The gate found a real
defect in the change rather than merely passing.

LINE-NUMBER DELTAS (bead read at 9555881fe3; based 24 commits later at 1dbef19ef9): ZERO on six of
seven cites — config.cljc:1837-1838, :1469-1471, config_test.clj:561-574, persistence_cljs_test.cljs
:176-228 and 015:477-480 all exact; mount.cljs:1304-1307 exact but the sentence runs to 1308.
registry.cljs:614 MOVED TO 618 (+4), the only one of the seven files trunk had touched.

RED THEN GREEN, WITH THE RED PROVED DISCRIMINATING. Four one-line plants on a sabotaged tree, each
anchor verified unique (match count 1) BEFORE running so no plant was a no-op. Node lane captured exit
1: 12 failures, 0 errors across 12220 tests / 60933 assertions — counts IDENTICAL to the green run, so
nothing was skipped or crashed out. The key red is (not (= 20 15)): the host's configured 15 sitting on
the user's persisted 20. The rows that correctly did NOT move are as informative as those that did (the
in-range width, the init-opt precedence, the JVM rows). Restored and verified: all four blob hashes
match git rev-parse HEAD:<path>, git diff --quiet HEAD exit 0.

GATES, each from its own captured status, none read through a pipe: node lane 0 (12220/60933/0),
browser lane 0 (1112/6088/0), tools/xray JVM 0 (1288/6195/0), clj-kondo 0 (errors 0), 46 check_*.py 0
each, check-no-hardcoded-paths and check-ai-tracking-ratchet 0, attribution and beads-boundary 0 on
both commits and the PR body.

THE BROWSER LANE WAS NOT NOMINATED AND THE WORKER RAN IT ANYWAY, CORRECTLY:
resize_handle_dom_cljs_test.cljs asserts apply-panel-width! against literal 700/480/560, and the change
made it clamp against live innerWidth. Green — and argued non-fragile rather than asserted: the runner
launches Playwright Chromium with no viewport override, so innerWidth is the documented 1280 default in
CI as locally, giving a ceiling of 1152 against a largest literal of 700. Asking which gates cover your
paths that nobody nominated is the habit that caught this.

NOT RUN, DECLARED: examples_compile, mcp_conformance, story_xray_browser — armed by the classifier
(handed PATHS, not revisions, per item (v)), but all three compile the same Xray sources the two CLJS
lanes already compiled clean, and each is a multi-minute build on the exclusive another worker was
queued for. Also declared: the worker's clj-kondo is v2025.10.23 where CI pins v2026.04.15, so the CI
job is the authority — a version difference named rather than left for someone to discover.

Line endings, Python on bytes, CR == CRLF and bare LF 0 on all seven files: config.cljc 1991/1991/0,
core.cljs 386/386/0, keybinding.cljs 634/634/0, effects.cljs 812/812/0, persistence_cljs_test.cljs
286/286/0, effects_cljs_test.cljs 651/651/0, config_test.clj 634/634/0. No sed -i anywhere.

JUDGED NOT WORTH CHANGING, per the stance: mount.cljs (it was the correct half); clamp-for-display
instead of converge, rejected for consistency with the drag path's stated posture, with the trade-off
recorded in the docstring rather than argued in the PR; a DOM-lane row for the 1-arity viewport read,
whose only home is outside the fence.

THE LANE: held exclusively for this dispatch and RELEASED with a fresh statement, zero processes
remaining verified by effect and filtered on its own worktree path. It used npm ci in its own worktree
rather than junctioning, so the mayor's node_modules canary never moved.

CARRIED FORWARD: tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md:477-480 — "Hosts MUST set this BEFORE the Xray
preload runs ... setting it afterwards is a no-op" — is now FALSE. Outside the fence, so named in the
PR body rather than edited; it has since been placed as a rider on rf2-y8doi.42, which owns chapter
015. The detach! section at 515-530 stays correct.

ONE METHOD SELF-REPORT, VOLUNTEERED: two intermediate scratch files were written with generic names
(py-one.tmp, sh-one.tmp) rather than worktree-suffixed — a collision hazard in a shared scratchpad with
several workers live. Nothing was read back from them, both were deleted, and peers' artefacts were
left untouched. Worth keeping because the hazard is invisible until two workers collide.

AI attribution trailers declined in the commits and the PR body.

title: review(xray/fresco-trace): senior-developer findings, 9 ranked, 4 spec chapters drift, trunk 9555881fe3 (2026-09-17)
description:
# Senior review: xray-fresco-trace

Reviewer persona: senior engineer who has built render-performance tooling (React DevTools profiler, "why did this render" analysers) and distrusts any advisor that recommends a change it cannot prove from the evidence it shows.
Tree: xray-review-sep17 worktree, trunk 9555881fe3
Scope read: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/{fresco.cljs, fresco_helpers.cljc, fresco_advisor.cljc, fresco_causal.cljc, fresco_reads.cljs, trace.cljs, trace_helpers.cljc, shared/coord_link.cljs, shared/coord_chip.cljs, shared/focus_resolver.cljc} (5,966 lines, every file in full); tests skimmed: fresco_advisor_cljs_test.cljc, fresco_causal_cljs_test.cljs, fresco_cljs_test.cljs, sensitive_trace_cljs_test.cljc, sensitive_trace_loop_cljs_test.cljs; producer read for the joins: implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/tool.cljs:90-290; privacy path traced through tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/{epoch.cljs, trace_collector.cljs, config.cljc, egress.cljs, panels/local_render.cljc, panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs}, implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/{capture.cljc, assembly.cljc}, implementation/core/src/re_frame/{router.cljc, subs.cljc, subs/memo.cljc, classification.cljc, trace/tooling.cljc}.
Owning specs consulted: tools/xray/spec/027-Fresco-Evidence.md, 028-Fresco-Advisor.md, 023-Trace-Panel.md (each end to end); DESIGN-RATIONALE.md (heading census + Lock #11 in full — it carries NO Fresco ruling, see census); docs/xray/11-fresco-tab.md and docs/core/fresco/16-diagnostics.md (end to end); spec/009-Instrumentation.md §Privacy and the `:rf.sub/*` vocabulary rows; tools/xray/spec/013-Trace-Consumer.md §Privacy gate; 018-Event-Spine.md §6.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Trace panel DB rows render declared-sensitive app-db values RAW; the App-DB Diff tab redacts the same record  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: privacy] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:1003-1004 (`db-changed-diff-triples` diffs `:db-before`/`:db-after` as found), trace.cljs:592-603 (`db-diff-row` prints `before`/`after` through `edn/inspect-inline`), trace.cljs:1206-1214 (`:rf.xray/trace-feed` threads no observed frame, so nothing downstream can project).
- What: under the default `:rf.egress/local-redacted` profile a `~ [:auth :token] "old" → "new"` row prints the secret, because the epoch record ships app-db raw and this panel is the one consumer that never runs it through the local-render projection.
- Evidence: the record is raw by design — implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:769 "sensitive app-db values ship RAW" and :813, assembly.cljc:13 "redaction happens at [egress]". Xray seeds `:epoch-history` verbatim (epoch.cljs:113, :140, :181). The App-DB Diff sub redacts both images with `local-render/local-render-value v observed-frame` before diffing (app_db_diff_subs.cljs:299-311, comment at :280-294 names the profile and the fail-closed arm). Grep `local-render|suppress-sensitive|egress` over `panels/trace*` reads ONE hit, a comment (trace_helpers.cljc:629); the same grep over app_db_diff_subs.cljs reads 5 real calls — that is the control. Second limb, bounded: the feed applies no `config/suppress-sensitive?` to the record's `:trace-events`, while the ring snapshot does (013:278-282, trace_collector.cljs:218-223), so a `:sensitive? true` cascade the spine hid and the `[● REDACTED N]` rail counted still renders row by row here. Its VALUES are already sentinels — `classification/project-trace-event` (classification.cljc:1137-1221) substitutes `:rf/redacted` for declared event/fx/sub payloads at emit — so that limb leaks the event's existence and undeclared tags, not data. The head-fallback in shared/focus_resolver.cljc:68-69,85-92 plus `sync-epoch-history` stamping the newest epoch (epoch.cljs:176-183) means the FIRST thing this tab shows on Ctrl+Shift+C can be that cascade.
- Action: in the feed sub, take the observed frame (as `app-db-current+diff` does) and run `:db-before`/`:db-after` through `local-render/local-render-value` BEFORE `diff-paths`; filter `:trace-events` with `config/suppress-sensitive?` for parity with the buffer. Add one privacy sentence to 023 (it has none). A planted `:sensitive` path in a fixture epoch makes the pin.

### 2. Advisor fan-out and Causal link 4 join on `[frame-id sub-id]` and drop the projected query, so every parameterization of a sub is summed into every boundary that reads one of them  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: fresco_advisor.cljc:295-303 (`read-edges` keys by `(juxt :frame-id :sub-id)`), :305-317 (`fan-out-index` sums `:fan-out` per `[frame sub-id]`); fresco_causal.cljc:371-379 (`moved`/`matched` compare `[frame-id sub-id]`).
- What: a list of N rows each reading its own `[:todo/by-id n]` cell (fan-out 1 each) prints "fan-out N" on every advisor row, and when one cell moves link 4 names all N boundaries as "notified" with join `:evidenced` — the reverse edge `notify!` walks is the DIRTY cell's readers, not the registration's.
- Evidence: the projected query is on both sides of every join — attribution edges (fresco_helpers.cljc:821 builds `[frame sub-id query]`), mounted `:reads` (tool.cljs:141-149), `:latest-reads` (027:321-323). The advisor's docstring justifies the pair key for TIMING (trace events carry only `:rf.sub/id`), then reuses it for fan-out where the finer key exists. Under whole-query redaction identical triples are already one cell, so the triple join loses nothing. Tests never exercise it: `fan-out-is-summed-across-the-cells-a-boundary-reads` (fresco_advisor_cljs_test.cljc:396-408) has one cell per sub-id per frame and the boundary reads both; every causal link-4 row mounts one boundary reading one sub (fresco_causal_cljs_test.cljs:342-359). docs/core/fresco/16-diagnostics.md:129-130 tells the reader "one subscription fans out to hundreds of views" is THE failure to look for; this defect manufactures exactly that reading on a healthy per-row list.
- Action: key `fan-out-index`, `read-edges` (for fan-out only) and `link-notified` on `[frame-id sub-id query]`; add a two-cell fixture asserting fan-out 1 and a one-boundary notified set. 028:105 "summed over the boundary's edges" should say "per cell".

### 3. `:read-orders > 1` is reported as an oscillating read set with `:loss nil` and a rung-2 route, but the producer defines it as a FOLD count that also covers redaction collapse  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: M]
- Where: fresco_advisor.cljc:393-394 (`:oscillating?`), :507-515 (the `:read-topology` arm, "an oscillating read set", basis `:derivation`, no loss); recommends rung 2 via `ladder` :631-642.
- What: the advisor asserts a topology fact the census cannot establish and routes to topology surgery on it — at any `:observed`, including an empty window (028:135 sanctions that half).
- Evidence: producer `:read-orders (count entries)` (tool.cljs:237) over entries grouped by PROJECTED key, which merges (a) one set in several orders, (b) two views with different orders, (c) different raw read sets an egress policy elided onto one key — tool.cljs:194-201 and 027:291-293 say so in terms. The producer computes the discriminator `::one-raw-readset?` and deliberately hides it as metadata (tool.cljs:219-231, rf2-h9lt). Advisor fixtures hand-build `:read-orders 4` (fresco_advisor_cljs_test.cljc:240, 284); no redaction-fold row exists. The persona's objection: a recommendation with no loss chip on a signal the producer documents as ambiguous.
- Action: decide A or B. (A) producer promotes `one-raw-readset?` to a field (schema v3→v4, lockstep pin bump) and the arm requires it — exact, costs a version. (B) keep the arm, stamp `:loss {:reason :uncorrelated}` and say "N entries folded onto this key: an oscillating set, two views' orders, or an elided-argument fold — the entry cache does not say which" — one sentence, honest, no schema move. B fits the stance; A if Mike wants the arm to stay a finding.

### 4. The Causal slice ignores the spine focus, retargets on every app dispatch, and never says whether the dispatch touched the ranked boundary  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: ergonomics] [size: M]
- Where: fresco_causal.cljc:101-115 (`newest-dispatch`), fresco.cljs:822-825 (slice anchored to top-ranked boundary + newest ring dispatch; `:rf.xray.fresco/data` inputs are `[:rf.xray/trace-buffer]` only, :790-792).
- What: the one view whose job is "one dispatch, walked" gives you no way to pick the dispatch, moves under you while the app runs, and prints "4 of 7 links evidenced · 2 of 6 joins evidenced" identically whether or not the dispatch recomputed anything this boundary reads.
- Evidence: code matches 028:257-259 and docs/xray/11-fresco-tab.md:159-161. It contradicts 018 §6: an L4 detail panel reads `:dispatch-id :epoch-id :frame` from the spine (018:1136) and "No panel maintains its own selection state; no panel reads `(peek history)`" (018:1138); `newest-dispatch` is `(peek ring)` under another name. The docs' loop (11-fresco-tab.md:184-195) has you click the spine row, then use Causal — a reader will assume the chain is about that row. The data to say "this dispatch recomputed 0 of this boundary's reads" is in hand: link 2's named sub-ids (:244) against link 3's `:latest-reads`.
- Action: decide — (i) prefer `(:dispatch-id focus)` when the ring holds it, else newest, with one 028 sentence; (ii) add the intersection count to link 3's `:says` so an unrelated pair reads as one. Both S in code; the ruling is whether 018's single-axis rule binds this tab.

### 5. docs/core/fresco/16-diagnostics.md teaches a tab that does not exist  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift] [size: S]
- Where: docs/core/fresco/16-diagnostics.md:15 ("select the view occurrence that ran"), :76-84 (five-cause table), :182 (`:opaque / :no-static-analysis`), :183 and :276 (`:host-opaque` = "hidden behind a host or native crossing … Xray still names and times the crossing"), :185 and :275 (`:uncorrelated` → "reproduce with a scripted interaction").
- What: nothing in the Fresco tab is selectable, the Why view shows own-reads plus dispatch leads only (props/context/host/retry are all `:host-opaque` here), and 028:304-323 forbids reading `:host-opaque` as a crossing in terms ("a consumer must not read it that way"); `:uncorrelated` is structural (027:326-329) so a rerun does not fix it; `:no-static-analysis` is no state this tab emits (fresco_helpers.cljc:174-202).
- Evidence: read against fresco.cljs (no click handlers on rows), fresco_helpers.cljc `explain-rows` :858-898, fresco_causal.cljc:146-181. docs/xray/11-fresco-tab.md is accurate; this page is the one that drifts, and it is the application-side entry point the other links to.
- Action: rewrite the cause table to what the Why view holds (latest-reads, leads, three named absences), fix the two `:host-opaque` rows and the `:uncorrelated` remedy to 027/028 vocabulary, drop `:no-static-analysis`. Docs only.

### 6. Causal sub-view renders the `:idle` sentence on a host with no Fresco door or a mismatched schema  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: fresco.cljs:562-570 (`causal-view` takes only `slice`; `(if (nil? slice) (presence-note :idle :causal) …)`), :675 (called without the envelope).
- What: on a Reagent app the Causal tab says "the advisor named no boundary to trace" instead of "No Fresco evidence on this host"; the Advisor view beside it does it right (:497-502 via `hh/presence envelope`).
- Evidence: 027:29-30 and the code's own comment (:640-646) say Advisor and Causal inherit the census's presence; 027:403-407 and 11-fresco-tab.md:19-21 promise the absent sentence. `a-host-without-fresco-is-ABSENT-not-empty` drives `:mounted` only (fresco_cljs_test.cljs:300-308) — control: it does assert the absent testid there.
- Action: `(or (presence-note (hh/presence envelope (nil? slice)) :causal) …)` and pass the envelope; extend that test's loop to `:causal`.

### 7. `:rf.sub/create` is counted as a body run; Spec 009 defines it as a registration event  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift] [size: S]
- Where: fresco_helpers.cljc:110-135 (`sub-recompute-operations #{:rf.sub/run :rf.sub/create}`); consumed at fresco_advisor.cljc:194-209 and fresco_causal.cljc:242-250; 028:174, :212, :264.
- What: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:199 — "A sub was registered into the reactive graph (emitted at registration time, not first reference)"; the only emit sites are `reg-sub` (subs.cljc:370, 395), carrying no duration. Counted here as an untimed recompute, it pushes a boundary to `:unattributed :host-opaque` "the owner is lowering, React or layout" and lists the sub in link 2 as recomputed.
- Evidence: frameless emits skip the ring (sensitive_trace_cljs_test.cljc:400-407), so this is inert at boot and live for a `reg-sub` run inside a handler scope (lazy module install, hot reload mid-dispatch). The four-operation matrix in fresco_skip_semantics_cljs_test pins create-as-run, so it is a deliberate but wrong reading of 009.
- Action: drop `:rf.sub/create` from the set, flip the matrix's create rows, fix 028's three mentions. One sentence in 028 explaining why create is not work.

### 8. The trace feed re-projects the whole focused epoch on every settled app epoch, even with focus pinned to an older one  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: perf] [size: S]
- Where: trace.cljs:1206-1214 (`:rf.xray/trace-feed` inputs `[:rf.xray/focus] [:rf.xray/epoch-history]`); trace_helpers.cljc:862-893 (`project-row`: ~25 keys and ~10 `area` classifications per row via area-badge/phase/stage/stage-label/stage-colour/op-family/target-detail/readable-description); rendering is uncapped by contract (023 §2) and unvirtualised.
- What: `:epoch-history` is re-read wholesale per `:rf.xray/epoch-recorded` (epoch.cljs:135-141), so in RETRO a pinned 200-row epoch is re-projected and re-rendered on every dispatch the inspected app makes, though its record is the same object.
- Evidence: grep `virtual|cap-rows|windowed|overscan` over views/resizable_table.cljs reads 0 (control: `cap-rows` reads 5 call sites in fresco.cljs). App-DB Diff already has the layer-2 record sub this needs (`:rf.xray/selected-epoch-record` over history + focus-epoch-id, app_db_diff_subs.cljs:132-136).
- Action: split `[status record]` into its own sub so the projection's input is `=` when the record did not change and the memo `:rf.sub/skip`s; the LIVE case is unchanged. Not a hot path per trace, but per epoch on a running app, and the fix is the pattern next door.

### 9. 023-Trace-Panel.md promises three sections the code does not ship and does not mark them as pending  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift] [size: S]
- Where: 023 §5/Appendix A row labels (recalculated · ran-unchanged · cache-hit · re-rendered · mounted); §10 per-step results on EVENT/FLOW rows; §12 child-epoch `↗` and parent breadcrumb; §15 cross-panel jump map.
- What: `what-happened` prints the operation's terminal segment (`run`, `skip`, `dispose`, `render`) except nine overrides (trace_helpers.cljc:453-478); EVENT rows print the event vector and FLOW rows `flow-id → path` only (:562-563, :590-594); `:parent-dispatch-id` is projected (:888) and never rendered; the only affordances are the source-coord `↗` (trace.cljs:757-771) and the `⟲` cascade button. 023 §1 calls itself "the destination", but rf2-aqusw shipped the flat list into the same document, so a reader cannot tell shipped from pending.
- Evidence: read end to end against trace.cljs / trace_helpers.cljc; 023 §3a stage labels DO match (badge.cljc:127-129), §6/§7/§13/§14 match.
- Action: stamp §5-verbs, §10, §12, §15 as "not shipped" (or move them to a roadmap section) and add the one privacy sentence from finding 1. Spec edit only.

## Spec drift by chapter
- tools/xray/spec/027-Fresco-Evidence.md: DRIFTS (minor). :29-30 and :403-407 say Advisor and Causal inherit the census's presence and an absent door renders `rf-xray-fresco-absent`; fresco.cljs:562-570 renders `:idle` for Causal regardless — code is wrong (finding 6). Everything else checked matches: sub-modes six (fresco_helpers.cljc:585-609), one-turn read + self-exclusion filter upstream of all six views (fresco.cljs:803-825), `own-frames` singleton+instance (:674-708), cap-rows on the four rosters, every testid in the rendering contract, `install!` registrations (:759-837), the seam witness (`fresco_cljs_test/the-seam-reshapes-nothing` :592 exists; note fresco_reads.cljs:25-26 cites a `fresco-reads-cljs-test` that does not — docstring only).
- tools/xray/spec/028-Fresco-Advisor.md: DRIFTS. (a) :174/:212/:264 treat `:rf.sub/create` as work; 009:199 says registration — spec and code are both wrong (finding 7). (b) :105 "fan-out summed over the boundary's edges" — code sums over the REGISTRATION across every cell (finding 2); spec should say per cell. (c) :135 states `:read-orders > 1` IS oscillation; the producer's own contract (027:291-293, tool.cljs:194-201) says it is a fold count (finding 3). (d) :396-421 describe `trace-windows` as the second producer but say nothing about the `:sensitive?` gate; it reads `rf.trace.tooling/trace-buffer`, which applies none (tooling.cljc:552-557), so a cascade the spine suppressed still anchors the slice and prices the advisor — bounded to ids and counts (the Fresco door itself ships event ids), but 013:147 says consumers MUST default-suppress and 028 should state its posture. (e) :399-401 name explain-render's `:window :frames` as the frame source; code also falls back to `:intents :frames` (fresco_reads.cljs:128-130) — undocumented, harmless. (f) :257-259 match the code (newest dispatch); the tension is with 018 §6, not with this chapter (finding 4). The native refusal (:67-92) holds: `classify` emits only `#{:computation :read-topology :unattributed}` (:486-585) and `recommend` (:722-741) reaches a `:native? true` entry through no owner it emits; empty and partial windows produce `:cap`/`:host-opaque` refusals, never a route, EXCEPT the `:read-orders` arm above. Test table (:431-436): all four suites exist at the named tiers.
- tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md: DRIFTS. §5 verb taxonomy and Appendix A row labels, §10 per-step results, §12 child/parent links, §15 cross-panel map are not implemented and not marked pending (finding 9); no privacy sentence for a panel that prints event vectors, fx args, sub old→new and app-db diffs (finding 1). §2 "no top chrome" vs the column-widths header bar (trace.cljs:979-987) — a header, not a title bar; left alone. Matches: §3 columns and row click → edn-inspector (:486-500), §3a stage mapping and labels, §6 duration sourcing (trace_helpers.cljc:760-767), §7 severity edge, §13 outcome as ordinary row, §14 empty states (:875-893) and truncation.
- tools/xray/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md: carries NO Fresco ruling — grep `Fresco|fresco` reads 0 against a control of 18 `## Lock #N` headings; the Fresco rulings live inside 027/028 themselves and docs/design/fresco/. The one lock touching this slice is #11 (:425-482, handler-coord fallback with a `(?)` annotation): Trace rows take the handler coord by construction (`:rf.trace/trigger-handler`, trace_helpers.cljc:706-716) and render no annotation — MATCHES in substance, since on this panel every row's coord is the handler's and the title names the file; left alone.
- docs/xray/11-fresco-tab.md: MATCHES the code, with two promises broken elsewhere: :19-21 (absent sentence on every view — finding 6) and the loop at :184-195 implying Causal follows the spine click (finding 4).
- docs/core/fresco/16-diagnostics.md: DRIFTS (finding 5).

## Considered, left alone
- trace.cljs:1240-1243 says "Dispatch ids are unique only within a frame"; router.cljc:41-66 allocates one process-monotonic counter. The frame-strict lookup is harmless — comment fix, not a finding.
- `advice-summary` prints "window N retained runs" where N is bundles (fresco_advisor.cljc:263, :845-848); the producer's own `:window :retained-runs` uses the same word (16-diagnostics.md:313) — consistent, leave.
- Under `:time` ordering untimed rows sort after every timed row, secondary by key string (fresco_advisor.cljc:784-791); with finding 7 fixed the memo path times every real run (memo.cljc:268-271, :367-368), so the case is near-empty.
- `op-row-attrs`/`op-row-cells` allocate three closures per row per render (trace.cljs:665-675, :763-781); styles are hoisted, closures are not — no measured cost beyond finding 8.
- focus_resolver reports `:epoch-evicted` for a host-focused `:epoch-id` that never existed (a typo'd Story beat) — the message says "evicted"; trust the programmer.

## Instruments and controls
- `git -C … rev-parse --short HEAD` → 9555881fe3; `wc -l` over the ten scope files → 5,966.
- Grep `Fresco|fresco` in DESIGN-RATIONALE.md → 0; control `^## |^### ` → 18 lock headings + subsections (instrument live on that file).

title: core+adapters: ratom sub-cache slots retire by Reaction auto-dispose — no :rf.sub/dispose on a real unmount, :ref-count is a render counter, no test can see either (rf2-pk4i6 item 8, ruled A)
description:
Shortlist item 8 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave. Size L. Sourced from FIVE findings across two independent reviews: rf2-pk4i6.4#2, .4#3, .12#1, .12#3, .12#4.

**MIKE RULED OPTION A.** His words on the wave: *"rule rf2-pk4i6 as your recommendation"*, and the recorded ruling for this item, verbatim:

> **Item 8 (Reagent dispose path): A.** Make the ratom render path a real reader, one ref per owner reaction and slot, released on the owner's on-dispose, mirroring what the UIx adapter already does. Reason: spec 006 promises the dispose emit and a live reader count, and the reference implementation exists to validate the spec; three shipped adapters telling three stories about one lifecycle is the kind of inconsistency that misleads the next implementor and the AI. B would relabel a wrong number rather than fix it. The two DOM tests (real unmount, then under StrictMode) and the holder-clear ride along.

That decision is made and is not yours to reopen. If you come to believe B is better, say so in the PR body as a recommendation and build A.

## The defect

On Reagent AND reagent-slim, a view's `@(subscribe q)` bumps `:ref-count` on every render and nothing ever decrements it. The slot is removed when the component's render Reaction drops its last watch — Reaction auto-dispose, then `compute-and-cache!`'s on-dispose closure, then a silent `dissoc`. Three consequences:

1. **`:rf.sub/dispose` never fires for the view's own slot on a real unmount.** Only its layer-2 INPUTS emit, via `release-input-ref!`. Spec 006 §Disposal guarantees promises the emit at the eviction site; Spec 009 makes dispose the fourth leg of the created/run/skip/dispose lifecycle that Xray reads.
2. **`:ref-count` is a cumulative subscribe counter**, not a live reader count, so the 1→0 edge Spec 006 describes never happens — while `subs/tooling.cljc` documents it as "the live consumer ref-count" and Xray displays it as such.
3. **No gate can see either**, which is why this survived. Every `:rf.sub/dispose` assertion in the adapter tests is driven by an explicit `rf/unsubscribe` or a direct `dispose!`.

On UIx the same view goes through `unsubscribe-if-reaction` and does emit with a live count. **Three shipped adapters, three stories about one lifecycle.**

## What option A is

In `make-ratom-spine`'s derived-value deref, take the reference ONCE per (owner reaction, slot) and register `unsubscribe-if-reaction` on the owner's on-dispose. This mirrors what `use-subscribe-2` already does on the UIx spine — **it is not a new mechanism, it is the existing one extended to the ratom path.** Then `:ref-count` is live and `:rf.sub/dispose :no-more-derefers` fires on unmount on all three adapters.

Option B — keep Reaction auto-dispose as the ratom lifetime, emit from the on-dispose closure, and relabel `:ref-count` as a subscribe counter — was considered and REFUSED, in those words: *"B would relabel a wrong number rather than fix it."* Do not build it.

## What rides along, and the one CONDITIONAL in it

Mike's ruling folds in two further findings. Both are in scope:

* **The two DOM tests (from .12#3), unconditionally.** One per ratom adapter: mount a subscribing `reg-view`, `unmount` for real under `flushSync`, await the macrotask window, assert one `:rf.sub/dispose :no-more-derefers` for the view's own query and one `:rf.view/unmounted`. Then the same body wrapped in `React.StrictMode`. A helper `await-teardown!` already exists at `frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs:168-176` — find it by content and reuse it rather than writing a second one.
* **The `component-lifecycle-reaction` holder-clear (from .12#4), CONDITIONALLY — "if the StrictMode test reads red".** So: write the StrictMode test FIRST, run it, and let its result decide. .12#4 is rated PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED, and its author says outright it was "traced by reading, not run (no browser allowed)". **If the StrictMode test passes, the holder-clear is NOT in scope — say so and stop.** A verified "the StrictMode half does not reproduce" is a complete and good deliverable for that half. Its predicted signature, so you can recognise it: the unmount count reads 1 BEFORE `.unmount` and 0 within the awaited window.

## Every citation here is STALE and that is measured, not cautious

The source findings were taken at trunk `d89a41e057`. Trunk has moved a long way since, and this artefact has been edited repeatedly today. Anchor EVERY citation to CONTENT.

The wave's own dispatch guidance, binding on you: *"Every worker opens BOTH cited anchors (the spec line and the code line) at trunk tip BEFORE editing; one of item 18's fourteen citations was mis-attributed and the same rate should be expected elsewhere."* The measured premise-failure rate across items run so far is roughly one in fourteen — and today alone one item's headline seam was refuted outright by measurement while another's stated file turned out to be in a different artefact entirely. **A verified "this premise no longer holds at tip" is a complete and good deliverable.**

- `subs.cljc` — the ref-count bump on the hit path, and the on-dispose closure that releases INPUT refs then `dissoc`s the slot with no decrement and no emit.

* **Give every negative assertion a PRECONDITION that must bite.** A pin that asserts "no stale owner" against a path where the entry is `nil` reads green because `(:active-owners nil)` is nil — that exact near-miss was caught yesterday on the resources item. Assert the thing EXISTS before asserting its shape.

**Shortlist item 15 is SEQUENCED BEHIND THIS PR.** It deletes the sub-arg cache-fragmentation guardrail from `subs.cljc`, the same file you are editing. It will not be dispatched until you merge.

## The machine exclusive matters more on this item than most

This is a DOM-test item on the ratom adapters, so it needs shadow-cljs and a browser. **That exclusive is MACHINE-WIDE and two such runs wedge silently — no error, no exit file.** Three other workers are live. Announce to the mayor when you take it and when you release it.

title: epoch: off-box egress ships the malformed fx entry raw on the :rf.error/effect-map-shape :value and :reason slots
description:
Found while fixing rf2-75yrq (PR #9902), reported rather than folded in because it is a DISTINCT carrier with its emit site in core.

`re-frame.fx/fx-entry-ok?` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc) refuses a malformed `:fx` entry and emits `:rf.error/effect-map-shape` through `emit-fx-error!`. That trace stamps the offending entry on `:value` AND interpolates `(pr-str pair)` plus `(pr-str (first pair))` into the human-facing `:reason` string. Nothing in implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc projects either slot, so the payload egresses verbatim through `rf/project-egress` with DEFAULT opts.

MEASURED THROUGH A REAL DISPATCH AND THE PUBLIC EGRESS DOOR at re-frame2 trunk 4b445388ce, no synthetic trace injection. One cascade returning three malformed entries (map head, vector head, string head), each carrying the secret, produced NINE leak paths in the projected record. Three were the rf2-75yrq `:rf.event/fx` head leak and are now closed by PR #9902. The remaining SIX are this item, two per rejected entry:

  [:trace-events 3 :tags :value 0 :password]
  [:trace-events 3 :tags :reason]
  [:trace-events 4 :tags :value 0 1]
  [:trace-events 4 :tags :reason]
  [:trace-events 5 :tags :value 0]
  [:trace-events 5 :tags :reason]

The `:reason` strings embed the secret inside prose, e.g. "Effect-map for `:do-malformed` returned an `:fx` entry `[{:password \"...\"} {:arg 1}]` whose fx-id (the first element) is ...", so a shape-driven projector reading that slot as an opaque scalar cannot see it.

WHY IT MATTERS. spec/Security.md §Off-box egress says the fx-arg payload "cannot be proven safe" and MUST fail closed, and rf2-79fvm closed `:rf.fx/args` and `:rf.event/fx` on exactly that reasoning. This is the same bytes through a third carrier on the same record, reached by the same public door. Note the category is DELIBERATELY always-on (the fx.cljc comment records that: a production build must still hear about a dropped `:fx` entry).

THE FIRST ACT IS A REACHABILITY CHECK, NOT A FIX. The same fx.cljc comment says `:failing-id` EQUALS `:event-id`, so `emit-error-both!`'s component-attribution lift does not fire and "the interpolating `:reason` stays on the DCE'd dev trace". So whether `:reason` survives a production build is NOT established, and `:value` and `:reason` may need different answers. Establish that before designing anything.

SCOPE WARNING. The emit site is in core and the projection site is in epoch. Deciding this at BOTH ends would create a second place that decides what an effect may disclose, which is what rf2-75yrq was explicitly scoped away from. Pick one end.

DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED by PR #9902. Pinning a leak as expected behaviour is what left epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj's :1715-1720 assertions encoding the rf2-79fvm leak, which the rf2-79fvm work then had to undo. A comment beside `forwarder-malformed-fx-head-redacts-whole` records the gap instead.

SIBLING. rf2-536ax / rf2-yzgnn cover `validate-fx!`'s `:received` / `:value` aliases on the `:where :fx-args` schema row — a different row, same family of "one value, several carriers, one rule".

description:

The new spec/001-Registration.md:204 correctly explains that reg-flow, reg-app-schema/reg-app-schemas and reg-http-interceptor do not write source-store descriptors, then says: For all of these the MACRO form ... is the route to an image-selectable registration. The new rf/image docstring in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:984-986 similarly says Where :ns does not work, use the corresponding MACRO immediately after listing all three exception categories.

Macro coordinate capture cannot change ownership. In that same landed core.cljc, defreg-macro reg-flow delegates to rf.core-flows/reg-flow; reg-app-schema(s) delegates to the schema functions; reg-http-interceptor delegates to rf.core-http/reg-http-interceptor. No macro creates the absent descriptor. The eight corrected individual fn-alias docstrings are otherwise consistent and useful.

Required bounded correction: scope the macro remedy in these TWO shared paragraphs to the source-store-backed resource family and routes. Say frame-owned definitions remain frame-owned through either spelling and are installed against the explicit/ambient frame. Preserve the valid macro advice for registrar-backed kinds. No ownership change, new API, diagnostic, or broader refactor.

Open rf2-nrc93 asks whether resource/route metadata should accept or forward :ns and does not cover this prose error. No open item explicitly records this macro/frame-owned counterexample. title: Correct Resources migration summary for GC retention and public policy spellings
description:
Correct three concrete statements in docs/resources/coming-from-tanstack-query.md. This is a documentation correction on one surface; preserve the existing runtime and the public API reference.

1. Line 182 describes :gc-after-ms as running after the last owner is released and says the default matches TanStack gcTime. The values match, but the retention guarantees do not. Resources arms GC on settlement, re-arms when a check finds an owner or in-flight work, and leaves that check armed on owner release. A newly owner-free idle entry can therefore be collected at the next pending check without receiving a full new interval. TanStack Query 5.102.8 starts a fresh gcTime timer when its final observer leaves.

   Independently executed controlled-scheduler comparison: both policies 1000 ms; Resources settle at t=0, owned check at t=1000 re-arms t=2000, owner leaves t=1990, collection t=2000. TanStack observer leaves t=1990, collection t=2990 (entry still present at 2989). The probe captures scheduling/delivers due events, not real browser timing. Sources: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc release-owner-from-identities and gc-fired-handler; existing resources_invalidation_gc_cljs_test.cljc; TanStack query-core query.ts removeObserver and removable.ts scheduleGc.

2. Line 194 says :keep-previous? is on the route/resource. State the supported route-entry/ensure projection policy without suggesting a reg-resource metadata key.

3. Line 220 says the registration functions have their clear-* counterparts. The public facade uses rf/clear with the registrar kind and id. Internal re-frame.core-resources wrappers are not re-frame.core exports. The API reference already documents the correct grammar; do not add aliases or rewrite it to match the stale summary.

Acceptance: the three rows describe current behavior and public spellings. Keep GC and previous-data capability credited as implemented; qualify comparison semantics rather than demoting Landed. Verify links/Markdown through the applicable docs checks. A new runtime policy or a runtime test that simply mirrors this wording is not requested.

Evidence: ai/findings/Resources/astra/review-round-2.md; evidence/gc-review-re-frame2-1.log and gc-tanstack-review.json (both probes passed); evidence/facade-portability-re-frame2-1.log; source pin f2f9ffd654b70da97e907758cc73daa3bd205d57. title: SSR hydration retains an install claim after refusing the payload
description:
Only retain hydration's install claim after the seed was accepted and committed. hydrate! currently infers successful installation from a still-live frame incarnation, which also remains live when :rf/hydrate correctly refuses malformed server data. The refused seed then poisons subsequent valid roots sharing the frame.

Remediation fence: this is the independent split of rf2-fzbj.10 Finding 2. Preserve the existing hold until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj; review/filing is authorized, implementation is not.

Ownership: impl_ssr. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc:348-354,401-422,494-507; install.cljc:211-241; hydrate.cljc:275-284. Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Reproduction through actual production-JVM public helpers:

    (rf/init! ssr/adapter)
    (rf/make-frame {:id :review/bad :platform :client})
    (ssr/hydrate! {:frame :review/bad :payload {:rf/app-db []}})
    (install/installed-payload :review/bad)
    ;; => {:digest "d6342952" :installed-by nil}; actual app-db is still {}
    (ssr/hydrate! {:frame :review/bad :payload {:rf/app-db {:server true}}})
    ;; throws :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict; app-db remains {}

This does not request new programmer-misuse validation: Spec 011:400 already expressly requires rejecting non-map transport partitions without changing either client partition. The handler implements that supported recovery path. preflight! has nevertheless already installed a digest claim; dispatch-sync returns normally after rejection, and the live-incarnation test incorrectly treats refusal as commitment. hydrate! returns the malformed payload and even calls render-tree-fn/verification as if it installed.

Fresh page-level witness in the real -Dre-frame.debug=false posture uses three roots: malformed app-db for A, corrected payload for A, valid payload for independent B. Actual statuses [:hydrated :failed :hydrated]; mount callbacks [:bad :peer]; malformed-root render-tree-fn called once; A remains {} with :installed-by :bad; B receives {:peer true}. A malformed :rf/runtime-db [] also retains a ledger claim while leaving app-db {}. Thus both partition refusal paths poison the ledger, and independent peers show the page's general isolation still works.

Expected: refusal cannot leave a successful install identity, trigger verification as a committed seed, or block a later valid root. Preserve the existing documented client-only/degraded fallback semantics and make the boot outcome consistent with them. A later verify/mount failure AFTER a real successful seed must retain the claim: reinstalling then would reset actual client state.

Suggested repair: share the existing pure payload-acceptance guard before the claim, or propagate explicit seed-commit success and release the exact claim when it is absent. A frame's continued existence proves no commit. Keep failure/release handling at the seed transaction boundary, including contained or escaping seed failures as applicable; do not broaden it over verification/mount or introduce a retry subsystem/new validation policy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Through hydrate!, malformed app-db and runtime-db partitions leave no installed-payload entry and do not verify a seed that never landed; the next valid payload installs successfully on the same frame.
- Through hydrate-page!, a refused first root cannot prevent a corrected sibling sharing its frame from installing; unrelated roots still boot.
- Preserve identical-payload idempotence after intervening local state, different-payload conflicts after a successful seed, claims after post-commit verify/mount failures, and release on missing/destroyed/replaced-frame seed paths.
- Exercise public helpers on JVM and CLJS, including production posture; handler-only/ledger-only tests miss the composition error.

Validation: fresh source-loaded Java 21/Clojure 1.12.4 -Dre-frame.debug=false probe with assertions, ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_ssr/probe-impl-ssr-2.log and .exit, exit 0. Boot resource URL prints this checkout. Controls prove a repeated successful payload preserves {:peer true :local true}, and destroy-frame! clears all three ledger entries. Attempt 1 ended on a probe-only unavailable helper during compilation and is not passing evidence. No CLJS build, browser hydration, or broad gate ran; source is unchanged.

Closed rf2-tax2, including its newest history and close reason, fixed nil-preserving DATA identity and its repair is present; it did not prove installation committed. title: Story: resolve inherited and composed effective args for canvas and saved variants
description:
Make the canvas and save/share effective-args readers use the normalized scenario args, including extends and compose. Their current raw-body resolver can show/export story defaults while run-variant executes inherited values. Saving the resulting snapshot makes the wrong defaults explicit on a new child, changing a value the programmer never overrode.

Surface and revision
- Ownership: tools_story, tools/story/**, under rf2-gwye.
- Reviewed source: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261, 2026-09-13. No owned-path change from baseline at verification.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Independently actionable split of rf2-fzbj.3 finding 3. Fresh witness expands prior evidence to BOTH extends and compose, nested args, and the real generated-form registration round trip.

Source evidence
- args.cljc:126-135 obtains :args only from raw variant metadata and merges global/story/mode/raw-variant/control layers. No parent-chain or fragment layer is resolved. get-effective-args shares this result at :137-141.
- runtime.cljc:717-770 executes and reports the compiled plan's effective args with run-arg-layers, correctly retaining inheritance/composition.
- ui/canvas.cljs:535-544 uses the raw resolver at :539 for view props and arg-dependent sub overrides. The recent selected-run-key change narrowed subscriptions but left this semantic reader unchanged.
- save_variant.cljc:60-79 and :462-465 snapshots the same raw resolver. gen-variant-snippet at :290-329 emits that snapshot as the new variant's own :args.
- ui/share.cljs:337-343 also uses the resolver for Copy EDN. Browser/share consequences are source-traced rather than dynamically executed.
- tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:1490 requires the inherited/composed args merge; :3817-3834 describes effective args feeding the view.

Concrete reproduction
Initialize Story with the plain-atom adapter and canonical vocabulary. Require save as re-frame.story.save-variant and registrar as re-frame.story.registrar:

    (story/reg-story :story.review {:args {:count 0 :nested {:value 0}}})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/parent {:args {:count 42 :nested {:value 7}}})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/child {:extends :story.review/parent})
    (def result @(story/run-variant :story.review/child))
    (def snapshot (save/snapshot-args :story.review/child))
    (def form (read-string (save/gen-variant-snippet
                 {:variant-id :story.review/saved
                  :extends :story.review/child :args snapshot})))
    (registrar/reg-variant* (second form) (nth form 2))

Measured actual outputs:
- result :effective-args = {:count 42 :nested {:value 7}}.
- snapshot = {:count 0 :nested {:value 0}}.
- New saved variant's compiled [:world :effective-args] = {:count 0 :nested {:value 0}}.

The same witness using a reg-fragment containing {:args {:count 42 :nested {:value 7}}} and a variant with only :compose reproduces exactly the same values. The explicit cell override {:count 99} is honored by snapshot-args, providing a working override control. The generator output itself is read and registered through the macro's real runtime helper, not replaced with a hand-built body.

Expected versus actual and impact
The resolved scenario should give identical values to execution, rendered props and saved export under the same run options. Actual runtime is correct, while canvas/save substitute lower-precedence defaults; if no such defaults exist, inherited-only keys disappear instead. A saved scenario then permanently shadows the inherited values with those defaults. The canvas and save agree with each other because they share the same flawed reader; the executed JVM probe does not claim to observe browser DOM.

Suggested repair
Route consumers needing effective scenario args through a resolver based on the already-normalized plan and the same run-arg-layers/cell overrides as execution. Retain one inheritance/composition authority. Avoid an args -> plan -> args require cycle: use a suitable higher-level shared resolver, or extract only the needed shared resolution boundary. Do not duplicate extends/compose traversal in every UI/export caller or change the registrar's raw-body semantics. Preserve existing mode precedence and explicit controls.

Acceptance
- Conflicting story defaults plus inherited args produce identical run result, actual canvas view prop, save snapshot and generated-form read/register/plan result.
- Include compose and nested-map counterparts, active-mode precedence, and explicit cell override controls.
- Include at least one actual CLJS canvas test observing a view prop/rendered value; JVM-only helper tests cannot prove the rendering route.
- Preserve Copy EDN's distinct generated ID behavior. This repair concerns args, not the older self-extension identity issue.

Validation and limits
Executed actual-source JVM probe ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_story/probe-tools-story-1.clj against cached Clojure 1.12.4/Malli 0.20.1, with current-source URLs printed and checked. Asserted inherited/composed run-vs-snapshot mismatch, nested values, the real generator round trip and explicit override control; bounded run derefs, cleaned frames and shutdown-agents. Probe exit 0 confirms the documented defects, not a passing suite. Evidence lives at probe-tools_story-1.log/.exit. Source-traced canvas and Copy EDN callers; no browser, full suite, packaging build, dependency install or production edit.

Deduplication and references
Read rf2-fzbj.3 current body/notes/status and newest three history entries. Current full issue-list scan and focused Story/args/snapshot searches found no dedicated nonclosed owner for this defect. rf2-fzbj.31 covers Story-MCP transport and is a different surface; no duplicate is created against it. rf2-499z and rf2-ad25 corrected compiled scripts and UI run-option threading; those changes are retained and this resolver still diverges. rf2-fjax's Copy EDN identity history is distinct: this witness uses a new, different ID and still changes the saved scenario. No closed ruling is reopened.

title: [implementation/resources] Preserve work owners and repair infinite-feed tags/error settlement
description:
Recommendation: repair three reproduced resource-runtime defects before relying on shared background reads or mutation-driven infinite feeds. Carry existing entry owners into each new read work record, evaluate/index infinite-feed tags on accepted page settlement, and route infinite background-refresh failures to the refresh error channel. No new public API or defensive validation layer is needed.

This is the single implementation/resources/** report for parent rf2-fzbj, correctness surface review 2026-09-12. Three confirmed P2 defects; remediation remains open.

Revision and scope

- Baseline and reviewed HEAD: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. git status --short -- implementation/resources was empty after review.
- Owned slice: implementation/resources/**. Principal inspected source paths: src/re_frame/resources.cljc; src/re_frame/resources/{events,state,work_ledger,timers,registry,subs,reply_handlers,mutation_events,ssr}.cljc; deps.edn, plus focused resource-runtime, work-ledger, invalidation/GC, infinite-load-more/state/subscription and optimistic-settle tests. All source paths below are relative to implementation/resources/ unless explicitly prefixed spec/.
- Covered acquisition/dedupe versus fresh-refetch transitions, entry/work ownership, release cancellation, transport work identity/frame qualification, scalar/page completion and errors, tag matching/indexing, advisory timer rearm/cancel, public projections, registry disposal, restore dangling-work reconciliation, selected mutation-settlement integration and optional-artifact dependency shape.
- Bounded coverage, not an exhaustive audit of every function: route composition/planning, SSR egress/redaction and hydration projection, scope resolver classification, mutation target validation and optimistic algebra, tooling/trace egress, browser listener attachment, actual HTTP/abort timing and packaging/deployment were not comprehensively exercised. No broad suite, browser run, compilation, server, dependency install or production/source change was made.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

F1 — P2: new read attempts forget existing entry owners and abort a still-shared request

Sources: src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:708-720 creates a new ensure/refetch work record with only payload :owner; events.cljc:990-1000 does the same for load-more (owner normalized to nil at :900); events.cljc:1159-1169 does it for refetch-page. src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:247-260 turns that single owner into :owners, or an empty set. src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:952-973 preserves the entry's existing :active-owners on entry-start-load. The cancellation decision at events.cljc:1881-1894 removes the released owner from the new record and aborts if that record is owner-free, without observing the surviving entry owners. Focus/reconnect revalidation intentionally dispatches ownerless refetches at events.cljc:1364-1369.

Trigger/reproducer, using ordinary supported commands:
1. Register a scalar resource and ensure the same key under owner A, then ensure it under owner B before settlement. The initial work row correctly holds #{A B} by dedupe.
2. Refetch that key with a :cause and no new :owner (manual refresh, focus, poll and invalidation all use this idiom). The entry still holds #{A B}, but the new work row has :owners #{}.
3. Release A before the new reply arrives. The entry still has B, yet the handler marks the new row :abort-requested and emits :rf.http/managed-abort for that request.
The same sequence after loading page 0 and issuing ownerless load-more reproduces it for an infinite feed. A refetch with :owner A also loses pre-existing B and is aborted when A releases.

Expected: existing live owners continue to need the shared key's current request. Releasing one owner cannot cancel work while another holds the entry. This is Spec 016's no-abort-shared-work rule, distinct from its intentional ownerless load-more rule at spec/016-Resources.md:1536: load-more must not MINT an owner, but the existing owners still keep the feed alive.
Actual measured: initial owners and work owners were both #{[:app :a] [:app :b]}; the initial-load release control emitted []; refetch owners remained both but work owners became #{}; releasing A left #{[:app :b]} and produced :abort-requested plus [:rf.http/managed-abort [:rf.req :review/frame [:rf.work/resource [:rf.scope/global :review/item {}] 3]]]. The infinite load-more witness produced the same abort with B still present.
Impact: route/machine/app owner release can cancel another view's live refresh or load-more. This can leave stale data or drop an expected page until another cause starts a request; it also makes the ledger's ownership evidence misleading.

Repair: when issuing a new resource attempt, initialize the work record's ownership from the resulting entry's full :active-owners, including any newly attached payload owner. Apply the same rule to ensure/refetch, load-more and refetch-page, preserving the ownerless command contract and cause attribution. Keep release's no-remaining-owner decision coherent with that set. Avoid a special-case rule for focus or load-more.
Acceptance:
- Public command tests hold A and B, force a refetch with no payload owner, release A, and prove no transport abort, B in both entry and current ledger row, a joinable running request and accepted completion. Releasing B then aborts once.
- Pair a refetch carrying A with the ownerless variant, and an ownerless infinite load-more/refetch-sweep leg. None may mint a new owner; all must inherit the already-held ones.
- Retain the initial-load dedupe control and the last-owner cancellation control. A focused negative control restoring payload-only work owners must fail the new shared-refetch assertions.

F2 — P2: successful infinite reads never produce tags, so tag invalidation cannot find the feed

Sources: src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:2861-2906 accepts a page success through entry-replace-page, settles/prunes its ledger row and reconciles readiness, but never reads the resource :tags callback, installs produced tags or reindexes the changed entry. state.cljc:1160-1202 and :1230-1275 append/replace page facts without producing tags. Contrast the scalar success at events.cljc:2440-2446 and :2464-2473, which evaluates :tags, installs them and reindexes. The actual invalidation matcher at events.cljc:1530-1538 intersects each entry's stored :tags, so this fails even though that matcher scans entries rather than relying solely on the missing reverse index.

Trigger/reproducer:
1. Register a valid infinite resource with :scope :rf.scope/global, :params-schema :map, :infinite true, :next-page-param (fn [_ _] nil), and :tags (fn [_ _] #{[:review/items]}). Register a scalar control with the same tag producer. A vector page needs no page->items accessor.
2. Ensure each resource under a live owner, then deliver its accepted success with value [1 2]. Use page-succeeded-handler for the infinite read and succeeded-handler for the scalar control, as their actual lowering dictates.
3. Send [:rf.resource/invalidate-tags {:scope :rf.scope/global :tags #{[:review/items]} :cause :write}].
Expected: both successfully loaded resources expose the declared produced tag and match invalidation. In particular spec/016-Resources.md:1604-1605 says a feed's tag invalidation and mutation :invalidates operate on the whole feed.
Actual measured: infinite :tags #{}, :tag-index nil, invalidation :fx [], :invalidated-at nil; scalar :tags #{[:review/items]}, matching index membership, :invalidated-at 100 and a :rf.resource/refetch dispatch. An instrumented tag callback was invoked only for the scalar control, never for page success.
Impact: the normal mutation-invalidates/feed pattern silently leaves stale feed data. Declaring tags does not make an infinite read invalidatable, and successful further pages/refetches do not repair the missing tag facts. This is a failed shipped invalidation contract, not a request for deferred item-level optimistic feed patching.

Repair: on every accepted infinite page success, evaluate the registered tag producer against canonical params and the resulting feed data under the resource's existing tag callback contract; install the produced tag set and update reverse indexes for that entry. Do so after page append/replacement has assembled the authoritative accumulation, so tags follow the current feed, not just an old or isolated page. Preserve unrelated owners and tags on other keys and scopes. Align any callback-data documentation only if necessary to make the accumulated data contract precise; do not add a second tag API.
Acceptance:
- A public resource test declares a constant feed tag, loads page 0, invalidates it under an active owner, and observes a request; an owner-free twin becomes durably stale without a request. Include the scalar control.
- A mutation :invalidates integration test updates an item, invalidates the declared feed tag and observes authoritative feed refresh while preserving the visible page window.
- Append/replacement tests use data-dependent tags and prove tag/index membership is updated, including removal of obsolete tags and preservation of other scopes. A negative control skipping page-success tag production must fail the new tests.

F3 — P2: infinite background-refresh failure is reported as load-more failure

Sources: src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:3014-3016 defines only first-load? (page index zero with no accumulated pages). Its non-abort/non-first-load fallback at :3187-3207 unconditionally calls entry-page-failed and emits :rf.resource/page-failed, including page zero of an already loaded feed. state.cljc:1204-1228 writes :page-error; the existing entry-failed helper at :1015-1045 is the refresh-error branch for entries with data. Public readers at src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:251-256 and :413-418 expose the two distinct error slots.

Trigger/reproducer:
1. Register an infinite feed, ensure page 0 and accept {:items [1 2] :next :cursor} (with :page->items :items).
2. Refetch the already loaded feed with cause :focus. Deliver the accepted page-zero failure {:kind :rf.http/http-5xx :status 503} through the generated page-failed reply shape.
3. Read the refresh-error and page-error projections.
Expected: the visible feed survives, status returns to :loaded and :refresh-error records the failed background refresh. :page-error means failed load-more, as specified at spec/016-Resources.md:1542, :1554 and :1570; the worked view renders a load-more retry from that field. A load-more failure should continue to use :page-error.
Actual measured: status :loaded and data unchanged, but :refresh-error nil and :page-error equal to the 503 envelope. The actual public refresh-error projection returned nil and the page-error projection returned the envelope. A real load-more failure control produced that same page-error shape, demonstrating that the two distinct operations are collapsed.
Impact: consumers following the documented UI grammar suppress the background-refresh warning and instead offer a misleading 'could not load more' retry. That retry can append the next page while the failed refresh target remains stale.

Repair: distinguish a refresh of existing feed data from an append failure at the accepted page-failure boundary. At minimum, page zero with existing data must use the existing refresh failure transition and :rf.resource/refresh-failed trace, while page-zero first load retains :error and actual load-more retains :page-error. Preserve the current accumulated pages and stop any failed sweep coherently. Do not reinterpret the existing page>0 sweep regression without checking its established rule; this finding directly proves the ordinary/default page-zero refresh case.
Acceptance:
- One public event/subscription regression covers successful page 0, failed default refetch, :refresh-error envelope, nil :page-error, unchanged data and :loaded status; the next successful refresh clears the refresh error.
- Pair first-load page-zero failure (:error) and load-more failure (:page-error) controls, plus abort controls (no user-visible failure). Preserve established multi-page sweep failure behavior unless deliberately clarified.
- A negative control routing the refresh through entry-page-failed must make the new refresh projection assertion red.

Validation evidence and limits

These are executed source-handler counterexamples, not grep-only findings. Three completed defect probes used java -cp with the existing implementation/.cpcache/B4312067B0B791B77AE2C8443688A27C.cp dependencies and clojure.main reading a PowerShell single-quoted here-string from stdin. They required the actual resources event/registry/state/work-ledger namespaces plus existing schema and managed-HTTP hooks, called production handlers with explicit causal coeffects, and asserted the observed erroneous results and controls. Each printed the loaded source URL file:/C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc, verifying the inspected checkout, and each returned its own exit 0 (roughly 9.4 s, 8.1 s and 8.4 s). A preliminary load probe passed; an initial ownership probe failed closed with :rf.error/http-artefact-missing before re-running with the required re-frame.http.managed namespace. No fixture stub replaced the handlers, ownership decisions, tag producer/matcher, transitions or public projection functions.

The probes execute the CLJ arms of the shared CLJC source. They pass effects forward as ordinary values and inspect emitted abort/refetch instructions; they do not execute a network request, browser AbortController, renderer, reactive subscription invalidation, timer callback, full cascade or CLJS compiler. No suite is claimed green. Remediation should add/run focused CLJS event-path tests and appropriate existing resource gates in an isolated worker checkout.

Existing coverage inspected: resources_invalidation_gc_cljs_test.cljc:449-479 and resources_work_ledger_cljs_test.cljc:461 onward prove shared ownership only on initial in-flight dedupe, not inheritance into a later attempt. resources_infinite_load_more_cljs_test.cljc:131 declares feed tags but its success/invalidation coverage does not assert their production. That file's :334 onward and :416 onward cover load-more/first-load error channels; :563 onward intentionally covers a failed page>0 refetch-sweep leg, which this report does not reclassify.

Prior-work / duplicate review

Read bd prime; searched resources memories and an all-status 1326-row bd list snapshot by resource/mutation titles and ownership/refetch, page-error/page-success, infinite-feed/tag/invalidation terms in descriptions, notes and close reasons. Read current rf2-veef and rf2-wcdj4, and fetched their histories: both are closed corrections to optimistic rollback's live-work preservation or exact-key invalidation/affected-key evidence, not the fresh read ownership or infinite page settlement defects above. rf2-y8jjk is the closed same-token route-replanning/subset-release work; it deliberately reuses the same release core but does not populate inherited owners on new resource attempts. No matching current bead was found for these three defects. Older source comment IDs are historical provenance, not evidence of a currently open duplicate.

Unverified risks are not counted as findings: stale-subscription liveness under memoising browser adapters and wrong-frame replies' stale-branch ledger/handle cleanup received preliminary inspection only. Neither is asserted as a demonstrated defect here. The three findings above stand independently of those questions.
