title: ssr/streaming: the walker emits a fragment's attribute map as a child, same defect as rf2-3357
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 by the rf2-3357 worker, in the file next door to the one it was fixing. It is the SAME defect as rf2-3357 in a SECOND code path, so read rf2-3357's close reason first — the diagnosis, the fix shape and the ruling on what to do with a fragment's attributes all transfer unchanged. THE DEFECT. `re-frame.ssr.streaming`'s `:<>` arm is `(walk-children (rest element) …)`. `(rest element)` does not skip a props map at position 1, so the map itself is walked as a CHILD and emitted into the stream. MEASURED at source, on the landed code: render-shell [:<> {:key "k"} [:div "x"]] => {:shell-html "{:key "k"}
x
"} WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD RATHER THAN A PASSENGER: it was outside rf2-3357's write surface, and that worker declined to widen a bounded repair — correctly. But it means the fix that landed for the non-streaming emitter did NOT fix this path, and anyone reading rf2-3357 as "fragments are fixed" would be wrong. THE FIX IS THE SAME ONE LINE. rf2-3357 landed `(if (map? (second el)) (drop 2 el) (rest el))` in `re-frame.ssr.emit`, which is the spelling the DOM-tag branch in that same file already uses and is equivalent to the React-side codec's `props-map?`. Apply the same shape here. CHECK WHETHER THE ROOT-ATTRS ANALOGUE EXISTS ON THIS PATH TOO, because on the non-streaming side that was the worse half of the bug: there, the props map becoming the first child meant root-attrs were threaded onto a value that cannot carry an attribute, and the `data-rf-render-hash` marker VANISHED ENTIRELY — a silent hydration-mismatch hazard hiding behind a visible garbage-text one. If the streaming walker threads anything onto its first child, expect the same shape and prove it either way. THE ATTRIBUTE RULING IS ALREADY MADE AND MUST NOT BE RE-LITIGATED: a fragment's attributes are SILENTLY DROPPED, `:key` included. A fragment is not an element, so no attribute on one has a wire representation; every sibling emitter here already drops; React itself only warns in dev; and refusing would mint a new server-stricter-than-client divergence. rf2-3357's close reason carries the full argument. GATES: whatever covers the streaming path — the JVM SSR suite and `test:ssr-node` were the substance for rf2-3357. Prove the new row can fail by reverting to `(rest el)` and watching it go red naming the emitted EDN, then restore and verify by git BLOB hash, committing before you plant.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON PR #9593, merged as 4f3f60c46a. The streaming `:<>` arm now uses rf2-3357's exact spelling — `(if (map? (second el)) (drop 2 el) (rest el))` — which is also this file's OWN idiom, twenty lines above in `walk-dom-tag`. No helper was extracted, deliberately: the parent's fix used the file's existing spelling rather than minting an abstraction, and a second path is not yet a reason to generalise. REPRODUCED AT BASE BEFORE FIXING, all in the worker's own tree: render-shell [:<> {:key "k"} [:div "x"]] => {:key "k"}
x
render-shell [:<> {} [:div "x"]] => {}
x
render-shell [:<> {:key "k"}] => {:key "k"} where the already-fixed render-to-string gave "" That third reading is the useful one: it isolates the defect from any child rendering at all. THE ROOT-ATTRS ANALOGUE DOES NOT EXIST ON THIS PATH, AND WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSERTED — which is what the brief asked for, since "no equivalent here" is a fine answer but not a free one. Three independent readings: the walker fns take only `[element continuation-accumulator]` and `render-shell` only `[root-hiccup]`; `root-attrs` occurs in exactly ONE file under `implementation/ssr/src` — emit.cljc, control 48 hits there; and `data-rf-render-hash` never occurs in streaming.cljc at all. The `render-hash` this file does carry is a payload argument, not a root attribute. So rf2-3357's worse half — root-attrs threaded onto a props map that cannot carry an attribute, making the hydration marker vanish — has no counterpart here. The streaming defect was the visible one only. AI attribution declined in the commit and the PR body.

title: [tools/story-mcp] Nested JSON cell overrides do not reach existing keyword-keyed args
description:
Surface: tools/story-mcp, nested scenario argument mapping. Reviewed snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d has no relevant source drift.

Supported contract and exact causal trace:
- Story explicitly supports nested keyword-keyed args and deep-merging cell overrides: tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md:176 and tools/story/src/re_frame/story/args.cljc:37-58,102-135.
- The shipped registered fixture tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/controls_nested_cljs_test.cljc:403-429 uses :args {:settings {:title "Nested title" :enabled? true}}. A native [:settings :title] edit is required to resolve to {:settings {:title "Edited" :enabled? true}}.
- Story MCP advertises :cell-overrides as an object / {keyword any} on preview-variant, run-variant and snapshot-identity (tools/story-mcp/spec/API.md:102 and tools/testing.cljc / tools/dev.cljc descriptors).
- Normal JSON ingress deliberately preserves nested string keys (protocol.cljc:116-145,276 ff). The shared safe-cell-overrides at tools/args.cljc:132-159 only resolves the top-level settings key; its values pass through verbatim. read-run-opts uses it at :477.
- Consequently JSON arguments {"variant-id":"story.nest.roundtrip/map-arg","cell-overrides":{"settings":{"title":"Edited"}}} produce opts {:cell-overrides {:settings {"title" "Edited"}}}. Against that registered base, resolve-args yields {:settings {:title "Nested title" :enabled? true "title" "Edited"}}. The consumer reading [:settings :title] still sees "Nested title". No unknown-id guard fires: settings is valid, and the inner key is not considered. The requested nested change was not made even though the run/preview/hash accepts the supplied tuple.

Impact: the ordinary nested controls scenario supported by Story cannot be expressed faithfully through the MCP object override. A run can evaluate the unchanged nested keyword arg and snapshot-identity can key the unintended mixed-key tuple, defeating the agent's test/edit loop. This is a supported-nested-args versus MCP-wire-mapping contract tension, not a request to coerce all data values.

Smallest repair: at the shared run-options seam, resolve a nested wire key to an EXISTING effective-args key only when that mapping is unambiguous; preserve exact existing string keys and verbatim string-key payload data, and never intern fresh keywords. An explicit path/value representation is another possible contract resolution, but the lean existing-key-aware seam is preferable where unambiguous. Define ambiguous mixed-key behavior explicitly without blanket recursive keywordization. Keep top-level unknown-id refusal and no-interning behavior.

Dedupe: active+closed searches for story-mcp/cell-overrides and description searches safe-cell-overrides/nested override found no equivalent. Fully read closed rf2-sw1d: it corrects unknown TOP-LEVEL scenario identifiers, not this known nested-key mismatch; its no-intern and atomic-refusal decisions remain. Relevant Story-MCP memories had no matching nested-key ruling. Historical rf2-3luf3 is absent from current tracker search; its current ingress spec and tests were read directly.

Evidence limits: exact source trace plus existing supported Story fixture; no JVM/CLJS MCP execution, browser, build or suite run. No claim about duplicate JSON key serialization.
acceptance_criteria: Drive actual JSON normalization through each shared consumer with a registered {:settings {:title "Nested title" :enabled? true}} base and {"settings":{"title":"Edited"}} override. Assert the effective keyword :title is Edited, untouched :enabled? remains true, and native/MCP scenario hashes agree for the same intended tuple. Cover legitimate existing string-keyed maps without converting their keys, unambiguous keyword-key alignment, and explicit ambiguous-key policy. title: spec(004B): the ismap row is falsified against react-dom 19.2; record the boolean value disposition
description:
004B §Booleans and their neighbours names `ismap` in the boolean-attribute set explicitly — "the set is the react-dom/server 19.2.0 boolean-attribute list, probed row-by-row (S1b) — it includes `hidden`, `muted`, and `ismap` (React 19 dropped the camel `isMap` prop)". MEASURED AGAINST THE INSTALLED react-dom 19.2.0, THAT ROW IS FALSE. A boolean `ismap` is not a boolean-class attribute in react-dom 19.2 at all: - `pushAttribute` has no `case "ismap"` / `case "isMap"`, so a boolean falls into the default branch, where a boolean survives only behind a `data-`/`aria-` prefix. It is DROPPED. - The dev build's `validateProperty` boolean case list does not carry it either: `
` warns "Received `true` for a non-boolean attribute `ismap`" and emits nothing. - Measured directly: `renderToStaticMarkup(React.createElement('div', {ismap: true}))` → `
`; same for `false`; same for the camel `isMap`. `hidden` and `muted`, the row's two other named members, ARE correct — both presence-serialise. Only `ismap` is wrong. WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is NOT obviously a defect to fix by deleting the name: `ismap` is a genuine HTML boolean attribute on ``, so presence IS the HTML-correct rendering, and react-dom simply does not support a boolean spelling for it. What is unsettled is whether 004B's conversion table tracks HTML or tracks react-dom where the two part. 004B declares itself the react-dom 19.2.0 list, which says remove it; the attribute's own HTML semantics say keep it. That is a spec decision, not an implementation one. STATE ON MAIN. `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers/boolean-attrs` still carries `"ismap"`, following 004B, and `re-frame.ssr-boolean-attr-react-parity-test` records the divergence explicitly (in `divergences`, with the reasoning) and PINS it — the test asserts both that react-dom's evidence carries no `ismap` row and that `boolean-attr-class` says `:presence` — so whichever way this is ruled, the test names the place to change and cannot drift silently. SECOND, SMALLER ITEM ON THE SAME TABLE. 004B does not mention react-dom's generic boolean `value` grouping at all. react-dom stringifies a boolean `value` (`value="true"`) because `value` shares a serialiser branch with `contentEditable`/`draggable`/`spellCheck`, not because it is booleanish. rf2-r9kf disposed of it from the SSR side — `value` stays `:ordinary`, because a string or number `value` (the only kinds a form control carries) serialises identically under the ordinary rule, a boolean `value` on a form control is an author error rather than a state, and `value` is already a 004B form-control special form whose meaning varies per element (`` attribute, `
close_reason: Fixed on PR #9215. READING TAKEN: 004B is describing REACT, not HTML — the row scopes itself in its own words ("the set is the react-dom/server 19.2.0 boolean-attribute list, probed row-by-row (S1b)") and cites a probe, so the HTML-vs-React scoping alternative is refuted by the text rather than left open. Outcome (1): 004B was wrong about React's behaviour. MEASURED against installed react-dom 19.2.0, stronger than the bead recorded: the string 'ismap'/'isMap' appears NOWHERE in react-dom 19.2.0's dev builds (0 occurrences in react-dom-server-legacy.node.development.js, react-dom-server.node.development.js and react-dom-client.development.js), so it is absent from possibleStandardNames — the probe's own candidate source — and there was no ismap boolean for React 19 to have 'dropped the camel isMap prop' of; the name could never have come from the S1b probe. Direct probe: div/img ismap={true} and {false} and camel isMap={true} all emit NOTHING (dev warns 'Received true for a non-boolean attribute ismap'; camel warns as an unrecognized prop), while a STRING ismap="" DOES reach markup on — via the pass-through default, react-dom's only route for it. Fixture regenerates byte-identical modulo CRLF, carries no ismap row, carries value="true"/value="false". title: Seven GUIs Timer counts delayed callbacks instead of elapsed time
description:
## Correctness finding

The runnable Seven GUIs Timer advances `:elapsed-ms` by the configured 100 ms sampling interval each time a delayed callback happens, rather than by the time that actually elapsed. `:dispatch-later` promises “not before this delay”, not an exact clock pulse. Any late callback therefore makes the timer permanently slow: if the main thread is blocked for 5 seconds, the next callback moves the display by only 100 ms and schedules the following callback from that late point. Browser throttling, a busy event loop, or a suspended tab can make the nominal 10-second timer take arbitrarily longer.

That is the classic timer mistake in the example whose stated purpose is to teach concurrent time/user interactions. It can mislead both a programmer and an AI into copying a callback-counter as an elapsed-time clock.

## Exact evidence

- `examples/core/seven_guis/timer/core.cljs:31-34` defines `tick-ms` as 100. `:timer/initialise` schedules `[:timer/tick 0]` after that delay at lines 81-88. The live tick at lines 90-103 computes `next-elapsed` as `(min (+ elapsed-ms tick-ms) duration-ms)` and only then schedules another 100 ms callback. No event timestamp or clock sample participates.
- The runtime does not promise periodic precision. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:275-344` arms each `:dispatch-later` using `rf.interop/set-timeout!`; the CLJS implementation is exactly `js/setTimeout` at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:141-149`. The HTML Living Standard explicitly says timer callbacks are not guaranteed to run exactly on schedule and delays from CPU load or other tasks are expected: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/timers-and-user-prompts.html#timers .
- The canonical 7GUIs task describes a gauge and label for elapsed time, and names concurrency, competing user/signal interactions, and responsiveness as the challenge: https://eugenkiss.github.io/7guis/tasks/#timer . Its cited FrTime source computes elapsed as current time minus the reset/start time, rather than counting wakeups (`Crossing State Lines`, pp. 3-4): https://cs.brown.edu/~sk/Publications/Papers/Published/ick-adapt-oo-fwk-frp/paper.pdf .
- re-frame2 already has the small, replay-honest input this example needs. The router stamps every dispatch (including a fresh `:dispatch-later` child) with recordable `:rf/time-ms` at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:122-152`; a handler opts in with `:rf.cofx/requires [:rf/time-ms]` and receives the value flat. `docs/core/coeffects.md:22-53,87-95` teaches exactly that contract. No ambient `Date.now`, new scheduler, or public API is needed.
- The only focused Timer behavior test positively pins the wrong model. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_generation_guard_cljs_test.cljs:97-105` dispatches a live tick and requires `elapsed-ms` to become `before + timer/tick-ms`. The test replaces `:dispatch-later` with a capture function (lines 28-33, 75-78), so it proves generation-chain ownership but cannot observe a late host callback. `example_frame_scoping_cljs_test.cljs` only covers schema registration, and `test:examples-compile` only compiles declared builds. Repository search found no browser-level Timer behavior test.
- History shows the fixed-step accounting dates to the initial example import. `e296c072b3` correctly added the generation token for Reset races, `e0e7a5aaec` correctly re-armed after raising a completed timer's duration, and `be375bc4c8` later added the generation-guard test; none changed elapsed accounting. The current test consequently protects the cancellation/re-arm idea and the callback-counter together even though only the former is correct.

## Impact

A user can open this ordinary 10-second example, switch tabs or make the main thread busy, return well after the duration, and still see a timer far from complete. More importantly, this is a canonical teaching example: it currently says time lives honestly inside the event pipeline while demonstrating that callback count equals time. Real SPAs routinely experience delayed tasks. Copying this pattern into cooldowns, progress indicators, session timers, or polling UX produces clocks that drift under exactly the load where correctness matters.

The fix is valuable because it showcases re-frame2's intended ergonomic answer: scheduling decides when to sample; a declared recordable coeffect says what time it was when the sample entered the pipeline. That keeps handlers pure, replay deterministic, and the API minimal.

## Bounded recommendation

Keep the 100 ms `:dispatch-later` chain as the display sampling cadence and keep the existing generation guard. Change only elapsed accounting:

1. Add a durable last-sample/reset timestamp to `TimerState` (or an equivalent minimal anchor).
2. Declare `:rf/time-ms` on the handlers that establish or consume the anchor. On a live tick, advance by the non-negative observed delta since the prior live sample, clamp at `duration-ms`, store the new anchor, and schedule at most one next tick. A stale-generation tick must still be a complete no-op.
3. Reset should zero elapsed, bump the generation, and establish the new time baseline. When increasing a completed timer re-arms it, establish the baseline at that user event so time spent stopped is not charged after restart.
4. Rewrite the focused example test to inject explicit `:rf.cofx {:rf/time-ms ...}` values. Keep its exact-one-chain/stale-generation teeth, but prove a 450 ms late tick advances by 450 ms rather than 100 ms and a tick beyond the deadline clamps once and stops.
5. Make the comments/Seven GUIs README distinguish the 100 ms sampling cadence from elapsed-time measurement.

An equivalent anchor-based formulation is fine; the invariant is that elapsed state follows recorded causal time, not callback count.

## Non-goals

- No new timer, cancellation, clock, or public framework API.
- Do not replace the event pipeline with `requestAnimationFrame`, a component-local interval, or direct mutation.
- Do not remove or redesign the generation token, post-completion duration re-arm, slider, subscriptions, or view.
- No attempt to provide a general pause/resume/countdown library or define every possible wall-clock adjustment policy.
- Do not broaden this into a review of machine `:after`, resource timers, or other examples.

## Posture fit

This is a small honesty repair to a high-leverage example, not gold plating. One built-in coeffect and one timestamp make the happy path correct under ordinary browser behavior while teaching the library's elegant existing time boundary. It reduces surprise and gives programmers/agents a pattern worth copying without adding machinery.

## Duplicate search

All-status `rg` searches over `.beads/issues.jsonl` covered the exact path and namespace, `:timer/tick`, `tick-ms`, callback/elapsed combinations, fixed-tick and timer drift, browser/background/hidden throttling, callback counting, and `:rf/time-ms` with Timer. I also enumerated every issue title containing “timer”. No issue owns this example outcome. The timer-titled beads concern machines hydration/cancellation, Hicasso reaper coalescing, a schemas fixture rewrite, and skill prose; all are distinct.

## Uncertainty

I did not compile or run a browser in this review because the assigned worktree intentionally had no `node_modules` link and the task forbade creating one. The defect is source-level and does not depend on timing luck: the handler unconditionally adds 100 for one callback, while the production effect delegates to `setTimeout`, whose late-fire behavior is explicit. `:rf/time-ms` is epoch wall time rather than a monotonic duration clock, so the minimal implementation should clamp negative deltas to zero; inventing a new monotonic recordable clock would be disproportionate to this example.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The Timer's live elapsed value is derived from recorded `:rf/time-ms` deltas (or an equivalent recorded time anchor), never from “one callback equals `tick-ms`”. There is no direct ambient clock read in an event handler.
2. A deterministic focused CLJS test supplies an initial timestamp and a live tick 450 ms later; elapsed becomes 450 ms (the current implementation must fail this control by producing 100 ms). A later timestamp beyond the duration clamps elapsed exactly to the duration and schedules no further tick.
3. The existing generation semantics remain pinned: a stale-generation tick changes neither db nor scheduling, Reset produces observable zero, bumps the generation, establishes a fresh time baseline, and arms exactly one chain.
4. Raising duration after completion still re-arms exactly one chain, and the first resumed tick counts from the re-arm event rather than including time spent stopped.
5. The 100 ms value remains only the sampling/scheduling cadence; comments and the Seven GUIs teaching prose no longer describe fixed callbacks as elapsed time.
6. The example schema/frame-scoping test, focused generation/timing test, consolidated CLJS Node lane, and all-example compile gate pass. A temporary mutation back to `(+ elapsed-ms tick-ms)` makes the delayed-timestamp assertion red and is restored before handoff.
7. No new public API, general timer abstraction, component-local timer state, or changes outside the Timer example and its existing focused test/teaching row are introduced.
close_reason:
Fixed on branch worker/extimer-a, PR #9260 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9260). Premise VERIFIED at source before acting: origin/main's examples/core/seven_guis/timer/core.cljs line 98 still read (min (+ elapsed-ms tick-ms) duration-ms), and the brief's cited line numbers (31, 88, 98, 103) matched exactly.

WHAT LANDED. Elapsed time is now measured rather than counted. :timer/initialise, :timer/tick, :timer/set-duration and :timer/reset each declare :rf.cofx/requires [:rf/time-ms] and read the recorded reading flat, so no handler reaches for an ambient clock and the run stays replayable (AC 1). A new :sampled-at-ms anchor on TimerState holds the reading of the last accepted sample; a live tick advances by the observed interval since it, clamps at :duration-ms, and re-anchors. A negative delta clamps to zero, so an NTP step backwards cannot rewind the timer. Reset and the post-completion re-arm both re-anchor so time spent stopped is not billed to the resumed run (AC 3, AC 4); set-duration deliberately leaves the anchor alone when a live chain owns it, since moving it there would discard the interval since that chain's last sample. The generation guard, re-arm, slider, subs and view are untouched, and no new timer, clock or public API was added (AC 7).

TEACHING PROSE (AC 5). tick-ms' docstring, the ns docstring and the EVENTS note now name 100ms as a sampling cadence and say why a callback count is not an elapsed time. examples/core/seven_guis/README.md's Timer row and its 'what this demonstrates' bullet say the same in the cluster's own voice.

REGRESSION (AC 2). implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_generation_guard_cljs_test.cljs — the canonical home for this example's behaviour, per its own docstring, and examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). That file POSITIVELY PINNED THE DEFECT (it asserted elapsed becomes before + timer/tick-ms), so it could not be left alone. All three deftests now inject the clock as data via {:rf.cofx {:rf/time-ms t}}, so every assertion is an exact equality with no wall clock: a 450ms-late callback advances 450ms; a punctual sample adds exactly 100ms; a sample far past the deadline clamps once and stops the chain, and a straggler cannot push past the duration; Reset and re-arm each establish a fresh baseline. The stale-generation tick is now dispatched with a MOVED clock reading, so the whole-db comparison additionally pins that a retired tick does not even re-anchor.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (AC 6, partially). The CLJS node-test lane was NOT run: five sibling workers were live and a cold consolidated shadow-cljs compile wedges rather than fails; this worktree had no node_modules and no build cache. CI owns that lane and the examples-compile sweep. In its place, a JVM harness transcribed the two competing tick formulae and ran the exact scenarios the CLJS test asserts (captured exit 0): the shipped formula meets the assertion in 5/5, and both designated controls are red under the pre-fix one — the 450ms case reads 100 (old) vs 450 (new), and the clamp case 650 vs 10000. Three further scenarios agree under both formulae BY DESIGN and are labelled guards, not controls: the punctual case is the point, and the Reset/re-arm cases discriminate on the anchor being re-established, which a tick-only harness cannot model since the pre-fix code has no anchor at all. A Clojure reader check over all changed CLJS files also passed (exit 0). The harness is a transcription of the arithmetic, not the example source, and is not a substitute for the CLJS lane.

title: hic tooling: chapter 20 step 2 of 3 (hm/shadow! comparison) is unreachable - it inherits the L3 DOM gap, and its :reference premise needs the original the same chapter tells you to delete
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit), a
BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F13 · outcome 2 · `unresolved` · `tooling`

**Trying to**

Execute step 2 of the migration chapter's three-step process. The chapter is
emphatic about the order — "Do not start with the codemod. Read the report,
port **and prove** a screen, then apply mechanical edits and run the proof
again" — and §3 is the proof: `hm/shadow!` mounts the Reagent original and the
Hicasso candidate against isolated copies of one seeded frame, drives both with
one script, and compares canonical DOM and intent streams.

**Instead**

Could not run it, for two independent reasons, and the second is the
interesting one.

**(a) It is a mounted-tier door.** `hm/shadow!` lives in
`re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted`, so it needs the DOM that P1-F12 says the
documentation never provisions. That alone blocks it.

**(b) Its premise conflicts with the chapter's own advice, in the ordinary
case.** `hm/shadow!` needs `:reference` — the Reagent original — *still
mounted*, and the sample makes that concrete with two namespaces,
`app.views.article-row-reagent` and `app.views.article-row`. So proving a port
requires keeping the original alongside the port for the length of the
migration. But the same chapter says, three paragraphs later, "When the screen
is green and its browser tests pass, remove the Reagent original." Those are
compatible in principle — keep it, prove it, then delete it — and the chapter
never says so, never shows the intermediate two-namespace state, and never
mentions that the *unported* callers (P1-F08) are pointing at one of the two.

Concretely, for a `reg-view` application (P1-F06) there is a further problem
neither half addresses: to keep a `:reference` at all I would have had to keep
the old `reg-view` **and** the old `dispatch`-closure props **and** a second
copy of every shared view, in one namespace, compiling. That is a substantial
amount of scaffolding to stand up for a comparator I then could not run.

**Looked at**

- `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §3 in full, including the sabotage-control
  paragraph
- `15-testing.md` "Migration shadow tests"
- `api-reference.md` `hm/shadow!` row (the `:reference` / `:candidate` /
  `:initial-events` / `:script` roster)

**Resolved by**

Nothing. I substituted a different proof, and I want to be explicit that it is
weaker in one specific way and stronger in another. Weaker: it is not a
DOM-for-DOM comparison against the original, so a cosmetic divergence I did not
think to assert on would pass unnoticed — and shadow comparison's whole value is
catching exactly that. Stronger: it drives the *real* release bundle through a
real interaction sequence (sign in → open the editor → type → publish →
navigate → page the feed → favourite a card), which the chapter's own §3 note
concedes shadow comparison does not do ("It does not prove untested paths").

I also could not perform the chapter's sabotage control, since there was no
comparator to sabotage.

**Bead**

Two: (i) `hm/shadow!` inherits the L3 DOM gap and is the single most costly
place to inherit it, since it is a named step of the migration process; (ii) §3
should show the intermediate state — original kept, port beside it, callers
pointing where — because that state is what a migrator actually has to build.
close_reason:
Chapter 20 §3 rewritten (PR #9131). Both halves of the bead's ask are addressed at the chapter, and one thing the bead did not name turned out to be the concrete reason step 2 is unusable.

THE SAMPLE WAS WRONG. §3 passed the Reagent original as a plain Hiccup head, :reference [old/article-row {:article-id 7}]. shadow!'s own docstring says both sides are handed to Hicasso by mount!, so a foreign original arrives 'through the runtime's own crossing, [:> C props] or a declared h/defhost' - and a plain function in Hicasso head position is a loud refusal, not a Reagent render. The sample is now [:> old-article-row {:id 7}] with (def old-article-row (r/reactify-component old/article-row)) hoisted to top level, and the paragraph beneath says why :reference is a crossing and :candidate is a plain head.

Two consequences of that crossing are now stated. Prop names do NOT round-trip on this route - codec/host-entry camelCases the key, reagent impl.util/shallow-obj-to-map keywordizes the name React carried, so :article-id reaches the original as :articleId - which is why the sample crosses :id and lets both sides read the rest from the seeded frame. And the original's callbacks reach the frame through the crossing's declared contract, not through its own ambient dispatch closures.

(ii) THE INTERMEDIATE STATE, the bead's explicit ask: '### The intermediate state' is a three-namespace table - the original moved verbatim into app.views.article-row-reagent and rendered only by the shadow test; the port at app.views.article-row rendered by the shell and the test; the unported shell. Callers point at the PORT, including unported ones, which is what the new 'Views shared across the boundary' section (rf2-4387) is for. The removal advice is sequenced rather than free-floating: delete the original and the shadow test together, after checking no caller still points at it.

(i) THE L3 GAP: §3 now opens with '### What this step needs first' - hm/shadow! is an L3 door needing the test kit and a target with real React and a real DOM - so a reader is not ambushed at step 2 of 3, and the last section is named for when that is more than the screen is worth. The underlying gap (chapter 15 never says where the DOM comes from) is rf2-w4yz and is untouched here.

NOT RUN, and stated as such in the PR body. No in-repo test drives hm/shadow! with a foreign :reference - test_kit/test/re_frame/hicasso/shadow_dom_cljs_test.cljs uses Hicasso views on both sides of every row. The correction is derived from shadow!'s docstring and from reading Reagent's reactify-component and Hicasso's host-entry. The docstring's own example carries the same :article-id mis-naming and the same inline reactify-component; filed as rf2-rx99 (test_kit was outside this fence), which also notes the missing witness for the foreign-:reference route.

Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs build --strict 0, check_guide_samples.py 0, each sabotage-controlled, all re-run green after rebase.

Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F08 · outcome 2 · `unresolved` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Port "the feed" as a screen. Two of its views — `article-preview` (the article
card) and `pagination` — are also rendered by `profile.cljs`, which is not one
of my two screens and stays on Reagent.

**Expected**

Chapter 20 to say something. Its §2 is called "Port one screen by hand" and its
whole argument is that a screen is the right unit: "Migrate a complete screen
rather than changing all component declarations… A screen-level port gives
shadow comparison a useful unit." A shared view is what makes "a complete
screen" ambiguous, and in any real application there is always one.

**Instead**

Silence. The chapter's only nearby advice points the other way — "When the
screen is green and its browser tests pass, remove the Reagent original.
Keeping both copies invites future divergence" — which forbids the duplication
route without offering the alternative.

**Looked at**

- `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §2, §3
- `09-interop.md` "Render a Hicasso view from native React"
- `escape-ladder.md` — the `h/as-component` rung, which is about "going
  outward" generally rather than about this boundary

**Resolved by**

Choosing to move both shared views to Hicasso and bridge them back out with
`h/as-component`, so `profile.cljs` mounts them as `[:> article-preview-component
{…}]`. This worked and I now think it is right — the boundary lands on the
*view*, so there is one implementation — but I want to record how uncertain it
was at the time. I nearly duplicated instead, which the chapter would have let
me do without a word of warning beyond a general one about divergence.

One consequence I did not anticipate and should have: bridging a view outward
makes its props cross React, so the props contract stops being a CLJS-only
concern. It worked here (a CLJS map at `:article` and a vector at `:on-select`
both survived the round trip intact through the Reagent adapter's `[:>]`), but
nothing in the docs promised that, and `09-interop.md` only says React props
come back "with canonical names… and identity-preserved values" from the
*Hicasso* side. I could not find a statement about what a **Reagent** parent
does to a CLJS value on the way in.

**Bead**

Chapter 20 needs a short section on views shared across the migration
boundary, and `09-interop.md`'s `h/as-component` section should say what a
Reagent parent's props do at the crossing.
close_reason:
Chapter 20 now carries '### Views shared across the boundary' (PR #9131). Premise HELD for the chapter half: §2 argued a screen is the right unit and said nothing about a view rendered by both a ported and an unported screen, while its only nearby advice ('remove the Reagent original ... keeping both copies invites future divergence') forbade duplication without offering the alternative.

The section says the boundary lands on the VIEW - port it once with the first screen that needs it and bridge it back out with h/as-component, so there is one implementation - and shows both sides, the Hicasso view with its minted component and the Reagent caller rendering ^{:key id} [:> article-preview-component {:id id}].

ONE HALF OF THE PREMISE DID NOT HOLD, and the chapter now states the opposite. The bead reports that a CLJS map at :article and a vector at :on-select 'both survived the round trip intact through the Reagent adapter's [:>]'. Reagent 2.0.1's own source contradicts both: impl.template/convert-prop-value sends a keyword to its name, a CLJS map to a camel-cased JS object with values recursively converted, and any other coll? through clj->js (deep); only js-val? things - strings, numbers, booleans, nil, functions - cross unchanged. Prop NAMES do round-trip (dash-to-prop-name camel-cases, codec/prop-key decodes back), which is probably what the pilot was seeing. So the chapter now states the conversion and gives the shape that avoids it: cross an id, read the rest with h/sub - which is what re-frame2 wants anyway - and prefer h/as-element where the Reagent caller is an ordinary body, since those props never cross React at all.

09-INTEROP HALF NOT DONE: docs/core/hicasso/09-interop.md was outside this dispatch's fence. Filed as rf2-d4n8 with the verified mechanism sentence ready to lift.

Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs build --strict 0, check_guide_samples.py 0, each sabotage-controlled, all re-run green after rebase.

title: hic docs: chapter 15's L3 rung mounts real React and never says where the DOM comes from - 'jsdom', ':browser-test' and ':karma' appear in none of the 29 pages
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F09 · outcome 1 · `unresolved` · `docs`

**Trying to** Get a DOM so I could run the chapter-15 L3 level — "Mounted
facade with Testing Library and user-event" — for claims the browser-free levels
cannot make.

**Expected** Chapter 15 to say how. It is precise about everything else: which
namespace each level uses, that the test kit needs its own `:local/root`
coordinate under `:test`, that the alias must also be named in
`shadow-cljs.edn`, and that Testing Library is an npm install.

**Instead** It stops one step short. "L0–L2 are browser-free and need no DOM,
while L3 mounts real React and L4 wants real engines" — and then never says
where the DOM for L3 comes from. My build's `:test` target is `:node-test`,
where `document` does not exist, so `hm/mount!` has nothing to mount into. The
word `jsdom` does not occur anywhere in the 29 pages; neither does
`:browser-test`, `:karma`, or any other shadow-cljs target name. The only npm
line the chapter gives is `@testing-library/dom`, which needs a DOM and does not
provide one.

**Looked at** `15-testing.md` in full, twice — §"Put the test kit on the
classpath" and the L3 section; grepped all 29 pages for `jsdom`,
`browser-test`, `karma`, `node-test`, `happy-dom`.

**Resolved by** Guessing `npm install --save-dev jsdom` and injecting the
globals with `node -r`. It works, but it is my invention: the chapter's L3
example is written as if `(:container m)` simply exists, and a reader on a Node
test lane cannot get there from the page. This is the second-clearest hole after
P2-F04, and unlike P2-F04 it is on the path of anyone who follows the ladder the
chapter itself recommends.

**Bead** One sentence in §"Put the test kit on the classpath", beside the
Testing Library line: name the DOM. Either "L3 needs a DOM: on a `:node-test`
lane install `jsdom` and install its globals before the suite loads; on a
`:browser-test` lane the browser is the DOM", or say which of the two the
project itself uses. The chapter already accepts responsibility for classpath
and npm setup, so this is inside its declared scope rather than beyond it.
notes:
CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE SECOND BLINDED PILOT. This bead was filed from pilot 2
(LinearLite); pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit) hit the L3 DOM gap in the same
session, in a different application, from the same 29 pages, without either agent
seeing the other's workspace, log or output. Two independent readings landing on one
gap is the strongest signal this instrument produces, and it moves the finding out of
the range where one reader's idiosyncrasy explains it.

Pilot 1's entry, verbatim:

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F12 · outcome 1 · `asked` · `tooling`

**Trying to**

Reach L3 — "Mounted facade with Testing Library and user-event" — to prove the
React-level claims that L2 explicitly cannot: that the `h/as-component` bridge
resolves the frame from the Reagent parent, that the controlled fields keep
their caret, that `hm/assert-clean!` sees no residue after unmount.

**Expected**

Chapter 15 to name the DOM environment. Its L3 setup paragraph is precise about
everything else — the classpath alias, the `test_kit/src` root, the
`:local/root` coordinate, and one npm line: "Testing Library is the one further
thing L3 reaches for, and it is an npm package rather than a classpath entry:
`npm install --save-dev @testing-library/dom`."

**Instead**

That is not enough, and the omission is silent. `@testing-library/dom` is a
*query* library; it does not supply a DOM. This application's test build is
shadow-cljs `:node-test`, where there is none:

```
exists? js/document => false
exists? js/window   => false
```

So every `hm/*` name resolves, compiles, and cannot run. The chapter's own L3
example is written with `cljs.test` and `async`, which reads as a Node test —
and gives no hint that Node needs anything further. Nothing in the corpus
mentions jsdom, happy-dom, `:browser-test`, or karma.

**The question I would have asked a human**: *what DOM is L3 meant to run
under — a `:browser-test`/karma build, or `:node-test` with a DOM shim the
guide has not named?* Recording it as `asked` per the brief, since there is no
one to ask.

**Looked at**

- `15-testing.md` "Put the test kit on the classpath", "L3: mounted React and
  DOM", and its troubleshooting table
- `00-installation.md` npm dependencies (React and shadow-cljs only)
- `api-reference.md` `re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted` roster
- grep across all 29 pages for `jsdom`, `happy-dom`, `karma`, `browser-test` —
  zero hits for each

**Resolved by**

Not resolved through the documentation. What I did instead: kept the migrated
screens' view coverage at L2 (`ht/tree`, 17 tests, 170 assertions, green), and
proved the React-level and DOM-level claims *outside* the test kit — by booting
the release bundle in a jsdom I installed myself and driving it with real DOM
events (`realworld/boot-check.cjs`, `realworld/drive-check.cjs`). That is
evidence, and good evidence, but it is not the documented route and it does not
give me `hm/assert-clean!`'s residue check, which I would have wanted.

**Bead**

Chapter 15 must name L3's DOM environment and show the build config for it.
This blocks the whole mounted tier for any consumer starting from
`:node-test` — and `:node-test` is what the guide's own examples look like.
close_reason: PR #9136. Premise HELD, corroborated by both blinded pilots. Chapter 15 named the classpath alias, the :local/root coordinate, the shadow-cljs.edn alias line and the npm install and then stopped: hm/mount! renders through react-dom/client and needs a document, which :node-test does not have and @testing-library/dom does not supply (it queries a DOM, it does not create one). New section 'Where L3's DOM comes from', placed immediately after the Testing Library line where both pilots looked. It names the two build shapes, RECOMMENDS the :browser-test target -- verified as what this repo itself uses: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn's :browser-test build carries ns-regexp '.*-dom-cljs-test$' and is driven by 'npm run test:browser' (shadow-cljs compile browser-test && node scripts/serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs, i.e. a real engine via Playwright), NOT jsdom. Also shows the two-lane shadow-cljs.edn split by namespace suffix and covers the regex overlap (:node-test's cljs-test$ also matches -dom-cljs-test) with the stated-skip idiom the repo's own mounted suites use ((defn- browser? [] (exists? js/document)) in forms_dom_cljs_test.cljs). Gates: check_guide_samples.py 0, check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs build --strict 0; first two proven to read the branch by planted faults.

title: Stop template CI fan-out from retired schemas, Story, and Xray inputs
description:
## Evidence

The changed-surface classifier still sets template_expensive for implementation/schemas/** and every non-spec Markdown change under tools/story/** or tools/xray/**. Its comments and the matching assertions in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs say the generated app loads re-frame.schemas, the Xray preload, and the with-Story entry point.

That premise ended in commit 18b9486664 (rf2-zq34m): the current twelve-file contract forbids day8/re-frame2-schemas, day8/re-frame2-xray, day8/re-frame2-story, reg-app-schema, the Xray preload/host, and every Story flag. Current emitted files require only core, the selected adapter, plain-atom test support, and substrate libraries. The setup-skill leaf is byte-locked to the same reduced emission. Core, adapter, implementation package pins, template files, and setup reference files remain real inputs and already have their own template_expensive arms.

## Impact

Schema, Story, and Xray-only PRs unnecessarily schedule the roughly 30-minute jvm-tools-template job, including npm ci and Playwright Chromium provisioning. Worse, classifier comments and tests now assert coverage the template suite cannot provide, which can mislead future maintainers about which consumer gates actually exercise those surfaces.

## Recommendation

Remove only the obsolete schemas/Story/Xray template_expensive fan-out and invert or replace the three stale classifier assertions with negative controls. Retain all actual template inputs: implementation/core, both adapters, implementation/package.json and package-lock.json, tools/template itself, and skills/re-frame2-setup/references.

## Risks and contracts

Do not narrow tools_jvm, MCP, examples, Story/Xray browser, schemas JVM/CLJS, or any other independent lane for those surfaces. This change is solely the generated-template consumer edge that no longer exists. Re-add fan-out only with a real emitted dependency and a fixture proving it.
acceptance_criteria:
- report-changed-surfaces.sh no longer sets template_expensive for a schemas-only change or a Story/Xray-only change.
- The stale rf2-jdj17.1 classifier comments and positive assertions are replaced by current-contract negative controls.
- Core, reagent/uix adapter, implementation package pin/lockfile, tools/template, and setup-skill reference changes still set template_expensive.
- The changed-surfaces classifier test suite passes and other per-surface lane outputs are unchanged.
close_reason: template_expensive no longer fires for a schemas-only or a Story/Xray-only change. Both rf2-jdj17.1 arms removed from report-changed-surfaces.sh (the implementation/schemas/* case, and the tools/{story,xray}/* default arm), plus two adjacent prose rosters that still listed template_expensive for Story macros.clj and for schemas. The three stale positive assertions in _changed-surfaces.test.cjs are replaced by negative controls that ALSO pin each surface's own lanes (tools_jvm + mcp_conformance + story_xray_browser for the tools; implementation_jvm + cljs_node_test + cljs_browser + cljs_prod + bundle_isolation for schemas), so an over-broad narrowing edit reds instead of passing. Premise verified with two instruments and a control that fired: (1) git grep -F census over tools/template/resources/ and the setup-skill leaf found 0 hits for re-frame.schemas, reg-app-schema, re-frame.story, mount-shell!, devtools/preloads and re-frame2-xray, with controls returning hits; the emitted shadow-cljs.edn declares no :devtools/preloads key at all, and the only xray/story strings in the emitted tree are two Next-steps doc links in root/README.md pointing under docs/, not tools/. (2) the classifier itself executed per surface before and after: across all 28 outputs for the three surfaces exactly three lines move, all template_expensive true->false, and every retained input still reads true (core, both adapters, implementation/package.json, package-lock.json, tools/template, skills/re-frame2-setup/references). Gate liveness proved once: planted the removed schemas arm back, the mirror test went red naming the new negative control, restored byte-identical by git hash-object. Gates: node --test _changed-surfaces.test.cjs exit 0 (335 passed); eslint exit 0. NOTE: this touches the one-toucher classifier/mirror pair in ONE commit, as required when a change alters both what the script outputs and what the test pins. PR #9091.

title: (BUG) reagent-slim callable-prop regressions never reach the Fn/IFn branches
description:
## Correctness finding

The two callable-prop regression tests added for rf2-wyocr do not execute the production branches their names and comments claim to protect.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:485-486,596-618` puts `(js-val? v)` before `(fn? v)` and `(ifn? v)`. `js-val?` is true for every ordinary JavaScript function (`goog/typeOf` is `function`), so the plain `(fn ...)` values used by `convert-prop-value-fn-preserves-identity-rf2-wyocr` at test lines 197-216 return from the first branch. Deleting both explicit `fn?` arms would leave that regression green.
- ClojureScript 1.12.42's `cljs.core/with-meta` wraps a JavaScript function in object-backed `MetaFn`; `fn?` is true because `MetaFn` satisfies `Fn`, while `goog/typeOf` is `object`. That is the ordinary value shape that actually reaches the explicit `fn?` branch, but the test never supplies one.
- `convert-prop-value-non-fn-ifn-still-wrapped` at test lines 218-234 explicitly admits its keyword reaches `named?` and its map reaches `map?`. It never supplies a value reaching `(ifn? v)`, never invokes a wrapper, and would remain green if the `ifn?` arms were deleted.
- Commit `874eb9ef49` introduced both branches/tests and states the identity regression is pinned. Its claim that every fn had previously been wrapped overlooks the pre-existing `js-val?` first arm; the implementation change materially protects object-backed Fn values, not the plain JS function used in the regression.

## Impact

Future cleanup or condition reordering can silently remove MetaFn identity preservation or non-fn IFn wrapping while the named regressions stay green. Metadata-bearing callbacks would then receive fresh wrappers and defeat React memoisation; custom object-backed callable props could cease to be invokable from JavaScript.

## Proposed disposition

Make the tests branch-real: add metadata to a function for both public arities and assert exact identity; define a focused object-backed value that satisfies `IFn` but not `Fn`, `named?`, `map?`, or `coll?`, then prove conversion returns an invokable JS function with correct argument/return behavior. Correct the production docstring's examples (`keywords`, maps, sets, and vectors are intercepted by earlier branches and are not evidence for the `ifn?` wrapper).

## Risks

Do not reorder the production ladder merely to make the old examples true: map/coll/named conversion is part of the published prop-conversion behavior. The fixture must model a genuinely reachable callable object and avoid compiler-specific accidental classification.

## Duplicate search

Searched all 575 bead records in every state for `convert-prop-value`, `MetaFn`, `wyocr`, `callable`, `fn identity`, and the test path. The only matches (`rf2-y1jkm`, `rf2-6sqv`, `rf2-oz7wr`) concern Hicasso performance, console rendering, and UIx registry heads; none owns these reagent-slim branches.
acceptance_criteria:
- The 1-arg and 2-arg identity regressions use an object-backed metadata-bearing Fn and prove `identical?` with the input and across repeated conversions.
- A focused non-fn IFn fixture actually reaches the wrapper arm, returns a JavaScript-invokable function, forwards representative arities, and preserves the fixture's return values.
- Non-vacuity is demonstrated: removing/bypassing the `fn?` arm fails the MetaFn identity test, and removing/bypassing the `ifn?` arm fails the callable-object test.
- Plain JS functions still pass through unchanged; named values, maps, and collections retain their current earlier-branch semantics.
- The `convert-prop-value` docstring and test names no longer claim that keywords/maps/sets/vectors exercise a wrapper they cannot reach.
- Focused template tests pass in the normal CLJS test target and production build mode remains unaffected.
close_reason: Confirmed at tip. This is a TEST defect, NOT a production ordering defect -- the bead's own Risks section rules the ladder must not be reordered, and that is correct: map/coll/named conversion is published prop-conversion behaviour. js-val? is (not (identical? 'object' (goog/typeOf x))), so it is true for every plain JS function; the plain fns in convert-prop-value-fn-preserves-identity-rf2-wyocr and the keyword and map in convert-prop-value-non-fn-ifn-still-wrapped all returned from earlier arms, and both tests would have stayed green with the fn? and ifn? arms deleted. Repaired by moving each test to the value shape that actually reaches its arm: a MetaFn ((with-meta f m), object-backed and satisfying Fn) for the identity regressions in both public arities, and a deftype satisfying IFn but not Fn/named?/map?/coll? for the wrapper, proven to come back as a real JS function invoked via .call with arguments forwarded to the fixture's own -invoke. Each test now asserts its routing preconditions rather than assuming them. Non-vacuity proved both ways: removing the fn? arm reds ONLY the MetaFn test (4 failures, identity replaced by the wrapper); removing the ifn? arm reds ONLY the callable test (3 failures, 'function' vs 'object'); both restores verified by blob hash. Docstring corrected -- it cited keywords, maps, sets and vectors as ifn?-arm examples and all four are intercepted earlier; it now walks the cond in the order taken. No executable production change. PR #9077.

title: routing/resources: a :url-bound? make-frame plans route resources AT CONSTRUCTION and a failed plan is never retried (NOT a live-frame reprojection bug — mechanism in the original title is refuted; needs ruling)
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 by rf2-xkhul (PR #8990) while running the pilot baselines from a clean external workspace built per docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md on the published :local/root route (Node 24, shadow-cljs 3.4.10, dev compile of a :node-test build, goog.DEBUG default).

SYMPTOM. implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs copied VERBATIM into app/test/ of the LinearLite workspace (deps: core, adapters/reagent, http, routing, resources, hicasso) fails 16 of 51 assertions across 7 of 10 tests, while the identical file is green on the in-repo consolidated :node-test bundle. Its init! (the fixture :init-fn) does (rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true}) FIRST and then registrar/register! the snapshotted :resource/:mutation rows, reg-fx :rf.http/managed (capture stub) and :rf.nav/push-url. In the workspace bundle the frame never sees anything registered after make-frame: :rf.route/navigate to :linearlite.app/board lands :transition :error with :rf.error/resource-route-plan / cause :rf.error/resource-not-registered ('no resource is registered under :linearlite/board') even though (registrar/lookup :resource :linearlite/board) is truthy at that moment; moving ONLY the resource re-registration before make-frame clears that error but the capture stub registered after make-frame is still not what the read lowers through (entry stays :loading, last-managed-args nil). Moving EVERY registration before make-frame (frame made last) -> 51/51 green. Probes confirmed the ns-load state is identical to in-repo (registrar and source store both hold the resource + 3 mutations; :routing/on-route-entry and :resources/reg-resource hooks live).

WHY IT MATTERS. re-frame.live-frame documents the sealed-generation freshener as a CORRECTNESS invariant with NO debug gate (rf2-9c2jf): make-frame installs a registration hook so a later reg-* marks the projection dirty and a read-time coalesced flush reprojects (EP-0026 / rf2-h1vqa4). In the consumer bundle that reprojection does not take effect for the make-frame -> reg-* -> dispatch sequence, which live_frame.cljc names as 'exactly the broken one'. Either the in-repo bundle carries something (a sibling suite, the test-quiet runner, an artefact only it loads) that arms the flush and a consumer never gets, or the flush is not reached on this path. Unknown which; not chased under rf2-xkhul (fence was pilots/** only).

REPRO (about 3 minutes). Build the LinearLite workspace per workspace.md at tip of PR #8990 (or main once merged); replace app/test/linearlite/baseline_test.cljs with the adapter suite verbatim (ns re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test also matches the -test$ regexp); npm test -> exit 1, 16 failures. Then in its init! move (rf/make-frame ...) to the end -> exit 0. The committed baseline under docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/linearlite/ already makes the frame last and is green; this bead is about the framework behaviour the verbatim suite exposes, and about whether any in-repo fixture is green only because the consolidated bundle masks it.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP. Reproduce with a minimal consumer test: make-frame, reg-event, dispatch-sync -> expect :rf.error/no-such-handler in the consumer bundle if the theory holds; then diff what re-frame.live-frame/ensure-reprojection-installed! and the :live-frame/flush-projection! consult do in each bundle.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-09-02 19:57:00 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2-xkhul worker with a 3-minute repro. This is a FRAMEWORK bug (core/live-frame), not a hicasso or pilots one, and it is the highest-priority thing filed this session by a worker — a registration made after make-frame being invisible to that frame in a :local/root consumer bundle would bite any consumer following the published route, and it was found the only way it could be: by building a workspace outside the repo. Not fenced by any live surface. Next solo dispatch when a slot frees.
DISPATCHED 2026-09-02 20:07:19 AUSEST by the mayor. SOLO, DIAGNOSIS-FIRST, fresh worktree worker/liveframe-ma8r off origin/main 07c76826c2. Premises verified at that tip: live_frame.cljc:1790 carries the 'exactly the broken one' sentence verbatim; ensure-reprojection-installed! is referenced ~:377 and ~:512; the linearlite adapter suite has 11 deftests; the committed pilot baseline that makes the frame LAST is on main. LEAD HYPOTHESIS handed over AS A HYPOTHESIS: live_frame.cljc ~:386 reaches the flush through (late-bind/get-fn-cached :live-frame/flush-projection!) inside a when-let, so a bundle where nothing registers that publisher falls through SILENTLY — no error, no warning, exactly the observed symptom shape. The competing reading this bead names (flush reached but ineffective on this path) must be EXCLUDED rather than argued away. Worker is told the diagnosis is the deliverable, that no code change may be warranted, and to leave this bead OPEN for a ruling if the honest answer needs one.

DIAGNOSIS 2026-09-02 20:31 AUSEST (rf2-ma8r worker, PR #9000). The bead's
numbers reproduce EXACTLY (16 failures across 7 of 10 tests, 51 assertions,
exit 1, in a LinearLite workspace built per pilots/workspace.md on the
published :local/root route) — but the MECHANISM in the description is
refuted, and so is the flush-publisher hypothesis. No live-frame defect is
involved. Nothing is invisible to the frame.

WHAT IS REFUTED (each measured, not argued).

1. "Registrations made AFTER make-frame are invisible to the frame in a
   :local/root consumer node-test bundle." REFUTED. A minimal probe —
   make-frame, then reg-event, then dispatch-sync — PASSES in the very
   consumer bundle where the suite fails 16/51 (exit 0). In that same
   bundle the frame's own reprojection is demonstrably live: an explicit
   flush-pending-reprojection! taken mid-suite returns
   :added #{[:resource :linearlite/board] [:mutation :linearlite/create-issue]
   [:mutation :linearlite/edit-title] [:mutation :linearlite/change-status]}
   and :changed #{[:fx :rf.http/managed] [:fx :rf.nav/push-url]} — i.e. the
   post-make-frame registrations ARE picked up and swapped onto the frame.

2. "A late-bound :live-frame/flush-projection! that nothing registers in a
   consumer bundle makes the when-let fall through silently." REFUTED twice.
   At source: make-frame calls ensure-reprojection-installed! UNCONDITIONALLY
   (live_frame.cljc:928), and late-bind/get-fn-cached does NOT cache nil
   resolutions, so there is no negative-cache variant either. Empirically:
   in the consumer bundle the probe prints flush-publisher-resolvable? true
   and mark-dirty-publisher-resolvable? true.

3. "Or the flush is not reached on this path." REFUTED. The failing lookup
   happens strictly BEFORE the registrations exist at all, not against a
   stale generation — see below.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE — a construction-time route plan, in routing/resources.

A println planted in registry/require-resource-spec!'s miss branch shows the
failing lookup happening with the registrar genuinely EMPTY
(atom-has? false, lookup-direct? false, ids-in-scope []), and — the decisive
ordering datum — it fires BEFORE the end of init!:

    PRE-MAKE-FRAME  resource-ids []
    MA8R-PLANT miss :linearlite/board where rf.resource/route-entry
                    gen-bound? true atom-has? false ids-in-scope []
    POST-MAKE-FRAME routing-slice {... :transition :error
                    :error {:rf.error/id :rf.error/resource-route-plan ...}}
    INIT-END        resource-ids [:linearlite/board] atom-has? true

So the route entry runs INSIDE (rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true}).
A :url-bound? frame performs a synchronous initial URL sync at construction:
frame/upsert-frame!'s post-create hook fires routing's
:routing/on-frame-registered!, which reconciles the URL listener and "syncs
the current URL into the owner's slice" (routing/history.cljc). Under Node,
history/current-url is "/". The LinearLite example registers
:linearlite.app/board at path "/" (examples/.../linearlite/core.cljs:458-464)
and that route declares :resources [{:resource :linearlite/board :blocking? true}].
The construction-time sync therefore PLANS the board resource while the
suite's init! has not yet reinstated the :resource/:mutation rows the
fixture's reset hook cleared — init! re-registers them on the NEXT line —
and the plan fails :rf.error/resource-not-registered, recording
:transition :error on the slice.

The error is then STICKY. The test's own
(dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :linearlite.app/board}]) does not
re-plan: the planted probe fires EXACTLY ONCE per test, at construction, and
never again — including in a probe test where the resource was verified
present and visible inside the frame immediately beforehand. Every one of the
16 assertions then reads nil off the never-populated entry.

DECISIVE CONTROL. Changing ONLY the example's route path from "/" to "/board"
in the workspace copy takes the identical suite from 16 failures / exit 1 to
0 failures / exit 0, with the planted probe firing ZERO times. Nothing else
was touched.

WHY THE IN-REPO BUNDLE IS GREEN — and YES, THIS IS A FALSE GREEN.
This answers the bead's second question. re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test
is green in the consolidated bundle ONLY because a co-loaded sibling owns "/".
At least seven in-tree apps register a route at "/" (infinite_feed, linearlite,
resources, routing, todomvc, realworld_http, realworld_resources), plus many
test suites. In the consolidated bundle "/" resolves to some other app's route,
so linearlite's board resource is never planned at construction and the suite's
explicit navigate is a genuine transition performed with everything registered.
In a consumer bundle only linearlite's routes exist, so "/" matches its board.
The in-repo suite's colour therefore depends on which siblings happen to be
co-loaded — it is not evidence about its own subject.

WHAT THE HONEST REPAIR IS — A RULING, NOT A PATCH, so this bead stays OPEN.
Two candidate framework defects, and they are different calls:

  (A) A :url-bound? frame plans route resources at construction. Arguably
      CORRECT and the whole point of :url-bound? — an app must register its
      resources before constructing a URL-bound frame, which is exactly what
      the committed pilot baseline does and what the "frame last" workaround
      does. If this is ruled correct, the defect is documentation plus the
      false green above, not code.

  (B) A FAILED route plan is never retried. A same-route navigate does not
      re-plan, so an app that RECOVERS (registers the resource afterwards)
      stays wedged in :transition :error permanently with no retry short of
      navigating away and back. This is fail-open on recovery and is the more
      interesting of the two.

Both live in routing/resources, NOT in core/live_frame.cljc. No core change is
warranted and none was made. Nothing under spec/ was touched.

NOT CHASED (named rather than argued away): whether (B) is deliberate
same-route-navigation semantics or an oversight; and whether any OTHER in-repo
suite is likewise green only by co-load masking — the "/" census above is the
place to start, and the cheap test is to build each app's suite in a
single-app bundle.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern websocket — canonical declaration does not register (4 dangling action ids → :rf.error/machine-unresolved-action) and calls an undefined current-socket? helper
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md` §Canonical declaration (L68-176) is presented as copyable code ("the canonical declaration below is the leaf-level summary" L7; "Read the source first; the declaration above is the leaf-level summary" L231). Its `:actions` map (L95-118) declares eight ids: `:record-connection-opts :rotate-cred :on-socket-lost :fail-in-flight :on-fatal-error :on-connected :flush-queue :enqueue-message`. Its states reference four more that are never declared: `:send-auth` (L147 `:authenticating {:entry :send-auth …}`), `:route-message` and `:refuse-frame` (L158-159), `:send-now` (L160). Its `:trusted-frame?` guard (L91-93) calls a bare fn `(current-socket? data source-socket-id)` that the leaf never defines — `:current-socket?` exists only as a guard KEY in the same `:guards` map (L81-87), and a guard keyword is not callable from another guard's body.

## TRUTH AT TIP

Machine registration resolves action refs eagerly: `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1651,1812` — "`:rf.error/machine-unresolved-action` on dangling refs". So `(rf/reg-machine :ws/connection …)` as written throws at registration on `:send-auth` (the first dangling ref hit), before any state is entered. And `current-socket?` is an undeclared symbol — a CLJS compile warning / undefined var at load. The example the leaf calls ground truth already has both fixes: `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:110-118` defines the shared helper `from-live-socket?` and all three guards (`:current-socket?` L215, `:own-request-timeout?` L242, `:trusted-frame?` L266) call it; the four actions are defined at L355-364 (`:send-auth`), L404-409 (`:send-now`), and the receive/refuse pair (`:receive-message` L515+, `:refuse-frame` — note the example names it `:receive-message`, not `:route-message`).

While there, one drift worth lifting in the same edit: the example guards the lifecycle transitions too — `connection.cljs:42-46` "This covers the whole socket-sourced surface — the lifecycle transitions (`:ws/opened`, `:ws/auth-ok`, `:ws/auth-failed`, `:ws/closed`) as much as `:ws/received`" — whereas the leaf's `:connecting {:on {:ws/opened {:target :authenticating}}}` (L146), `:authenticating` (L148-149) and the parent `:ws/closed` (L139) carry no `:current-socket?` guard, so a straggler `:ws/closed` from a torn-down socket would bounce the NEW connection into `:reconnecting`. The leaf's feature table (L26) claims the guard "rejects events from a torn-down prior socket" generally.

Everything else in the leaf checks out against the 2026-09-01/02 spec + example commits (`2ef4147f8f`, `510e758f7e`, `f552191c3d`, `3113303ff4`, `7fb6031db7`, `cc2d3e5d71`): request-reply is taught as app-level (`:origin :ws/server` / `:ws/local`, no envelope, L200), the registration-token rule is in the anti-patterns (L225-226), three doors out of `:active` settle `:in-flight` (L52-66, L139-141), and `:cred-ref` timing matches. The token / `:next-token` mechanics live in prose only, which the "example is ground truth" framing covers.

## IMPACT

The one code block an agent copies for a WebSocket machine fails at registration with `:rf.error/machine-unresolved-action` and a compile-time undefined symbol. The agent then either invents four action bodies and a helper (plausibly wrong — `:route-message` must clear the `:in-flight` slot by REGISTRATION token, which only the example shows) or abandons the leaf for the example, which is what the leaf should have handed it in the first place.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, `patterns/websocket.md` only)

- Add a `(defn current-socket? [data source-socket-id] …)` helper above the machine (mirroring the example's `from-live-socket?`) and have both guards call it; or rename to `from-live-socket?` to match the example verbatim.
- Add the four missing actions in compact form — `:send-auth` and `:send-now` are two lines each (lift from `connection.cljs:355-364, 404-409`); `:route-message` and `:refuse-frame` can be one-line stubs whose comment says "lifted in full from `connection.cljs` `:receive-message` / `:refuse-frame`" — or rename `:route-message` → `:receive-message` so the reader greps the right symbol.
- Guard `:ws/opened`, `:ws/auth-ok`, `:ws/auth-failed` and the parent `:ws/closed` with `{:guard :current-socket? …}` as the example does.
- Keep the leaf's length in mind (it is already 29 KB — see the patterns leaf-size bead); prefer lifting over adding prose.

## GATE

No gate compiles skill code fences — `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` still run (both exit 0 today; both blind to this). Verify by hand: every `:action` / `:entry` id referenced in the declaration appears in `:actions`, every bare symbol the guards call is defined in the leaf, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

The canonical `:ws/connection` declaration references no action id absent from its own `:actions` map and no undefined symbol; lifecycle transitions carry `:current-socket?`; the leaf's `:in-flight` / token prose is unchanged.

title: skill(re-frame2-xray): tab mnemonics taught as key-wired (m opens the active mode tab) — they are tooltip letters only; no bare-letter tab handler exists, tab-jump is the palette verb
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md:94-95` (§The inventory): "Static mode holds **5**: **Machines · Routes · Schemas · Flows · Interceptors** (mnemonics are mode-scoped — `m` opens the active mode's tab)."

`skills/re-frame2-xray/references/panels.md:60-62` (§Static mode): "Mnemonics are mode-scoped (`m` here opens the Static Machines browse, not the Dynamic instance-inspector)."

Both sentences affirm that pressing a bare letter opens a tab.

## TRUTH AT TIP

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panel_registry.cljc:44-50` (the `reg-l4-tab!` entry contract):

    :mnem   string — single-letter LABEL mnemonic, rendered into the
                     tab button's `title` ("Trace (t)") by both
                     shells and read by nothing else. Not a key: no
                     bare-letter tab handler exists in
                     `keybinding.cljs`, and tab-jump is a
                     command-palette verb (spec/007 §Trimmed pending
                     demand).

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/shell.cljs:69`: "`:mnem` into each tab button's `title` and are read by nothing else". Dynamic shell: `shell.cljs:2186` ("mnemonic letter is exposed via the `title` attribute") and `:2221` `:title (str label " (" mnem ")")`.

`keybinding.cljs` `spine-key-id` (:265-310) maps exactly Space / l / G / j / k / , / s; there is no `m`, `e`, `a`, … arm, and `handle-keydown` (:330-418) has no tab branch. The shipped keyboard-first tab jump is the palette: `palette/sources.cljc:78-91` `panel-items` → "Open <label> panel", `:368-378` `static-tab-items` → "Open <label> (Static)".

## IMPACT

A wrong hotkey taught. It contradicts the skill's own §Wired hotkeys ("Only these are wired") and §Style guidance ("Don't invent controls … cite `keybinding.cljs`"). A user told "press `m`" gets nothing, and the mode-scoping explanation is built on the false premise. The `e a v t m r s g u h` roster itself is correct (the drift gate pins the `:mnem` values) — only the "opens" verb is wrong.

## FIX SHAPE

Prose only, two files. Reword both sentences: mnemonics are the parenthesised letter in each tab button's tooltip (`Trace (t)`), a label hint, not a key; keyboard tab-jump is `Cmd/Ctrl+K` → "Open <tab> panel" / "Open <tab> (Static)". Keep the roster and the Mnem columns in panels.md / shared-components.md (relabel the column header to "Tooltip letter" if wanted). No tools/xray change.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_xray_tab_inventory_drift.py --verbose` must stay green (it pins `:mnem` values, not the verb). The wording itself: no gate — verify by hand (`git grep -n "opens the" -- skills/re-frame2-xray/`).

## ACCEPTANCE

No sentence under `skills/re-frame2-xray/` says a bare letter opens or selects a tab; the palette is named as the keyboard tab-jump; drift gate green.

WHY IT IS NOT BLOCKED. The edge assumed the first tag would supply a coordinate for the reporter. It is also immune to rf2-fo4ng's `day8/*` -> `io.github.day8/*` rename, since no Maven group appears in it. Do NOT write "flips to :mvn/version after the tag" on the page.

THE DEFECT — FOUR FENCES, NOT ONE. `docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md:28` prints `cd re-frame2/migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod` on a PUBLISHED page (nav entry at `mkdocs.yml:287`); step 4 at `:449-454` has no `cd` of its own and inherits it. THE CONSTRAINT. `migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/deps.edn:77`'s escaping `:paths` entry `../../../implementation/hicasso/src` MUST SURVIVE. `shared_rule_test.clj:55` pins the tool's slot resolver to the runtime's by `identical?`, and `:57-71` further pins its RESOURCE PROVENANCE to a path under `implementation/hicasso/src/`. Do not transcribe `prop-name` into `src/`; do not swap the path for a published Hicasso dependency (it fails the provenance assertion, imports Hicasso's dependency graph into a bare-JVM tool, and would still need the git route anyway); do not touch `shared_rule_test.clj`. The deprecation warning the escaping path prints is expected — `deps.edn:67-76` explains why a `:local/root` is not the fix.

THE WORK. Step 1: run the probe in the DECISION note from an empty scratch directory outside the repo. It confirms a cold-cache gitlib fetch; it does NOT gate the dispatch, because a failure only selects the larger fallback diff (an alias swapping the relative `:paths` entry for a git coordinate on `implementation/hicasso`, with the default `:paths` unchanged so the in-repo pin holds). ACCEPTANCE. The command printed on the public page runs the reporter against a sample source directory from an EMPTY directory with no re-frame2 checkout beside it, with BOTH caches isolated — `GITLIBS` as well as `:mvn/local-repo`, since git deps cache under `~/.gitlibs` and the latter alone does not isolate them (this corrects the original acceptance wording). EXIT 0 IS NOT EVIDENCE: `codemod.clj`'s `-main` exits 0 for any run completing without a `:parse-error` and always writes a report. Assert the expected FINDINGS in the report, assert the fixture's bytes are unchanged by scan and by `--rewrite` dry run, and assert the slot resource resolved from the fetched git tree. The codemod's `clojure -M:test` stays green, unmodified.

OUT OF SCOPE. A second Maven coordinate, a "released tool", a wrapper API, a `-T` spelling (tool fns take an EDN map; keep `-M -m re-frame.migration.hicasso.codemod`), or un-excluding the codemod tree from the site (`mkdocs.yml:35` excludes it deliberately; the answer is one canonical public explanation in chapter 20).
