MERGED-PR AUDIT #9138 (2026-09-04): this PR edited docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/README.md gap table to add G4 but left G2 saying No bead filed and expected to move with G1. This exact owner has existed since 2026-09-02 and establishes why that claim is false: publishing the Hicasso jar does not publish the migration reporter. Keep rf2-lb566 open; when its public reporter command lands, update the G2 row as its acceptance criteria already require.

--- MAYOR 2026-09-09 AUSEST — BACKLOG REREAD: PREMISE RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, HOLD IS CORRECT AND UNCHANGED ---
The §3 category this bead was checked against is "a fence that has cleared". It has NOT cleared. Recording
the check rather than the conclusion, so the next reread does not re-derive it from the description.

Measured at trunk `44be7d8ab2`, three probes, each with a live control:

1. **The migration guide still sends readers into a source checkout.** `docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md:22-32` still instructs `cd re-frame2/migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod` — i.e. it assumes the reader has cloned this repository, which is exactly the thing this bead exists to stop assuming. Read at source, not from the bead's own quotation of it.

2. **The codemod is not packaged by the release workflow.** `codemod` reads **0** in `.github/workflows/release.yml`, against a live control of **97** for `deploy` in the same file — so the zero is the file answering, not the instrument failing. (CLAUDE.md instrument item (f): a zero is the answer a census WANTS here, so it needs the control.)

3. **No release has ever been cut.** `git tag -l 'v*'` reads **0** locally and `git ls-remote --tags origin` reads **0**, against a control of **0** tags of ANY kind — this repository has never been tagged at all. That control is degenerate on its own, so the instrument was proved separately: `git ls-remote --heads origin` reads **2**, so the remote query does reach the remote. The zero is real.

**CONCLUSION: the hold on rf2-kmqx3 is correct and stays.** This bead cannot be dispatched to rewrite the guide's install instructions until there is something to install — and probe 3 says the first tag is still the deliverable, not the precondition. It sits in the same cohort as rf2-8urba, rf2-8o66x (both deferred to 2026-09-16), rf2-fgb1, rf2-pv7p and rf2-hic-063: six beads, one fence, and the fence is the release, whose own gate is **rf2-uelji** (Clojars — awaiting Mike, gating 8 beads by the same computation).

**NOT A REVERTED CLOSURE.** This bead carries a `MERGED-PR AUDIT` note, which is the shape a reopened bead wears, so it was checked: `bd history rf2-lb566 --json` shows **0 snapshots in which it was ever closed**. The audit note is an append to an always-open bead. Same finding for rf2-uelji. Neither is a silent revert.

=== DECISION 2026-09-09 (decision close-out, rf2-lb566) ===

DECIDED: DISPATCH NOW. The pinned-git-source invocation is the reporter's
PERMANENT delivery path, not a pre-publish stopgap. The blocking edge
rf2-kmqx3 -> rf2-lb566 was WRONG and has been REMOVED. No probe gates the
dispatch; the probe below is step 1 of the WORK.

WHY THE BLOCK WAS WRONG, AND IT IS A HARDER FACT THAN "the git route is
available today". Hicasso's jar does not contain the reporter:
`implementation/hicasso/deps.edn:176` is `:src-dirs ["src" "resources"
"test_kit/src"]`, and `re-frame.migration.hicasso.codemod` is in none of them.
Corroborated by the release DAG: `codemod` reads 0 and `migration` reads 0 in
`.github/workflows/release.yml` against a control of 97 for `deploy`. So NO TAG
EVER SHIPS THIS TOOL. Waiting for rf2-kmqx3 does not produce a better command,
a shorter command, or any command at all -- it produces the same git coordinate
later. The dependency was worded around a published jar by someone who had not
checked what that jar contains. That is the whole of the scheduling question,
and it is now answered.

Corollary that must survive into the published page: DO NOT write "flips to
`:mvn/version` after the first tag" beside this command. It does not flip. A
released tag may later supply a nicer SHA to pin (`v<VERSION>`), and that is the
only thing publication changes here.

--- 1. THE PROBE (worker's first act; it no longer gates dispatch) ---

Run OUTSIDE the repository, from a directory with no re-frame2 clone beside it,
with BOTH caches isolated. Naming only `:mvn/local-repo` -- which is all the
bead's own acceptance clause said -- does NOT isolate a git route: git deps
cache under `~/.gitlibs`, which only the `GITLIBS` env var relocates. That was a
hole in this bead's acceptance wording and is hereby corrected.

    mkdir -p "$HOME/scratch/rf2-lb566-clean" && cd "$HOME/scratch/rf2-lb566-clean"
    mkdir -p .m2 .gitlibs sample/src

    cat > sample/src/demo.cljs <<'EOF'
    (ns demo (:require [reagent.core :as r] ["react-select" :as Select]))
    (def state (r/atom nil))
    (defn view [] [:> Select {:value :ready}])
    EOF

    SHA=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git refs/heads/main | cut -f1)

    GITLIBS="$PWD/.gitlibs" clojure -Srepro \
      -Sdeps "{:mvn/local-repo \"$PWD/.m2\"
               :deps {day8/re-frame2-hicasso-codemod
                      {:git/url \"https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git\"
                       :git/sha \"$SHA\"
                       :deps/root \"migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod\"}}}" \
      -M -m re-frame.migration.hicasso.codemod sample/src/
    echo "EXIT=$?"

Three things about that command, each of which a naive version gets wrong:

 - `git ls-remote`, NOT `git rev-parse HEAD`. The published page must name a SHA
   that exists on the PUBLIC remote. A local-only SHA fails for every reader.
 - `-Srepro` alongside `-Sdeps`. `-Sdeps` MERGES with user-level `deps.edn`; it
   does not replace it. Without `-Srepro` a green run may be leaning on the
   operator's `~/.clojure/deps.edn` and the recipe is not reproducible for a
   reader. (Codex's correction; accepted.)
 - `GITLIBS` AND `:mvn/local-repo`, per the paragraph above.

READING THE OUTCOME -- and EXIT 0 IS NOT EVIDENCE. `codemod.clj`'s `-main`
exits 0 for ANY run that COMPLETED without a `:parse-error` entry, by deliberate
design ("a migration tool that fails a build because a consumer's code needs a
human decision is a tool that gets run once"). It also ALWAYS writes a report.
So "exit 0" and "a `:census` key exists" are both satisfied by a tool that found
nothing, which is exactly what a half-resolved classpath would look like.

PASS requires all four:
 (a) exit 0, and the run prints the absolute path of the report it wrote;
 (b) the report contains ONE `:local-reactive-cell` census entry (the `r/atom`)
     AND ONE `:named-value` fixer entry (the `:value :ready` crossing) -- i.e.
     assert the FINDINGS, not the file;
 (c) `sample/src/demo.cljs` is BYTE-IDENTICAL afterwards, and still is after a
     `--rewrite` dry run. Only `--rewrite --write` may touch it;
 (d) `.gitlibs/` is populated, `.m2/` is populated, and NO `re-frame2`
     directory was created beside the workspace.

FIXTURE NOTE, and it is why the fixture above is not the one this dossier
originally proposed. Codex measured the original `[:> Select {:is-multi true
:class-name "x"}]` in-memory and got ONE census site and ZERO fixer entries --
correctly, since neither prop is a fixer family. A probe demanding a fixer
finding from it would have reported FAIL against a perfectly working
installation. Not re-measured here; the worker verifies the expected findings
against the in-tree corpus before pinning them as the acceptance, and adjusts
the fixture rather than the tool if they differ.

FAILURE READINGS:
 - `Could not locate re_frame/hicasso/impl/slot.cljc` / `ClassNotFoundException`
   on `re-frame.hicasso.impl.slot` -> tools.deps did not honour the escaping
   `:paths` inside a gitlib. Take fallback (2) below. STILL DISPATCHABLE, still
   pre-publish, just a larger diff. This does NOT restore the rf2-kmqx3 hold.
 - `Manifest type not detected` / `:deps/root` error -> wrong `:deps/root`
   shape for this tree. Adjust and re-probe.
 - Resolution succeeds but the in-repo `clojure -M:test` goes red -> the shared
   rule broke. Non-negotiable. Revise.

FALLBACK (2), if the escaping `:paths` does not survive the gitlib: add an alias
that swaps the relative `:paths` entry for a git coordinate on
`implementation/hicasso`, while the DEFAULT `:paths` keeps the relative entry so
the in-repo `identical?` pin is unchanged.

--- 2. THE GIT ROUTE, AND WHY IT IS IMMUNE TO BOTH THE RENAME AND THE TAG ---

`skills/re-frame2-setup/references/deps-versions.md:98-107` documents it under a
heading that says the quiet part out loud -- "The `:git/sha` route (pre-publish,
no checkout on disk)" -- and `:66` of the same page calls a `:local/root` or a
`:git/url` + `:git/sha` coord "the ONLY working manual route today". The shape:

    {:git/url "https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git"
     :git/sha "<SHA>"
     :deps/root "migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod"}

RENAME-IMMUNE: a git coordinate names a URL and a SHA. No Maven group appears in
it, so rf2-fo4ng's `day8/*` -> `io.github.day8/*` sweep cannot touch it. (57
tracked files still name `day8/re-frame2-hicasso`; none of them is this
command.)

TAG-IMMUNE, and this is the stronger half: per item 1 above, the published jar
excludes the reporter, so the tag never offers a replacement coordinate. The git
route is the destination, not the waypoint.

--- 3. THE DEFECT, WHICH IS FOUR SURFACES AND NOT TWO ---

`docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md:28` prints
`cd re-frame2/migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod` -- a path inside a source
checkout of this repo, printed on a PUBLISHED page (chapter 20 is at
`mkdocs.yml:287`, in the nav). A reader who installed Hicasso from a jar has no
such directory. Step 4 at `:449-454` carries NO `cd` of its own and is
executable only because step 1 put the reader inside the checkout, so it moves
with step 1.

The dossier stopped at those two fences. It under-counted: the shipped AI skill
repeats the same instruction, verified here --

title: docs(story-mcp): three pages still promise false-empty browser reads
description:
## Scope

Align the three remaining Story-MCP documentation statements for unreachable browser-only capabilities with the shipped `capability-unavailable` error contract. Documentation only: `tools/story-mcp/README.md`, `tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md`, and `tools/story/spec/Principles.md`. No runtime, schema, tool, or transport change.

## Correctness finding

PR #8865 correctly rewrote `docs/story/api/mcp-surface.md` to say that the headless JVM cannot inspect the CLJS substrate registry or a11y-panel atom and therefore returns `isError true` / `:rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable`, never a false-empty success. Three committed authorities still state the retired opposite:

- `tools/story-mcp/README.md:18-20`: browser-only surfaces return an explicit empty result.
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:462-463`: `read-a11y-violations` returns an empty list plus a hint.
- `tools/story/spec/Principles.md:168-170`: substrates/a11y violations return empty plus a hint.

The implementation, tool descriptors, focused tests, `tools/story-mcp/spec/API.md`, and the opening host-boundary section of `002-Tool-Registry.md` all enforce the error. The stale prose is operationally material: an empty violations vector means a reached provider observed no findings, while capability absence means the host could not look.

## Deduplication

All-status searches over `read-a11y-violations`, `capability-unavailable`, `false-empty`, `empty list`, and the exact sentences found no issue owning these residual pages. rf2-udumn / PR #8865 owns the public chapter and retired `record-as-variant` residue; its enumerated scope is complete and closed, so this narrowly owns the separate capability-result contradiction.

## Recommended minimal fix

Replace the three stale clauses with one consistent rule: unreachable provider -> machine-readable capability error; empty collection -> a reached provider genuinely reported none. Keep the canonical links rather than adding another catalogue.
acceptance_criteria:
1. README, Tool-Registry §read-a11y-violations, and Story Principles all describe the same `isError true` / `:rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable` result for an unreachable browser provider.
2. Each distinguishes capability absence from a reached provider returning an empty substrate/violation collection.
3. No runtime, descriptor, schema, tool inventory, or transport behavior changes.
4. The applicable documentation link gate passes; tables/links touched are hand-checked where the gate does not cover prose.

title: surface-review(routing): preserve literal surrogate code units in url-decode
description:
## Owning item

Found while implementing rf2-j3tud (component URL ENCODING host-parity, PR #8873), which asked whether the reverse direction carried a matching asymmetry. It does not — this is a SECOND, different defect, so it is filed separately rather than folded in. rf2-j3tud's non-goals explicitly keep decoding out of scope ("No change to ... decoding", "Keep decode behavior and the literal-+ rule intact").

## Correctness finding

`re-frame.routing.url/url-decode` documents itself as HOST-SYMMETRIC and claims the JVM path "reproduces `decodeURIComponent` exactly". It does so for the `+` rule (rf2-9a9ix) and for structurally malformed input (`%`, `%a`, `%zz` are nil on both hosts). It does NOT for INVALID UTF-8 BYTE SEQUENCES.

`java.net.URLDecoder/decode` decodes with a REPLACE malformed-input action, substituting U+FFFD and returning a string. `js/decodeURIComponent` throws URIError, which `safe-url-decode` converts to the nil fail-closed sentinel.

## Evidence (production code, both hosts)

| input | JVM `safe-url-decode` | CLJS `safe-url-decode` |
|---|---|---|
| `%C0%80` (overlong NUL) | 2x U+FFFD, NON-NIL | nil |
| `%ED%A0%80` (lone surrogate) | 1x U+FFFD, NON-NIL | nil |
| `%FF` (invalid lead byte) | 1x U+FFFD, NON-NIL | nil |
| `%E0%80%80` (overlong) | 3x U+FFFD, NON-NIL | nil |
| `%C3%A9` (valid) | "e-acute" | "e-acute" (agree) |
| `%`, `%a`, `%zz` | nil | nil (agree) |

Measured consequence at the public predicate:

    (url/malformed-url? "/p/%FF")  ; JVM => false ; CLJS => true

## Why it matters

`malformed-url?` is the discriminator `:rf.route/transitioned` / `:rf.route/handle-url-change` use to separate a bare route-miss (`{:url url}`) from the fail-closed malformed case (`{:url url :reason :malformed-url}`). So for a URL carrying an invalid UTF-8 escape:

- CLJS (browser): fails closed, route-miss with `:reason :malformed-url`.
- JVM (SSR): decodes to a param containing U+FFFD replacement characters and MATCHES the route.

Two consequences, both in classes this repo already treats as defects:

1. **Host divergence on a security-adjacent sink.** `safe-url-decode`'s own docstring names the motivation as "hostile URLs, partner integrations with broken escaping". The fail-closed posture the JVM arm was written to have is not the one it has.
2. **Spec 011 hydration mismatch.** The server renders the matched route's tree; the hydrating client renders not-found for the same URL. That is a whole-tree disagreement, strictly worse than the attribute-level one rf2-j3tud fixed.

## Recommended direction (not a ruling)

Make the JVM arm fail closed on malformed UTF-8, matching `decodeURIComponent` — the same direction rf2-9a9ix took for `+` and rf2-j3tud took for the encoder, i.e. CLJS normative. Mechanically this means decoding percent-escapes to bytes and running them through a UTF-8 decoder with REPORT (not REPLACE) malformed-input action, so invalid sequences throw and `safe-url-decode` returns its existing nil sentinel. No caller changes: every consumer already propagates that sentinel.

Worth deciding explicitly: whether a legitimately-encoded U+FFFD (`%EF%BF%BD`) must still decode successfully. It should — it is valid UTF-8 — and any fix must not conflate it with the substituted one, which is exactly the bug a naive "does the output contain U+FFFD?" check would introduce.

## Acceptance criteria

- A shared CLJC test asserts `safe-url-decode` returns nil on JVM and CLJS alike for a table of invalid UTF-8 escapes (overlong, lone surrogate, invalid lead byte), with valid multi-byte input (`%C3%A9`) and legitimately-encoded U+FFFD (`%EF%BF%BD`) as controls that must still decode.
- `malformed-url?` agrees across hosts for a URL carrying such an escape in a path segment, a query key, a query value and a fragment.
- Reverting the JVM decoder makes the JVM half red while the valid-input controls stay green.
- Focused JVM and CLJS routing suites pass.

## Non-goals

- No change to the `+`-literal rule, to encoding, to route patterns/matching/ranking, or to the nil-sentinel propagation contract.
- No inbound URL normalisation or sanitisation beyond the decode-failure classification.
acceptance_criteria: safe-url-decode returns nil on BOTH hosts for invalid UTF-8 escapes (overlong, lone surrogate, invalid lead byte), with %C3%A9 and %EF%BF%BD as controls that must still decode; malformed-url? agrees across hosts for such an escape in path segment, query key, query value and fragment; reverting the JVM decoder reds the JVM half while the valid-input controls stay green; focused JVM and CLJS routing suites pass.

FENCED 2026-09-01 14:01 AUSEST by the mayor: implementation/routing/** is held by a LIVE fix worker on branch worker/routing-encoding-j3tud (PR #8873), which is repairing a cross-artefact break the url-ENCODE change caused in implementation/http. This item is the url-DECODE counterpart and touches the same namespace, so it waits for #8873 to merge — not merely for that worker to finish. Two things to carry into the dispatch when it comes, both from the worker that filed this: the defect is that java.net.URLDecoder substitutes U+FFFD where decodeURIComponent throws, so malformed-url? reads false on JVM and true on CLJS and a hostile URL matches under SSR while failing closed in the browser; and a legitimately-encoded U+FFFD (%EF%BF%BD) is valid UTF-8 that MUST still decode, so a naive 'output contains U+FFFD' check would introduce a new bug.

---

VERDICT 2026-09-01 (worker, PR #8882, branch worker/urldecode-k2d2t)

FINDING CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, not taken on faith. The five-input probe was
reproduced against production code on both hosts before any edit. JVM
safe-url-decode returned non-nil for %C0%80 (2x U+FFFD), %ED%A0%80 (1x),
%FF (1x) and %E0%80%80 (3x) — codepoints read as 65533, so these were
genuine substitutions, not an artefact of console encoding — while
decodeURIComponent threw for all four. (malformed-url? "/p/%FF") read
false on JVM and true on CLJS. Every claim on this bead held exactly.

FIX. url-decode's JVM arm now decodes in three stages: pre-escape (bare
`+`, then every literal non-ASCII character), URLDecoder under
ISO-8859-1 — the 1:1 byte<->char charset, which performs the SAME
structural validation as before (%, %a, %zz still throw
IllegalArgumentException) while substituting nothing — and finally a
strict UTF-8 decode of the recovered bytes through a CharsetDecoder set
to CodingErrorAction/REPORT. safe-url-decode's existing nil sentinel
carries the result; no caller changed.

HOW THE NEAR-MISS IS DISTINGUISHED — the trap this bead warned about.
The check is made at the BYTE level, under the UTF-8 decoder's own
validity rules, and the decoded OUTPUT is never inspected for U+FFFD.
%EF%BF%BD is a legal three-byte sequence, so it decodes to U+FFFD; %FF
is not, so it throws. An output-inspecting check cannot separate the two
— the substituted character and the legitimate one are identical — which
is exactly why that approach was refused. %EF%BF%BD is pinned as a
positive case and stayed green throughout, including under sabotage.

LITERAL NON-ASCII, which the recommended direction did not mention and
which a naive strict-decoder fix silently regresses. Both hosts pass an
unescaped non-ASCII character through today (decodeURIComponent("cafe"
with an acute e) returns it unchanged), and a strict decoder reached via
a bare latin-1 round trip would newly reject it — re-introducing the
very divergence class this bead is about. Hence the pre-escape stage.
Folding a literal into an ADJACENT escape run cannot change the verdict
either way: a literal's UTF-8 always begins with a lead byte (C2-F4),
never a continuation byte, so it can neither complete a truncated run
nor spoil a valid one. Verified against node in both directions.

TWO LATENT DIVERGENCES FOUND THAT THIS BEAD DID NOT NAME. "%C3" followed
by a literal non-ASCII character, and "%E2%82" likewise, threw on CLJS
and returned a U+FFFD-bearing string on the JVM. Both now fail closed on
both hosts and are pinned in the suite.

NO SPEC EDIT OWED — checked rather than assumed. Spec 012 §`+` is a
literal ¶1 already names decodeURIComponent as the de-facto reference
and states the browser is the canonical host "so the JVM matches it",
and the paragraph above it names a host-divergent decoder as the Spec
011 hydration-mismatch class; §Route-miss ¶5 already requires malformed
percent-encoding to fail the whole match closed. So this is a
conformance repair to standing normative text, the same conclusion
rf2-j3tud reached for the encode half. spec/011-SSR.md and
spec/012-Routing.md are untouched, and neither needed touching.

TESTS. New implementation/routing/test/re_frame/
routing_url_decoding_parity_cljs_test.cljc — one .cljc table asserted
identically on both hosts against literal expected values, extending the
mechanism rf2-j3tud built rather than inventing a second one. Pins the
invalid-UTF-8 set, the valid-decode controls (%EF%BF%BD, an astral code
point, %2B, +-literal) so it cannot pass by nil-ing everything, the
literal-non-ASCII passthrough, malformed-url? across path segment /
query key / query value / fragment with valid-escape controls in the
same four positions, the production match-url prism, and the route-url
-> match-url round trip over a value containing a real U+FFFD.

GATES, exit codes captured on one command line and quoted from the
captured .exit file (not from harness-reported status), re-run on the
final base after rebasing onto 77d6ecbbaa:
  JVM focused                  exit 0 — 6 tests, 60 assertions
  JVM full routing artefact    exit 0 — 542 tests, 3279 assertions
  CLJS focused                 exit 0 — 6 tests, 60 assertions
  CLJS full node-test          exit 0 — 11143 tests, 54841 assertions
The focused counts are identical on both hosts (6/60), which is the
host-symmetry the suite exists to assert.

CONTROL. Single-line plant (CodingErrorAction/REPORT -> REPLACE on
.onMalformedInput), anchor match count checked as 1 before running so
the plant could not silently no-op. Sabotaged JVM run: exit 1, 19
failures over the same 6 tests / 60 assertions, so nothing crashed and
no assertions were lost. All 19 are fail-closed assertions. ZERO
failures mention %EF%BF%BD — every valid-decode control stayed green
under sabotage, which is what proves the fix does not over-reject.
Restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object (line
endings are translated in this checkout, so a byte digest of the working
file would not have been sound), then re-run green (exit 0, 6/60).

Worker worktree guard ran and exited 0 before the first edit.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8882 — REOPENED EXACT DECODER OWNER; NO DUPLICATE.

COMPLETENESS: The strict byte decoder correctly closes invalid percent-encoded UTF-8 and preserves valid scalar inputs, including a real U+FFFD. The literal-non-ASCII repair is incomplete at the UTF-16 boundary. Java strings, like JavaScript strings, can contain an unpaired surrogate code unit. The new percent-escape-non-ascii path sends that literal through String.getBytes(UTF_8), whose replacement action silently turns it into ASCII '?'; the previous JVM URLDecoder path and native decodeURIComponent both preserve the raw literal code unit.

CORRECTNESS — measured against production code at PR #8882: lone high U+D800 decodes on JVM to code unit [63], lone low U+DFFF to [63], and a/U+D800/b to [97 63 98]. The pre-PR JVM path and Node decodeURIComponent return [55296], [57343], and [97 55296 98] respectively. Thus this PR introduces a JVM/browser decode divergence and aliases malformed UTF-16 to a legitimate question mark, despite its exact decodeURIComponent claim. This is distinct from percent-encoded %ED%A0%80, which must continue failing closed, and from rf2-j3tud's outbound encoder work.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / NARROW REMEDY: Preserve literal UTF-16 code units while strict-decoding only the bytes contributed by percent escapes, or use an equivalently small segmentation seam; do not add a general URI abstraction. Extend the existing shared CLJC parity suite with lone-high, lone-low, embedded-lone, and valid-pair controls. The percent-encoded lone-surrogate row must remain nil, so the fix cannot weaken strict escaped-byte validation.

instruction; the description describes the ORIGINAL defect, which PR #8882
already fixed. No comments on the bead (comment_count 0). No children; one
dependency, rf2-j3tud, already closed.

PREMISE HELD AT TIP, reproduced against production code before any edit rather
than taken from the audit. Inputs built from NUMERIC code units and outputs read
as VECTORS of code units — a lone surrogate, a `?` and a U+FFFD are all mojibake
in a terminal and indistinguishable by eye, and the node-side census was
re-instrumented after the first attempt: `Array.from(s, c => c.charCodeAt(0))`
iterates CODE POINTS and silently collapsed the surrogate-pair control to one
element. An index loop over `.length` / `.charCodeAt` is code-unit-exact on both
hosts and is what the suite now uses.

                              JVM at tip     node decodeURIComponent
  lone high U+D800            [63]           [55296]
  lone low  U+DFFF            [63]           [57343]
  a U+D800 b                  [97 63 98]     [97 55296 98]
  valid PAIR U+1F600          [55357 56832]  [55357 56832]   (agreed)
  reversed U+DFFF U+D800      [63 63]        [57343 55296]
  %ED%A0%80 escaped lone      nil            nil             (agreed)
  %ED%BF%BF escaped lone low  nil            nil             (agreed)
  %ED%A0%BD%ED%B8%80 CESU-8   nil            nil             (agreed)
  %F0%9F%98%80 escaped pair   [55357 56832]  [55357 56832]   (agreed)
  %EF%BF%BD real U+FFFD       [65533]        [65533]         (agreed)

All fifteen rows of the probe agreed after the fix, JVM row for row with node.

FIX — the segmentation seam the audit named, and nothing wider. The JVM arm is
now ONE left-to-right walk: consecutive %XX escapes accumulate into a byte
buffer, and the moment a non-% character arrives (or the string ends) that
buffer is flushed through the existing strict UTF-8 decoder while the literal
character is appended VERBATIM. That is decodeURIComponent's own decode loop,
so java.net.URLDecoder leaves the path entirely — and with it BOTH stages that
existed only to feed it: the +-preescape (URLDecoder is the form-urlencoded
decoder; nothing else ever turned + into a space) and percent-escape-non-ascii,
which was the lossy step. Net effect on the file is one helper removed and one
added, not a new abstraction. NO general URI abstraction was added, as both the
audit and the project stance require.

WHY THE OLD SHAPE LOST THE CODE UNIT. percent-escape-non-ascii reached the byte
level by running each literal non-ASCII run through String.getBytes(UTF_8),
whose REPLACE malformed-input action emits 0x3F for an unpaired surrogate.
decodeURIComponent never encodes a literal at all, so there was nothing to align
with: the repair is to stop encoding literals, not to encode them better.

THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS INTACT AND IS ASSERTED IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION. A
PERCENT-ENCODED lone surrogate must still be nil, because UTF-8 has no encoding
for a surrogate however those bytes arrived. %ED%A0%80, %ED%BF%BF and the CESU-8
spelling %ED%A0%BD%ED%B8%80 (U+1F600's two halves escaped individually) are all
nil on both hosts, while the SAME code point escaped properly as one four-byte
sequence, %F0%9F%98%80, decodes to the pair — so those rows refuse the encoding,
not the code point.

ONE DELIBERATE CHOICE WORTH RECORDING: the new hex reader is ASCII-only.
Character/digit — and Integer/parseInt, which defers to it — accepts non-ASCII
digit characters such as the Arabic-Indic six, which decodeURIComponent refuses.
The old pipeline reached the right verdict there only by accident (the non-ASCII
escaping stage mangled such input into a structurally bad escape). Verified: a
% followed by two Arabic-Indic digits is nil on both hosts.

NO SPEC EDIT OWED — checked, not assumed. spec/012-Routing.md and
spec/011-SSR.md are untouched and neither needed touching, the same disposition
rf2-j3tud and this bead's first pass reached: Spec 012 names decodeURIComponent
as the de-facto reference and the browser as the canonical host, and the JVM arm
is explicitly the emulation, so an incomplete emulation is a conformance bug in
the emulator. The hot-zone fence was never approached.

TESTS — the EXISTING shared .cljc parity suite was extended, not replaced.
implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_url_decoding_parity_cljs_test.cljc
gains the four controls the audit named (lone-high, lone-low, embedded-lone,
valid PAIR) plus: the reversed-halves case, three literal/escape adjacency rows
(a literal surrogate before and after %C3%A9, and after %41), the truncated-
escape-against-a-literal-surrogate row, the escaped counterweights, the CESU-8
row, malformed-url? over a literal code unit in a path segment and a query
value, and a surrogate-pair slug added to the route-url -> match-url round trip.
Two code-unit instruments are defined index-wise on purpose and the reason is in
the source: iterating a JS string by code POINT collapses a pair.

GATES, runner's own captured exit codes read from the .exit file (never the
harness-reported status), ALL re-run on the FINAL base after rebasing onto
28b3e3e604 — sixteen landings on from the first run, including
implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs and the machines hydrate work:
  JVM    clojure -M:test in implementation/routing    exit 0   548 / 3340
  CLJS   compile-node-test.cjs node-test              exit 0   1873 files, 0 warnings
  CLJS   node out/node-test.js                        exit 0   11149 / 55142
  LINT   clj-kondo --fail-level error                 exit 0   0 errors
The CLJS lane was discriminated by its printed root: shadow-cljs named this
worker checkout's own shadow-cljs.edn. No markdown, spec/ or workflow file
changed, so neither doc-link gate has a path here and neither was nominated.

CONTROLS — TWO PLANTS, EACH REDDING EXACTLY ONE DIRECTION. The whole risk in
this change is coupling the two directions, so a single plant redding both would
have proved nothing. Each plant's anchor match count was read as 1 BEFORE the
run so it could not silently no-op, and each restore was verified by git blob
hash against the committed object (line endings are translated in this checkout,
so a byte digest of the working file would not have been sound).

  A — THE SEAM REMOVED. One line: the literal branch round-trips each character
  through getBytes(UTF_8), restoring the replacing encoder. Blob 16399d8f ->
  bea02e6c, restored and re-verified back to 16399d8f. Captured exit 1, EIGHT
  failures, counts 548 / 3340 identical to the green run so no namespace crashed
  and no lane was truncated. All eight are literal-code-unit rows. ZERO mention
  any percent-encoded row — a grep of the whole log for %ED / %C0%80 / %E0%80%80
  / %FF / %EF%BF%BD returned 0.

  B — THE ESCAPED-BYTE CHECK WEAKENED. One line: CodingErrorAction/REPORT ->
  REPLACE. Blob 16399d8f -> 6fb2c013, restored and re-verified back to 16399d8f.
  Captured exit 1, TWENTY-SIX failures, counts again 548 / 3340. Every one is a
  fail-closed assertion; ZERO literal-passthrough rows redded (0 failures at
  that table's line). The single failure mentioning 55296 is itself a fail-closed
  nil? assertion.

  A and B are the same suite redding in OPPOSITE directions under opposite
  plants. That is what proves the literal seam and the escaped-byte check are
  independent properties rather than two names for one, which is the exact
  failure mode the audit's "the percent-encoded lone-surrogate row must remain
  nil" clause exists to catch.

  C — A WRONG EXPECTED VALUE IN THE SHARED TABLE ([97 55296 98] -> [97 12345
  98]). Blob 2b229131 -> 2d53893a, restored and re-verified back to 2b229131.
  Run on the CLJS lane: captured exit 1, exactly ONE failure, reporting the CLJS

Worker worktree guard ran and exited 0 before the first edit. The node_modules

title: bug(skill-setup): generator resolves tools/template from the fresh target
description:
## Scope

Fix the explicitly requested generator route in `skills/re-frame2-setup/**`: how the installed skill locates the pre-publish `tools/template` checkout, chooses the generator command's working/target directory, and evaluates that workflow. The default manual scaffold remains unchanged. This task may add a focused command-level fixture that invokes the actual documented route, but does not redesign `tools/template` output.

## Correctness finding

The skill promises to execute the generator itself for a user standing in a fresh project directory, but its only working pre-publish command passes `{:local/root "tools/template"}`. A Clojure local root is resolved against the command's current working directory, so from the directory being scaffolded it means `<target>/tools/template`, which does not exist. The command fails before deps-new loads the template. Running the literal command from the monorepo root makes the dependency resolve, but changes the output base to the monorepo rather than the user's requested location. The advertised executor route therefore has no specified command that both finds the template and writes into the intended target.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:57` calls the generator a complete alternative that the skill runs itself when requested, and says the pre-publish working form is the local-root invocation against a checkout.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:23-24` grants the corresponding `clojure -Tnew create` and `clojure -Sdeps ... -Tnew create` commands.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:24-31` presents the pre-publish command with literal `{:local/root "tools/template"}`; unlike the template's own README, it does not bind that relative path to an execution cwd or derive the installed checkout path.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:37` reiterates that the skill executes the command, while the product is advertised as scaffolding from an empty directory at lines 5 and 41.
- `tools/template/README.md:50-58` says its relative-local-root form must run from the repository root. That premise is incompatible with treating the user's fresh target as the command cwd unless output placement is made explicit.
- `tools/template/deps.edn:19-25` already records the correct clean-directory form for in-repo smoke testing: use an absolute `<abs-path>/tools/template` local root when the command runs from an empty directory.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/evals/evals.json:26` mentions the generator as a complete UIx alternative but has no executable expectation proving path resolution or output placement from a directory outside the monorepo.
- Command witness: from a newly created empty temporary directory outside the checkout, the exact advertised `clojure -Sdeps ... {:local/root "tools/template"} ... -Tnew create` form exited 1 with `Local lib day8/re-frame2-template not found: <clean-target>/tools/template`; it emitted no project files. The temporary directory was removed after the witness.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install/link `re-frame2-setup` from a reviewed checkout, then create and enter a separate empty directory where the new app should be generated.
2. Ask the skill to use the generator route, or run the pre-publish command printed in `skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:30-31` unchanged.
3. Observe exit 1 before template hooks run: tools.deps resolves the relative local root beneath the empty target and reports that `day8/re-frame2-template` is not found.
4. Change cwd to the monorepo root and retry the same literal command. The local root now resolves, but deps-new's relative output base is the monorepo cwd rather than the original empty target unless a separate target path is supplied.

## Failure scenario / invariant

An explicitly requested generator run must satisfy both coordinates at once: its template dependency resolves from the reviewed installed checkout, and its generated files land in the user's requested project location. Neither coordinate may be inferred from one shared cwd. Today the skill conflates them, so the only documented pre-publish command is wrong in the normal fresh-target execution context.

## Recommended minimal fix

At runtime, resolve the template directory from the installed skill/repository location and pass that reviewed directory as an absolute, EDN-safe `:local/root`. Keep command execution/output targeting anchored to the user's requested project directory (or its parent using deps-new's normal target option), and state that relationship once in the generator route. Reuse the existing deps-new template and command; do not add a wrapper generator, copy template resources, or introduce an interactive path prompt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused integration fixture creates a clean target directory outside the re-frame2 checkout, invokes the same generator-command construction the skill teaches with the resolved template checkout path, and asserts exit 0 plus representative emitted files (`deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, `package.json`, and the selected substrate's entry namespace) under the requested target.
- The fixture asserts the resolved local root is the reviewed `tools/template` directory associated with the installed skill, not a `tools/template` child of the target cwd; path rendering works on Windows and POSIX without hand-authored escaping.
- Non-vacuity: the same fixture substitutes the current literal relative local root while remaining in the clean target and must fail before emission with the missing local library resolved under that target. Removing the path-resolution fix therefore makes the positive arm red.
- Control: the generator still receives `day8/re-frame2-template`, the requested project name and substrate, and no generated project directory or manifest is written into the re-frame2 checkout.
- Add an outcome-graded eval for an explicit request such as “Use the generator to scaffold a UIx app in this empty directory.” It must require the skill to execute successfully in that target, not merely print the command or assume the target is the monorepo root.
- The existing setup structural/eval checks and generator tests remain green. The fixture reports its own generator exit code and verifies a non-empty emitted manifest so a skipped command cannot pass.

## Non-goals

- Do not change the default manual scaffold, substrate API, generated application design, or template feature matrix.
- Do not publish/split the template repository, rename Maven coordinates, or solve Clojars availability; those have separate owners.
- Do not add a setup wizard, path questionnaire, copied template snapshot, compatibility command, or second generator implementation.
- Do not broaden into schema hot reload (`rf2-a0442`) or the template-minimisation program (`rf2-zq34m`).

## Related / duplicate search

Searched every tracker status across titles, descriptions, notes, acceptance criteria, and close reasons for `tools/template` with cwd/current-directory/local-root/target terms, generator with cwd/empty-directory/path terms, and setup-generator path terms. No bead owns resolution of the skill's pre-publish generator local root from a fresh target. Open `rf2-rc0yh` established the executor posture and still owns later default-manual simplification; it does not specify or test generator cwd/path resolution. Open `rf2-zq34m` owns the generated product shape, not how this installed skill locates that generator. Deferred `rf2-uelji` and `rf2-fo4ng` own publication/group coordinates and are explicitly outside this local invocation fix.

empty directory outside the checkout, the exact advertised pre-publish command exited 1
with 'Error building classpath. Local lib day8/re-frame2-template not found:
<target>/tools/template' and emitted nothing. Running the same literal from the monorepo
root resolves the dependency but relocates the emitted project into the checkout.

FIX (skills/re-frame2-setup/** only). Separated the two coordinates one working directory
was being asked to carry, and stated the relationship once in a new README section
'Running the generator pre-publish', cited from SKILL.md cardinal rule 5 and from
references/entry-namespace.md:
  * :local/root = where the TEMPLATE comes from. The ABSOLUTE path of tools/template
    inside the reviewed checkout the skill was installed from. The skill is installed by
    link, so SKILL.md's own resolved location is <RE_FRAME2>/skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md
    and the template is that path's grandparent plus tools/template. Forward slashes on
    every OS, so the EDN string needs no hand-authored escaping.
  * working directory = where the PROJECT lands. Run from the directory that should
    CONTAIN the new project; deps-new emits ./<artefact>/. For generating into an empty
    directory you already occupy, deps-new's own :target-dir . plus :overwrite true
    (:overwrite is required because '.' always exists — verified: without it deps-new
    exits 1 with '. already exists (and :overwrite was not true)').
No resolution framework, no path-discovery layer, no fallback chain, no wrapper generator.
The default manual scaffold is unchanged and tools/template/** is untouched.

THE ONE COMMAND A USER CAN NOW RUN, standing in the directory that should contain the
new project (verified exit 0, emitted ./my-app/ under the target, nothing written into
the checkout):
  clojure -Sdeps '{:deps {day8/re-frame2-template {:local/root "<RE_FRAME2>/tools/template"}}}' -Tnew create :template day8/re-frame2-template :name acme/my-app

FIXTURE: skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/generator_route_test.clj. Deliberately NOT a string
comparison against expected command text — such a test would have passed throughout this
defect's entire life, because the broken command WAS the documented command.
  * Resolution arm (always runs, needs only bb, so it gates in the existing
    skills-structural CI job that loops tests/*_test.clj — no workflow file was added or
    edited). Reads the :local/root out of the skill's own documented command, resolves it
    the way tools.deps does against a FRESHLY CREATED target directory, and fails unless
    the result is a real directory holding the template's deps.edn and hooks namespace.
    Runs that same resolution once against the old relative form as a control, so a green
    can never be the inert kind.
  * Live arm (opt-in, RF2_SETUP_RUN_GENERATOR=1) shells the real
    clojure -Sdeps ... -Tnew create ... :substrate :uix out of a clean directory created
    outside the checkout: asserts the generator's own exit code is 0, asserts a non-empty
    emitted manifest (deps.edn, shadow-cljs.edn, package.json, src/acme/my_app/core.cljs)
    under the requested target, asserts no project lands in the re-frame2 checkout, and
    requires the relative-root substitution to fail before emission with the missing lib
    reported UNDER the target. Opt-in because it needs the Clojure CLI and the -Tnew
    deps-new tool, which the skills-structural runner (Babashka only) does not provision;
    with the flag unset the file prints a loud LIVE ARM NOT RUN banner rather than passing
    silently. Editing that workflow was out of this item's fence.

NON-VACUITY MEASURED, both arms. Reinstating the exact original defect (the relative
:local/root, restored afterwards and verified by git blob hash against the committed
object) turned the fixture red: resolution arm 4 failures naming the temp target it
resolved under; live arm 10 failures including 'Generator exit 1 (expected 0)' and 'The
generator did not create my-app/ under the requested target'. So removing the
path-resolution fix does make the positive arm red, as the acceptance criteria required.

EVAL: added id 17 'generator-route-in-empty-dir' with outcome-graded expectations — the
skill must EXECUTE the command with an absolute root derived from its own installed
checkout, keep cwd at the author's location, report the real exit code and emitted files,
and fall back to the manual path rather than guess if no checkout resolves.

GATES, each captured exit code, all re-run on the final rebased base:
  check_doc_slugs.py                       exit 0   (the gate for skills/ markdown:
                                                     'skills' is in its DEFAULT_ROOTS and
                                                     is excluded from check_readme_links.py
                                                     via DOCS_GATE_ROOTS — verified at source)
  bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj            exit 0   33 tests / 108 assertions
  bb tests/generator_route_test.clj        exit 0   3 tests / 12 assertions (CI arm)
  RF2_SETUP_RUN_GENERATOR=1 same           exit 0   3 tests / 24 assertions (live arm)
  check_skill_setup_counter_drift.py --verbose --ci  exit 0
  check_skill_eval_packaging.py            exit 0
mkdocs was NOT nominated: docs_dir is 'docs' and nothing under skills/ is inside it.

WHAT NO GATE COVERS, and how it was checked by hand. Neither doc gate reads inside a
fenced code block, and the command being fixed lives in one — so the command's content is
invisible to check_doc_slugs.py. That is precisely what the fixture exists for, and both
its arms were run and sabotaged. Gate-reads-my-tree control: a broken anchor planted in
prose in the file being edited turned check_doc_slugs.py red naming
skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:85 and the planted anchor; restored and verified by blob
hash.

CENSUS of the broken relative form across tracked files, fixed-string, with two
shape-matched controls that both returned hits (so the search was not silently inert): no
PRESCRIPTIVE page in skills/re-frame2-setup/ carries it any more — the single remaining
hit in that tree is inside the new fixture's own header comment, where it appears as the
quoted defect being pinned.

RESIDUE OUTSIDE THIS ITEM'S FENCE, for the template owner rather than for here.
tools/template/README.md carries the relative form four times, but its Quick start
explicitly says 'run from the repo root', which makes it correct in its own stated
context. tools/template/spec/API.md:172 carries it WITHOUT stating a working directory,
which is a milder latent instance of the same trap; tools/template/** was fenced out of
this item, so it was left alone and is noted here instead.

FENCE NOTE: rf2-zq34m was not pre-empted. Nothing here touches what the generator emits —
only how the skill invokes it — so the fix survives either zq34m ruling, exactly as the

title: mcp-conformance: project-stories execution proof is vacuous
description:
## Scope

Tighten only the consumer-project Story-MCP witness in tools/mcp-conformance/test/fixtures/project-stories/ and tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs so its run-variant phase proves that project-authored lifecycle work executed. Preserve the existing first-connect, no --allow-writes, consumer-alias launch and missing-namespace failure arms.

## Correctness finding

The new project-stories end-to-end gate claims to prove that a pre-authored project variant is runnable on first connect, but its run arm is vacuous. The fixture variant deliberately has no :setup, no :script, and no assertions. The harness accepts isError false plus :status "pass". Story's result contract intentionally assigns :pass to an empty assertion set with a clean tape, so that response is the default for doing no observable lifecycle work.

Consequently the gate proves registration, lookup, request routing, and a success-shaped result envelope, but it cannot prove the correctness claim named by phase 5: that run-variant executed the project-authored variant lifecycle.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From tools/mcp-conformance, run npm run test:story-project on the current fixture. Phase 5 reports run-variant green.
2. Read the registered variant in test/fixtures/project-stories/src/app/stories.cljc: it has no :setup, :script, or assertion.
3. Read the phase-5 check in test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs: it accepts the response after only isError false and aggregate status "pass".
4. Compare Story's production aggregation rule: an empty assertion vector with no unmet/failure evidence returns :pass. The same gate verdict is therefore available without any project-authored lifecycle action to observe.

Expected: the execution phase requires evidence produced only by running the fixture variant.
Actual: the default empty-program pass is sufficient for the phase and the overall gate to be green.

## Evidence

- tools/mcp-conformance/test/fixtures/project-stories/src/app/stories.cljc:27-29 says the fixture has no :setup and no :script and is therefore "vacuously runnable".
- tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs:193-205 calls this a "vacuous pass" and checks only runResp.isError and runStruct.status.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/result.cljc:44-49 states the production rule directly: a run with zero assertions and a clean tape is :pass.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/requirements.cljc:547-555 implements that rule: with no error, failure, or unmet record, aggregate-status falls through to :pass.
- Closed bead rf2-cfq8a and the harness header describe the delivered outcome as discovering, reading, and running the project story on first connection. The current last verb has no execution-only witness.

The focused Node unit cluster is green (105 passed, 9 platform skips), which is expected: it does not make this end-to-end arm non-vacuous.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A regression can stop executing :setup and/or :script for launch-preloaded project variants while still resolving the known variant to an empty, clean run result. list-stories, get-story, and get-variant continue to pass. Phase 5 still sees isError false and status "pass", so the advertised golden path remains green even though the project's lifecycle never ran.

Invariant: any gate that claims a variant executed must assert evidence that can exist only if that variant's lifecycle executed. A default success status over an empty program is not such evidence.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the existing fixture variant perform one deterministic JVM-headless lifecycle action and emit one distinctive passing assertion. A small fixture-local event used by :setup, followed by a :script path assertion over the seeded value, is sufficient and exercises both halves without a renderer or browser. In the SDK test, assert the returned assertion record (identity, passed verdict, and expected/actual evidence), not merely the aggregate :status.

Keep this inside the existing fixture and test. No new server option, MCP tool, transport, test job, fixture project, or general assertion framework is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The existing project fixture variant contains non-empty, deterministic JVM-headless lifecycle work whose result cannot be produced without executing the variant (for example, fixture-local setup state followed by a distinctive script assertion).
2. end-to-end-project-stories.cjs still launches through the fixture project's -M:story-mcp alias before any MCP write, but now requires the run-variant response to contain the exact execution-only assertion/evidence and a passing aggregate status.
3. The test fails if run-variant returns the current empty-assertions :pass shape; checking only :status is not sufficient.
4. Non-vacuity control: temporarily make the fixture's expected value wrong, or disable the setup action that produces it, and run npm run test:story-project from tools/mcp-conformance. The command must exit non-zero and name the missing/failed execution witness. Restore the plant and require the same command to exit zero.
5. The existing missing-namespace launch arm, first-connect discovery/read arms, no --allow-writes posture, and clean SDK teardown remain covered and green.
6. Focused Story-MCP tests relevant to the chosen lifecycle action remain green; no browser, Chromium, nREPL, or Pair-MCP runtime is introduced.

## Non-goals

- Changing Story's intentional rule that an assertion-free variant is vacuously green.
- Adding a blanket requirement that every user-authored variant contain assertions.
- Testing rendering or browser-only Reagent/UIx stories in the headless JVM server.
- Expanding the tool catalogue, wire schemas, launch flags, token budgeting, or CI job matrix.
- Refactoring the mature Story runtime or adding a second consumer fixture.

## Related / duplicate search

- rf2-cfq8a (closed) delivered the first-launch project-story path and this witness. This issue is a correctness correction to its execution proof, not a duplicate of its bootstrap outcome.
- rf2-a9l6e (open) concerns one honest command/profile for running MCP compatibility and explicitly excludes new protocol assertions. It does not own this vacuous run arm.
- rf2-k9rzr (closed) mentions an unrelated vacuous assertion in bundle-isolation tooling.
- All-status tracker searches over project stories, project-story, run-variant, vacuous, mcp-conformance, dedup envelope, and serialized issue descriptions found no issue owning a non-vacuous execution witness for end-to-end-project-stories.cjs.

## Priority rationale

P2: this is a real false-green in an authoritative SDK/CI compatibility witness for the first-use Story-MCP workflow. It can allow an execution regression to ship while the named golden path stays green. It is not P1 because no current production execution failure was observed; the defect is in the gate's ability to detect one.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing project fixture performs deterministic JVM-headless lifecycle work.
- SDK test asserts exact execution-only assertion/evidence, not only aggregate pass.
- Empty-assertions pass is rejected.
- A planted wrong expectation or disabled setup makes npm run test:story-project exit non-zero; restoration exits zero.
- First-connect/no-write and missing-namespace arms remain green; no browser or new server surface.
notes:
FENCED (mayor, 2026-09-01 12:18:46 AUSEST): collides with a LIVE worker on tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs — the rf2-cfq8a audit-residual worker (branch worker/mcp-host-cfg-cfq8a) may edit a comment in that exact file. This bead's scope is that file plus its project-stories fixtures, so two workers would conflict. DO NOT DISPATCH until worker/mcp-host-cfg-cfq8a's PR merges (or that worker reports without touching the file). Clears when: worker/mcp-host-cfg-cfq8a's PR is MERGED.
FENCE CLEARED (mayor, 2026-09-01 12:27:07 AUSEST): the tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs hold is discharged — worker/mcp-host-cfg-cfq8a's PR #8861 MERGED at cd03ceffbf, and it did NOT touch that file (its report states the witness needed no change because :120-124 already states the cwd property generically). No live worker holds the file now. DISPATCHABLE.

WORKER (2026-09-01 12:49 AUSEST, branch worker/conformance-proof-3n3dk, PR #8866): finding CONFIRMED at source and repaired.

Premise check. end-to-end-project-stories.cjs phase 5 asserted exactly two things — !runResp.isError and runStruct.status === 'pass' — over a fixture variant with no :setup and no :script. Vacuous as described.

Repair. The run arm's assertion is REPLACED, not supplemented. The fixture variant now carries renderer-free lifecycle work (:setup dispatches the fixture project's own :fixture-app/seed-article, seeding [:fixture-app/article :headline]; :script asserts it back with :rf.assert/path-equals). The witness requires the single assertion record — id, :path, :expected, the live :actual read from the frame app-db at assertion time, and :passed? true / :status "pass" — and rejects an empty :assertions vector by name, BEFORE the aggregate :status is read at all. The expected literal is written by hand on both sides rather than shared through a def: a shared constant would have made AC 4's wrong-expected-value plant a no-op.

SECOND FINDING, one level below the bead's. run-variant on the headless JVM stdio host is INERT without a reactive substrate: setup dispatches reach no adapter, the script plays nothing, and the run still answers :status "pass" over an empty app-db and zero assertions. Measured directly (clojure -M -e in the fixture project: BARE-APPDB {} / BARE-ASSERTIONS [] without rf/init!; a full passing record with it). story-mcp's server installs Story's canonical vocabulary but deliberately chooses no substrate — per spec/006 that choice is the app's, and tools/story-mcp's own JVM tests supply it in their fixture (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) which is why they see records where the server does not. So the FIXTURE PROJECT now makes the choice in the namespace its launch alias preloads, as a consuming project would. No server, transport, tool-catalogue or launch-flag change; the bead's non-goals hold.

Non-vacuity control (AC 4), all from tools/mcp-conformance, exit captured in the same shell, never piped:
  :setup []                       -> npm run test:story-project EXIT 1, names the null read at the seeded path
  :script []  (pre-fix shape)     -> EXIT 1, names 0 assertion records; its rejected payload still reads status "pass" — i.e. the OLD arm would have been green on that tree
  expected literal made wrong     -> EXIT 1, names the expectation mismatch
  restored                        -> EXIT 0, full golden path green
Each plant verified applied and each restore verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object (aa4c94e7dac3a646766c6bf8e74f813de216254c); no plant silently no-opped.

Other gates, all on the final rebased base 96c224e904: npm run test:story EXIT 0 (this witness plus the 20-tool catalogue harness); npm run test:unit EXIT 0 (119 tests, 110 pass, 0 fail, 9 platform skips). No markdown touched, so neither doc-link gate applies.

AC 5 preserved and green: missing-namespace launch arm, first-connect list-stories/get-story/get-variant arms, no --allow-writes posture, consumer-alias -M:story-mcp launch, clean SDK teardown.

Files: tools/mcp-conformance/test/fixtures/project-stories/src/app/stories.cljc, tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs. Nothing else touched.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8866 (branch worker/conformance-proof-3n3dk, head e55d6b3c63, base 96c224e904). The phase-5 run arm's assertion is REPLACED: it now requires the :rf.assert/path-equals execution witness — id, :path, :expected, the live :actual read from the frame app-db, :passed? true — and rejects an empty :assertions vector by name before the aggregate :status is read. The fixture variant carries deterministic renderer-free lifecycle work (:setup seeds [:fixture-app/article :headline], :script asserts it back). Non-vacuity control per AC 4: three plants (:setup [], :script [], wrong expected literal) each drive npm run test:story-project to EXIT 1 naming the missing witness; restored EXIT 0. The :script [] plant's rejected payload still reads status 'pass', so the old arm would have been green on it. Second finding recorded on the bead and in the fixture: run-variant is inert on the headless JVM host without a reactive substrate and still answers 'pass' over an empty app-db — the fixture project now installs plain-atom in the namespace its launch alias preloads, no server change. AC 5 arms preserved and green.

title: surface-review(xray): make Pair the single agent runtime and retire the duplicate Xray seam
description:
## Scope

Make the human/agent boundary around Xray explicit and singular for pre-alpha users:

- Xray's preload and public API own the in-app human panel.
- `re-frame2-pair.runtime` plus `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/` own out-of-process programmer/AI inspection and mutation.
- Retire the unused `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` agent contract, its sentinel, tests, manifest rows, and documentation.
- Preserve the small fail-closed egress projection that Xray itself needs when copying app-db snapshots and diff values, but keep it internal to the panel.

Review and update the affected Xray source, specs, docs, tests, testbeds/build wiring, and repository API manifests. The desired outcome is one honest setup story, not a new capability.

## Findings

1. Xray documents an agent integration that does not exist. `tools/xray/README.md` and `tools/xray/spec/API.md` say Pair MCP evaluates `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` and that Xray's preload installs the agent sentinel with no second preload. Pair MCP instead hard-codes `re-frame2-pair.runtime`, probes `js/globalThis.__re_frame2_pair_runtime` before runtime-backed tools, and contains zero references to the Xray runtime namespace or sentinel.
2. The two seams are not interchangeable. The canonical Pair preload supplies the current coarse-grained workflow (`orient`, `snapshot`, event-bundle/cascade reads, dispatch consequence/dry-run, recording/watch, DOM/UI reads, restore/replace). Xray's older runtime still exposes a parallel catalogue of trace/epoch/app-db/registrar/resource/subscription/mutation calls and explicitly leaves event-bundle reads to a follow-on.
3. The duplication is substantial and already drifting: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime.cljs` is about 91 KB / 1,700 lines and its dedicated CLJS test is about 115 KB / 1,884 lines. The Pair preload is about 230 KB / 4,000 lines and has continued evolving after Xray runtime's last direct change on 2026-07-11.
4. Xray itself does not need that public agent catalogue. Within `tools/xray/src`, the only functional callers of the runtime namespace outside the preload are three calls to `runtime/egress-value` in the palette snapshot and app-db diff copy paths. The preload requires the whole namespace solely to install the second sentinel.
5. The contract contradicts Xray's own product boundary. `spec/Principles.md` says Xray is the human surface and AI belongs in the separate Pair MCP; `018-Event-Spine.md` says the agent reads raw instrumentation rather than a Xray-curated facade. Xray already has a large panel/tab information architecture, and its restraint principle explicitly argues for subtraction rather than another surface.
6. Four Xray runtime exports are nevertheless published as post-v1 tooling rows in `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` / generated `spec/api-manifest.edn`, turning an unused pre-alpha seam into prospective compatibility cost.
7. Testbed wiring proves the real setup: `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` explicitly loads `re-frame2-pair.runtime` alongside Xray in builds that Pair MCP drives, while Xray-only and Pair-only builds load their respective preloads independently.

## Recommended Action

Take a clean pre-alpha cut:

1. Remove `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` as a public/tooling namespace, including `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime`, its preload require, external accessor catalogue, mutation helpers, streaming state, dedicated runtime test bulk, and API-manifest rows.
2. Move or re-express only the panel-local `egress-value` behavior needed by palette snapshot and app-db diff copying in a small internal Xray namespace, preferably as a thin call to the canonical framework projection. Keep its current frame-owned, fail-closed sensitive/large-value behavior and focused tests.
3. Rewrite Xray's README and specs around one accurate boundary: load `day8.re-frame2-xray.preload` for the panel; load `re-frame2-pair.runtime` and use Pair MCP for programmer/AI access. A build may opt into either or both explicitly; neither preload silently stands in for the other.
4. Remove the obsolete stable-accessor/sentinel contract and future-consumer promises from Xray's API/spec material. Link to Pair's setup and tool contract rather than duplicating it.
5. Reconcile Xray testbeds/builds and generated manifests with that boundary. Keep Pair preload entries only where the build is actually Pair-driven and Xray preload entries only where the panel is exercised.

## Evidence

- False consumer/setup claims: `tools/xray/README.md:29-32,231-235`; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:56-58`; `tools/xray/spec/API.md:256,668-697,676-953`.
- Pair's actual boundary: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_form.cljs:64`; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs:14-15`; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md:28-39,429-452`; `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs`.
- Exact searches under `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` and `skills/re-frame2-pair` find no `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` or `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime` references.
- Xray-local callers: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/palette/events.cljs:181`; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_events.cljs:68-69`.
- Duplicate implementation/test: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime.cljs`; `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime_cljs_test.cljs`. The Xray trace accessor itself says event-bundle reads are deferred at `runtime.cljs:544-557`.
- Product boundary: `tools/xray/spec/Principles.md:59-79,148-157,172-178`; `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:24-29`.
- Published surface: `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:183-186` and corresponding generated rows.
- Real preload topology: `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1216,1320-1423,1460,1500-1531,1822-2120`.
- History: Xray runtime's last direct commit is `d22417a0b7` (2026-07-11); Pair runtime has subsequent direct commits through `2b0b482eb3` (2026-08-06).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Tracked product source, specs, docs, test config, and manifests contain no `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` namespace, `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime` sentinel, or claim that Pair MCP consumes/arrives through Xray. No compatibility alias, tombstone namespace, or dual-probe path remains.
2. `runtime.cljs` and its agent-contract test suite are removed. Any surviving privacy tests are focused on the two panel-local copy/export behaviors rather than re-specifying Pair's tool protocol.
3. Palette app-db snapshot and app-db diff copy still project under the observed frame and default-redact sensitive/large values. A focused CLJS test proves both a normal value and a seeded sensitive value at the actual copy boundary.
4. Xray's README/API gives copy-pasteable, separate setup for the panel and for Pair MCP. It states that loading both requires both explicit preloads and links to Pair's canonical tool documentation instead of reproducing an accessor table.
5. API manifest metadata is regenerated with zero Xray runtime rows; the manifest consistency gate passes.
6. Testbed/build preload lists match intent: Xray-only panel fixtures run without Pair, Pair-driven fixtures carry `re-frame2-pair.runtime`, and combined fixtures declare both. No Xray code depends on the skill-owned Pair namespace.
7. Xray's focused JVM/CLJS tests and browser smoke for shell startup plus the two copy paths pass. Pair MCP's conformance/runtime structural suite remains green, demonstrating that the one surviving agent path was not disturbed.
8. The implementation PR reports the source/test line reduction and names any residual public Xray namespace that remains for tool access; expected answer is none.

## Non-goals

- No new panel, dashboard, AI rail, workflow wizard, event-dossier variant, or information-architecture redesign.
- No redesign or expansion of Pair MCP, its protocol, privacy flags, write gates, or preload.
- No merged Xray/Pair mega-preload and no automatic loading of Pair from Xray.
- No deprecation period, compatibility wrapper, alias namespace, sentinel fallback, or migration framework; this is pre-alpha.
- No general rewrite of the framework egress/classification machinery.
- No broad audit of `day8.re-frame2-xray.core` facade exports.

## Related beads

- `rf2-hic-059` (closed) proves the current Pair MCP + `re-frame2-pair.runtime` path through a real emitted-eval/result flow; reuse that canonical boundary rather than creating another.
- `rf2-2hpxo` (deferred) is the broader external-alpha classification of `day8.re-frame2-xray.core` and other facades. It does not own this concrete duplicate tooling seam.
- All-status title, description, and notes searches for Xray runtime, Xray-MCP, Pair runtime, agent runtime, preload, sentinel, duplicate/retire/consolidate terms, and `surface-review(xray)` found no existing owner for this outcome.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-30 21:55:20 AUSEST (read-only agent at 556b8fabbc): premises HOLD (runtime.cljs 1,708 lines; test 2,027 not 1,884). CARRIERS THE BEAD MISSED: implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/test/.../cljs_manifest_probe_cljs_test.cljs:81,109 REQUIRES the namespace (must be edited or the probe reds); docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md (mkdocs.yml:454 nav row), docs/xray/api/{index.md:32,reference.md:74}, skills/re-frame2-xray/references/chrome.md:161, tools/xray/deps.edn:17 comment. shadow-cljs.edn names re-frame2-xray.runtime 0 times (reached via the xray preload only) — state 'shadow unchanged because' rather than touching the hot file. Recommend egress-value moves to day8.re-frame2-xray.egress (internal, no manifest row). - Excluding tests and bench data the package is ~22% library / ~78% apparatus by line: scripts 10,759 + spec ledgers 3,685 + frozen-sources 246 + docs/design/hicasso 67,541 lines against ~22.8K of library.
- Test side: 629 files / ~183K lines (10.7 lines of test per line of src) plus 82 MB of committed bench JSON (237 files). The bench tree alone is 197 files / 102K lines with 12 donor copies of the runtime (8,990 lines, 6,202 byte-identical to src) and 574 deftests that run per PR against the COPY, not the shipped runtime.
- 59 refusal ids emitted from src: 24 protect a plausible silent wrong result, 29 police ceremony the library itself introduced, 5 guard cases a competent programmer never writes or React already reports.

title: hic: frameless overlay with :on-dismiss reaches the declared-unreachable two-owners state — needs a ruling
description: Found by rf2-dr90's coverage audit; verified at source. impl/overlay.cljs's dismissal-handler returns nil when there is no frame dispatch (~:655-659), but popover-dismissal-attrs (~:746-751) reads only the props — so a popover mounted with NO frame above it and :on-dismiss written still renders popover="auto" with no handler: the platform light-dismisses it, no intent lands, and app-db keeps open? true — exactly the open-flag/second-owner desync overlay.cljs's docstring (~:80-83) declares unreachable. Same shape on the modal (closedby="closerequest", no cancel handler). The presence module ruled its frameless case explicitly (legal until a child writes an intent, presence_react ~:50-57, tested at presence_intent ~:334-365); overlay has no equivalent ruling or witness. Needs Mike's ruling on direction before any test or fix: refuse a frameless overlay that carries :on-dismiss, or degrade the attrs to manual/none when dispatch is nil. Then the witness follows the ruling.
notes:

The bead's own title names the hold: the frameless-overlay :on-dismiss path reaches a state the design declares unreachable, and whether the state is admitted (design amendment) or refused (code fix) is a RULING. BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:31:44 AUSEST: ruled; dispatchable.

WHY D, AND HOW THE REVIEWS WERE WEIGHED. The dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-4e5b.frameless-overlay-on-dismiss.md, now deleted; this note carries everything it held) recommended D. A second review appended to it ("Codex Recommendation") independently chose D on the same grounds and added implementation bounds (small guard, no id, no dispatch threading through the attrs fns, no grammar broadening, amend the one Spec 009 row, no compat layer). The two agreed, so this is adoption of a concurring recommendation rather than a tie-break. Decisive facts: (1) :on-dismiss IS an intent - the public docstring says so (overlay.cljs:79-80 "routed back as an ordinary intent - which is what :on-dismiss is") - and every other intent position in hicasso that cannot land REFUSES (require-dispatch, intent.cljs:397-402; event-callback, intent.cljs:586-595); this is the one silent path in the module. (2) Presence and the error boundary already ruled the identical frameless case exactly this way (presence_react.cljs:51-56, boundary.cljs:153-158). (3) rf2-6c12m.11 is cutting the refusal roster from 59 to ~30; a new id (option A) would add vocabulary carrying no information the existing id does not. (4) Degrading to manual/none (option B) silently ignores a line the programmer wrote - "trust the programmer" means report the impossibility, not hide it. (5) Admitting the state (option C) documents a desync and would have the witness pin a defect as a feature. One alternative both reviews left implicit is closed here: routing :on-dismiss through intent/lower-prop (intent.cljs:1212-1228) so the emitter stays in impl.intent was considered and rejected - it changes :on-dismiss's dispatch mechanics (intent-handler's per-key policy, key-maps, placeholders), which is the grammar broadening the Codex review rules out, and the popover would still need its beforetoggle direction filter wrapped around the result. Direct guard it is.

THE MECHANISM (all paths implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/ unless stated).
- impl/overlay.cljs:687-688: body resolves the frame via adapter-context/context-value->current-frame on react/useContext frame-context; with no provider above, the reader answers nil by design (core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs:330).
- :702: dispatch (when frame-kw (collector/frame-dispatch frame-kw)) - nil when frameless.
- :655-656: dismissal-handler [dispatch on-dismiss closed-only?] is (when (and dispatch on-dismiss) (fn ...)) - returns nil when dispatch is nil, silently.
- :741-744 modal-dismissal-attrs and :750-751 popover-dismissal-attrs read PROPS ONLY: :on-dismiss present => closedby="closerequest" (or "any" with :light-dismiss?) / popover="auto". So the element tells the platform "you may dismiss me" while nothing listens.
- :669 own-keys strips :on-dismiss from the props before element-attrs/lowering, and :706 hands it to dismissal-handler directly, so it BYPASSES intent/with-frame (:726) and require-dispatch (intent.cljs:397-402) - the one intent position in the module that skips the loud path. Children's intents inside the overlay do take the loud path.
- :604-631 make-cell: show! (showPopover/showModal) runs ONLY from the once-attached stable ref callback; body (:681-729) has no effect. A re-render therefore does NOT re-show a platform-closed element.

USER-VISIBLE SEQUENCE (popover, :open? true, :on-dismiss written, no frame): 1. mounts, ref callback calls showPopover once on attach, element in the top layer with popover="auto". 2. user clicks outside; platform fires beforetoggle/toggle, nothing listens, panel hides. 3. the flag driving :open? is still true - no intent ran. 4. a re-render does not re-show it (stable ref, no effect). 5. to reopen the author must flip the flag false (element unmounts; hide! is a no-op) then true again - two actions for one open, and any aria-expanded mirrored from the flag lies in between. Modal: same shape with closedby="closerequest" - Escape closes the dialog, no cancel handler runs, flag stays true. This is exactly the two-owners state overlay.cljs:76-83 declares unreachable.

WHEN FRAMELESS ACTUALLY HAPPENS. Every shipped door installs a frame: h/mount! takes {:frame ::frame} (impl/mount.cljs:141); server/render allocates a per-request frame (server.cljs:333); Story wraps every variant in rf/frame-provider (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs:622, 673); a UIx/Reagent island under frame-provider or frame-root reads the same context object (context.cljs:38-40, impl/mount.cljs:33-36). An overlay under an h/defview never reaches this code because the boundary shell refuses :rf.error/no-frame-context first (impl/collector.cljs:1753-1760). So the case is reached only when the overlay is the OUTERMOST hicasso component in a React root nobody wrapped: a test mounting it alone (presence's suite does this via mount/root! with adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel), or a consumer's hand-built root / unwrapped island. Rare, mostly test-time - and it is the case where :open? cannot be an h/sub and :on-dismiss can never land, i.e. an authoring error worth naming. A frameless overlay WITHOUT :on-dismiss is a legitimate case (static manual popover, non-dismissible dialog) and stays legal.

PRECEDENT. presence_react.cljs:51-56: "No frame in scope is not an error here. Presence reads nothing, so a tray mounted outside a frame is legal until one of its children writes an intent - at which point the existing loud error fires and names the intent, which is better attribution than a generic no-frame-context throw from the tray." boundary.cljs:153-158 carries the same paragraph. Witness: test/re_frame/hicasso/presence_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs:327-365 - frameless-root! (mount/root! (mount/fresh-container!) adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel hiccup); testing block 1: quiet frameless tray renders; block 2: a child with :on-click [...] under a boundary with :on-error raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary and (:intent (ex-data e)) equals the vector. overlay_dom_cljs_test.cljs has no frameless row (its manual witness is :652-655, :680-694).

OPTIONS REJECTED.
