B (thread dispatch into the two attrs fns so nil dispatch yields manual/none): one owner, docstring stays true, but the :on-dismiss the author wrote is silently dead - the only swallowed intent in hicasso. C (amend the docstring to say two-owners holds only inside a frame): honest but documents a desync; witness would pin a defect.

THE CHANGE (one guard, shared path, covers modal AND popover).
1. impl/overlay.cljs dismissal-handler (:633-659), called once from body at :706 for both heads while :open? is true: when on-dismiss is non-nil and dispatch is nil, (fail! :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary 're-frame.hicasso.impl.overlay/dismissal-handler "<reason>" :lower-intents-inside-a-boundary-render {:intent on-dismiss}) instead of returning nil. Keep the existing (fn [e] ...) branch untouched. Reason text names what happened and the direct recovery: the overlay carries :on-dismiss <intent> but no frame is in scope, so the platform would be told it may dismiss while nothing could route the dismissal; mount the overlay under a frame (h/mount!, rf/frame-provider, frame-root) or drop :on-dismiss if it should be non-dismissable. fail! is already referred at :108 and the anchor refusal at :218 shows the local call shape; write to fail!'s signature AT TIP (rf2-6c12m.5 may drop :recovery/:where - do not pre-empt it). Reuse the recovery keyword above so R10 of check_complaint_catalogue.py stays green without a new row. Placing the guard in body immediately after :702 is an acceptable equivalent; ONE site only, no dispatch threading through the attrs fns, no new abstraction.
2. Docstring: overlay.cljs:76-83 posture paragraph gains one paragraph modelled on presence_react.cljs:51-56 - no frame in scope is not an error for an overlay; without :on-dismiss it is manual/none and single-owner; WITH :on-dismiss and no frame it refuses at render with the existing intent-outside-boundary, naming the intent, so the two-owners state stays unreachable outside a frame too. Also correct impl/overlay.cljs dismissal-handler's first line ("or nil when there is nothing to route" -> nil when there is no :on-dismiss; the loud refusal when there is one and no frame).
3. docs/core/hicasso/13-overlays-and-focus.md: one Troubleshooting row (table at :344ff): Symptom - an open overlay raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary naming the :on-dismiss intent | Cause - it has :on-dismiss but no frame above it (rendered outside h/mount!, frame-provider, frame-root or Story) | Fix - mount it under a frame, or drop :on-dismiss if it must not be dismissable. title: design(story): deprecate Story's RHS scrubber/trace/actions inspectors in favor of embedded Causa
description:
Story's RHS panel was designed before Causa was a mature devtool. It carries three inspector panels (Scrubber, Trace, Actions) that each duplicate work Causa now does — and does better.

## The duplication

| Story RHS panel | Causa equivalent | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Scrubber (per-variant epoch nav) | Causa ribbon [◀ ▶ ⏭] + L2 event list | Duplicate |
| Trace (event-bus log) | Causa Trace tab (richer filtering, focus, cascade nav) | Duplicate |
| Actions (dispatch + fx log) | Causa Event tab cascade view + filtered Trace | Duplicate |
| Dispatch Console | (none in Causa) | Story-unique; keep |
| Controls (per-variant) | (none in Causa) | Story-unique; keep |
| Play status + viewport + backgrounds | (none in Causa) | Story-unique; keep |

## Strategic move

Delete the three duplicated panels. Mount Causa in the RHS by default (or via a single toolbar toggle). Story becomes purely: variant chrome + interaction surfaces + canvas + Causa.

## Wins
- Removes ~3 panels of duplication
- Eliminates 'RHS shows internals of the panel that IS the inspection view' recursion (the trigger for Mike's observation)
- Causa-side improvements (UC1 Sim, scrubber, machine inspector, panels we haven't built yet) automatically flow into Story
- Forces Causa-quality inspection everywhere by default
- Smaller Story chrome surface; less to maintain

## Concerns / open questions
1. Stories that showcase non-Causa apps (counter, cart) still need an inspector. Causa is now Story-aware (rf2-q9kv5 Causa preset; #1413 viewport awareness) — does it embed cleanly enough to replace the scrubber/trace/actions for those cases?
2. Causa-embedded means TWO Causa instances when showcasing a Causa-panel variant — needs the modal-scoping fix (rf2-om6fa) first
3. Performance: Causa is heavier than the three lightweight Story panels. Lazy-mount?
4. What's the toggle UX — Causa always-on by default? Toolbar button? Keybinding?
5. Migration path for users who pin Story's scrubber/trace/actions in their workflow

## Dependencies
- rf2-om6fa (modal scoping fix) should land first OR be part of this work
- Verify rf2-q9kv5 (Causa preset) handles all the embedding cases

## Acceptance
- Design proposal for the new RHS shape
- Spec proposal for Story's reduced surface
- Migration plan for users on the old shape
close_reason: Shipped via PR #1478 — Causa mounted as Story's RHS; 3 panels deleted (scrubber/trace/actions) ~-3000 LoC; pre-alpha pure delete (no compat shims); trace_buffer.cljs facade extracted for schema-validation dependency. Embedding works through existing [data-rf-causa-host] contract from rf2-q9kv5+rf2-om6fa.

description:
FOUND 2026-09-17 by the §5 METHOD-REREAD LOOP. The band had been re-derived four times this session
and read 88 every time. **The band is right. The bullet that tells you how to read it has gone stale
in the direction that fails OPEN**, which is the half of the merge criterion CLAUDE.md scopes that
trap list to.

## WHAT trap (c) SAYS

> **(c) `All required checks passed` is a REAL JOB — never subtract it from the band, and never
> merge on it alone.** It is `test.yml`'s `all-required-passed` aggregator (`if: ${{ always() }}`,
> `needs:` every gating job in that file), and it presents in the rollup as an ordinary three-second
> CheckRun in workflow `tests`, which is exactly what invites the misreading: it reads like a
> host-generated "everything is green" summary row, so the reflex is to discount it and derive a
> band one LOWER — after which a rollup genuinely one job short reads as at-band and merges.

Definite singular throughout: *the* aggregator, one row, a band *one* lower.

## WHAT THE TREE HAS — THREE, VERIFIED AT SOURCE

Read out of the workflow files themselves, not inferred from rollup names:

    .github/workflows/test.yml         all-required-passed   "All required checks passed"
                                       always()=True   needs: 70 jobs
    .github/workflows/docs.yml         docs-required        "Docs required"
                                       always()=True   needs: 4 jobs
    .github/workflows/lint.yml         lint-required        "Lint required"
                                       always()=True   needs: 6 jobs
    .github/workflows/portability.yml  (none)               6 job keys, no aggregator

All three appear in the rollup as ordinary CheckRuns and all three are COMPLETED/SUCCESS inside the
band of 88 (measured on PR #9918: 88 entries, tests 71 / lint 8 / docs 6 / portability 3, all
`CheckRun`).

## WHY IT MATTERS, AND IT IS THE FAIL-OPEN DIRECTION

The bullet's own described reflex is to discount the summary row. A reader who has internalised it
looks for ONE such row and subtracts it, deriving 87. A reader who notices the pattern and discounts
all the "summary-looking" rows derives **85**. Either way a rollup genuinely short by that many
reads as at-band, which is exactly the failure the bullet exists to prevent, now with three times
the room.

**The arithmetic in the bullet is simply wrong for this tree**: "a band one LOWER" is "three lower".

## A SECOND, SUBTLER STALENESS IN THE SAME BULLET

Its next sentence reads:

> GitHub's `needs:` cannot span workflow files, so the aggregator covers `test.yml` jobs ONLY,
> while `lint`, `docs` and `portability` are separate workflow runs outside it — a green aggregator
> is not a green rollup.

Every clause is TRUE and the conclusion is correct. But it names lint, docs and portability as the
things *outside* the aggregator, which invites the reading that those workflows have no aggregator
of their own — and two of the three now do. The sentence is not wrong; it is no longer a map.

## WHAT IS NOT WRONG, SO THE FIX DOES NOT OVERSHOOT

  * **The principle holds for all three**: each is a real job, none may be subtracted, and none may
    be merged on alone.
  * **The mechanism described for `test.yml`'s is accurate** — `always()`, `needs:` the gating jobs
    in that file, presenting as an ordinary CheckRun.
  * **The cross-file claim is still true**: `needs:` cannot span workflow files, so each aggregator
    covers only its own workflow, and three green aggregators are still not a green rollup.
  * **The band itself is unaffected.** 88, unanimous over 9 PRs merged after the last matrix change,
    qualified by ancestry. Nothing about this changes the number; it changes how a reader is told to
    arrive at it.

## THE LIKELY FIX

Small: make the bullet plural and name the count as measured-at-the-time rather than fixed. Note
that portability has none, so "one per workflow" would itself be a new wrong universal. The safest
shape is the one this file already uses elsewhere — state that the tree currently carries several,
say how to ENUMERATE them rather than how many there are (`always()` + `needs:` at a two-space job
key, or simply: any job whose `needs:` lists other jobs in its own file), and keep the rule as
"never subtract any of them".

**Do NOT add a gate**, and do NOT rewrite the rest of trap (c), whose mechanism and cross-file
reasoning are correct.

## NOT ESTABLISHED

  * **When the docs and lint aggregators landed.** No history was taken, so whether trap (c) was
    correct when written and drifted, or was incomplete from the start, is unknown. It does not
    change the fix.
  * **Whether any merge was ever made on a subtracted band.** Not searched. Every band reading this
    session was taken as a raw total with no subtraction, so no instance is known.
  * Whether `portability` will gain one, which would make any number written down stale again —
    which is the argument for enumerating rather than counting.

The worker reported the duplication at source; it did not trace either key to an off-box wire. description:

- S: a tools/story/package.json (or an equivalent declared list the install page cross-references) naming the closure with the versions the tree pins.
- M: lazy-load the machines canvas so a consumer whose app registers no machines never loads @xyflow/react or elkjs; still declare the remainder.

title: surface-review(impl_epoch): correlate replay results with the actual dispatch across trace callbacks
description:
Correlate replay results with the replayed dispatch's identity, rather than the first epoch committed for its frame while an observation is armed. The current one-call replay API can return another event's retained epoch as its own even when the real replay epoch is retained. This review confirms ONE P3 defect; leave this bead OPEN for that focused repair.

Scope and revision
- Owned slice: impl_epoch, every tracked path under implementation/epoch/** (40 files; exact inventory below).
- Reviewed source revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. Source stayed unchanged throughout this read-only review.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). No worker guard pass, production edits, installs, builds, commits, or pushes claimed. Root owns the tracker checkpoint/push.

Confirmed finding F1 — P3: a trace-listener dispatch steals replay's result epoch

Owned source and causal path:
1. implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:740-758, perform-replay!: arm a frame observation before calling router/dispatch-sync!, consume it in finally, then return the observed epoch if it is still retained.
2. implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:298-327, arm-commit-observation!, take-observed-commit!, note-commit!: the observation records the FIRST commit under the frame id; it carries no target dispatch identity.
3. implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:1934-1941: commit-frame-owner-record! fills that frame-level observation for every committed record.
4. Neighboring execution seam, inspected only: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:4615-4648 emits :rf.event/dispatched before starting its own drain. A public trace callback can synchronously dispatch another event to that frame here, which commits first. This is an allowed callback: implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:809-814 explicitly accounts for trace listeners calling dispatch-sync.

Contract: spec/Tool-Pair.md:170 says the successful :epoch-id is the REPLAYED EVENT's own new epoch, or nil when it is no longer retained. It must never attach another event's causal evidence to the replay result. tool_pair.cljc:722-735 makes the same promise. This is a returned-evidence defect, not a retention-policy or event-execution defect.

Public trigger / standalone reproducer (actual source; plain-atom adapter; no private state mutation or with-redefs required):

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf] '[re-frame.epoch]
         '[re-frame.substrate.adapter :as adapter]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as plain])
(adapter/install-adapter! plain/adapter)
(rf/make-frame {:id :review/frame})
(rf/reg-event :review/add
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ amount]]
    {:db (update db :n (fnil + 0) amount)}))
(rf/reg-event :review/other
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :other true)}))
(rf/dispatch-sync [:review/add 1] {:frame :review/frame})
(def seed-id (:epoch-id (last (rf/epoch-history :review/frame))))
(def fired (atom false))
(rf/register-listener! :trace :review/interleave
  (fn [e]
    (when (and (= :rf.event/dispatched (:operation e))
               (= :review/frame (get-in e [:tags :frame]))
               (compare-and-set! fired false true))
      (rf/dispatch-sync [:review/other] {:frame :review/frame}))))
(def result (rf/replay-epoch! :review/frame seed-id))
(prn result)
(prn (mapv #(select-keys % [:epoch-id :dispatch-id :trigger-event])
           (rf/epoch-history :review/frame)))
```

Actual behavior: the source add is epoch 1, the listener's other event is epoch 2, and the replayed add is epoch 3. The result says :event-id :review/add but :epoch-id 2. Both events did execute correctly; app-db is {:n 2 :other true}. Expected :epoch-id 3, because the actual replay is retained. No ring eviction is involved.

Discriminating controls from the persisted multi-case probe:
- Ordinary replay: source 1, returned 2, actual replay 2, returned trigger [:review/add 1], db {:n 2}.
- Different-handler interleave: source 3, returned 4 with trigger [:review/other], actual replay 5 with trigger [:review/add 1], db {:n 2 :other true}.
- SAME-HANDLER interleave: source 6, returned 7 with trigger [:review/add 100], actual replay 8 with trigger [:review/add 1], db {:n 102}. Thus filtering by :event-id would still return the wrong event. The history carries distinct :dispatch-id values (nested 8, actual replay 7) even though both have the same event keyword.
- Depth 0 empties all three live histories, and re-enabling 50 keeps them empty. This control confirms the older depth-transition defect is not being re-reported.

The different-handler case reproduced identically (returned 4, actual 5). Nothing had changed since the review baseline.

WHAT LANDED. The commit observation no longer takes the FIRST epoch committed for the frame; it correlates on DISPATCH IDENTITY.
  - `trace/deliver!` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc) runs epoch capture as its OWN stage before the public tooling fan-out. So epoch capture sees the armed caller's `:rf.event/dispatched` strictly before any listener body for that event runs — hence strictly before a listener can create a nested dispatch at all. That ordering is unconditional and is what makes the identity exact.
  - epoch/capture.cljc: `capture-event!` reports the first `:rf.event/dispatched` dispatch-id per frame to the armed observation (`note-observed-dispatch!`), ahead of `skip-ops` and every routing branch — it records identity and buffers nothing. A one-map-read no-op when nothing is armed.
  - epoch/state.cljc: `note-commit!` now takes the whole record and fills the slot ONLY from the record carrying the armed dispatch-id. `take-observed-commit!` returns that. The historical first-commit reading survives as `:fallback-epoch-id`, used only when no dispatched emit was captured at all — which is also the posture in which no dispatch ids exist, since both are dev-gated and vanish together.
  - epoch/tool_pair.cljc: `perform-replay!`'s docstring corrected — it claimed the identity came from COMMIT ORDER, which is the defect. The `finally` take and the retained-in-ring check are unchanged, so strict `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx` propagation and observation cleanup are untouched.

NO ROUTER CHANGE, and none is needed. The bead's repair note allowed "a private router/epoch correlation seam if needed"; implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc is untouched, because the capture-before-fan-out ordering already supplies the identity. Two candidate correlations were MEASURED and rejected rather than shipped, and both are worth recording:
  - `:parent-dispatch-id` is nil on BOTH the replay dispatch and the nested one. Handler scope is not bound during the `:event/dispatched` emit, so a dispatch started from a listener on that emit inherits no parent. A parent-equals-ambient filter would have selected both.
  - "the first `:rf.event/dispatched` seen" read off the PUBLIC listener stream is listener-order dependent: if the interleaving listener is registered before the observer, the nested dispatch's event arrives first. Only the capture stage's position ahead of the fan-out makes the ordering unconditional.

Both effects occur (app-db {:n 2 :other true}); the reported epoch is the replayed dispatch's own new record and resolves to `[:review/add 1]`, never the callback's.

title: Stale post-rf2-k97c.3 prose, third site: mount.cljs's open! docstring still claims the installed adapter renders the shell
description:
THIRD SITE OF THE SAME POST-rf2-k97c.3 STALENESS, found while landing rf2-52rj and NOT fixed there
because tools/xray/ was fenced for that dispatch (c4arm-a was live in that tree).

THE SITE. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs, the `open!` docstring, which begins at
line 1010 at trunk f882486af0. It says the verb will "render the shell via the installed substrate
adapter". That is measurably false: mount.cljs carries ZERO adapter/render call sites, and `open!`
reaches `mount-shell-into!` (385) -> `render-shell!` (373) -> `rf.fresco/render!` (382) on
`xray-root`, a `rf.fresco/client-root` handle Xray owns (367).

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN LEAVING. `open!` is the ODD ONE OUT OF THREE in its own file.
Its two siblings already read correctly and both cite the bead that made them so:
  * open-overlay! (1045): "Indifferent to the installed adapter's render shape, same as open!
    (rf2-k97c.4)."
  * popout! (1641): "WHICH adapter that host installed is not consulted (rf2-k97c.4): the pop-out
    paints through xray-popout-root, Xray's own React root in the pop-out's document."
So a reader who reaches open! first gets the stale claim, and open-overlay!'s "same as open!" then
POINTS AT IT - the correct sibling inherits the wrong sentence by reference.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS rf2-zaat, IN A THIRD FILE. rf2-zaat site 2 fixed shell.cljs's ns docstring
(PR #9713); rf2-52rj fixed tools/story/deps.edn's :exclusions rationale (PR #9715). This is the
same sentence-level staleness in mount.cljs itself - the file the other two were describing.

SCOPE. One docstring sentence. The verb's BEHAVIOUR is correct and is not in question; only the
sentence describing who renders. Do not restate rf2-l1jm's open question (whether the embed door
follows the mount verbs onto an owned root) - that is about panels.cljs, not about these verbs,
which moved under rf2-k97c.3 and are settled.

GATE NOTE. mount.cljs is .cljs, so this arms the cljs test surfaces - the same surface rf2-zaat
site 2 armed, where a docstring edit is invisible beyond compilation. Ask
.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh with the PATH rather than assuming.

MEASURED at trunk f882486af0 with the ripgrep-backed search tool, with a live positive control on
the same file (adapter/render 0 against fresco 9), so the zero means absence rather than a broken
instrument.

DONE. Draft PR #9716, branch worker/opendoc-a, one commit (d7be1e3c1c), one file, +2/-2, docstring prose only.

THE DEFECT WAS SHARPER THAN THE BEAD STATED, and the sharper reading is what was fixed. The bead says
`open!`'s docstring "still claims the installed substrate adapter renders the shell". True, but
incomplete: this was ONE DOCSTRING CONTRADICTING ITSELF, eleven lines apart, already citing the bead
that settles the question. At this branch's base (8789d7cf28) the STEP LIST at 1014-1015 said first
call would "render the shell via the installed substrate adapter", while the SAME docstring at
1027-1032 said "WHICH adapter is installed no longer matters (rf2-k97c.4): the shell paints through
Xray's own React root, so an element-shaped host (UIx / Fresco) mounts exactly as a ratom-family one
does." The later paragraph is the authority, is correct, and is UNTOUCHED. Only the step-list clause
moved, to "render the shell through Xray's own React root, mark visible."

The bead cited 1010 for `open!` and gave line numbers at trunk f882486af0; re-derived at this
branch's base, `open!` is still 1010 and the siblings are still 1045 / 1641, but the authority
paragraph is 1027-1032 rather than the 1031-1034 a dispatch brief carried. Line numbers were
re-derived rather than trusted.

PRESENCE IS NOT IDENTITY, and the correction keeps BOTH halves. The over-correction available here
was a clause reading "the adapter is irrelevant", which would have replaced one false sentence with
another in the very file being fixed for false sentences. `open!`'s body still reads
`(when (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter) ...)` at 1040, so the neighbouring sentence "If the
substrate adapter is absent, returns nil so preload retry can wait" is TRUE and survives untouched.
The adapter's PRESENCE still gates the mount; only its IDENTITY stopped selecting the render path.
This is not an invented framing: mount.cljs already says so twice in its own words, at its ns
docstring (line 19, "the mount verbs read `current-adapter` only to") and at line 260
("`current-adapter` only as a PRESENCE check - the map, never `:kind`"). The replacement clause
agrees with the file.

THE SIBLING-BY-REFERENCE ARGUMENT, which is the strongest reason this was worth fixing rather than
leaving. `open-overlay!` (1045) reads "Indifferent to the installed adapter's render shape, same as
`open!` (rf2-k97c.4)". So while `open!` read wrongly, the CORRECT sibling inherited the wrong
sentence by pointing at it. `popout!` (1641) was already right on both halves - it returns
`{:ok? false :reason :no-substrate-adapter}` when no host has booted AND says "WHICH adapter that
host installed is not consulted (rf2-k97c.4)" - and served as the worked example of getting the
presence/identity split right in one docstring.

mount.cljs carries ZERO `adapter/render` call sites (exit 1), against a live positive control on the

-> `rf.fresco/render!` (382), where `xray-root` (367) is a `rf.fresco/client-root` handle Xray owns.

title: docs: dehistoricalise TESTING.md — it states how each gate came to be, not what is true now
description:
OPERATOR REQUEST (Mike, 2026-09-11): dehistoricalise `/TESTING.md`.

`TESTING.md` is the canonical test-matrix document — the page that answers "which gate covers this
surface, and what does it prove?". It has accreted a large amount of CHANGE NARRATIVE that answers a
different question: how each gate came to be what it is.

## MEASURED AT TRUNK, BEFORE FILING

  357 lines
  73  `rf2-` bead references
  23  dated statements (`20NN-NN-NN`)
  17  lines carrying `previously` / `used to` / `no longer` / `formerly` / `has since`

Single table cells run to several hundred words, much of it retrospective. Representative, and the
clearest statement of the problem in the file's own words:

  * one cell: "**FREEZE — RETIRED 2026-08-29 (rf2-6c12m.1).** What follows is the record of the gate
    that used to open this chain ... **nothing below runs any more**" — followed by a long account of
    a retired gate's design.
  * another: "**The two Freehand release-bundle probes that used to sit here retired with their
    artefact**", then a paragraph on how they worked.
  * another: "This row twice said 'three' while the chain ran four and then five".

## THE GOAL

Make the page state WHAT IS TRUE NOW. A reader should be able to answer "what covers this surface?"
without reading the history of what used to.

## WHAT TO KEEP — THIS IS NOT A DELETE-ALL-HISTORY PASS

Three classes of retrospective text EARN their place and must survive:

1. **A hole a gate exists to close, where the account is what stops someone removing it.** E.g. the
   perf-bundle row explains that the gate ran NOWHERE until rf2-eegpw while the spec claimed it was
   enforced — that is a live argument for the gate, not history.
2. **A measured trap or a hollow-gate account** that would otherwise be rediscovered. E.g. the freeze
   gate hashing donors while only checking the package path EXISTED, so a changed value passed — the
   lesson generalises even though the gate is gone.
3. **"Read the live roster from X, not from this paragraph"** instructions. These are the file's own
   defence against staleness and are the most valuable sentences in it. KEEP EVERY ONE.

## WHAT TO REMOVE OR COMPRESS

* Accounts of RETIRED gates written as though narrating their retirement. If a retired gate taught
  something (class 2 above), keep the LESSON in one or two sentences and drop the mechanism.
* Bead ids used as narrative punctuation. A bead id justifying a current rule is fine; a chain of
  them recording who changed what when is not.
* Dated statements that are not themselves the claim. "As of 2026-08-30 the chain is X" should become
  "the chain is X" — with the existing pointer to the executable roster doing the freshness work.
* Self-referential corrections ("this row twice said three while the chain ran five"). Fix the row;
  the correction's provenance belongs in git.

## THE RULE OF THUMB

If a sentence would still be worth reading by someone who had never heard of the change it
describes, keep it. If it only makes sense as a diff against a previous version of this file, it
belongs in git history, which already has it.

## SCOPE

`TESTING.md` only. **Change no gate, no script, no workflow, and no other document.** This is a prose
pass.

If while reading you find a row that is FACTUALLY WRONG about a current gate — as opposed to merely
historical — do not quietly fix it: RECORD IT SEPARATELY in your report. A stale factual claim in the
test matrix is a different and more serious defect than verbosity, and I want it visible rather than
folded into a tidy-up.

## GATE

`scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` covers repo-root markdown including `TESTING.md` (the docs-slug
gate does NOT — its roots are `docs/`, `spec/`, `skills/`, `migration/`, `tools/*/spec`). Neither
gate validates prose, tables, or rendering, and neither looks inside a fenced code block. So verify
link targets and TABLE COLUMN COUNTS by hand and say so in the PR body — this file is mostly tables,
and a dropped `|` is exactly the damage a large prose edit causes.
notes:
FENCE-STATE: 2026-09-11 17:24 AUSEST — DISPATCHED, DO NOT DISPATCH AGAIN.

Dispatched to testmd-a at 2026-09-11 17:02:57 AUSEST, worktree
`C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/testmd-a`, branch `worker/testmd-a`, PR #9674 open as a draft.

This bead carried ZERO notes while a worker was live on it, which is how a dispatched item reads as
free. Recording it here so a scan finds it.

SCOPE AS BRIEFED: `TESTING.md` only — no gate, no script, no workflow, no other document. The worker
was told that three classes of retrospective text EARN their place and must survive: an account of the
hole a gate exists to close, a measured trap or hollow-gate account that would otherwise be
rediscovered, and every "read the live roster from X, not from this paragraph" instruction.

IF IT DOES NOT LAND: `TESTING.md` keeps answering "how did each gate come to be" where a reader needs
"what covers this surface now" — 357 lines, 73 bead references, 23 dated statements at trunk, figures
the worker was told to re-run and report as a delta rather than trust.

ONE THING TO WATCH ON THE WAY BACK IN: the worker was asked to report separately any row that is
FACTUALLY WRONG about a current gate, rather than folding it into the tidy-up. A stale factual claim in
the test matrix is a different and more serious defect than verbosity.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON PR #9674, merged into a70b04c422. One file, +93/-130 — a net subtraction, which is what this
pass should look like. 357 lines -> 320; 73 bead-reference lines -> 52; 23 dated statements -> 0;
112,583 bytes -> 81,179.

=== THE CENSUS CLAIMS WERE RE-RUN AND ALL BUT ONE REPRODUCED EXACTLY ===

The file had not moved since `8b17cc53d5`, two days before filing, so tip equalled filing. Lines 357,
bead references 73 and dated statements 23 all reproduced to the digit. The fourth —
previously/used-to/no-longer/formerly/has-since — read 14 lines / 18 occurrences against the recorded
17, and since the file had not changed that is an INSTRUMENT difference rather than staleness. Worth
recording as the shape rather than the number: a count written without its instrument cannot be
re-derived, only approximated.

=== THREE FACTUAL DEFECTS, REPORTED SEPARATELY AS ASKED RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO THE TIDY-UP ===

1. A RETIRED GATE NAMED IN THE PRESENT TENSE. The `cljs_browser` row said `cljs_node_test` is "the
   only one scheduling the package smoke and the freeze gate". The freeze gate retired under
   rf2-6c12m.1 and neither `check_freeze.py` nor `frozen-sources.edn` is tracked. Corrected to the
   invariants gate. This is the more serious class the bead asked to have surfaced — a stale factual
   claim in the test matrix, not verbosity.

2. A STALE COUNT. `implementation_jvm` claimed "57 of the 60 tracked `spec/**.md`". There are 51 (50
   top-level plus `spec/conformance/README.md`), two instruments agreeing against a 1,003-file control.
   The count was DROPPED rather than re-derived, which is the right repair: the row already ends with
   "measure a path with the script rather than trust this paragraph", so a fresh number would just be
   the next thing to go stale.

3. A verbatim duplicated sentence in the `cljs_node_test` row.

=== THE WORKER CAUGHT ITS OWN NEAR-MISS, AND THE METHOD IS THE POINT ===

A token-level audit of the merge-base diff — every npm script, job name, classifier output, gate script
and repo path present before and absent after — caught its own first pass carrying out two LIVE names:
`cljs-schemas-bundle` (a required job) and `test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly` (still defined). Both restored.
Every other vanished token belonged to a retired artefact. A subtractive pass over a reference document
needs exactly that audit; a diff review would not have found it, because removing a live name looks
identical to removing a dead one.

=== HAND VERIFICATION, SINCE NO GATE GRADES ANY OF THIS ===

All 7 surviving tables clean, 0 column-count problems, each keeping its exact data-row count
(23/5/10/28/2/11/4 before and after); only the 4-row Freehand stage table was removed, deliberately.
All 7 links resolve including the in-page anchor. The one lost link was inside the deleted section, and
nothing in the tree links to a repo-root `TESTING.md` anchor, so renaming the heading stranded nothing.
Line endings finish CR 320 == CRLF 320, zero bare LF — the check CLAUDE.md prescribes for this file.

The gate control was run FIRST, before any green was trusted: one planted broken target took
`check_readme_links.py --ci` to exit 1 naming `TESTING.md:120`; restore verified by hash. `TESTING.md`
wants the DEFAULT `git hash-object` form and `--no-filters` did not match it — another instance of that
being a per-file fact.

=== WHAT THIS PASS REMOVED THAT SHOULD COME BACK — FILED AS ITS OWN ITEM ===

Three live gates — `check_doc_slugs.py`, `check_readme_links.py` and `check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py`
— had their only mentions inside the retired narrative, so they are now unnamed in the canonical
test-matrix document. The worker correctly declined to add rows, since that would widen a subtractive
pass into an additive one. Filed separately.

title: docs: two-space CONTINUATION blocks escape their list item entirely, and they block 4 sites rf2-3bq6 could not repair
description:
A NEIGHBOURING DEFECT OF THE SAME ROOT CAUSE, found while fixing rf2-3bq6, and it is strictly worse than the one that bead is about. Python-Markdown's four-column rule governs CONTINUATION content as well as child items. A paragraph indented two spaces under `- parent` has NOT merely lost a level - it has left the list item altogether and renders AFTER the closing tag. MEASURED, on this repo's toolchain, with the extension set mkdocs.yml produces: - item text continuation paragraph (two spaces) renders as
  • item text

continuation paragraph

while the same paragraph at FOUR spaces renders as

  • item text

    continuation paragraph

Three spaces behaves like two. The threshold is the same four columns. === WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY A WIDER SWEEP OF rf2-3bq6 === Fixing it MOVES PROSE INTO A LIST ITEM. That is a real change to the document's structure rather than the pure list reindent rf2-3bq6 is scoped to, so it wants its own decision rather than being folded in. It also makes the rendered diff larger in a way the list reindent's invariants deliberately refuse. === AND IT BLOCKS FOUR SITES THAT rf2-3bq6 COULD NOT REPAIR === Where such an escaped paragraph sits BETWEEN two sibling lists, repairing only the second list puts a four-space-indented list under a TOP-LEVEL paragraph - which is an indented CODE BLOCK. Measured on docs/api/re-frame.routing.md: the naive repair turns - is not a map, - carries `:path` (the path pattern belongs in the third slot), or into a code block with the backticks shown literally. Strictly worse than the flattening it was meant to cure, so rf2-3bq6 left those blocks alone. The four sites still standing after rf2-3bq6's docs/ half, one block each: docs/api/re-frame.core.md line 872 docs/api/re-frame.resources.md line 611 docs/api/re-frame.routing.md line 33 docs/EP/EP-0017-recordable-coeffects.md line 508 (file untouched) Each is repairable by ALSO moving the escaped continuation paragraph to the item's content column. Verified on a reduced sample: moving both the child items and the continuation gives the fully correct nesting with no code block. === SCOPE NOT YET MEASURED === The population of escaped continuation paragraphs across docs/, spec/ and migration/ has NOT been counted - the instrument built for rf2-3bq6 detects flattened list ITEMS and does not look at continuation blocks. Counting them is the first task here, and the same rendering method extends to it: a continuation line is defective when the block it belongs to renders outside the `li` its author indented it under.

title: CLAUDE.md: catalogue that gh reports status/conclusion UPPERCASE on statusCheckRollup and lowercase on run list, and one mismatch fails open
description:
`gh` REPORTS THE SAME TWO FIELDS IN TWO DIFFERENT CASES ON TWO SURFACES THE MERGE CRITERION
READS TOGETHER, and one of the two mismatched filters FAILS OPEN — it selects nothing and
reports a clean PR.

DELIVERABLE: a new instrument-catalogue item in CLAUDE.md's `## Workflow` section, in the
lettered list that currently runs (a)-(p). Nothing else.

=== MEASURED BY THE MAYOR, 2026-09-10, ON PR #9597 AT HEAD 08bd0d4fb3 (fact) ===

  gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup   ->  status=COMPLETED  conclusion=SUCCESS|SKIPPED
  gh run list --commit <oid> --json status,conclusion
                                           ->  status=completed  conclusion=success

Distinct values actually returned on that PR:

    ROLLUP    53x  status=COMPLETED  conclusion=SKIPPED
              34x  status=COMPLETED  conclusion=SUCCESS
    RUN LIST   4x  status=completed  conclusion=success

**THE MERGE CRITERION READS BOTH.** Clauses 1-3 come off the ROLLUP; clause 4 — "every
workflow run at the current head is COMPLETED" — comes off the RUN LIST. So a mayor writes
both filters in one tick, and the natural thing is to reuse the spelling that just worked.

=== BOTH DIRECTIONS MEASURED, AND THEY FAIL OPPOSITE WAYS ===

  UPPERCASE filter over the RUN LIST:
      [.[] | select(.status != "COMPLETED")] | length   ->  4   of 4
  Every healthy completed run is selected. **Fails CLOSED** — it blocks a merge that should
  proceed. Noisy, self-correcting, and this is how the defect was found.

  lowercase filter over the ROLLUP:
      [.statusCheckRollup[] | select(.status == "completed" and (.conclusion != "success"))] | length   ->  0
  The status conjunct is NEVER TRUE, so the filter selects NOTHING and reports **zero
  failures**. **Fails OPEN.** On a PR carrying real failures it returns the same 0.

  Correct, each in its own case:
      rollup   notpassed      = 0
      run list not_completed  = 0

**THE FAIL-OPEN FORM IS THE ONE A CAREFUL READER ARRIVES AT.** Having just learned that
`gh run list` speaks lowercase, reusing that spelling on the rollup is the obvious move —
and it produces a well-formed, plausible, reassuring zero on exactly the question the merge
criterion asks. Exit 0, no stderr, no warning.

=== IT IS THE SAME FAMILY AS ITEM (p), THROUGH A DIFFERENT DOOR ===

(p) records that `statusCheckRollup` reports a running check with `conclusion: ""` — an
empty string, not null — so a null-guarded filter counts every in-flight check as a
failure. Both are "the obvious `gh` JSON filter is wrong about a field's VALUE, silently".
**Say so in the new item and cross-reference (p)**; a reader who has internalised (p) is
already primed for the class and needs one sentence, not a re-derivation.

=== THE GUARD, TWO PARTS ===

  1. **Take the case from the surface you are querying, never from the surface next to it.**
     `statusCheckRollup` is UPPERCASE; `gh run list` is lowercase.
  2. **Case-fold before comparing, so neither spelling can be wrong**: `(.status|ascii_downcase)`
     and `(.conclusion // "" | ascii_downcase)`. This is the recommendation to lead with,
     because it removes the class rather than asking the reader to remember which surface
     is which — and it composes with (p)'s empty-string guard in the same expression.

Verify the fold works on BOTH surfaces before writing it down; the mayor did not, and this
item should not assert what it has not measured.

=== SCOPE, AND ONE WARNING SPECIFIC TO THIS FILE ===

CLAUDE.md ONLY. Do not add a script, do not add a gate, do not touch the loops doc.

**The lettered list's own opening sentence warns that a COUNT in it goes stale first, and it
has been wrong before** — it carried the word FIVE while there were six. Add a letter; do
NOT add or update any count of how many letters there are, and check the surrounding prose
does not carry one you would be invalidating.

**AND THE CRLF TRAP IN ITEM (e) IS ABOUT EDITING THIS EXACT FILE.** Writing that entry
inserted four REAL carriage returns where an escape was meant literally; git reclassified
`CLAUDE.md` from `w/crlf` to `w/-text`, stopped normalising it, and staged 156 changed lines
for a one-clause edit. **After editing, check that the total CR count equals the CRLF count
and that `git diff --stat` shows the number of lines you actually changed.** Report both
numbers and the `git check-attr text -- CLAUDE.md` result in the PR body. Your entry quotes
`jq` expressions, so this is live for you rather than boilerplate.

GATES: `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` owns repo-root markdown, CLAUDE.md included —
`check_doc_slugs.py` does NOT (its roots are `docs/`, `spec/`, `skills/`, `migration/`,
`tools/*/spec`, and it exits 0 on a broken link outside them). Both run in `test.yml`'s
`verify-readme-links` job. Nominate by PATH, not by job name. `mkdocs build --strict` does
NOT cover CLAUDE.md at all — `docs_dir` is `docs`, and repo-root markdown was never a
candidate. Do not nominate it.

Plus the attribution guard, which reads BOTH your commits and the PR BODY, and which has
gone red on prose that merely NAMES the trailers. A whole-line trailer at column 0 offends;
indent by one space to quote one on purpose.

SABOTAGE: plant a broken link target on a line you added, show `check_readme_links.py --ci`
going red naming file and target, restore, verify by BLOB hash with `--no-filters`.

title: method: a browser lane chained behind a failed compile serves the PREVIOUS bundle and returns green
description:

GREEN OVER A TREE THAT DID NOT COMPILE.** It fails OPEN, which is the property that makes it worth a bead
rather than a footnote.

WHAT HAPPENED. An intermediate compile failed — a missing paren. The browser run chained behind it did not
fail, and did not refuse: **it served the PREVIOUS BUNDLE**, ran 885 tests, produced entirely plausible
readings, and returned its own exit code. Nothing in the browser run's output said the code under test was
stale. The only thing that betrayed it was the COMPILE's separately captured exit status.

WHY THE ESTABLISHED GUARD DOES NOT CATCH IT, and this is the part that matters. Every brief this project
sends already says: capture the runner's OWN exit code, unpiped, from the run's own artefact — never a
pipeline's status and never a number something else reported about the run. That rule is correct and it is
NOT sufficient here, because the browser runner's own exit code is HONESTLY ZERO. It ran, the tests it ran
passed, and it is not the component that knows the bundle is stale. Capturing more carefully cannot help; the
number being captured is the wrong number.

**THE GUARD IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE: GATE THE BROWSER STEP ON THE COMPILE'S CAPTURED EXIT, rather than chaining
the two and reading the second.** The worker adopted exactly this for its later runs, which is how the rest
of its evidence stands up.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY WRONG. It fails in the reassuring direction for the one question a
gate is asked, and it is INTERMITTENTLY invisible: a stale bundle only differs from a fresh one where the
edit mattered, so a run that exercises unrelated rows passes identically either way. And the test COUNT moves
plausibly with a stale bundle (885 here), so a reader watching counts for reassurance gets it.

title: CLAUDE.md: the Bash tool strips backslashes inside a QUOTED heredoc, defeating the catalogue's own guard
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 by the rf2-6plj worker. Belongs in CLAUDE.md's "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport on this
machine" catalogue, whose own opening states that its letters are labels rather than a census and that it
grows.

THE HAZARD. The Bash tool STRIPS BACKSLASHES even inside a QUOTED heredoc (`<<'EOF'`), which is precisely the
construct the catalogue already prescribes as the guard against the backtick-substitution trap. Measured: a
Python `'\\'` arrived as `'\'`, and a JavaScript `/\\/g` arrived as `/\/g`. Both are fatal to the code that
receives them — one is a syntax error, the other silently changes what the regex matches.

WHY IT BELONGS BESIDE THE BACKTICK ENTRY RATHER THAN BURIED IN IT. It is the same class through a different
door: content that is correct in the source arrives damaged at the callee, with the shell reporting success.
But the existing entry's REMEDY is the quoted heredoc, and this hazard defeats that remedy — so an author
following the catalogue's own advice meets it. That makes it a qualification the catalogue currently lacks,
not merely another instance.

WHICH DIRECTION IT FAILS IN, and both are bad in different ways. A stripped backslash in Python is usually a
LOUD failure (SyntaxError, or an obviously wrong string). A stripped backslash in a REGEX is SILENT: `/\\/g`
becomes `/\/g`, which is still a valid pattern and matches something else. So the same defect is
self-announcing in one language and invisible in the next, and a reader who met the loud form will not expect
the quiet one.

THE GUARD: write the file with the Write tool rather than through a heredoc whenever the content contains
backslashes, and verify by reading a distinctive backslash-bearing line back out of the written file before
running it. The catalogue's standing rule applies here too — verify by EFFECT, not by the writer's exit code,
which is 0 either way.

CONTEXT WORTH ONE LINE: this session hit two unexplained heredoc parse failures from the mayor's own side,
resolved at the time by switching to the Write tool without diagnosing them. This is the likeliest
explanation and was not established for those two cases; record the measured hazard, not the retro-fit.

SCOPE: a CLAUDE.md catalogue edit and nothing else. Keep the established entry shape — what the instrument
did, the measurement in both directions, which direction it fails in, and the guard. Do not renumber, do not
add a count, and do not build a wrapper or a check script: the catalogue is the artefact.

THE EDITING TRAP FOR THIS FILE, which has bitten twice: an entry that MENTIONS carriage returns has
previously inserted REAL ones, git reclassified CLAUDE.md from `w/crlf` to `w/-text`, and 156 lines staged for
a one-clause edit. After editing, check the total CR count equals the CRLF count and that the diff is the
size you expect. The last worker to edit this catalogue avoided it by construction — quoted heredocs verified
at 0 CR bytes, spliced in binary mode — which is worth copying, ALLOWING FOR the fact that this very entry
says the heredoc is unsafe for backslashes.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON PR #9589, merged as 6e5c84aa21. CLAUDE.md catalogue item (o), one line changed.

THE FINDING AS FILED WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE PLACE AND WRONG IN THREE DETAILS, AND THE CORRECTIONS ARE THE
VALUABLE PART — each makes the entry reproduce where the bead's version would not.

1. IT HALVES RUNS; IT DOES NOT STRIP. `\` arrives as `\`, `\\` as `\`, `\\\` as `\\`, `\\\\` as `\\`, eight
   as four. A lone backslash before an ordinary character (`\t`, `\d`, `\"`, `\$`) is UNTOUCHED. That
   selectivity is the whole reason it hides: nearly every backslash in an ordinary script survives, and only
   the doubled ones move — which are exactly the ones that mean A LITERAL BACKSLASH.

2. THE SHELL IS EXONERATED, AND THAT CHANGES THE REMEDY. The identical quoted heredoc, placed inside a script
   written to disk and then run, preserves all 11 of its backslashes. So the damage is done to the COMMAND
   TEXT before any shell sees it, no shell setting reaches it, and quoting harder cannot help. The remedy is
   to move the content OUT of the command.

3. THE BEAD'S "SILENT" EXAMPLE IS ACTUALLY LOUD. `/\\/g` arriving as `/\/g` is a SyntaxError (`missing ) after
   argument list`, exit 1) — the surviving `\/` escapes the regex's own closing delimiter and swallows it. The
   silent register is real but needs the backslash away from the delimiter: `/a\\b/` becomes `/a\b/` (a WORD
   BOUNDARY), `/\\d/` becomes `/\d/` (a DIGIT), `"C:\\Users\\dev"` becomes `"C:\Users\dev"` which evaluates to
   `C:Usersdev`. All three ran to completion in one file: exit 0, nothing on stderr, three wrong answers.
   **So the loud and the quiet form arise from THE SAME CONSTRUCT IN THE SAME LANGUAGE** — a sharper statement
   than the bead's Python-loud/JS-silent split, and the one that reproduces. Meeting the loud form teaches you
   nothing about the quiet one.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERED ENOUGH TO CATALOGUE RATHER THAN NOTE: the quoted heredoc is the construct CLAUDE.md
ALREADY PRESCRIBES as the guard against the backtick command-substitution trap. So an author following the
catalogue's own advice walks into this. The two are a PAIR and neither guard covers both — build the file with
the Write tool, THEN pass it as `"$(cat <file>)"`.

TWO INSTRUMENT FACTS RECORDED IN PASSING, both measured here:
  * `grep -c $'\r$'` reads 0 on CLAUDE.md against 156 real CR bytes — MSYS grep strips the CR before matching,
    so it is not a usable CRLF counter on this box.
  * The known CLAUDE.md editing trap (an entry MENTIONING carriage returns inserting real ones, flipping the
    file to `w/-text` and staging 156 lines for a one-clause edit) was avoided by construction, and the extra
    wrinkle is that THIS entry makes the usual heredoc remedy unsafe. The text was written with a file-writing
    tool (45 backslashes in, 45 out) and spliced in BINARY MODE by a script that refuses to write unless the
    CR and LF counts are unchanged. After the edit and again after the rebase: CR=156 LF=156 CRLF=156
    lone_CR=0, classification still `i/lf w/crlf`, `git diff --stat` 1 insertion 1 deletion.

GATES: eight `check_*.py` and `check-*.sh` at exit 0, each captured to its own file and read back, all re-run
after the rebase. Gates nominated BY PATH, not by job name — `check_readme_links.py` owns repo-root markdown,
which is CLAUDE.md's gate; `check_doc_slugs.py` runs in the same job and does NOT cover it.

SABOTAGE, and it doubles as the discrimination that no link gate prints its own root: committed first, then
planted a broken anchor on the very line being edited. `check_readme_links.py --ci` exit 1 naming
`CLAUDE.md:119`; `check_doc_slugs.py` exit 0 and SILENT on the same tree, confirming the roots claim by
measurement. Restored and verified by BLOB hash against the committed object — fa97a43f63 before and after,
with 5b7510bb in between proving the plant genuinely applied rather than silently no-opping.

title: docs(core): decide whether the three-line v = f(s) layering salvaged from the 2026-07-17 pairing draft belongs in the render-phase teaching
description:
Salvaged from the `pairing-2026-07-17` triage under rf2-cu38 (2026-09-09). That directory holds three
markdown files whose blobs are absent from the object store; all three are EARLIER drafts of
`docs/core/{introduction,hiccup,events}.md` and are superseded at tip. Measured, normalised word-level
against tip: hiccup 94.4% matched (its only unique run of >=6 words is a Ctrl-Enter instruction tip
already carries elsewhere), introduction 25.7% (pairing 653 words against tip's 1194, and the pairing
side is the rougher one - `excitment`, `vies`, a mistyped `[]:div ...]`, and a truncated closing
section that only repeats a code block), events 8.2% (genuinely different, but the tip page was
RE-SCOPED to be the language of the pipeline with the pipeline walk moved into introduction.md, and
the pairing side carries an empty `## Phase 2 - The COmmit Phase` heading plus `anonomous`, `enques`,
`the users presses`).

ONE FRAGMENT IN IT IS NOT IN THE TRACKED TREE, which is the whole of this bead. The pairing
events.md draft layers React's `v = f(s)` into three lines:

    view-model = subscribe(app-db)  ;; derive a projection of state suitable for use in a view
    vdom       = views(view-model)  ;; render a data representation of DOM (hiccup)
    dom        = reconcile(vdom)    ;; React does this part

Measured over the tracked tree: `v = f(s)` appears once, in README.md section 2 ("Views are derivative,
not causal"), where it is used rhetorically rather than decomposed; `reconcile(vdom)` and
`view-model = subscribe` appear NOWHERE under docs/ or spec/ (the term "view-model" is common, the
layering is not). So the decomposition itself is unpublished.

THE QUESTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: does the render-phase teaching in `docs/core/` want that
three-line ladder - it names exactly where reg-sub and reg-view each sit, and where React's job
starts - or is it redundant beside what introduction.md's pipeline walk already says? A judgement
call about teaching prose, not a defect. Small either way.

The three source files are recorded here because the directory they live in is RECOMMENDED FOR
RELEASE under rf2-cu38 and will not survive it; nothing else in it is worth keeping. Do not go
looking for the directory.
notes:
## VERDICT (2026-09-09): DECLINE. No PR opened, no file changed.

The three-line ladder is redundant beside the tracked render-phase teaching, and two of the
three things the case-for claims it uniquely supplies are already in `docs/core/` verbatim,
while the third would be a small REGRESSION against a deliberate abstraction. Detail below so
nobody re-derives this.

### Premises re-verified at source (own controls, three axes)

Instrument: fixed-string census over `git ls-files` (4920 files, `.beads/` excluded), run three
ways per needle - line-oriented, whole-file whitespace-collapsed, and comment-markers-stripped
then collapsed. Positive control `app-db` read 1878 files / 14566 line-hits / 16132 collapsed;
negative control `zzqqxx-not-present-anywhere` read 0 on all three axes. The collapse axes are
not decorative: `reconcile` reads 1567 line-oriented against 1619 collapsed, so they reach 52
matches the line-oriented axis cannot see.

* CONFIRMED. `v = f(s)` appears exactly ONCE in the tracked tree, `README.md` line 33, in
  section 2 "Views are derivative, not causal", used rhetorically: "Back in 2014, React embraced
  `v = f(s)` and it was beautiful." Identical count on all three axes.
* CONFIRMED. `reconcile(vdom)` = 0 and `view-model = subscribe` = 0 across the whole tracked
  tree on all three axes. Also probed and 0: `vdom = views`, `dom = reconcile`. The layering is
  genuinely unpublished.
* REFINED, and the refinement CUTS AGAINST adding it. The filer's note that the term
  "view-model" is common is true TREE-WIDE (128 line-hits / 59 files) but FALSE in the scope
  this bead is about. In `docs/core/` the token `view-model` appears exactly ONCE, in
  `docs/core/hicasso/glossary.md`, and there it means a list-read GRANULARITY choice -
  "Coarse | One view-model represents the collection" - not "the projection a subscription
  produces". The spaced form "view model" appears 4 times, all in `docs/core/hicasso/`, in a
  THIRD sense: "the Hicasso view model" (`docs/core/hicasso/index.md`). So the core teaching
  pages do not carry the term at all, and importing it would put a third sense of the word into
  the same doc tree.
* NEW, not in the brief. `vdom` appears ZERO times in `docs/core/` (0 on all three axes);
  `VDOM` likewise 0 there, living only in `spec/` and `skills/`. `virtual DOM` and `virtual-dom`
  are 0 tree-wide. And `v = f(s)` is 0 in `docs/core/`. So the ladder's premise formula is
  absent from the tree it would join, and it would import two unglossed tokens into pages whose
  glossary keeps explicit headword discipline (`docs/core/glossary.md` rules its own vocabulary:
  "Casual 'sub' is fine; not as a headword"; "Use 'component' only in React-analogy callouts").
  The case-for's "no new concepts" does not survive measurement.

### Where each of the three lines is already taught, quoted with file and heading

LINE 1 - `view-model = subscribe(app-db)  ;; derive a projection of state suitable for use in a view`

* `docs/core/subscriptions.md`, heading "What Is a Subscription, Exactly?": "A function from
  app-db to a value some view wants, registered under a name". That is line 1 in prose,
  including its `app-db` argument.
* `docs/core/glossary.md`, headword "derive": "Fifth stage; first of the render phase: recompute
  subscriptions (and the derivation graph) that watch changed parts of committed app-db."
* `docs/core/glossary.md`, headword "subscription": "A named, registered, pure, cached
  derivation of state - how a view reads what it needs."
* `docs/core/views.md`, heading "Rendering reads; interaction dispatches": "A view is a
  derivative projection: it turns state into hiccup". The ladder's own comment word,
  "projection", is already the tree's word for this.
* `docs/core/introduction.md`, heading "The event pipeline in one pass", step 6: "Render phase.
  Subscriptions whose inputs changed recompute."

LINE 2 - `vdom = views(view-model)  ;; render a data representation of DOM (hiccup)`

* `docs/core/views.md`, pull-quote under heading "Views: pure functions of data": "A view is a
  pure function from subscription values to hiccup." One sentence, and it carries lines 1 and 2
  jointly.
* `docs/core/glossary.md`, headword "view": "A pure render function from subscription values to
  hiccup."
* `docs/core/hiccup.md`, opening pull-quote: "Hiccup is HTML as data: a vector per element, a
  map for attributes, strings for text."
* `docs/core/glossary.md`, headword "hiccup": "Clojure data for UI ... Markup as data; a view
  composes it".
* `docs/core/introduction.md`, step 6: "Views that depend on those values re-render."

LINE 3 - `dom = reconcile(vdom)  ;; React does this part`

* `docs/core/introduction.md`, step 6: "React reconciles the DOM." Word for word the ladder's
  third line, comment included.
* `docs/core/glossary.md`, headword "render": "Sixth stage: views that deref a changed
  subscription re-run, produce fresh hiccup; the substrate patches the DOM that moved."
* `docs/core/glossary.md`, headword "hiccup": "the substrate turns it into React elements (or a
  server string)."

AND THE LADDER AS A WHOLE, three separate times, each in the surrounding page's own voice:

* `docs/core/introduction.md`, heading "The event pipeline in one pass":
  click -> dispatch -> queue -> handler -> {:db ...} -> commit -> subs -> views -> DOM.
  The tail "subs -> views -> DOM" IS the ladder.
* `docs/core/views.md`, heading "The pure pipeline is complete":
  intent (event) -> one map (app-db) -> named conclusions (subs) -> screen (view).
* `docs/core/explanation/inside-out.md`, heading "Why your architecture shouldn't be Turing
  complete": "Every event flows through the same invariant sequence - dispatch -> event handler
  -> effects -> derivations -> view -> DOM."

### The two reasons this is a decline rather than a coin-toss

1. THE THIRD LINE WOULD BE LESS ACCURATE THAN THE PROSE IT SAT BESIDE. `;; React does this part`
   hard-codes React. The tree deliberately routes that step through "substrate" instead, because
   the same views render through three substrates and to a server string with no React present:
   `docs/core/glossary.md` headword "substrate" - "The React-family rendering layer - Reagent,
   UIx, or reagent-slim ... Core is substrate-agnostic"; and `docs/core/views.md` under "Hiccup:
   the screen is data" - "A pure function that walks hiccup and emits an HTML string can run on
   the server - which is how server-side rendering renders the same views without a browser in
   the building." Introduction's step 6 can say "React reconciles the DOM" because it is a
   first-pass narrative naming the common case; a standing pseudo-code ladder asserting it as
   the definition would contradict the glossary a reader meets two pages later.

2. THERE IS NO HOME FOR IT THAT IS NOT ALREADY OCCUPIED. Checked every candidate.
   `introduction.md` already closes its summary with the tree's one pseudo-equation,

title: CLAUDE.md instrument list: MSYS rewrites a leading-slash Windows FLAG into a path, so a piped schtasks check reads EMPTY while the tasks exist
description:
Found 2026-09-08 by the mayor while verifying rf2-fmst's git maintenance registration. This is a NEW labelled item for CLAUDE.md's "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport on this machine" list, which that section says explicitly is a growing census rather than a fixed set.

THE DEFECT: from Git Bash on this box, MSYS rewrites a leading-slash WINDOWS-STYLE FLAG into a path. `schtasks /query /fo LIST` is executed as `schtasks 'C:/Program Files/Git/query' /fo LIST`. schtasks refuses it with `ERROR: Invalid argument/option - 'C:/Program Files/Git/query'` and exits 1, writing nothing to stdout.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY WRONG: the natural idiom suppresses the only evidence. Piped as `schtasks /query /fo LIST 2>/dev/null | grep "Git Maintenance"`, it yields an empty result that is indistinguishable from an honest "no such tasks" — and a pipeline's exit status is its LAST command's, so the 1 is invisible too. Measured here: that form read EMPTY while all three Git Maintenance tasks (hourly, daily, weekly) existed and were Ready. It fails in the reassuring direction for anyone checking that something is ABSENT, and it nearly caused a second `git maintenance start` against an already-registered repo.

MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS:
  schtasks /query /fo LIST 2>&1 | head -3   -> the ERROR above; exit 1 read via PIPESTATUS
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 schtasks /query /fo LIST | grep -c "Git Maintenance"  -> 3

THE GUARD, two forms, either acceptable: prefix MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1, or use PowerShell's structured cmdlet (Get-ScheduledTask), which is immune because it never crosses the MSYS argument rewriter.

RELATION TO THE EXISTING LIST: same class as item (d) (`git show <ref>:<path>` mangled when ref and path both contain slashes) but reached through a DIFFERENT DOOR — a Windows-style /FLAG rather than a ref:path pair. Item (d) fails LOUDLY (exit 128 with a message); this one is quiet whenever stderr is suppressed, which is the commoner idiom. Worth its own letter rather than a clause on (d).

DELIVERABLE: add the item to the CLAUDE.md list, in the established voice (measured in both directions, with the guard named). Do NOT renumber or recount the existing items — that section warns that a count in its own opening sentence is the thing that goes stale first.

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING WORTH FOLDING IN IF IT FITS THE SAME EDIT, otherwise leave it: a `bd update --append-notes` written as a DOUBLE-QUOTED shell string containing BACKTICKS silently loses the backticked text — bash runs it as command substitution and inserts its stdout. It damaged a note on rf2-fmst in exactly the places carrying the evidence, while bd still reported success. The guard is to write the note in a QUOTED heredoc and pass it as "$(cat file)". CLAUDE.md already records the adjacent ~27,000-character silent-rejection trap for note values, so this belongs beside it.

PR #9466 merged 2026-09-08. Item (h) appended to CLAUDE.md's "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport on this machine" list. No existing item renumbered or recounted, and the "it carried the word FIVE while there were six" sentence left alone, as the section's own warning requires.

THE WORKER WIDENED THE FINDING BEYOND WHAT I FILED, and the widening is the valuable part: the defect is NOT schtasks-specific. `tasklist /FO CSV` fails identically at 'C:/Program Files/Git/FO'. So the guard is written against ANY native Windows exe taking /FLAG arguments, not against one command. My bead described the instance; the item describes the class.

RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY by the worker rather than taken from my note: unguarded read 0 while all three Git Maintenance tasks exist and are Ready; MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 read 3; PowerShell Get-ScheduledTask read 3.

THE SECOND FINDING WAS FOLDED IN, on the worker's judgement as invited — backticks inside a double-quoted shell string are command substitution, so a `bd update --notes` value written that way silently loses the backticked text while bd still reports success. title: [implementation/hicasso] Make canonical-dom distinguish text data from element markup
description:
Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant source unchanged at mayor HEAD a7b6793a0d6a0614a1cc64d5988afa93d1e4c490. The public test-kit canonical-dom equality oracle can call visibly and structurally different pages equal because it emits text and attribute values without escaping their delimiters. Minimal supported browser reproduction: (let [a (js/document.createElement "div") b (js/document.createElement "div")] (set! (.-textContent a) "

x

") (set! (.-innerHTML b) "

x

") [(ht/canonical-dom a) (ht/canonical-dom b)]) Source trace predicts ["

x

" "

x

"], although A displays literal markup text and B contains a paragraph. This is ordinary rendered content containing angle brackets, not malformed DOM or hostile-input validation. implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs:498-558 promises a canonical DOM-shape equality. In walk, element structure is emitted with literal and ; attribute values are interpolated raw inside quotes; text nodes append .nodeValue raw at 556. Data can therefore imitate the serializer's structure. Attribute values containing quotes create the analogous ambiguity between one value and extra attributes. Expected: different element/text structure or attribute data must produce different canonical bytes (except the documented intentional comment, annotation and adjacent-text normalization). Actual: this comparison returns equal and can pass a DOM parity assertion for a wrong page. Concrete consumer: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/raw_escape_dom_cljs_test.cljs:304-305 compares this exact public oracle to establish raw-escape/defhost DOM parity. test_kit_dom_cljs_test.cljs:47-78 covers ordinary value/text differences but no delimiter-bearing data. mounted/shadow! uses its own structured node comparison and is NOT claimed affected. Smallest repair: escape text/attribute data for the serializer or otherwise encode node kinds and data unambiguously, keeping sorted attributes and the documented exclusions. Do not widen canonical-dom into lifecycle, hydration, visibility or live form-property assertions. Dedupe: active+closed search canonical and description canonical-dom, plus relevant canonical-dom memories; no matching existing issue or intentional delimiter-loss contract found. Verification limits: source-level causal validation and actual public consumer/test inspection only. No browser/CLJS build/test suite was run; no code changed.

Assert a container with literal '

x

' text differs from a container with a real paragraph, and quote-bearing attribute values cannot impersonate extra attributes. Preserve equality across attribute order, ignored comments/dev annotations and adjacent text-node splits. Run focused canonical-dom browser rows; mounted/shadow! does not need redesign.

PR #9393. Premise verified at source post-#9375 and it held: canonical-dom emitted text-node data and attribute values raw into a serialisation whose alphabet is <, > and ", so a container whose TEXT reads

x

produced the same bytes as one holding a real paragraph, and one attribute valued 'y" data-z="w' the same bytes as two attributes. ## Problem

Four HTTP surfaces have zero consumers outside their own tests after months of corpus growth (the demand bar, `spec/Principles.md:124`, has ruled retroactively), and two more have zero consumers but a written discriminator both reviewers say to PARK rather than delete. This bead deletes the four and records the two parks with dated un-park triggers. **It owns the `:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor` / `:rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor` deletion**; the registration-spellings area writes the fx-form rule and should reference this bead rather than re-file the pair.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b)

**(A) `:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor` + `:rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor`** — registered at `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/managed.cljc:226-266` (comment block `:204-224`, ns docstring `:12,:17`). Consumers in `examples/ tools/ testbeds/ skills/`: **0** (both real consumers register at boot with the macro: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/core.cljs:445`, `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/core.cljs:358`, `:before` only). The fx pair's only driver is the conformance corpus, which had to grow a mini-DSL to describe a `:before` fn as data: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/conformance.cljc:267-338` (`realise-interceptor-before-fn`, operators `[:assoc-in-request …]` / `[:dispatch …]`), `:348-350`, `:377-383` (the `resolve-fx-args` case branch); fixtures `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-interceptor-before-transforms.edn` and `http-interceptor-clear.edn`; roster rows `spec/conformance/README.md:539-540`. The fx form invented a consumer to justify itself — an interceptor's payload is a fn, and putting a fn inside an fx vector makes it less data-shaped, not more. `tools/mcp-conformance`: 0 references. Direct unit tests: `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:878-1059` (7 deftests, rf2-oyd1b block); the CLJS interceptor test has no fx-form case.

**(B) `:rf.http/decode-schemas`** — a `reg-event` metadata key "pair tools read" (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:273-295`, `spec/API.md:449`). Writers: **22** metadata lines (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/`: `article_editor.cljs:327,400`, `articles.cljs:239`, `auth.cljs:294,556,617`, `comments.cljs:240,316,392,569`, `favorites.cljs:66,158`, `profile.cljs:243,305,362,438,463`, `settings.cljs:319`, `tags.cljs:164`; `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs:356`) plus the README claim `realworld_http/README.md:20` and a comment `auth.cljs:286` — each a second copy of the `:decode` schema in the fx args a few lines below. title: xray: no CI workflow builds the managed_http testbed, so nothing gates its compile
description:
https://github.com/day8/re-frame2 — filed by the mayor 2026-09-05 from a finding the rf2-s4dp worker made and correctly reported rather than acting on.

THE FINDING, in that worker's words: `npm run test:cljs`'s `:node-test` build is `:ns-regexp "cljs-test$"`, which matches neither file it changed, and **no CI workflow builds `:examples/managed-http`** — so nothing gates that testbed's compile at all. It verified all four call arities against their definitions by hand precisely because no compiler reaches the file locally OR in CI.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE TESTBED. A testbed that nothing compiles is a file that can rot silently: rf2-s4dp existed because #9195 changed a registry contract underneath this testbed and nothing caught it — not a test, not a compile, not a lint. The defect was found only because a human-directed audit went looking. That is the same shape as the vacuous-proof findings this session (a poison test that never threw, a cleanup that graded a wrapper, a parity test that agreed with itself): coverage that reads as present and inspects nothing.

AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL HERE — the same worker's census found a SECOND unstamped site in the same file (`issue-as-actor`, keying actor handles under `[nil actor-id]`), which had also survived unnoticed.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST, and this may dissolve the bead: whether the testbed is meant to be compiled by CI at all. `tools/xray/testbeds/` may be deliberately browser-only, exercised by a `spec.cjs` that this one lacks, in which case the right answer is either to give it one or to record why it has none. CLAUDE.md's testing section says framework testbeds "carry their own non-adapter spec.cjs for cross-cutting surfaces" — this one does not, and that gap is the thing to explain or close.

DO NOT ASSUME THE ANSWER IS "ADD A GATE". The stance rejects gold-plating, and a browser build for one testbed may cost more than it holds. A recorded, reasoned "this testbed is not gated, and here is why that is acceptable" is a complete and good outcome. What is not acceptable is the current state, where the absence is undocumented and reads as an oversight.

SCOPE NOTE: this is about the GATE, not about rf2-s4dp's defect, which is fixed in PR #9216 (merged or merging). Do not re-fix that.

THE PREMISE IS WRONG. "No CI workflow builds :examples/managed-http" is true as a NAME grep and false as a fact. implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs DERIVES its build list from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn by scanning for :examples/<name> and :testbeds/<name> keys; `--list` returns 58 builds and examples/managed-http is one. It runs as the cljs-examples-compile job in .github/workflows/test.yml and unconditionally nightly in expensive-tests.yml. The classifier (.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh) arms it from BOTH relevant directions: `tools/xray/testbeds/*` AND `implementation/http/*` — so both a change to the testbed and a change to the substrate contract that broke it (PR #9195) schedule the job.

AND A COMPILE WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT rf2-s4dp — measured on :examples/managed-http, not asserted:
  - tip: exit 0, 555 files, 0 warnings
