title: story-mcp: remove unreachable JVM CLJS-var auto-probes
description:
Evidence
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cljs_resolve.cljc:77-113` retains `resolve-cljs-var`, `registered-substrates-var`, and `violations-by-frame-var`; their only production purpose is to auto-discover two browser-side providers from the JVM process.
- Both targets are impossible in the shipped JVM artifact: `re-frame.story/registered-substrates` is defined only inside `#?(:cljs ...)` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:1816-1822`), and `re-frame.story.ui.a11y/violations-by-frame` lives in a `.cljs` namespace (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/a11y.cljs:59-64`). Story-MCP is JVM-only and has no in-process browser bridge.
- Commit `82ec7aa84f` established the symmetric contract: neither provider auto-wires; a future bridge binds both dynamic seams. The old CLJ probe defaults at lines 132-133 and 190-191 survived that migration.
- Repo-wide usage finds no consumer of `resolve-cljs-var` outside its dedicated unit test (`tools_test.clj:637-644`); the two private probe vars are source-only. `[re-frame.story]` at line 75 exists only to support this probe path.

Impact
The package loads the large Story facade and maintains/test-documents an auto-wiring mechanism that can never make either capability available. This obscures the actual explicit-provider contract and creates false confidence that browser state may be reachable from the JVM.

Recommendation
Remove the resolver, both private probes, the resolver-only test, and the resolver-only Story facade require. Initialize both dynamic provider vars to nil on every platform, while retaining the dynamic provider seams, availability predicates, accessor semantics, and capability-unavailable behavior.

Risks / contracts
`resolve-cljs-var` is a public var in an internal namespace even though it is absent from Story-MCP's documented/package/protocol API. Check downstream source consumers before deletion. Do not remove or rename `*substrate-provider*`, `*a11y-provider*`, `substrate-provider-available?`, `a11y-provider-available?`, or their explicit binding behavior; those are deliberate test/future-bridge seams.
acceptance_criteria:
- A repo-wide consumer check documents that no supported caller depends on `resolve-cljs-var`.
- The resolver, its two cached probe vars, resolver-only test, and now-unused Story facade require are removed (or a concrete supported external contract is documented instead).
- Both provider vars default to nil and remain independently bindable; availability distinguishes absent providers from reached providers returning empty data.
- Story-MCP unit tests, descriptor drift check, and stdio round-trip pass.
close_reason: PR #9089. Premise held. Removed resolve-cljs-var, registered-substrates-var, violations-by-frame-var, the resolver-only unit test, and the [re-frame.story] require that existed only to feed the probe; both provider vars now read a plain nil on every platform. Consumer check: repo-wide search finds resolve-cljs-var only in its own ns and the deleted test - absent from the documented/package/protocol API. Seams kept intact: *substrate-provider*, *a11y-provider*, substrate-provider-available?, a11y-provider-available?, accessors, capability-unavailable routing. Verified: clojure -M:test exit 0 (278 tests / 1473 assertions), clojure -M:gen --check exit 0 (in sync, 19 tools). Gate proved live by planting the exact removed auto-wire ((fn [] []) as the substrate default): exit 1, 9 failures including list-substrates returning a false-empty {:substrates []} success.

title: Prune strict-subset frame-resolution cases from event-conformance
description:
## Finding

`implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_frame_isolation_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` carries three cases whose observable contract is already exercised more strongly by `implementation/core/test/re_frame/live_run_frame_resolution_cljs_test.cljc`:

- `two-frames-sharing-one-image-keep-independent-app-db` repeats the same image, seeds (0/100), three-dispatch stream, distinct runnable ids, numeric results, and non-global resolution as core's `two-frames-from-one-image-keep-independent-state`; the core owner additionally proves independent subscription values and cache identity. The conformance-only second `not= :global` is implied by the exact `= 101` assertion.
- `absence-is-default-no-image-frame-uses-the-global-registrar` repeats core's `no-image-frame-resolves-through-the-global-registrar`: same image-less explicit frame, global event + sub, committed marker, subscription value, and nil generation binding.
- `the-global-sentinel-is-genuinely-registered` repeats that same absence/default path again. The headline isolation test registers its sentinel in its own fixture scope, and its exact `:todo` / `:counter` results already establish that the image handlers ran; a cross-test registration probe cannot arm another fixture's sentinel.

Both files are `.cljc` namespaces ending `-cljs-test`, so all of these rows ride the consolidated Node suite and JVM test lanes. The duplication adds maintenance and runtime without another platform or code-path boundary.

## Recommendation

Delete the three strict-subset cases, or consolidate their genuinely useful assertion into the canonical core owner. Keep the conformance rows that add independent teeth: exact two-image app-db shape + distinct generations, runtime-db partition isolation, and child-dispatch sibling-frame isolation. Update suite commentary/counts to describe that narrower ownership.

## Risks and contracts

Do not weaken dual-runtime coverage of image resolution or delete the unique runtime-db/sibling-isolation assertions. Preserve at least one positive absence-is-default event+subscription test and one directly armed global-fallback sentinel in the canonical owner.

## Evidence

The event-conformance file has 6 tests; the core owner has the corresponding live-run cases plus stronger state/sub-cache assertions. History shows core's live resolution suite predates the conformance copy (`22229d483c` / `78d4d2eca8` before `4bacc2f05c`), and both remain enrolled through `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` plus their JVM aliases.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The three strict-subset cases are removed or reduced to assertions not present in the core owner.
2. The canonical core suite still proves image-less global event+sub resolution, nil generation, and shared-image independent event/sub-cache state on JVM and CLJS.
3. Event-conformance retains the distinct-generation/exact-db headline, runtime-db isolation, and child/sibling isolation teeth.
4. Event-conformance JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS Node suite pass, with updated test/assertion tallies and no stale ownership prose.
close_reason: Premise held for all three; containment demonstrated per case. (1) absence-is-default-no-image-frame-uses-the-global-registrar is OPERATIONALLY IDENTICAL to core's no-image-frame-resolves-through-the-global-registrar -- same frame id, event, sub and three assertions, differing only in prose strings (verified by a paren-balanced form extraction and string-elided compare: identical True). Two copies of one program cannot be distinguished by any fault, which is stronger evidence than a plant. (2) the-global-sentinel-is-genuinely-registered repeats that same path plus a registrar/lookup some? probe; the probe's value is real but its PLACEMENT was not -- the :each fixture means it could never arm another test's sentinel -- so it was MOVED INTO the headline isolation row, where it backs the not= :global assertions that actually depend on it. (3) two-frames-sharing-one-image-keep-independent-app-db: five of its six assertions are textually identical to core's two-frames-from-one-image-keep-independent-state; the sixth (not= :global on frame B) is entailed by the exact = 101. Core adds frame-object?, subscription values and sub-cache identity. Plant (a constant frame/anon-frame-id collapsing two no-id frames onto one record) reds both: conformance 3 failures/6 assertions, core 6 failures/11 -- core strictly stronger. All three deleted. AC1-4 met: core still owns image-less global event+sub resolution and nil generation and shared-image independent state on JVM+CLJS; event-conformance retains its three teeth (exact two-image app-db with distinct generations, runtime-db partition isolation with untouched sibling, child/sibling isolation); ns prose rewritten to name the narrower ownership; JVM 44 tests/186 assertions exit 0 and node suite 11163/55721 exit 0. shadow-cljs.edn NOT touched -- the file stays enrolled, no build-id change needed. PR #9123.

title: Correct Test-React's stale CI, adapter-count, and UIx-consumer claims
description:
## Finding

The Test-React packaging and consumer commentary contains three stale architecture claims:

1. `implementation/adapters/test-react/deps.edn:11-14` and `implementation/adapters/README.md:25` say the local fixture is absent from the CI JVM job set. That stopped being true when commit `2458b99ee7` added required job `jvm-adapters-test-react`; `.github/workflows/test.yml:1753-1807` runs `clojure -M:test`, and `all-required-passed` names it at `:6358`. `TESTING.md:193,241` likewise documents its real 35-test JVM coverage. It remains absent from publishing/release, but not from JVM CI.
2. The same deps comment says "four published adapters" while listing only Reagent, reagent-slim, and UIx. `implementation/adapters/README.md:69` repeats "All 4 published adapters", and `:73` says "The 4 React-shaped adapter namespaces" even though its own inventory has three shipped view-adapter directories and its factory-family list has Reagent + reagent-slim + UIx. Commit `e1f38e5ddf` removed Helix and edited the lists but left these counts behind. Spec 006 `:2164` is explicit that the shipped view-adapter sources under this directory are those three and Test-React is a local-test-only fixture.
3. `test_react_cljs_test.cljc:31`, `:975`, and `:1120` claim UIx browser suites consume/lean on/route through Test-React's public harness. A repository search outside this adapter has no code require or call of `re-frame.adapter.test-react` from `implementation/adapters/uix`, and `git log -S're-frame.adapter.test-react' -- implementation/adapters/uix implementation/adapters/helix implementation/core/test` is empty across history. The UIx suites use the shared React suite and real adapter/testbed paths; the Test-React contract guards are self-tests of this local harness, not a downstream UIx dependency.

## Impact

Readers are told both that a required gate does not exist and that nonexistent fourth/view consumers do exist. That misstates which gate is authoritative for a Test-React edit, preserves a phantom Helix-era count, and makes the simulator's self-tests appear coupled to UIx when they are not. In a vestigial-code review, that false consumer claim is particularly costly: it can cause maintainers to retain or gate a helper for a downstream user that has never existed.

## Disposition

Truth the comments without changing behavior: distinguish "not published/released" from "covered by a required JVM CI job"; say three shipped view adapters/React-shaped adapter namespaces where those are the named set; and describe section C as contract guards for Test-React's own documented public driver/substrate entry point. Keep the genuine local-only status, both JVM and CLJS lanes, and all lifecycle contracts.

## Risks and boundaries

Do not reclassify Test-React as a shipped/public Maven artefact, remove it from bundle isolation expectations, or weaken `jvm-adapters-test-react`. Do not rewrite the canonical six-adapter inventory in Spec 006; this correction is only for stale local comments and counts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No Test-React documentation claims the fixture is absent from CI's JVM job set; it clearly remains absent only from publication/version-lockstep/release matrices and points to the required JVM lane where useful.
2. The adapters README/deps comments no longer claim four published or four React-shaped adapter namespaces for the three-name Reagent/reagent-slim/UIx set, and agree with Spec 006's canonical inventory.
3. Test-React's own test commentary no longer claims UIx suites consume its harness; it accurately states that the guards pin the local harness's documented contract.
4. Fixed-string searches for `CI JVM job set`, `four published adapters`, `All 4 published adapters`, `The 4 React-shaped`, and `uix browser suites consume` either return no stale claim or only an explicitly historical quotation.
5. No source, adapter map, lifecycle test, gate condition, or publishing metadata changes as part of this documentation-only correction.
close_reason: Landed in PR #9100. All three claims verified false at today's tip and corrected. (1) CI: test.yml:1753 defines jvm-adapters-test-react running the artefact's own clojure -M:test, and all-required-passed names it at :6358, so deps.edn and adapters/README.md now separate the (unchanged) absence from the lockstep array + release deploy matrix from the CI JVM job set it IS in. (2) Counts: measured from git ls-files, implementation/adapters/ carries three published adapter directories (reagent, reagent-slim, uix) plus the unpublished test-react fixture and the shared scripts/ smoke tooling, matching Spec 006:2155-2160's repository-home paragraph — 'All 4 published adapters' and 'The 4 React-shaped adapter namespaces' both now read 3, and deps.edn's 'four published adapters' reads three. Spec 006 untouched. (3) UIx consumers: two independent instruments with controls that fire. Fixed-string census over tracked files finds no reference to re-frame.adapter.test-react or test_react anywhere under implementation/adapters/uix (control: the same instrument for re-frame.adapter.uix on that path returns hits); git log --all -S over uix/helix/core-test is empty across history (control: the same search on the test-react artefact returns three commits). The only non-test mention repo-wide is the quoted producer roster in re-frame.late-bind.directory. All three sites (ns docstring, the section-C header, the substrate-render testing string) now describe self-tests of this local harness's own documented public surface. Post-fix census: 'four published adapters', 'All 4 published adapters', 'The 4 React-shaped', 'uix browser suites consume/lean', 'uix adapters route through' all return exit 1; the sole surviving 'CI JVM job set' hit is the corrected positive statement. No source, adapter map, lifecycle test, gate condition or publishing metadata changed. Out of fence and filed as rf2-3nw7: adapters/README.md:37 and implementation/core/.../adapter.cljc:643-647 both count test-react as one of the 'six shipped adapter kinds' where Spec 006 has hicasso as the sixth.

title: Use the orphaned ssr-node chunk-frame constructor at its live boundary
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs:497-498 defines chunkFrame(seq, html) as the canonical public body-frame constructor and exports it at :528.
- A whole-repository exact-identifier search finds no call to chunkFrame; its only sites are the definition and export.
- The actual worker-to-service boundary independently rebuilds the identical object literal at src/isolate.cjs:165-168: { type: 'chunk', seq: msg.seq, html: msg.html }.
- The adjacent completeFrame constructor is live: service.cjs imports and calls it to create the terminal public frame. The chunk constructor is the orphaned half of that intended pair.
- Both the helper and duplicate literal have existed since the initial implementation b2b35bf6e9. No existing bead found by chunkFrame, chunk-frame, or ssr-node searches owns the duplication.

## Impact

There are two sources of truth for the public chunk-frame shape, but only the hand-written isolate copy is exercised. A future field-list or hardening change can update the named protocol constructor while leaving every real response unchanged, or update the live literal while leaving a misleading exported helper behind.

## Disposition

Import chunkFrame into isolate.cjs and use it exactly where the parent translates a worker chunk into the public service frame. This mirrors completeFrame and preserves the boundary's explicit named-field projection. If the helper is rejected as an abstraction, delete it instead; do not retain both representations.

## Risks

Do not pass or spread the raw worker message. The explicit projection is an egress boundary that intentionally drops unrecognized application-controlled fields. The constructor must continue accepting only seq and html and returning only type, seq, and html.
acceptance_criteria:
1. There is one source of truth for the public chunk-frame object shape.
2. The live Isolate chunk path exercises chunkFrame, or the unused helper/export is removed completely.
3. No raw worker-message spread or extra field crosses the boundary.
4. Protocol, bytes, egress, and full ssr-node tests remain green.
5. A focused assertion or coverage reading shows the retained constructor executes on a streamed response.
close_reason: PR #9099. chunkFrame is now the single source of truth for the public chunk-frame shape: isolate.cjs imports it and calls it at the worker->service boundary, mirroring completeFrame's live use in service.cjs. No raw-message spread, no extra field; the constructor still takes only seq/html and returns only type/seq/html. A new egress.test.cjs row reads a MULTI-chunk response and asserts each frame's key set is exactly html/seq/type, so the retained constructor is proven to execute on a streamed response (criterion 5). Control fired: with the boundary spreading the raw worker message instead, the row reds on the t and id fields. Suite 9/9 green, 108 rows, eslint exit 0.

title: Remove the unused frame-id hop from flows tooling metadata
description:
Evidence
- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/tooling.cljc:39-47` defines private `with-metadata` as `[node _frame-id flow]`; its body reads only `node` and `flow`.
- Its sole call at line 62 is `(with-metadata frame-id flow)` in a thread-first form. `frame-id` is already consumed by `node-for` to build `:owner [:frame frame-id]` and has no role in metadata attachment.
- `d8bc29e2e0` replaced `frame-matched-source-coords [frame-id flow-id]` with `flow-source-coords [flow]` after flows moved to a frame-scoped single store. That migration renamed the now-unused parameter `_frame-id` but retained the call hop.
- Exact source and test searches find no other call to this private helper.

Impact and disposition
The extra argument falsely suggests source/schema/doc/derive metadata depends on frame identity and preserves a remnant of the retired frame-blind registrar lookup. Remove the parameter and stop passing it; keep frame ownership construction in `node-for` unchanged.

Risk
The change must not remove or alter `:owner [:frame frame-id]`, same-id cross-frame isolation, source-coordinate projection, schema/doc projection, or the opaque derive token.
acceptance_criteria:
- `with-metadata` accepts only the node and flow values it reads, and its sole call no longer passes `frame-id`.
- `node-for` still projects the selected frame as `:owner [:frame frame-id]`.
- Existing flows tooling JVM/CLJS projection tests cover source metadata and same-id flows in different frames and pass.
- Bundle-isolation controls for the tooling sibling remain green.
close_reason: with-metadata now takes [node flow] and its sole call passes only flow (PR #9082). Premise held: line numbers re-derived exactly as filed (defn- at :39, sole call at :62), body read only node and flow, and a fixed-string census found exactly two tree-wide hits — the defn- and that one call. The same-named private helpers in the machines and resources tooling siblings are separate vars in separate namespaces, and the two hits in core's handler_source_test.clj are deftest NAMES, not calls. node-for still projects :owner [:frame frame-id] unchanged. Closure had already inlined the hop away, so this is source hygiene with no emitted-output change. Gates: flows JVM suite 250 tests / 6102 assertions / 0 failures; test:cljs 11209 tests / 55849 assertions / 0 failures; CLJS compile 0 warnings (an arity mismatch would surface there); bundle-isolation 40 absent / 40 present, unmoved.

title: Resources: retire the unreachable legacy aborted reply event
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:2851-2940 labels aborted-handler a LEGACY/ad-hoc reply event and lowers it through a synthetic canonical failure.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:529-532 still registers :rf.resource.internal/aborted.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/transport/http.cljc:7-18,49-52,93-141 lowers managed HTTP completion only to :rf.resource.internal/failed; an abort is a canonical failure reply with status :cancelled. There is no production dispatcher of the aborted event anywhere in the repository.
- Exact repository search finds the event only in registration/handler code, reserved-event prose, and tests that dispatch the internal event directly. Commit f08e41dfcd explicitly described this handler as legacy after moving it onto the canonical reply path; the original skeleton was 2cd05677fb.

Impact
The package carries two cancellation settlement entrances although only the failed-event entrance is reachable from the live transport. This preserves a second internal protocol, duplicated tests, registration, event census, and stale documentation that can drift from canonical reply behavior.

Proposed disposition
Remove the :rf.resource.internal/aborted registration, aborted-event-failure, and aborted-handler. Re-express or delete the direct-dispatch tests through :rf.resource.internal/failed with a canonical cancellation reply so live/stale, cross-frame, ledger, completed-at, readiness, route, invalidation, and Epoch behavior stays covered on the production path. Reconcile Spec 016, Conventions, EP event rosters, and comments that reserve or describe the retired member.

Risks
Although user code is explicitly forbidden to dispatch this internal namespace, out-of-repository code may have done so. Check release/migration policy and call out the retirement. Do not weaken cancellation classification or stale-reply suppression while collapsing the path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repository search has no :rf.resource.internal/aborted registration or executable dispatch after the migration (except an intentional migration note if required).
- Managed HTTP abort coverage proves the canonical :rf.resource.internal/failed path yields cancelled settlement, including stale/cross-frame suppression, completed-at, ledger/reply targets, and blocking-readiness behavior.
- Internal-event rosters and normative prose match the shipped event set.
- Resource JVM and CLJS suites pass.
notes:
NOT DONE - FENCE-BLOCKED (worker/adaptcount-a, 2026-09-03; the rest of that dispatch landed as PR #9112).

PREMISE VERIFIED, so the bead's core finding stands. Two independent instruments over tracked files, excluding .beads:
  * git grep -F 'rf.resource.internal/aborted' -- 'implementation/*/src'  ->  exit 1, ZERO hits. There is no production dispatcher anywhere in implementation source.
  * CONTROL THAT FIRED: the same grep for the sibling ':rf.resource.internal/failed' returns hits in 20 files, 9 of them production source (resources.cljc, resources/events.cljc, resources/tooling.cljc, resources/transport/http.cljc, resources/work_ledger.cljc among them). So the empty result above is a real absence, not a broken search.
  * Every surviving reference is registration/handler code, reserved-event prose, or a test that dispatches the internal event DIRECTLY - exactly as the description says.

WHY IT WAS NOT LANDED. Completing the retirement requires two edits outside this worker's fence, and a partial would leave the tree self-contradictory (registration removed, epoch suite red):

  1. spec/Conventions.md:110 AND :111 list ':rf.resource.internal/aborted' as a RESERVED MEMBER of the ':rf.resource.internal/*' framework-internal sub-namespace. Conventions.md is a hot-zone one-toucher file this dispatch was explicitly barred from editing. Note this is also a judgment call worth making deliberately rather than mechanically: a reserved-namespace member is reserved DEFENSIVELY (the same shape as the ':rf.adapter/ui' / ':rf.adapter/freehand' reserved-kind contract), so whether retiring the HANDLER should also un-reserve the NAME is a real question the acceptance criteria assumes one answer to ('rosters match the shipped event set') without arguing it. Recommend the mayor settle that before dispatching, because the two readings produce different diffs.

  2. implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj EXECUTABLY dispatches it at :3946 (inside drive-aborted-event-reply-to-read!, :3923-3948) and treats it at :4067 as a NAMED BRANCH of a whole-record egress/secret-leak sweep, with its own :why prose explaining that the legacy handler synthesises its own envelope so its canary is the owner data beside it. That is not a line to delete - it is a coverage row that has to be re-expressed on the ':rf.resource.internal/failed' path with a canonical cancellation reply, in an artefact (implementation/epoch) held by another worker.

SCOPE ESTIMATE for whoever picks this up: production removal is small (resources.cljc:529-532 registration; resources/events.cljc:2851-2940 aborted-handler + aborted-event-failure). The work is the re-expression - 5 resources test files (resources_invalidation_gc, resources_route, resources_skeleton, resources_time_ms_cofx, resources_work_ledger) plus the epoch egress matrix, plus spec/016-Resources.md:460 and :645 and the two Conventions.md rows. Sequence it with whoever holds implementation/epoch, and settle the reserved-name question first.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03: RETIRE THE HANDLER, KEEP THE NAME RESERVED. These are two questions and the bead's acceptance criteria conflated them; worker adaptcount-a was right to stop and ask rather than assume.

The repo already has a settled precedent for exactly this shape, and it decides the second half. `:rf.adapter/ui` and `:rf.adapter/freehand` stay rostered in spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md, spec/Conventions.md and spec/API.md AFTER their implementations were deleted — not as residue, but because tooling still refuses those values DEFENSIVELY against a stale co-loaded build. A reserved name costs a roster line; an unreserved name that a stale build can still emit costs a silent wrong behaviour.

So: the unreachable legacy aborted-reply handler goes. spec/Conventions.md:110-111 KEEPS the reserved member, and NO hot-zone edit is required — which also unblocks this bead, since the Conventions dependency was the stated blocker.

The epoch test at implementation/epoch/test/.../epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj:3946 executably dispatches the event as a named branch of an egress sweep. That is a real consumer of the DISPATCH PATH, not of the handler's behaviour, so the test moves with the handler: either re-point that branch at a live event or drop the branch, whichever keeps the sweep's coverage honest. Do not delete the handler and leave the test dispatching into nothing.

Evidence that stands (verified by adaptcount-a, control fired): zero production dispatchers across implementation/*/src (git grep -F exit 1); control :failed returns hits in 20 files.
LANDED (all but one spec line) — PR #9116, branch worker/resretire-a, head f2ce1d677098b00f68e201bee93e7728d5a62b2c. Worker resretire-a, 2026-09-03.

WORKED THE MAYOR RULING ABOVE: the handler is retired, the name stays reserved.
- Removed `(events/reg-event :rf.resource.internal/aborted ...)` from resources.cljc, plus `aborted-handler` and `aborted-event-failure` from resources/events.cljc.
- spec/Conventions.md:110-111 UNCHANGED, exactly as ruled.
- Five resources tests plus the epoch egress sweep re-expressed on `:rf.resource.internal/failed` carrying an `{:kind :rf.http/aborted}` envelope.

THE EPOCH SWEEP BRANCH: DROPPED, not re-pointed — and it HAD to be, which the brief's "either/or" did not know. `continuation-settle-drives` is keyed by settle-event id, and `every-continuation-settle-path-is-inventoried-from-source` asserts those keys `=` the set derived by READING the family's own source. Removing the handler removes the key from the derived side, so the map entry could not survive; the gate is green only because both halves moved in one commit.

Nothing is lost by dropping it. The `:rf.resource.internal/failed` entry ALREADY drove both arms, and its second arm IS the accepted-cancellation settle — same whole-record egress sweep, same real owner, params and resolved scope. It is the STRONGER drive: the legacy branch had to carry an `:unplantable` exemption for `:error`, because the retired handler synthesised its own envelope and no drive could plant a canary in it. On the canonical arm the envelope comes from the drive, so that slot carries a real canary and the exemption is gone. `:unplantable` is still exercised by the three mutation entries, so no mechanism is left dead.

TWO FINDINGS THE BEAD'S EVIDENCE DID NOT HAVE.

1. The legacy handler had DRIFTED from the canonical branch, not merely duplicated it. `failed-handler`'s abort arm arms the first-load GC/stale timers (rf2-kz5op1); `aborted-handler` never picked that up. So the retired entrance was the WEAKER of the two, and a first-load abort through it left an owner-free `:idle` entry that was never reaped. Retiring it removes a latent leak, not just a duplicate.

2. A LINE-WRAPPED reference `git grep` cannot see. resources/events.cljc:404-405 splits the keyword across two comment lines (`` `:rf.resource.internal/ `` then `` aborted` ``), so every line-oriented census in this bead's history missed it. A multiline scan found it. Its claim was independently FALSE: it listed "a direct/internal aborted settlement" as a way a stale `:current-work` pointer survives because the handler "makes no entry write", but `entry-abort-settled` has cleared `:current-work` since rf2-iu0z8t. Fixed, and so was epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj:635's "all five" settle-branch count (four now, with the reason recorded rather than the count silently edited).

CENSUS CORRECTION, worth carrying past this bead: the pathspec `implementation/*/src` used in the note above MATCHES NOTHING. A git wildcard pathspec is matched against the WHOLE path, so it never reaches a file under `.../src/`; the control `:rf.resource.internal/failed` returns exit 1 through it too. The correct form is `implementation/*/src/*`, and through THAT: `aborted` -> registration plus two docstrings, no dispatcher; `failed` -> 5 production files. The earlier conclusion was right, but its control had not actually been exercised through the same command shape, so the zero was unearned.

GATES (foreground, exit codes captured to files and read from the files): resources 0 (828 tests / 7475 assertions), epoch 0 (552 / 7237), ssr-ring 0 (231 / 1163), core error-catalogue ns 0 (30 / 179). clj-kondo over `implementation` exits 3 on ONE error in epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc:939 — a file byte-identical to origin/main on this branch, reproducing on its origin/main content standalone; local kondo is v2025.10.23 against CI's pinned v2026.04.15. No kondo finding anywhere names `aborted`, `aborted-handler` or `status-defect`.

STILL OPEN ON ONE LINE — spec/016-Resources.md:460, outside this dispatch's fence.

That sentence reads: "The handlers that carry it: ... and the internal replies `:rf.resource.internal/succeeded` / `:rf.resource.internal/failed` / `:rf.resource.internal/aborted` / `:rf.resource.internal/stale-fired` / ...". It is a claim about SHIPPED, STAMPED HANDLERS, not about reserved names, so unlike Conventions.md:110-111 it does not survive the ruling.

EXACT EDIT: delete the two tokens "`:rf.resource.internal/aborted` / " from that list. Nothing else on the line changes.

spec/016-Resources.md:645 needs NO change — it is a reserved-member roster of the `:rf.resource.internal/*` sub-namespace, the same shape as the Conventions rows the ruling keeps.

CALIBRATION for whoever takes that line: :460's list ALREADY omits four registered internal handlers (`page-succeeded`, `page-failed`, `poll-fired`, `refetch-page`), so it is demonstrably illustrative rather than a shipped-set roster. Nothing mechanical reads it. This is bookkeeping, not a correctness gap, and closing this bead as-is and letting the line ride until someone next opens spec/016 is a defensible call.

SPEC/016:460 RULED — NO EDIT. Worker specfin-a, 2026-09-03 (hot-zone serial lane; PR #9118 carries this tick's other two beads, spec/016 deliberately untouched).

PREMISE FAILURE FIRST, because it changes the question. The brief I was given, and the note above, both say the code half "LANDED in PR #9116". IT HAS NOT. gh pr view 9116 returns state OPEN, mergedAt null. The handler is still registered on origin/main at implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:529, and it still carries the framework-authority stamp. So deleting the two tokens from :460 TODAY would make the spec assert that a shipped, stamped handler does not exist. That is strictly worse than the staleness it would fix, and it is the catalogue-vs-code drift the "dispatch code-dependent follow-up only after the source PR MERGES" rule exists to prevent. (Landing was tested by payload, not by ancestry: git log origin/main --grep for each of .52/.47/.80 returns nothing.)

THE CALIBRATION HOLDS, AND IS STRONGER THAN THE NOTE ABOVE RECORDED. The note said :460 already omits four registered internal handlers. Measured at source, the omission is NINE of TWENTY-ONE.

:460 names 6 public + 6 internal = 12. resources.cljc registers 11 public + 10 internal = 21. Omitted: public load-more, adopt-owner, release-owner-identities, window-focused, network-reconnected; internal refetch-page, page-succeeded, page-failed, poll-fired.

And every one of those 21 DOES carry the stamp, which is the part that settles it. The stamp is not written per registration — it comes from three meta vars, and generation-meta (resources.cljc:393) and time-meta (:377) are each (assoc framework-authority-meta ...). So all three derive from framework-authority-meta and every registered resource event is stamped. A list naming 12 of 21 stamped handlers under the words "The handlers that carry it" is therefore ILLUSTRATIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, not a roster that a retirement falsifies. Nothing mechanical reads it (no gate resolves symbols named in prose here).

RULING: no edit to spec/016:460, now or after #9116 merges. Deleting one token from an already-9-short illustration buys nothing, and the sentence does not become false when the handler goes — it was never claiming completeness. :645 needs no change either, as already established (reserved-member roster, same shape as the Conventions rows the mayor ruling keeps).

WHY THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN. Not because of the spec line — that is settled and needs nobody. It stays open because its actual subject, the handler retirement, is NOT on main: #9116 is an open PR touching 12 files including the epoch egress conformance matrix. Close this bead when #9116 merges; no further spec work is owed at that point.
AUDIT PR #9116: The implementation and test retirement is correct, but the documentation half is incomplete. docs/EP/EP-0003-resource-queries.md:595-602 still says the handlers that return :rf.db/runtime include :rf.resource.internal/aborted, and :2868-2876 still directs implementations to implement it. spec/016-Resources.md:460 still calls it a handler carrying framework authority; :645 calls every listed internal reply a carrier of the verification payload and canonical reply map. Keeping the name defensively reserved in Conventions is sound, but does not make these live-handler claims true. An illustrative list may omit real handlers, but a named member must still exist. Retain the reservation and distinguish the retired reserved name from shipped reply handlers; the implementation/test diff otherwise reviewed cleanly for correctness and quality.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED after the first close evaporated. Code half is on main as 01c1a5e17d (PR #9116): aborted-handler retired, name kept reserved per the mayor ruling and the :rf.adapter/ui reserved-kind precedent; five resources tests plus the epoch sweep re-expressed on :rf.resource.internal/failed with an {:kind :rf.http/aborted} envelope. Spec half ruled NO EDIT by the hot-zone lane worker (PR #9118): spec/016-Resources.md:460 names 12 of 21 registered handlers - all three registration meta vars derive from framework-authority-meta, so every registered resource event is stamped - making that list illustrative by construction rather than a roster, so it does not become false when one handler goes. spec/016:645 is a reserved-member roster and correctly unchanged. Bonus finding preserved: the retired handler had DRIFTED rather than merely duplicated - failed-handler's abort arm arms first-load GC/stale timers (rf2-kz5op1) and aborted-handler never did, so a first-load abort through it left an owner-free :idle entry never reaped; retiring it removed a latent leak. FIRST CLOSE LOST to the CLAUDE.md .beads hazard: a git checkout HEAD -- .beads run after the close reverted the export to its pre-close state and that revert reached the database. Recovered by re-closing and checkpointing BEFORE any checkout.

title: http privacy-body: remove the orphaned direct-projector helper layer
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.http.privacy-body` ships a test-only direct-projection layer that is disconnected from the actual off-box path: `off-box-classify-body` plus `off-box-body-marker`. The same namespace also exposes `whole-body-sensitive-mark?`, a zero-production-consumer predicate duplicating behavior already exercised through `classify-decoded`.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide resolved-var analysis and fixed-string searches find zero production calls to `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` (`privacy_body.cljc:219`), `off-box-classify-body` (`:309`), or `off-box-body-marker` (`:237`). Their only executable consumers are focused assertions in `http_privacy_body_test.clj:102-108,182-224`; remaining hits are self-docstrings/comments.
- The shipped off-box path is different. HTTP emit sites call `off-box-body-disposition` and stamp `:rf.http/off-box-body` on trace tags (`transport.cljc:435,768` and other raw-failure paths). `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1430-1512` reads that stamp and applies its own `omit-off-box-http-bodies` projection; it cannot call the HTTP helper because Epoch deliberately has no HTTP-artifact dependency.
- The real projector is extensively covered in `epoch_egress_trace_events_test.clj` and `epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`; HTTP integration tests cover the emit-side `:omit` / `:classify` stamps. Removing the disconnected helper tests does not remove runtime-path coverage.
- Current privacy-body namespace prose and `off-box-body-disposition` docs incorrectly claim Epoch “applies” `off-box-classify-body`. The integration-test comment around `http_privacy_integration_test.clj:551-556` similarly treats its unit test as part of the end-to-end path, although no call edge exists.
- `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` only asks whether `(decode-schema-marks decode)` contains root path `[]`. The neighboring `whole-body-root-sensitive-redacts-everything` test already proves the product behavior through `classify-decoded`; the standalone predicate is neither used to decide runtime policy nor listed in the API manifest.
- History confirms these were never connected: `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` arrived in `59bffbceaf`; `off-box-classify-body`/marker arrived in `39dcc2c889`, while that same commit implemented the actual stamp/Epoch projector split. Subsequent history added no production consumer. Bead searches by all three exact symbols and off-box/body terms found no existing issue.

## Impact

The orphaned layer adds public vars and tests for code the product never executes, duplicates the Epoch projector semantics in a package that cannot be its authority, and leaves architecture documentation claiming a nonexistent call path. Future security fixes could update the helper, turn its tests green, and still leave the real off-box projector unchanged.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `off-box-classify-body`, `off-box-body-marker`, and `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` plus only their direct self-tests. Correct namespace/doc/test comments to describe the real stamp -> Epoch enforcement path. Preserve `off-box-body-disposition`, `introspectable-schema-decode?`, `decode-schema-marks`, `classify-decoded`, all emit-side stamping, and the Epoch projector/tests.

## Risks / retained contracts

The vars are public at the namespace level but are absent from the generated API manifest and user API docs; an unknown downstream direct-require remains possible. Do not weaken fail-closed behavior or remove tests that exercise the actual projector. Keep schema root-mark behavior covered through `classify-decoded` and keep opaque schemas classified `:omit` by the live disposition function.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The three zero-production-consumer vars and their direct self-tests are removed, or a real shipped consumer is added and the documented call path is made true.
2. Privacy-body and integration-test prose names `off-box-body-disposition` stamping plus Epoch `omit-off-box-http-bodies` as the actual off-box path; it does not claim Epoch calls an HTTP direct projector.
3. Root sensitive and large marks remain tested through `classify-decoded`; introspectable schemas still stamp `:classify`, and unschematized/opaque decodes still stamp `:omit`.
4. Existing Epoch JVM/CLJS off-box projection tests and HTTP privacy JVM/CLJS tests pass, including raw 4xx/5xx/decode-failure and retry-body fail-closed cases.
5. Repo-wide searches show no stale reference to the removed helper/marker names and the API manifest remains unchanged unless compatibility policy explicitly promotes a retained API.
close_reason:
Confirmed and removed in PR #9081. This is PRIVACY code, so the disposition was gated on two questions answered before anything was deleted.

ONE — DOES THE LIVE OFF-BOX PATH DEPEND ON IT? No, and it never could have. The shipped path is: the emit site applies classify-decoded ON-BOX (transport.cljc:401 for :rf.http/replied's :value, :868 for :rf.http/accept-failure's :decoded, :1466) and stamps off-box-body-disposition forward under :rf.http/off-box-body (transport.cljc:435, :768); re-frame.epoch.tool-pair's omit-off-box-http-bodies then reads that stamp and substitutes :rf/redacted at the operation's body-slot paths for an :omit event, passing a :classify event through because its per-slot marks were already applied on-box. Epoch deliberately carries no HTTP-artefact dependency, so it could not call off-box-classify-body even in principle — the bead's claim that the documented call path does not exist is correct.

TWO — IS ANY PRIVACY GUARANTEE DROPPED? No: the live composition is EXACTLY the removed function on both arms. Introspectable schema -> classify-decoded applied on-box, stamp :classify, Epoch passes through = off-box-classify-body's first arm. Anything else — unschematized, opaque keyword registry ref, compiled schema object — -> classify-decoded is an identity or mark-less no-op, but the stamp is :omit and Epoch substitutes :rf/redacted, the SAME sentinel off-box-body-marker held = its second arm. The fail-closed property for an opaque ref (rf2-y1pgdl) comes from the stamp gating on introspectable-schema-decode?, not from the removed helper, so it is untouched.

AND NO DELETED TEST WAS THE SOLE ASSERTION OF AN INVARIANT. Each removed row has a live counterpart on the shipped path, checked one by one: unschematized omission and opaque-registry-ref / compiled-schema omission are asserted through off-box-body-disposition returning :omit (off-box-disposition-omits-* rows, kept), and schema classification through the classify-decoded per-slot rows (kept). For whole-body-sensitive-mark? the deftest whole-body-root-sensitive-redacts-everything asserted BOTH the predicate and the PRODUCT behaviour; only the predicate's own call was dropped and the (= :rf/redacted (classify-decoded ...)) assertion beside it was KEPT (AC3). Nothing that exercises the actual projector was touched.

CENSUS. Two instruments over git-tracked files with .beads excluded, line-oriented and whitespace-flattened, AGREEING exactly: off-box-classify-body 20/20, whole-body-sensitive-mark? 4/4, off-box-body-marker 5/5 — all confined to privacy_body.cljc's own definitions and docstrings plus their own test file (and one prose mention in http_privacy_integration_test.clj). ZERO production consumers, and zero references in spec/, docs/, tools/ or examples/, so no spec change was needed (AC5). CONTROL needle off-box-body-disposition fired at 17/17 across five files INCLUDING transport.cljc and spec/014-HTTPRequests.md — a live control, not a zero.

PROSE CORRECTED (AC2): the namespace docstring, the two section comments and off-box-body-disposition's own docstring no longer claim Epoch applies an HTTP direct projector; they name the real stamp -> Epoch enforcement path. The http_privacy_integration_test.clj:551 comment no longer cites the deleted unit test as part of the end-to-end path. Worth recording as a process note: three of these prose replacements silently NO-OPPED on the first attempt because the anchors used LF against this CRLF tree — nothing errored and the edit read clean; caught only by re-running the residual grep, which is why every removal here was verified by census afterwards rather than by inspecting the patch.

GATES: http clojure -M:test 506 tests / 3884 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0, including the raw 4xx/5xx, decode-failure and retry-body fail-closed rows (AC4). Consolidated CLJS 11209 tests / 55849 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0. Epoch's off-box projection suites were not re-run locally (that artefact was outside the touched surface and its files are unchanged); CI runs them on PR #9081, which is green at 51 SUCCESS / 35 SKIPPED / 0 failures with All required checks passed.

title: pair-mcp docs: retire stale bash-shim compatibility promises
description:
## Finding
The Pair-MCP package still presents the retired bash/babashka shims as a supported, mix-and-match transport in several current-state documents, although the shim implementation was deleted.

## Evidence
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md` lines 7-9 and 651-657 say the shims still ship, still work, and are not slated for removal.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/Principles.md` lines 117-143 and `spec/API.md` lines 379-405 make the same current compatibility promise.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md` Design Lock #6 (roughly lines 485-541) and its summary row (around line 958) still say both transports ship side-by-side with no removal scheduled.
- `git ls-files skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts` returns no files. Commit `31594b44c3` (`chore(pair): remove retired bash/babashka transport`) deleted the wrappers, operations, and shim tests under rf2-dduetj.
- Current repository documentation elsewhere already records MCP as the only implementation (`skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md`, `docs/TESTING.md`, and Pair-MCP input/design specs).

A related closed predecessor, rf2-435ah, corrected this claim only in `skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/**`; it did not cover the Pair-MCP README/spec tree listed above.

## Impact
Operators and agent authors can spend time looking for nonexistent scripts or design integrations around a transport that cannot be invoked. The stale promise also obscures the deliberate MCP-only migration.

## Proposed disposition
Rewrite current-state sections to say Pair MCP is the sole supported transport. Preserve genuinely historical comparisons, but mark Design Lock #6 and its summary entry as superseded by rf2-dduetj / commit `31594b44c3` instead of silently deleting the design history.

## Risks / retained contracts
Do not erase historical rationale or unrelated references that explain why MCP replaced the shim. Do not alter the live MCP protocol or compatibility guarantees.
acceptance_criteria:
1. README, Principles, and API no longer claim that bash/babashka shims ship, work, or may be mixed with MCP.
2. DESIGN-RATIONALE marks Lock #6 and its summary row as superseded, naming the MCP-only decision/removal lineage.
3. A repository search finds no present-tense support promise for the deleted shim; any surviving mentions are unambiguously historical.
4. Documentation link/slug checks covering the touched files pass, and changed tables/headings are manually checked where no renderer/gate applies.
close_reason: Done in PR #9076. Premise re-verified: commit 31594b44c3 (2026-07-11, 'chore(pair): remove retired bash/babashka transport', rf2-dduetj) deleted scripts/ops.clj, bencode.clj, six .sh wrappers and the shim tests; git ls-files skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts returns 0 against a control of 57 for tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src. All four documents carried the stale promise at the claimed locations. Design Lock #6 keeps its question, options, pick, reasoning and date VERBATIM under a dated DISCHARGED banner naming rf2-dduetj / 31594b44c3 — the lock was not overturned, it played out as its own final Why bullet anticipated ('future removal is cheap ... the decision is reversible'); summary-table row 6 marked discharged in-place. Name-mapping tables retained and relabelled historical so an old runbook naming a deleted script still resolves. Two present-tense claims BEYOND the bead's list were found and past-tensed: DESIGN-RATIONALE lines 280 and 299 ('The bash shims ship six') inside Lock #4's evolution narrative. Note for the record: the bead and brief located DESIGN-RATIONALE.md differently — it is tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md; there is no repo-root spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md. title: re-frame.hicasso.server is still unscanned by the api-manifest: enrol implementation/hicasso/src in roster-covered-roots with a :cljs-only sidecar row
description:
The third of the three namespaces rf2-8arzr.7 found shipping unscanned. PR #9040 fixed the other two and left this one deliberately: implementation/hicasso/** was held by PR #9035 while that work ran.

MEASURED (at 375d5dd899, by rf2-8arzr.7): re-frame.hicasso.server (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs) has genuinely public vars — payload-script, document, render, render-body — and ZERO ^:no-doc markers. spec/API.md:328 names render-body as 'the body-only entry a server bundle calls' and tiers all three crossing namespaces :implementation, 'on the same footing as re-frame.ssr.ring's own vars'. Re-measure at tip before acting: #9035 landed on that tree since.

IT IS CLJS-ONLY, so it does NOT go in jvm-namespaces — the JVM generator cannot require it. It needs :cljs-only rows in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn, which is already one of the three ways the restored roster gate accounts for a namespace: gen.clj's cljs-only-namespaces arm was built for exactly this case and is covered by a test (a-cljs-only-sidecar-row-accounts-for-a-namespace, which pins re-frame.hicasso.server by name in both directions).

THE COST, and it is the reason this is its own bead rather than a one-liner: adding 'implementation/hicasso/src' to roster-covered-roots obliges a classification for EVERY namespace under it — 25 unenrolled at last count — each recorded in internal-namespaces with a grouping comment, or enrolled. That is the same deliberate per-tree work #9040 did for the two SSR trees (33 internal entries). Do not add the root without doing it; the gate refuses to build otherwise, which is the point of it.

Also consider whether the CLJS enumeration probe (implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/, run by npm run test:cljs) should cover the namespace, which is what lets its rows carry :runtime-verified? true rather than false.
notes:
WORKED BY PR #9045 (rf2-8arzr.7 + rf2-3ne8 + rf2-63fw + rf2-ypom cluster). HALF LANDED; THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN FOR THE OTHER HALF.

LANDED: the four :cljs-only sidecar rows for re-frame.hicasso.server (payload-script, document, render, render-body) at :tier :implementation :owner 011 :status v1 :runtime-verified? false. Re-measured at tip: still exactly those four public vars, still zero ^:no-doc. It is CLJS-only because the ns :requires ["react-dom/server"], so ns-publics can never reach it. Manifest 506 -> 510. That closes the SHIPPING defect rf2-8arzr.7 named: the namespace is no longer unmanifested.

NOT LANDED, and this is the finding: implementation/hicasso/src was NOT added to roster-covered-roots.

NAMESPACE COUNT, derived with the generator's own namespaces-under rather than by file count: 26 namespaces under the root (26 .clj* files, all base paths distinct, so no .cljc/.cljs pair collapses). One (re-frame.hicasso) is already enrolled => 25 unenrolled, which matches this bead's own figure exactly. Confirmed by planting the root and running --check: exit 2, all 25 listed by name.

WHY THE ROOT WAS NOT ADDED. This bead assumes the 25 are 'each recorded in internal-namespaces with a grouping comment, or enrolled', with most going internal. They are not. At least FIVE are genuine public authoring surfaces, each with a require-me-directly example in its own ns docstring: re-frame.hicasso.forms (buffered-field), .motion (presence), .overlay (popover, modal), .native (use-sub, use-frame), .substrate (adapter, installed via rf/init!). tool and evidence are :tooling by their own docstrings and would be fine.

Their honest tier is :advanced/:adapter, which is docs-eligible. MEASURED with a control, not inferred, via doc_api_check/coverage-problems (public + pure): forms and substrate each yield {:kind :page-missing}, while the same-shaped control re-frame.hicasso/sub (which HAS docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md) yields (). So enrolling them honestly obliges FIVE new docs/api/*.md pages. docs/** was outside PR #9045's permitted file list.

The alternatives were all false records and were refused: tiering authoring surfaces :implementation purely to dodge the docs obligation, or putting forms/motion/overlay in internal-namespaces, which contradicts that roster's own docstring ('Nothing here is published, documented or rowed'). The gate was NOT weakened.

WHAT REMAINS: a tiering ruling for those five (plus tool/evidence at :tooling), the docs/api pages that ruling obliges, then adding the root. That is a decision plus a docs dispatch, not a mechanical follow-on.

PROBE QUESTION ANSWERED: NO. :runtime-verified? false is correct. Covering the ns would pull react-dom/server into the api-manifest probe's build graph, which is a shared-build change rather than a row change; #9040 set the same precedent for its two.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST, on the finding manifest-a returned rather than worked around. THE FIVE ARE PUBLIC, THEY GET PAGES, AND THIS BEAD SPLITS.

WHAT THE WORKER FOUND, and it is the right call to have stopped: both this bead and my brief assumed the 25 unenrolled namespaces under implementation/hicasso/src were mostly internal. AT LEAST FIVE ARE PUBLIC AUTHORING SURFACES — forms, motion, overlay, native, substrate — each carrying a require-me-directly example in its own docstring. It proved the consequence with a control rather than asserting it: doc_api_check/coverage-problems yields :page-missing for the target and () for a same-shaped control that has a page. So the honest tier is docs-eligible, which obliges five new docs/api/*.md pages, and docs/** was outside its fence.

THE RULING: TIER THEM HONESTLY AND WRITE THE PAGES. Do not reach for ^:no-doc to make the gate quiet. substrate is what an app requires to call (rf/init! substrate/adapter); these are not plumbing. Under the stance — excellent ergonomics, low friction, a library that is a masterpiece — a public authoring surface with no documentation page is precisely the friction we exist to remove, and the gate has just done its job by refusing to let five of them ship unrecorded. That is the opposite of gold plating: it is the gate catching a real gap the manifest was blind to.

SO THIS BEAD SPLITS, and the ordering is forced by the gate rather than by preference:
  (1) A DOCS dispatch writes the five docs/api/*.md pages. It needs docs/** and cannot run while another worker holds that tree.
  (2) The SAME PR (or one immediately after, but the same worker) adds implementation/hicasso/src to roster-covered-roots and classifies all 26 namespaces — five enrolled docs-eligible, the rest recorded in internal-namespaces with grouping comments. The gate REFUSES TO BUILD until every namespace under an added root is accounted for, which is the point of it, so the root and the classification are one commit.
Doing (2) before (1) reds the tree; doing (1) without (2) leaves the manifest still blind. One worker, both halves, docs/** free.

WHAT ALREADY LANDED AND MUST NOT BE REDONE: the four :cljs-only rows are in (manifest 506 -> 510), which fixes the actual shipping defect for re-frame.hicasso.server. This bead remainder is the ROOT plus the classification plus the five pages.

AND NOTE THE NUMBER IS CONFIRMED, NOT ASSUMED: the worker derived 26 namespaces using the generator own namespaces-under rather than the 26-FILE count I gave it in the brief, and 1 already enrolled leaves 25 unenrolled — matching this bead original figure exactly, by a different route. That is the kind of agreement worth trusting.

rf2-qvhx (how far the roster gate should widen, 243 namespaces under uncovered trees) is a SEPARATE and larger question and is not settled here. This ruling covers one tree.
close_reason: Enrolled implementation/hicasso/src in roster-covered-roots and classified all 26 namespaces; five docs/api pages written. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9053. Manifest 510 -> 528, gen --check exit 0, api-manifest suite 91 tests 0 failures. doc_api_check coverage 174 -> 182 eligible vars each with page+member. MKDOCS.YML NAV ENTRIES ARE NOT NEEDED — measured at source (validation.nav.omitted_files defaults to info, mkdocs.yml sets no validation.nav key, --strict promotes WARNING not INFO) and by planted probe page (strict build exit 0 with the page in the omitted list). The five pages ARE unnavigated in the left nav; docs/api/README.md (which is in nav) indexes all five. FOLLOW-UP RECOMMENDED: widen a fence to add the five mkdocs.yml nav entries for parity. Count derived with the generator's own namespaces-under: 26 total, door enrolled + hicasso.server accounted by #9045, leaving 24 unaccounted (bead said 25, written pre-#9045) = 5 public + 2 tooling + 17 impl.*. Tiers :advanced for forms/motion/overlay/native, :adapter for substrate (matching re-frame.adapter.reagent/uix), :tooling owner Tool-Pair for tool/evidence. spine-fns not rowed: it is ^:no-doc, which gen.clj:403 drops from every JVM namespace. No ^:no-doc added, gate not weakened. Coverage gate proven to bite on this tree by a planted member-heading rename (exit 1, named the var, ROOT printed this worktree; restored and blob-hash verified).

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): the ops.md catalogue-exemption ruling and the package's own spec contradict each other
description:
FOUND BY worker pairskill-e while executing rf2-wgvyx's ruling (PR #9037). NOT a re-argument of that ruling — a contradiction it leaves standing, which needs a maintainer call rather than a worker's reflex.

THE MAYOR RULING on rf2-wgvyx (2026-09-03 03:2x AUSEST) says: 'SPLIT THE HICASSO-EVIDENCE BLOCK OUT... THE CATALOGUE EXEMPTION IS REFUSED FOR THIS LEAF.'

THE SPLIT IT ORDERED WAS ALREADY DONE — eaf6591310 took the Hicasso block out WITH the screen-read block, in the same commit. Evidence on rf2-wgvyx.

SO THE REFUSAL NOW HAS NO EXECUTABLE REMAINDER, and that is the problem:

1. ops.md is 220 lines / 46,461 LF-normalised bytes — 2.8x the 16 KB per-leaf ceiling in skills/README.md.
2. Every section left in it is one rf2-wgvyx EXPLICITLY FORBIDS splitting: 'Do NOT split hot-reload or the v1 map (locked + tested), and do not split the op tables (that is the catalogue the exemption is for)'. Remaining headings: Read, Frames, Write, Trace, Live watch, Signal recording, Hot-reload coordination, Time-travel, Dropped from v1.
3. The hot-reload protocol and v1 surface-map placement is LOCKED by skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:135 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:33, and tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj reads ops.md by anchor (ops.md#hot-reload-coordination).
4. AND THE PACKAGE'S OWN SPEC STILL GRANTS THE EXEMPTION IN WRITING, in both places, unchanged: design.md:135 'the two catalogue leaves (ops.md, recipes.md) run longer where a split would not reduce tokens-per-session', and authoring-prompt.md:49 the same clause. A future re-authoring pass reads those and keeps ops.md whole, because that is what they say.

So the tree currently asserts both things at once: the ruling refuses ops.md the exemption, the package spec grants it.

THE DECISION NEEDED is one of three, and it is Mike's or the mayor's, not a worker's:
(a) RECORD THE EXEMPTION HONESTLY — accept ops.md as a documented exception in skills/README.md Leaf size discipline with the reasoning, and leave design.md:135 as is. rf2-wgvyx's own DESCRIPTION already names this as the honest alternative: 'If the maintainer would rather keep ops.md whole, the honest alternative is to record ops.md as an accepted exception... the current state is neither.'
(b) NAME WHICH LOCKED SECTION MOVES, and lift the lock on it in design.md + authoring-prompt.md in the same PR, re-pointing the prompt-regression anchors.
(c) RESTATE THE REFUSAL as applying only to non-catalogue blocks, which is what it in fact achieved, and strike the ceiling claim against ops.md.

Note recipes.md sits in exactly the same position (424 lines / 46,086 B) and is the exemption's own worked example, so whichever way this goes should say whether it binds recipes.md too.

NOT URGENT AND NOT A BUG: nothing is broken, no gate is red, no reader is misled by ops.md's content. What is wrong is that two normative records disagree, so the next re-authoring pass gets a different answer depending on which it reads.
notes:
MAYOR ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, 2026-09-03 04:2x AUSEST — THIS BEAD EXISTS BECAUSE MY RULING CONTRADICTED A NORMATIVE RECORD I DID NOT CHECK, AND THE WORKER WAS RIGHT NOT TO RE-ARGUE IT.

WHAT I DID. Two hours ago I ruled that ops.md is REFUSED the catalogue exemption, reasoning that a leaf from which a self-contained block can be lifted entire is not catalogue-shaped. I derived that from the first split's success and from the leaf still measuring 46 KB. I did not check whether any record already GRANTED the exemption. Two do, in writing: skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:135 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:49.

SO THERE ARE NOW TWO NORMATIVE RECORDS IN DISAGREEMENT, and that is a maintainer call rather than something a worker should resolve by picking the newer one. Filing it was the correct response and I am not overriding it here.

AND MY RULING'S FACTUAL PREMISE WAS ALSO WRONG, which the same worker established: the Hicasso-evidence block did NOT remain in ops.md. It came out WITH the screen-read block in the same commit eaf6591310 — 105 lines removed, screen-reads.md created with 106, carrying all three sections the bead's own recommendation nominated, Hicasso evidence among them. ops.md's only case-insensitive hicasso match is a Contents pointer. I inferred a remaining block from the bead's TITLE naming two things and from the leaf still measuring 46 KB; both facts were true and the inference was not. The leaf is 46 KB because of the catalogue the bead ITSELF forbids splitting — which is the same fact that makes the exemption question live rather than settled.

SO THE HONEST STATE IS: my ruling directed work already done, on a premise that was wrong, against a contract that already said the opposite. The worker measured, invoked my own STOP clause rather than inventing a block to lift, and shipped the bead's real live remainder instead — a forbidden SKILL -> screen-reads -> ops chain that skills/README.md and authoring-prompt.md:49 both prohibit, with a regression assertion that had been weak independently (a bare 'ops.md' substring test passes on the provenance sentence 'split out of ops.md' with the safety rule entirely absent).

FOR WHOEVER RESOLVES THIS BEAD: the question is not 'was the mayor right'. It is whether re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md, as a locked catalogue its own bead forbids splitting, should carry the exemption its spec already grants — and if so, whether skills/README.md's exemption bullet should name it the way it now names recipes.md and known-frictions.md. Decide the CONTRACT, then make the three records agree. Do not resolve it by deleting whichever record is easiest to edit.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 04:2x AUSEST. I AM WITHDRAWING MY OWN REFUSAL. The catalogue exemption APPLIES to ops.md remainder; RECORD THE EXCEPTION and do not split further.

WHY I AM REVERSING MYSELF, stated plainly because a ruling that quietly changes is worse than one that was wrong. On rf2-wgvyx I wrote "THE CATALOGUE EXEMPTION IS REFUSED FOR THIS LEAF". That refusal was wrong on two axes, both of which the pairskill-e worker demonstrated and I acknowledged when filing this bead: the split I ordered had ALREADY BEEN DONE (eaf6591310 took the Hicasso-evidence block out WITH the screen-read block, in one commit), and I refused an exemption that TWO EXISTING RECORDS ALREADY GRANT (skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:135 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:49). A mayor ruling does not outrank a landed record it did not read.

WHAT IS LEFT IS EXACTLY WHAT THE EXEMPTION IS FOR, and my own ruling says so. ops.md is 220 lines / 46,461 LF-normalised bytes, 2.8x the 16 KB per-leaf ceiling. title: skill(re-frame2-pair): SKILL.md/recipes teach eval-cljs as the first-class long-tail workhorse; the get-re-frame2-pair-instructions text SKILL.md:143 routes to says "eval-cljs is the last resort, not the default"
description:
CLAIM (two authorities the agent reads in the same session contradict each other on the eval-cljs posture)

skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:206 (§Style guidance):
> **Prefer a structured op when one FITS the gesture; `eval-cljs` is the workhorse for the long tail, not a last resort.**

skills/re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md:38 (§eval-cljs is the workhorse):
> **The rule:** *prefer a structured op WHEN ONE FITS the gesture — including the dedicated write tools for named rewrites; for the long tail and recovery, `eval-cljs` is first-class, not a last resort.*

skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:143 tells the agent to call `get-re-frame2-pair-instructions` for "six routing rules for which tool to reach for". That tool's text, tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_re_frame2_pair_instructions.cljs:61-63:
> Behind all six: a typed tool validates its arguments and names its failure, `eval-cljs` does neither — so `eval-cljs` is the last resort, not the default.

TRUTH AT TIP

Both texts are live. The SKILL.md/recipes wording landed 2026-06-03 (344754178f, rf2-re6as) and was elaborated since (recipes.md §eval-cljs is the workhorse enumerates four first-class eval gestures: epoch forensics via find-where/cascade-of/epoch-diff, arbitrary-selector DOM reads, cross-referencing, and recovery). The server wording landed later, 2026-08-11 (eb9f95b4aa, rf2-wyza, "replace the onboarding tool catalogue with routing rules"), and was written as a one-line preamble to the six rules, not as a reversal of the skill's posture. Nothing at tip reconciles them, and `check_skill_mcp_drift.py` compares tool names only, so this drift is invisible to every gate.

IMPACT

An agent that follows SKILL.md:143 reads "last resort" after having just read "not a last resort". The skill's own recipes (post-mortem, forensics, Story enumeration, frame-diff, dom-fire-click) are ALL eval-cljs-shaped and have no typed tool, so an agent that takes the server's line literally hesitates on exactly the gestures the skill wants it to run. Whichever text wins, the other is misinformation.

FIX SHAPE

One PR, two files. Align the server preamble to the skill's rule (the richer, deliberately-taught one): e.g. "a typed tool validates its arguments and names its failure, `eval-cljs` does neither — so reach for the typed tool whenever one FITS the gesture; `eval-cljs` is first-class for the long tail (epoch forensics, cross-referencing, Story enumeration, recovery), not the default for a gesture a typed tool owns." Then add one clause to SKILL.md:143 saying the instructions text restates the same rule, so the two cannot be read as competing. If Mike instead rules that "last resort" is the intended posture, the fix inverts: rewrite SKILL.md:206 and recipes.md:34-47 and the README's "Ask a question that doesn't have a pre-baked op" example — but that is the larger rewrite and contradicts three recipes, so the first shape is recommended.

GATE

tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp `onboarding_routing_test` pins the `## Routing rules` section's PARSE contract (backticked tool names inside the section) — it will stay green across a wording change but must still pass; `npm test` in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp. skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj for the SKILL.md side. No gate compares the two texts' meaning — verify by hand and quote both lines in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE

`grep -n "last resort" skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md skills/re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_re_frame2_pair_instructions.cljs` returns lines that all state the SAME rule (typed tool when one fits; eval-cljs first-class for the long tail), and the pair-mcp onboarding test is green.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): breaking-changes.md index drift — at-a-glance mis-types M-58/M-59, no M-72 trigger row, stale "two M-73 headings" (corpus is M-74, uncited by the skill)
description:
CLAIM. skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md calls itself the "one-page index of every M-/O-rule by trigger surface" (SKILL.md:100) and carries a second copy of the corpus's Type classification in its "Type A vs Type B — at a glance" paragraph. Four index facts in the file no longer match the corpus at tip:

 (a) line 88: "**The corpus carries two `M-73` headings:** the event-registration collapse ... and a separate v2-pre-rename **machine-identity naming** rule ... cite that one by its full heading, not the bare `M-73`".
 (b) line 187 (Type-A line) lists `M-58` and `M-59` as Type A with no Type-B qualifier.
 (c) the Required table (lines 25-86) has NO row for M-72, though `inject-cofx` / `:rf.world/inputs` / ctx-shaped `reg-cofx` are v1 surfaces; M-72 appears only in the at-a-glance line (189) and the preserved-list prose (268, 270).
 (d) neither Type line mentions M-31a (corpus: Type B).

TRUTH AT TIP (migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md).
 (a) The corpus has ONE `### M-73.` heading (line 879) and the machine-identity rule is now `### M-74.` (line 2817). `python scripts/check_skill_migration_cites.py --verbose` reports "MIGRATION.md defines 80 rule ids; skill references cite 79 distinct ids" — M-74 is the one id no skill leaf cites (`rg -n 'M-74' skills/re-frame-migration/` returns nothing). Line 88's disambiguation advice now sends an agent looking for a heading that does not exist.
 (b) Corpus M-58 (line 2348): "**Type B** (semantic — the rewrite depends on which data was being scrubbed and where it lives)". Corpus M-59 (line 2384): "**Type A** for the `at-boundary` boundary-validation ref; **Type B** for `unwrap`". The at-a-glance paragraph contradicts both. (Both rules are v2-pre-rename-only and live in pre-rename-upgrades.md, so a v1→v2 reader is not harmed — but this paragraph is the file's own second classification copy, and it is the copy that has drifted.)
 (c) Corpus M-72 (lines 836-878): "**Type B** for the durable-read judgment, **Type A** for the mechanical reshape" — a v1 surface (v1 apps used `inject-cofx` and `:now`/UUID cofx). The table is keyed by v1 trigger surface; an agent grepping it for `inject-cofx` finds no row. (SKILL.md:99 does route to causal-world-inputs.md, so the miss is index-level, not workflow-level.)
 (d) Corpus M-31a (line 1433): "**Type B** (touch test-namespace requires)" — the at-a-glance paragraph enumerates every other pre-rename id (M-55..M-69) and omits this one.

IMPACT. Index drift only — no rewrite target is wrong. But the at-a-glance paragraph is a duplicate of the table's own `Type` column and is the copy that has drifted, which is the standing family hazard (skills/README.md:63-70: "routes and sequences but never duplicates").

FIX SHAPE (one PR, primarily one file). (1) Line 88: replace the "two M-73 headings" sentence with "M-74 (machine-identity naming: `:spawn-id` / de-overloaded `:machine-id`) is v2-pre-rename-only and lives in pre-rename-upgrades.md" — and add the M-74 row to pre-rename-upgrades.md (that leaf is partition-C territory; land the row in the same PR so the cites gate reads 80/80). (2) Add an M-72 row to the Required table: trigger `inject-cofx` interceptor / `:rf.world/inputs` / ctx-shaped `reg-cofx` / `:now`-`random-uuid`-storage cofx; Type `A / B`; summary = reshape is mechanical, durable-read judgment is Type B; link `causal-world-inputs.md`. (3) The at-a-glance paragraph: RECOMMENDED — cut it to the hybrid-halves notes only (which half of M-5/M-16/M-17/M-21/M-23/M-26/M-30/M-34/M-40/M-42/M-71/M-72/M-73 is which) and delete the flat id lists, so the table's `Type` column is the single classification source; MINIMUM — move M-58 to the Type-B line, mark M-59 `A (at-boundary) / B (unwrap)`, add M-31a to Type B.

GATE. `python scripts/check_skill_migration_cites.py --verbose` (expect "cite 80 distinct ids" after M-74 lands in pre-rename-upgrades.md); `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (new anchors); `python scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py --verbose` (BREAKING_CHANGES_MD is on its scan list — must stay green). Classification correctness has no script — verify by hand against the corpus's `**Type` line for each id touched.

ACCEPTANCE. Line 88 names M-74 and routes it to pre-rename-upgrades.md; the cites gate reports 80/80; the Required table has an M-72 row; the at-a-glance paragraph either no longer enumerates ids or agrees with the corpus for M-58, M-59, M-31a.
