title: skill(re-frame2): examples-map.md omits five shipped examples (core/flows, infinite_feed, linearlite, resources_ssr, hicasso/login) and carries six stale example claims
description:
`skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md` promises (line 7, and README.md:26) "a one-paragraph index of every worked example", and SKILL.md's pattern table routes "Pattern → example app" through it. At tip it omits five shipped examples and carries a handful of claims that are no longer true of the examples it does describe.

CLAIM 1 — completeness. The map indexes 19 example directories. `ls -d examples/*/*/ examples/*/*/*/` at tip shows five more that no paragraph names:

- `examples/core/flows/` — the canonical Flows exemplar (`examples/README.md:87`). **`references/fundamentals/flows.md:72` already cites `examples/core/flows/core.cljs` as its canonical mini-example source**, so the fundamentals leaf points at an example the map does not know about.
- `examples/capabilities/resources/infinite_feed/` — infinite resource / load-more (`examples/README.md:120`, EP-0021).
- `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/` — the optimistic-mutation write-side flagship (`examples/README.md:121`, EP-0019).
- `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/` — resource SSR preload + hydration (`examples/README.md:129`).
- `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` — the Hicasso substrate example (`examples/README.md:72`); one line under "Adapter smoke-pairs" pointing at `reagent-migration` is enough, since Hicasso authoring is out of this skill's scope (views.md §Hicasso).

CLAIM 2 — stale descriptions (each quoted verbatim, with the truth at tip):

- `examples-map.md:30` (login): "a Malli machine-snapshot schema + a browserless headless test". `ls examples/core/login/` = README.md, core.cljs, index.html, model.cljs, stories.cljs, stories.index.html, stories_host.cljs — no test file. Examples are test-free by ruling (CLAUDE.md §Build & Test, rf2-8cevm, locked 2026-05-19).
- `examples-map.md:62` (state_machine_walkthrough): "with smoke tests for every section. Browser layer drives the canonical lockout scenario". `ls examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/` = README.md, core.cljc, index.html, views.cljs — no tests, same ruling.
- `examples-map.md:66` (todomvc): "an interceptor-based localStorage persistence pattern". `examples/core/todomvc/events.cljs:45` persists via `(rf/reg-fx :todo.storage/save ...)` and `db.cljs:81` reads via a recordable `reg-cofx`; there is no interceptor in the example (`git grep -n "interceptors\|reg-interceptor" examples/core/todomvc` is empty). `fx.md:53` already teaches the same file as the fx-based shape, so the map contradicts the leaf.
- `examples-map.md:22` (counter_with_stories): "four variants exercising three of the seven canonical `:rf.assert/*` events". At tip `tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories.cljs` has 30 `reg-variant` calls and uses six distinct `:rf.assert/*` events (`caused`, `dispatched`, `effect-emitted`, `no-cascade-rerender`, `path-equals`, `sub-equals`).
- `examples-map.md:14` (counter): "One `reg-event`, one `reg-sub`". `examples/core/counter/core.cljs` has three `rf/reg-event` and one `rf/reg-sub`.
- `examples-map.md:90` (Adapter smoke-pairs): "Per [Spec 006 §Adapter shipping convention](../../spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md)". The heading `## Adapter shipping convention` lives at `spec/Conventions.md:1798`; Spec 006 has no such heading. The map's own line 9 cites Conventions correctly. (The link resolves to a file, so `check_doc_slugs.py` stays green — the citation is wrong, not broken.)
- Footer `examples-map.md:109`: "@ main `89bd9c3`" — that commit is 2026-05-12; the file has been edited five times since (`git log --oneline -5 -- skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md`). Either refresh the pin or drop the pin claim.

IMPACT

Routing: an agent authoring flows, an infinite feed, optimistic mutations, or resource SSR follows SKILL.md → examples-map and finds no example, then either synthesises a shape (contrary to cardinal rule 5) or greps blind. Correctness: an agent pointed at todomvc for "interceptor-based persistence" finds none; one pointed at login/walkthrough for "the headless test" finds no test to match.

FIX SHAPE

One file, `skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md`: add five paragraphs (source: the corresponding `examples/README.md` rows and each example's README), correct the six quoted phrases, fix the Conventions citation, refresh or drop the footer pin. Keep it catalogue-shaped (one paragraph per example) — the file is already 19.6 KB and passes the family-contract catalogue test, so do not split it.

GATE

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers the new relative links and anchors under `skills/`; `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --verbose` covers in-package links. No gate reads the descriptions — verify each paragraph against `ls` + the example's README by hand and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE

Every directory in `ls -d examples/*/*/ examples/*/*/*/` (excluding `_shared` and `managed_http_counter/api`) has a paragraph or an explicit one-line pointer in examples-map.md; the six quoted phrases above are gone; `git grep -n "Spec 006 §Adapter shipping" skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md` is empty; both gates exit 0.

title: flake(http): supersede-stale poll-until backstop times out under CI load, redding unrelated PRs
description:
implementation/http test `re-frame.http-reply-lowering-test/supersede-distinct-work-ids-and-canonical-stale-trace` (http_reply_lowering_test.clj) fails intermittently on loaded CI runners with `poll-until timed out — supersede-stale`, reported as `0 failures, 1 errors` and exit 1 from `clojure -M:test` in implementation/http.

## Observed

- 2026-09-01, PR #8873 (a routing-only diff that cannot reach this code path): `:elapsed-ms 30022`, i.e. the full 30 s backstop elapsed. Re-running the identical tree on a fresh CI head was green with no code change.
- The test`s own source comment records a PRIOR occurrence of the same class and the mitigation taken then: the backstop was raised from 5 s to 30 s because "the async supersede landed AFTER the window, timing the machine, not the canonicalisation (it redded unrelated PRs, e.g. #6817)".

So the 5 s -> 30 s raise reduced the rate but did not remove the failure mode; 30 s is now demonstrably marginal too.

## Why it matters

This test is inside a surface-gated job, and implementation/http declares day8/re-frame2-routing as a {:local/root} dependency, so ANY routing-only change schedules the http job. A flake here therefore reds PRs whose diff provably cannot reach the code under test, and each red costs a diagnosis dispatch. PR #8873 cost exactly one.

## Shape of the problem, not a prescribed fix

The wait is already signal-based rather than a fixed sleep (`poll-until` on a predicate over delivered replies plus a `:rf.http/stale-suppressed` trace row), which is the right structure — the remaining `:timeout-ms` is a pure backstop. The question is whether the supersede round-trip can be made deterministic at the test boundary (await the transport reply and the trace row on a latch rather than polling), so the backstop is unreachable rather than merely generous. Raising the bound a third time is the option to weigh against that, not the obvious answer.

Deliberately NOT diagnosed here: whether the timeout indicates real contention in the supersede path under load, or purely runner scheduling. Worth one look before choosing a remedy — a genuinely slow supersede under load would be a product finding rather than a test one.

## Non-goals

- No change to supersede/stale-suppression semantics; those are what the test correctly pins.
- Not a licence to delete or weaken the assertion.
notes:
VERDICT (PR #8889, branch worker/http-robust-o9e15): FIXED, and the theory recorded on this bead and in the test source was WRONG.

FINDING 1 - the stale-suppression trace is NOT async. handlers/managed-handler calls registry/supersede! and then transport/emit-superseded-stale-trace! inline in the fx phase, so the :rf.http/stale-suppressed row has already landed before the SECOND dispatch-sync returns. Probed: present with ZERO wait. The source comment claiming a real async round-trip (transport reply -> reply lowering -> app dispatch -> stale trace) was factually wrong and is removed.

FINDING 2 - the failure mode is ABSENCE, not lateness. registry/supersede! returns nil when nothing is in flight under the request-id. The test gate was a CountDownLatch(1) whose FIRST act inside the handler was its own .countDown, so the following .await returned immediately and the gate never held request #1 at all. Request #1 was free to finish its whole loopback round trip in the gap between the two dispatch-sync calls; two app replies were then delivered, no supersede ever happened, and poll-until sat out its full backstop waiting for a row that could not arrive. That is why the 5s -> 30s raise reduced the rate without removing the mode, and why a third raise cannot help: no bound is large enough for an event that is never emitted.

REPAIR - a new start-held-server! holds every exchange until the TEST releases it, so #1 cannot finalise before #2 is issued and the supersede becomes a property of the ordering rather than of machine speed. The stale row is then asserted SYNCHRONOUSLY (the 30s poll is gone entirely), and the one genuinely async step, the surviving request app reply, is awaited on a CountDownLatch the reply handler itself counts down. The sibling supersede-suppresses-prior-app-reply carried the identical no-op gate and the identical latent race and moves to the same harness.

PRODUCT FINDING - none. This bead deliberately left open whether the timeout indicated real contention in the supersede path under load. It does not: the supersede path is correct and synchronous, and the test simply was not exercising it when the race was lost. The one seam worth recording is that a superseded attempt TRANSPORT completion offers no observable completion signal a test can await, which is why the repair holds the server rather than awaiting the abort.

EVIDENCE (a flake is not proved gone by one green, so stated in tiers). STRONGEST: the same planted 300ms pause widening the gap between the two dispatch-sync calls, applied to both structures. Old structure = exit 1, poll-until timed out - supersede-stale, :elapsed-ms 30017, 0 failures 1 errors - matching the CI signature of :elapsed-ms 30022 on PR #8873. New structure = exit 0, 25 tests 137 assertions. ARGUMENT: the timed wait for the stale row became a synchronous assertion. WEAK: five consecutive solo runs, exit 0 and a stable 137 assertions each.

GATES on the final rebased base, all captured exit codes: full suite (= jvm-http in test.yml, clojure -M:test from implementation/http) exit 0, 508 tests 3883 assertions; solo re-frame.http-reply-lowering-test exit 0, 25 tests 137 assertions. Sabotage control planted at http_reply_lowering_test.clj:640 drove exit 1 naming the planted value at the planted line, which also establishes the gate read this branch checkout. Restores verified by git blob hash.

Test-only change: no production source touched, no assertion weakened, no spec change. Related: rf2-zvbm9 rode the same worker; the two turned out INDEPENDENT.
AUDIT PR #8889: REOPENED. The held-server ordering correctly removes the original race, but the regression still does not prove that the one delivered app reply belongs to the superseding issuance. Both server responses are identical, while both tests assert only reply count 1 and :status :ok; canonical replies carry :rf.reply/work-id, so a broken path that delivers issuance 1 while losing issuance 2 can satisfy the advertised request-#2 claim. The final Thread/sleep 200 is also only a timing window for absence of a delayed second delivery. Minimal completion: assert the delivered reply work-id is [:rf.work/http :search 2 1] and make the existing harness's no-second-delivery observation deterministic. Keep the held-server harness; no production change or new abstraction.

VERDICT (PR #8923, branch worker/httpwid-o9e15, 2026-09-01 20:52 AUSEST): AUDIT COMPLETED. Both things the PR #8889 audit asked for are done, test-only, held-server harness kept, no production change, no new abstraction.

PREMISE HELD AT TIP. Verified before editing: both supersession tests asserted only reply count 1 and :status :ok (the stale-trace test asserted only the count -- not even :status), both closing Thread/sleep 200 lines were present, and canonical replies do carry :rf.reply/work-id (already pinned at success-reply-is-canonical). Nothing had been fixed in the interval.

AUDIT LITERAL WAS RIGHT. Read from the code rather than the note: reply.cljc work-id builds [:rf.work/http logical-id (or issuance 1) (or attempt 1)], logical-id = the caller's :request-id when non-nil (here :search); registry/next-issuance! bumps issuance per fresh request under one request-id, and neither request retries. So the superseding attempt is exactly [:rf.work/http :search 2 1], as the audit quoted.

THREE DEVICES, NONE OF THEM A CLOCK.

(1) ISSUANCE IDENTITY. Both tests now assert the DELIVERED reply's :rf.reply/work-id is [:rf.work/http :search 2 1]. Issuance is the only fact distinguishing the two byte-identical server responses, so this is what convicts a path that delivers issuance 1 and loses issuance 2.

(2) THE SUPERSEDE IS AN ORDERING, read while both exchanges are still HELD: the :search in-flight slot already holds issuance 2. registry/supersede! cleared issuance 1 out of it and fired its abort-fn INLINE during the second dispatch-sync's fx phase; that abort-fn wins the once-only :finalised? CAS and routes through dispatch-aborted!, where :request-id-superseded is in reply-suppressing-abort-reasons -- no app dispatch, and the won CAS makes issuance 1's later transport completion bail at already-replied?. There is therefore NO LATER MOMENT at which a second reply could originate. That is the real content of the no-second-delivery claim; the 200ms window was allowing for an event that cannot occur.

(3) A FIFO DRAIN BARRIER replaces Thread/sleep 200. dispatch-sync seeds at the FRONT of the frame's queue and then runs the drain loop to fixed point (router.cljc drain-block!), so every envelope enqueued before it has been PROCESSED by the time it returns. Honest scope: the barrier is a barrier for anything already enqueued; the guarantee against a genuinely later delivery is device (2), not any wait. Both are now stated in the source.

ALSO: registry/reset-issuance-counters-for-test! (an existing test-only helper, already used by http_managed_test.clj) now runs at the top of each test. issuance-counters is a process-global defonce and http_managed_test.clj ALSO uses :request-id :search, so the issuance literals held only because eviction happened to clear the counter -- a latent load-order dependency of exactly the kind rf2-ohfym observes the single full-suite jvm-http lane cannot see. The reset makes the new literals independent of what ran first. Group 3's second test also gains the :status :ok assertion it lacked.

GATES on the final rebased base (163aefb4c4, merge base 3cc654e45c), every exit code captured on one command line and quoted from the .exit file: full suite (= CI jvm-http, clojure -M:test from implementation/http) exit 0, 508 tests 3890 assertions; solo re-frame.http-reply-lowering-test run FIVE consecutive times, exit 0 each, a stable 25 tests / 144 assertions each. Baseline was 137 solo / 3883 full; the seven new assertions are the whole delta. The namespace was run solo deliberately, per rf2-ohfym: a full-suite ordering can supply a load-order dependency the namespace does not declare.

THE CONTROL BIT WHERE IT HAD TO. A plant that reds everything would not demonstrate the audit's gap, so the control makes the harness genuinely deliver issuance 1: one registry/reset-issuance-counters-for-test! inserted BETWEEN the two dispatch-sync calls, re-minting the superseding request as issuance 1. The supersede still happens (it keys on request-id, not issuance), one reply is still delivered, and it is still :status :ok. Exit 1, 25 tests 144 assertions, 2 failures 0 errors -- same assertion count as the clean run, so nothing was crashed out.
  RED (both new): "the surviving in-flight request is issuance 2..." (device 2) and "the delivered reply belongs to the SUPERSEDING issuance (2)..." (device 1), both actual [:rf.work/http :search 1 1].
  GREEN under the same plant -- the assertions that existed BEFORE this PR: reply count 1, ":status :ok", "the superseding request #2 is the live in-flight request", and the whole of supersede-distinct-work-ids-and-canonical-stale-trace. That green-beside-red IS the audit's finding, reproduced.

A FIRST SABOTAGE ATTEMPT CAME BACK GREEN and was treated as a reason to stop, not to proceed: the plant had landed AFTER both dispatch-sync calls, where both issuances were already minted, so it was inert. Moved between the two dispatches, it bit. Restores after every plant verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object (e27fd9f7aa3b14dd8011e275d1314bef137e50a5) -- line endings are translated in this checkout, so a byte digest of the working file would not be sound. The red also establishes the gate read this branch's checkout, since the fault existed nowhere else.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: no production change was needed and none was made; implementation/http/src is untouched. The adjacent rf2-ohfym (jvm-http runs no solo-namespace lane, .github/workflows, hot-zone) stays open and untouched -- but its concern is answered for THIS namespace by the counter reset plus the five solo runs recorded above.
close_reason: PR #8923 (draft->ready): audit completion. Both supersession tests now pin the DELIVERED reply's :rf.reply/work-id to [:rf.work/http :search 2 1] (verified against reply.cljc work-id, not the note - the audit literal was right), and the Thread/sleep 200 quiescence windows are replaced by two non-timed devices: an in-flight-slot ordering assertion read while both exchanges are still HELD (proving supersede! cleared issuance 1 and won its once-only :finalised? CAS inline, so no later delivery can originate) and a dispatch-sync FIFO drain barrier for anything already enqueued. reset-issuance-counters-for-test! added so the issuance literals do not depend on JVM load order. Test-only; held-server harness kept; no production change. Gates on the rebased base: full suite exit 0 (508/3890), solo namespace exit 0 x5 (25/144 each). Control: a plant re-minting the superseder as issuance 1 reds BOTH new work-id assertions while the pre-existing count-and-:status assertions stay GREEN - the audit's gap reproduced.

description:

So a change confined to implementation/core does NOT arm the codemod job even though the job now depends on that code — the classic surface-armed gate that is skipped on the very push that breaks it (loops.md clause 2 names this shape: a gate skipped on the breaking commit while the trunk rollup reads green throughout).

title: xray: epoch view keeps a fixture-only fallback onto the RETIRED bare :spec key
description:
A FIXTURE-ONLY FALLBACK ONTO A RETIRED KEY, in the epoch view's machine-spec resolver.
Nothing is blank because of it — this is a TIDY, not a live defect, and it is filed P4 for
that reason. What earns it a bead is that it is the SAME ANTI-PATTERN rf2-t8a8 just fixed
and ruled on one file over.

THE SITES, verified at trunk 3d8cd72b41 by reading the source:

  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:2090-2093
      (or (:rf/machine machine-meta)
          (:machine-spec machine-meta)
          (:spec machine-meta)
          (:rf.machine/spec machine-meta))

  the same shape again at :2803-2805.

The comment at :2088 states the intent outright: the registrar stores the spec under
`:rf/machine`, "with fixture-shape fallbacks for unit tests". So the fallbacks are a
deliberate test seam, not residue somebody forgot.

WHY THE BARE `:spec` ALTERNATIVE IS UNREACHABLE FROM PRODUCTION. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/reg_meta.cljc`
carries `{:spec :schema}` in its retired map (MIGRATION §M-54) and documents at :112 that a
RETIRED bare key throws `:rf.error/retired-registration-key`, "a HARD error in dev AND
prod". `machine-meta` here comes off a real `:event` registration, so a registration
carrying bare `:spec` cannot exist to be read — the alternative can only ever be satisfied
by a hand-built fixture map.

SCOPE IT PRECISELY — ONLY THE BARE `:spec` ALTERNATIVE IS THE DEAD ONE. Of the four:
  `:rf/machine`      namespaced, the live wrapper shape, passes.
  `:machine-spec`    bare and legacy, but NOT in the retired map — do not assume it throws,
                     measure it before touching it.
  `:spec`            RETIRED bare key, throws at registration. THIS is the dead branch.
  `:rf.machine/spec` NAMESPACED, so the retired-BARE-key rule does not reach it. Not dead.
A sweep that removes all three non-canonical alternatives on the strength of this bead
would be going further than the evidence, and `:rf.machine/spec` in particular is named in
the docstring at :2799-2800 as a supported legacy shape.

WHY IT IS WORTH REMOVING AT ALL, given nothing is broken: rf2-t8a8's merged ruling (PR
#9629) is that a fallback branch unreachable from production BY CONSTRUCTION is exactly
what hides an emptiness bug — it lets a fixture written on the retired spelling stay green
while the real path is empty. In the schemas panel that had already happened: the tab
showed zero rows against a live registrar and the tests did not notice, because the
fixtures used the retired spelling too. Here the live path genuinely works, so the seam is
only latent cover rather than active cover. That is the difference between P4 and P2.

WHOEVER TAKES THIS: if you remove the `:spec` alternative, check what the existing unit
tests actually feed this resolver first. If a fixture depends on it, the fix is to move
that fixture onto `:rf/machine` — the same repair shape rf2-t8a8 used — and NOT to keep
the branch alive for the test's benefit, which is the thing being ruled against.

PROVENANCE: reported by worker `schemakey-a` while working rf2-t8a8, explicitly labelled
INFERRED rather than measured. The mayor then verified both sites and the reg-meta
mechanism at source before filing this. Its other observation is also recorded and is NOT
part of this bead: the `tools/story` and `tools/machines-viz` `:spec` hits are unrelated
slots rather than registration metadata.
notes:
WORKER panelfix-a — PR #9638 (worker/panelfix-a). Bead left CLAIMED for the mayor to close on merge.

DONE, scoped exactly as the bead directs: the bare `:spec` alternative removed from
`machine-state-path-coord`, the other three kept.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE BEAD, and it is the reason this touched one site rather than two. The
bead reports "the same shape again at :2803-2805". The second site — `machine-spec-from-meta`,
now at ~:2811 — carries `(or (:rf/machine m) (:machine-spec m) (:rf.machine/spec m)
machine-meta)`: three alternatives plus an identity fallback, and NO bare `:spec`, so it has
never had the dead branch. Measured repo-wide: there is exactly ONE `(:spec ` form anywhere
under `tools/xray`, at view.cljs:2092, and this PR removes it. The two functions now carry
identical key lists, which is more mirroring than before, not less.

SCOPING MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `reg-meta/retired-bare-keys` is `{:spec :schema}` and
nothing else, and `events.cljc:958` runs `validate-registration-metadata!` on every
`reg-event`, so bare `:spec` on a real `:event` registration throws
`:rf.error/retired-registration-key` in dev and prod. `:machine-spec` is bare and legacy but
NOT retired — an unknown bare key is a dev-gated warning and the key is still stored, so such
a registration can exist; kept. `:rf.machine/spec` is namespaced, so the retired-BARE-key rule

title: xray: inspect-view's one-arity mints the constant mount-id rf-xray-inspect-root, which the first two callers will share
description:
`inspect-view`'s ONE-ARITY MINTS A CONSTANT MOUNT-ID, so the first two callers that use it
collide. Nothing is broken today; this is a trap being armed rather than a live fault.

VERIFIED BY THE MAYOR AT TIP ba26dd1aa7 (fact):

tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget.cljs:138

    ([v] (inspect-view v "root"))
    ([v node-key]
     [ei/edn-inspector-view
      {:mount-id (str "rf-xray-inspect-" node-key)
       :value    v
       :opts     (inspect-opts node-key)}])

So `(inspect-view v)` always mints `"rf-xray-inspect-root"`. **CALL SITES OF THE ONE-ARITY
TODAY: ZERO** — a repo-wide search over `tools/` and `implementation/` returns only the
definition, its own docstring mentions, and the arity-1 line itself.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY A BUG, AND WHY IT IS STILL WORTH CLOSING:

rf2-d2aj (PR #9597) keyed the inspector's per-mount store, `:ref` memo and projection cache
by a LIFECYCLE KEY — the mount-id qualified by the frame it renders under — so two panels
in DIFFERENT frames sharing a mount-id no longer collide. That covers the ordinary Xray
shape, where each shell is its own frame.

What the frame qualifier CANNOT cover is two mounts in the SAME frame. rf2-d2aj recorded
that boundary deliberately and left it: a React function component has no per-instance
storage a Fresco body may use — hooks do not belong in a body, and `rf.fresco/reg-state`
consumes an instance key rather than minting one — so nothing INSIDE the widget can tell
two structurally identical siblings apart. **The caller must supply the identity.** The
one-arity is precisely a caller declining to.

`inspect-view`'s docstring already says this correctly and at length ("two mounts sharing
one `node-key` now share a width slot and a projection cache as well as a panel-id, so
give each mount its own"). **That is why this is P4 and not higher**, and it is a real
argument for doing NOTHING — the tree trusts the programmer and the warning is at the
point of use.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN DISMISSED: a default arity is
not a warning, it is an INVITATION, and the failure it invites is silent — two panels
sharing a width slot render at each other's widths rather than erroring. The Fresco
migration (rf2-k97c.3) is actively converting panels, and each converted panel reaches for
`inspect-view`. The first two that take the convenient arity collide.

THREE DISPOSITIONS, AND THE DECISION IS YOURS TO ARGUE IN THE PR BODY:

  (a) DELETE THE ONE-ARITY. Callers must name their mount. Cheapest, loudest, and with
      zero call sites it breaks nothing. The cost is ergonomic: `inspect`'s own one-arity
      stays, so the two facade functions stop matching, and a migrating panel meets an
      arity error where it expected a rename.
  (b) KEEP IT AND MINT SOMETHING UNIQUE. Requires per-call identity a Fresco body cannot
      produce — read `ei/edn-inspector-view` before assuming this is available, because
      rf2-d2aj concluded it is not. If you find a route, that is a finding worth more than
      this bead.
  (c) LEAVE IT, ON THE DOCSTRING. Defensible under the project stance. If you choose this,
      say so and close — a verified "the premise does not warrant a change" is a complete
      deliverable here.

**CHECK (b) BEFORE ARGUING (a).** The whole question turns on whether a Fresco body can
mint per-instance identity, and rf2-d2aj's "not reached, deliberately so" paragraph is the
place that answers it. If it can, the shape of every one of these collisions changes.

DO NOT touch `inspect`, the Reagent head — its form-2 outer body mints a UUID per mount and
is unaffected. DO NOT re-open the lifecycle-key design; it is ruled and merged.

GATES: the Xray JVM suite, `test:cljs` (node), the examples-compile sweep (a facade arity
change can break a testbed build), plus clj-kondo and Splint. Capture your OWN exit codes,
unpiped, and gate any browser step on the compile's captured exit.
close_reason:
CLOSED WITH NO CHANGE, ON THE WORKER'S ARGUMENT. **No PR, no commit, no file touched** — the
dispatch offered "leave it" as a first-class outcome and the worker took it, with three
measurements rather than taste. That is the stance working, not a worker declining to find work.

DISPOSITION: **(c) — leave the one-arity, on the docstring.**

=== THE THREE MEASUREMENTS THAT DECIDED IT ===

1. **THE INVITATION HAS BEEN DECLINED 9 TIMES OUT OF 9.** Every executable `edn/inspect` call
   site in `tools/xray/src` passes an explicit node-key — `app_db_segment_inspector.cljs:263`,
   `managed_fx_template.cljs:221/247/259/272`, `static/flows/panel.cljs:197/203`,
   `static/routes/row_expand.cljs:66`, `static/schemas/panel.cljs:245`. **Zero** use the
   one-arity, INCLUDING inside a `for` over indexed inputs (`flows/panel.cljs:197`) where the
   temptation to skip the key is highest and the author instead composed
   `"static-flows/<flow-key>/input/<i>"`. `inspect`'s one-arity has stood for the whole life of
   that namespace and nobody has taken it.

2. **THE MIGRATION DOES NOT ROUTE THROUGH `inspect-view` AT ALL.** This refutes the bead's own
   central counter-argument, which assumed "each converted panel reaches for `inspect-view`".
   Exactly one migrated panel renders EDN — `panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:279` — and it calls
   `ei/edn-inspector-view` DIRECTLY, because it needs `:site-id`, `:card?`, `:zoomable?` and
   `:header`, none of which `inspect-opts` produces (it produces `:panel-id` and
   `:default-expanded-depth` and nothing else). **And the loud refusal option (a) wanted is
   ALREADY INSTALLED at the boundary those panels actually reach** — `edn-inspector-view` throws
   a six-line refusal on a non-string `:mount-id`.

3. **(a) IS NOT A ONE-LINE DELETION.** `edn_widget.cljs`'s ns docstring (L23-26) is a four-line
   menu in which `(inspect v)` / `(inspect v node-key)` / `(inspect-view v node-key)` line up,
   and the migration story it states is a pure RENAME. Deleting one head's one-arity while
   keeping the other's makes the two facades asymmetric and needs a paragraph explaining why —
   litigating a fine detail on a P4 with zero call sites, which is the thing the stance says to
   stop doing.

=== THE CENTRAL QUESTION WAS CHECKED AT SOURCE, AND rf2-d2aj's CONCLUSION STANDS ===

Option (b) — mint something unique — required overturning rf2-d2aj's finding that a Fresco body
cannot mint per-instance identity. Read at source rather than taken from prose:

  * `rf.fresco/reg-state` (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/state.cljc:193`)
    CONSUMES an instance key and mints nothing. Its ns docstring names this bead's exact failure:
    *"pick an app-db path, forget to vary it per instance, and every instance on the page silently
    shares one value... Nothing throws, nothing logs, and the screen is simply wrong."*
  * `defview`'s "Hooks do not belong in the body — a law" (`fresco.cljc:161`) is a CONTRACT, not
    a refusal: a body is dynamically composed, so a hook's call order would follow a Fresco data
    path.
  * `ei/edn-inspector-view` (`edn_inspector.cljs:4116`) is a plain React function component;
    `(gen-mount-id)` in that body would mint a fresh id per RENDER.
  * No `:instance-id`-style affordance exists in the Fresco authoring surface — the only
    `:instance-key` under `implementation/fresco/src/**` is `reg-state`'s consumed one.

**ONE ESCAPE ROUTE rf2-d2aj DOES NOT NAME, REPORTED AS INFERENCE AND CORRECTLY NOT PURSUED.**
`h/defhost` mounts a raw React island where hooks ARE legal, so a host wrapping the boundary could
call `useId` and hand the minted id down through a render-prop, with the inspected value closed
over lexically rather than crossing — which sidesteps the "the value cannot cross" objection that
killed the `as-component` bridge. The worker did NOT verify the render-prop lowering mechanically
and says so. Two things make it unattractive and **the second is fatal on its own terms**:
`testid-for` (`edn_inspector.cljs:1580`) embeds `mount-id` VERBATIM in every testid the widget
emits, so any auto-minted id makes the whole widget's testids nondeterministic and trades a shared
width slot for state lost on every remount. The Fresco head's design point is a STABLE,
caller-supplied, human-readable mount-id; auto-minting contradicts it.

That escape route is recorded here rather than filed: it is a real observation about `defhost`,
and if the per-instance-identity question is ever reopened for a shape that is NOT this one, it is
the first thing to check.

=== WHAT THE ARGUMENT CONCEDES, WHICH IS WHY IT CONVINCES ===

The worker engaged the counter-argument and granted it real force on TIMING — now is the cheapest
moment there will ever be to delete a zero-call-site arity. It loses to the measurement rather
than being waved away: the invitation is declined universally, the migration bypasses the facade,
and the boundary below already refuses the shape it can detect. The invited failure is also
bounded — an Xray-internal wrong width in a dev tool, visible to the author of the second panel,
not a production data path.

The docstring already carries a 20-line warning ending in the sentence an operator needs: *"two
mounts sharing one `node-key` now share a width slot and a projection cache as well as a
panel-id, so give each mount its own."* Under *trust the programmer*, a warning at the point of
use is a warning.

=== HOUSEKEEPING ===

No gates run and no sabotage, because no file changed. No commits, no branch push, no PR. The
worker read `views/edn_inspector.cljs` (testid-a's file) and edited zero characters of it, and
read but did not touch `static/flows/panel.cljs` and `static/schemas/panel.cljs` (static6-a's) —
the fences held in a dispatch whose whole method was reading other workers' files.

`bd history` showed 16 snapshots with `description` constant at 3948 chars and `notes` null
throughout, with `status` varying as the live control on the walk — so brief and item were the
same text and nothing had accreted.

| `worker/receipts-hic081` | `ae14841ab3` | *(none — 0 PRs)* | — | — | n/a | — | **EXCLUDED — RETAIN** |

Six for six. All six remote counterparts server-deleted (`git ls-remote --heads origin` returns 0 for each; control: `main` and `worker/receipts-hic081` each return 1). No worktree holds any of them (`git worktree list --porcelain`: only `main` plus three unrelated subagent worktrees).

**Why `headRefOid` equality and not merely "a MERGED PR exists under this name": worker branch names are REUSED.** Measured here — `gh pr list --head worker/epoch-a` returns **five** PRs, of which exactly one carries the current local tip. Matching on the name alone would have read one branch's state off another's PR. The other five names return one PR each today, but that is luck, not structure.

### 2. The instrument post-mortem — why the bead's counts inverted

The bead asked the right question ("is each branch's headline claim true of trunk today?"). Every contrary count answering it was an artefact. This is CLAUDE.md trap **(g)** — a census reading PROSE as evidence — reproduced cleanly, and it is worth keeping because the class recurs.

**(i) Self-announcing removal comments counted as evidence of non-removal.** `group-by-event` 2 / `domino-bucket` 1 "in `core.cljc`" are `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2494,2497` — the comment *the branch itself wrote*: `;; rf2-kuky.72: the group-by-event / domino-bucket facade twins are REMOVED.` The re-exports it deleted are absent from trunk, removed by `f702ad4bc0` — this branch's own merge commit. A removal's own bookkeeping is the single most likely surviving hit for the removed name, so a raw count of a retired name is biased toward "still here" by construction. Same shape for `projected-history` (retirement notes in test files, plus `.beads/issues.jsonl` — the bead's own text) and `:system-id` (a NEW test the branch added, `fixed_actor_id_addressing_test.clj`, whose docstring reads "With the `:system-id` family deleted, ...", plus executable NEGATIVE cases in `machine_node_keys_test.clj:141` asserting the retired key is rejected).

**(ii) The `render-head` 17-file reading — TWO stacked mechanisms, and the dossier named the wrong one for the larger half.** Measured on trunk, decomposed:

| Instrument | Files | What the gap is |
|---|---|---|
| plain substring `git grep -lF 'render-head'` | **17** | the bead's figure |
| word-boundary `git grep -lE '\brender-head\b'` | **10** | substring alone caught 7 files of `render-header` |
| of those 10, `render-head-hash` | **7** | `\b` STILL caught these |
| genuine residue | **3** plus `.beads/issues.jsonl` | all retirement prose |

Direct test of the boundary, both directions: `render-header` vs `\brender-head\b` gives **no match** (the following `e` is a word char, so there is no boundary); `render-head-hash` vs the same gives **MATCH** (the hyphen IS a word boundary). **So the dossier's "`render-header` matched because `\b` runs across the hyphen" is wrong** — `\b` correctly rejects `render-header`; only the plain substring caught it. What `\b` does wave through is `render-head-hash`, a genuinely different function (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj:271`). Codex named only `render-head-hash` and was the more precise of the two. The three genuine hits are `spec/API.md:364` (documenting that `head-model` REPLACED `render-head`), `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` and `spec/011-SSR.md:1290,1871` — all retirement bookkeeping. **No `render-head` definition exists anywhere** (`(defn render-head` gives 0 files; control: `(defn render-head-hash` gives 1).

**The reusable lesson: for a RETIREMENT census, a surviving-name count is the wrong instrument in both directions at once** — it over-counts on the removal's own bookkeeping and on hyphenated neighbours, and it cannot see a keyword slot at all. Ask the forge whether the change LANDED; do not ask the tree whether the name is GONE.

**(iii) A Var manifest cannot certify a KEYWORD retirement.** Codex's correction, accepted: `:system-id`, `:redact-fn` and `:child-machine` are keyword slots, not public Vars, so 0 rows in `spec/api-manifest.edn` is silence rather than evidence for them. It remains sound for the Var names — measured on trunk with controls (`dispatch` 4 rows, nonsense needle 0): `render-head` **0**, `active-head` **0**, `projected-history` **0**, `group-by-event-with-events` **0**; and the NEW handles present as intended, `client-root` **3**, `head-model` **2**. The verdict does not rest on the manifest either way — it rests on `headRefOid` equality.

**(iv) File deletions — all 8 absent from trunk, removed by these branches' own merged commits.** `bf077b4245` (egress7: 2 epoch redact-fn test suites) and `9f3c01a274` (mach70: 2 machines test suites plus 4 `spec/conformance/fixtures/` system-id fixtures); both ancestors of trunk. Control: `CLAUDE.md` gives 1 row, fabricated path gives 0.

### 3. Exact disposition commands (operator, from the mayor checkout)

    # re-confirm identity has not moved since this ruling, then delete LOCAL refs only
    git rev-parse worker/egress7-a worker/epoch-a worker/hicmount-a \
                  worker/mach70-a worker/ssrhead-a worker/tracereg-a
    git branch -D worker/egress7-a worker/epoch-a worker/hicmount-a \
                  worker/mach70-a worker/ssrhead-a worker/tracereg-a
    git for-each-ref refs/heads/worker/   # expect ONLY worker/receipts-hic081 to remain

**`-D` is required; `-d` REFUSES.** The project merges by rebase, so a merged branch never becomes an ancestor of trunk and git will never agree it is merged. That disagreement is the entire subject of this bead — `-d`'s refusal is the false negative, not a warning worth heeding here.

**STANDING SAFETY RULE, unchanged: never `git push origin --delete <branch>` before verifying `state == MERGED`** — deleting a head branch auto-closes its PR. **No remote deletion is needed here in any case**: all six remotes were server-deleted as their merges landed, so this touches local refs only.

**`git remote prune origin` is dropped from the dossier's proposed sequence** (Codex's call, accepted): it is broader than this decision and unnecessary.

**"Keeping preserves nothing" is overstated** (Codex, accepted). A local ref preserves the name, the original pre-rebase ancestry and the branch reflog, which `git branch -D` deletes with it. Release these six because no outstanding delivery and no retention ruling was found for them — not because deletion is consequence-free.

### 4. Exclusion — `worker/receipts-hic081`

Out of scope, **RETAINED**, do not touch. Verified independently in this pass: `gh pr list --state all --head worker/receipts-hic081` returns an empty list — **no PR was ever opened**, so the head-ref instrument that releases the other six says nothing about it. Its remote counterpart is still LIVE (`git ls-remote` gives 1, unlike the six), it carries 3 genuinely unmerged commits, and its keep-ruling lives in the memory `receipts-hic081-branch-is-deliberately-retained` with the release condition. It is the control that proves the six are the exception rather than the rule.

### 5. Deliberately OUT OF SCOPE — refused

- **No scheduled branch pruner, no CI orphan-branch report, no ratchet, no disposition ledger.** Server-side head-branch deletion already yields zero remote orphans by construction; what remains is a handful of local refs in ONE checkout, cleared by one command. A one-time sweep, not an apparatus.
- **No `loops.md` section 5 expansion.** The dossier recommended adding the concrete `gh pr list --head <branch> --json headRefOid,state` form. **Refused — Codex is right that the guidance is already there**, and verified at `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` around line 1518: *"Ask for the exact head-ref field and compare it for equality yourself. A search term substring-matches; only equality identifies"* and *"prefer an instrument that takes the identity as INPUT"*. Further, the document is deliberately TOOL-AGNOSTIC PROSE — measured: **zero** code fences and **zero** literal git/gh commands in the whole file (a `grep -cF 'gh '` reading of 15 is itself a substring artefact of "enough/through/though/weigh"; the word-boundary count is 0) — so pasting a `gh` invocation into it would break its register. The failure here was not a missing rule; it was a rule that existed and was not reached for.
- **No salvage / re-landing (dossier Option C).** Acting on the bead's original table would land a clean, compiling, fully-green PR re-applying deletions trunk already performed and churning eleven spec files for nothing. This is the `loops.md` section 1 "silently reverting green change" shape. **Do not do it.**
- **No archive tags**, no history rewrite, no merge simulation.

### 6. One follow-on filed

`loops.md` section 5 claims a head-ref query "cannot be windowed". **That is false for the tool actually used**: `gh pr list` caps at `--limit` (default **30**). Finding a matching head is positive evidence; an EMPTY bounded list is not proof of absence — which is precisely the reassuring-zero failure that paragraph exists to warn about, reproduced in its own remedy. Filed separately as a tracked-file edit this pass could not make. (Codex's find.)

### 7. Recommended close

**Recommend closing rf2-bipw once the operator has run the deletion above.** Not closed here. Suggested close reason: *all six merged via PRs #9437, #9452, #9456, #9457, #9459, #9461 on 2026-09-08, each verified by headRefOid == local tip; the "deletions trunk never performed" reading was a substring / self-announcing-comment artefact; six local refs released, receipts-hic081 retained.*

The 'deletions trunk never performed' reading in the original description was a substring / self-announcing-comment artefact and is refuted. Six local refs deleted by the mayor: worker/epoch-a, worker/ssrhead-a, worker/egress7-a, worker/hicmount-a, worker/tracereg-a, worker/mach70-a. worker/receipts-hic081 retained per the ruling.

title: RULED: no ;; PERF: marker convention — DECLINED (grep the spelling, not the word). No gate, no retrofit, no :host-transient rename
description:
RULED 2026-09-08 — DECLINED. There is NO `;; PERF:` marker convention in re-frame2, and
none is to be added. This bead is a RECORD OF A DECISION, not a proposal. Do not implement
anything from it. Do not brief a worker off it. See the closing note for the full reasoning
and the preserved analysis.

WHAT WAS DECIDED
- NO marker convention. Nothing is written into `spec/Conventions.md`. No SHOULD, no MUST,
  no standing obligation on any author. `;; PERF:` remains available to any author who wants
  it at a particular site (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:212` already
  carries `;; PERF / coherence:`), but it means nothing to any tool and indexes nothing.
- NO CI gate or lint, including the changed-lines ratchet variant.
- NO retrofit — neither the 169-file sweep nor "opportunistic retrofit" as a standing rule.
- NO `:host-transient` rename, and no rename of the SCXML "transient state" vocabulary.
- NO form-parsing mutation detector.

WHY, IN ONE PARAGRAPH
The bead's premise — that the hot-zone rule "cannot be audited by command" — is false. It
cannot be audited by a BADLY SPELLED command. Measured repo-wide: `(transient ` returns 71
occurrences across 47 files and `(volatile! |(vswap! ` returns 418 across 122, each in one
command, each completely free of the `:host-transient` and SCXML "transient state" domain-word
contamination that motivated this bead (`derivation/egress.cljc` and `machines/choice.cljc`
both drop to ZERO). Results are file:line, i.e. site-shaped. `CLAUDE.md` instrument-misreport
item (g) already prescribes exactly this remedy in exactly these spellings. So site discovery
already costs one correct grep and zero authoring tax. A marker would buy only a partial index
of authors' performance CLAIMS — and the dossier's own flagship demonstration marker, drafted
for `trace/cascade.cljc:129`, contained two false cost claims (the `cond` takes one arm per
event, not five; the two flow arms carry no cap at all), which is the convention failing in
the best case its advocate could construct. Under TRUST THE PROGRAMMER, a standing obligation
read only by an occasional auditor, enforced by nothing, and unreliable when written, is
ceremony.

STATUS OF THE THREE THINGS THIS BEAD ONCE HELD
1. The prose-census contamination finding — SHIPPED. Landed on main as `CLAUDE.md` item (g)
   via rf2-jok0. This was always the valuable half.
2. The `;; PERF:` marker convention — DECLINED here.
3. The `:host-transient` naming question — DECLINED here.

THE BEAD IS NOW EMPTY OF WORK. It is left OPEN for the operator to close. Priority stays P4.
The FP audit that produced it (rf2-5941) returned PASS: 819 files, 391,400 lines, 46 surfaces,
19 function-local scratch atoms tree-wide, 80% of mutation-bearing files already carrying
written justification. The discipline was never the problem; the measurement was.
acceptance_criteria: RULED DECLINED 2026-09-08 — nothing to build. This bead records a decision. Satisfied by the ruling itself: no marker convention, no spec/Conventions.md section, no CI gate or ratchet, no retrofit, no host-transient rename, no form-parsing detector. Any PR implementing a ;; PERF: convention contradicts this bead and should be refused. Left OPEN for the operator to close.
notes:
MAYOR TRIAGE 2026-09-07 11:53 AUSEST — SPLIT, NOT CLOSED. And a correction to my own first read.

I initially recommended closing this as over-engineering, from its TITLE ("deliberate-imperative
code has no greppable marker, so the hot-zone rule cannot be audited"), which reads like a proposal
to tax every imperative block so an auditor can run a census. Reading the body refutes that: the
bead already refuses the mass retrofit AND refuses a CI gate without Mike's word, and it says in
terms that the audit found no problem severe enough to warrant one. It is self-limiting. Judging it
from its shortest text was the error this project keeps recording, and I made it.

THE BEAD IS TWO THINGS, and they have different owners and different value.

(1) THE MEASUREMENT IS THE VALUABLE HALF, AND IT IS NOT A CONVENTION QUESTION AT ALL. A census of
this rule is contaminated in BOTH directions at once, both measured here:
  * FALSE NEGATIVES on the best-documented code. A grep for hot path|perf|performance|allocation
    rated core/source_coords.cljc — the exemplar, which explains its macro-expansion-time walker
    AND the non-obvious volatile!-around-transient constraint — as having only 2 justifications,
    and rated core/trace/cascade.cljc as having NONE. Both wrong.
  * FALSE POSITIVES on the mutation side. derivation/egress.cljc reads as the tree's largest
    concentration of undocumented transient use (12 hits, zero prose) and contains NO MUTATION AT
    ALL: every hit is the domain term :host-transient, an in-flight HTTP handle address, matched
    across the hyphen by \b. Nine more files carry that term.
So the naive census produces a plausible, ranked, entirely wrong worklist, and it is wrong in the
REASSURING direction — it manufactures findings against exactly the files that should be the
standard. An auditor who trusted it would file beads against exemplary code.

That belongs in CLAUDE.md's "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport" list, beside items (a)-(f), because
that list is what a worker reads BEFORE running a census. It is the same class as those items and
it is the half that will otherwise burn the next auditor. Whoever takes it: that list is labelled,
not counted — do not add a total to its opening sentence.

(2) THE MARKER CONVENTION IS A HOUSE RULE AND THEREFORE MIKE'S CALL, NOT MINE AND NOT A WORKER'S.
Adopting ";; PERF:" above deliberate mutation is a small ask and the bead scopes it honestly
(new code only, opportunistic retrofit, no gate). But it is still a standing obligation on every
future author, and under "trust the programmer" that is precisely the kind of tax the operator
decides on rather than the mayor. HELD FOR MIKE. Not dispatched.

(3) THE :host-transient NAMING QUESTION the bead raises is likewise the owner's, and the bead is
right that renaming is probably not worth it. It stays flagged rather than actioned; the cost it
names is real (two wrong readings in one audit) but item (1) discharges that cost without a rename.

SO: this bead stays OPEN, holding (2) and (3) for Mike. If (1) is split out to its own bead it can
be dispatched immediately by anyone, needs no ruling, and is worth more than the rest of this bead
combined.

--- MAYOR §3 BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-08 14:2x AUSEST — ITEM (1) IS DONE IN THE TREE; THIS IS NOW A PURE RULING BEAD ---
Measured on origin/main at 17be129b45. My previous note on this bead said item (1) — folding the
prose-census contamination finding into CLAUDE.md's "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport" list — "can be
dispatched immediately by anyone, needs no ruling, and is worth more than the rest of this bead combined",
and proposed splitting it out. IT WAS NEVER SPLIT OUT AND IT LANDED ANYWAY.
CHECKED AT SOURCE, not inferred: CLAUDE.md carries item (h) and, before it, item **(g) A census that treats
PROSE as the evidence is contaminated in BOTH directions at once, and its output is a plausible RANKED
worklist rather than an obvious error** — with the source_coords / cascade false negatives, the
egress.cljc `host-transient` false positive, the "\b matches across a HYPHEN" mechanism, and the two-part

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD IS THEREFORE ONLY MIKE'S, and the bead is smaller than it looks:
  (2) the ";; PERF:" marker convention — a house rule, a standing obligation on every future author, and
      under "trust the programmer" exactly the kind of tax the operator decides rather than the mayor.
  (3) the `:host-transient` naming question — the owner's, and the bead itself judges a rename probably
      not worth it. Item (1) landing already discharges the cost item (3) was pricing, so (3) can fairly
      be declined on its own terms.
NOTHING HERE IS DISPATCHABLE. Do not brief a worker off this bead: the only worker-shaped part of it is
already on main.

--- MAYOR §3 CHECK 2026-09-08 22:3x AUSEST — TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT PRICE THIS RULING, ONE IN EACH DIRECTION ---
Went looking for whether this is already answered. It is not, and it is genuinely Mike's — a convention
call is a taste call. But two things I measured change what it costs.

1. THE CONVENTION IS NOT ALREADY EMERGENT, which makes it MORE expensive than "write down what we do".
   Measured over implementation/*/src/*: `;; PERF:` reads 0, `;; PERF ` reads 1, `;;PERF` 0, `;; HOT:` 0,
   `;; PERFORMANCE` 0 — against a control of 9 for `;; NOTE`, so the instrument is live and the zeros are
   real. There is exactly ONE marker-shaped comment in the whole source tree. So adopting `;; PERF:` is
   introducing a new convention, not ratifying an existing habit. The bead's own evidence that 80% of
   imperative files already carry justification PROSE still stands — what is absent is the marker, not the
   discipline. That is the honest framing: the proposal formalises a real practice with a token that does
   not yet exist anywhere.

2. THE :host-transient COLLISION IS NEARLY TOTAL, which makes the auditing problem WORSE than the bead
   says and is the strongest argument for doing something. The bead notes "nine more files carry the same
   term". Measured in one scope with a live control (2079 defns, so the pathspec is alive):
       files carrying host-transient .............. 13
       files with real mutation ................... 39
       files with BOTH ............................. 2
   So ELEVEN of the thirteen host-transient files contain no mutation at all, and would appear in any
   naive \btransient\b census as undocumented-mutation findings. The contamination is not a handful of
   edge cases — it is 85% of the term's occurrences, and it runs in the direction that manufactures false
   findings against innocent files while the SAME census under-reads the best-documented real ones.

WHAT THAT DOES TO THE THREE OPTIONS THE BEAD LEAVES OPEN. The marker convention (write it down, apply to
new code, retrofit opportunistically) is unopposed by the stance: it constrains nothing an author may
write, costs one comment line at a new imperative site, and the bead explicitly rules OUT a gate without
Mike's word — so "trust the programmer" is not in tension with it. Against that, it is a brand-new token
in a tree that has none, and the stance's "do not litigate every last fine detail" is a real counterweight
if the answer is that nobody actually audits this often enough to care.
THE :host-transient RENAME, which the bead flags as an open question rather than proposing: my numbers say
the collision costs every future census the same two wrong readings this audit hit. Whether that is worth
a rename is a judgement about how often anyone runs such a census, which I cannot measure and you can.
I HAVE CHANGED NOTHING — no convention written, no rename, no gate. This note is the measurement.

=== RULING 2026-09-08 — NO MARKER CONVENTION. DECLINED. (Option E) ===

DECISION: re-frame2 adopts NO `;; PERF:` marker convention. Nothing is written into
`spec/Conventions.md`. No standing obligation is placed on any author. `;; PERF:` stays
AVAILABLE to anyone who wants it at a particular site (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:212`
already uses `;; PERF / coherence:`), but it carries no obligation, no spec paragraph and no
census meaning. Authors keep explaining non-obvious choices in their own words, which this
tree demonstrably already does well. The `:host-transient` rename is declined on its own terms.

WHO WON: the CODEX RECOMMENDATION, decisively, over the dossier's Option A+B (adopt as a
SHOULD in `spec/Conventions.md` plus opportunistic retrofit). Codex found three factual errors
in the dossier; each is confirmed at source below, and the corrections win. A fourth ground —
that the bead's founding premise is false — is mine, measured this session, and it is the one
that dissolves the bead rather than merely pricing it.

WHERE BOTH ANALYSES AGREE (recorded once): the CI gate is refused; the mass retrofit is
refused; the `:host-transient` rename is refused; the 2026-09-07 FP audit (rf2-5941) returned
PASS and the discipline is genuinely held; and the valuable half of this bead — the
prose-census contamination finding — already shipped to main as `CLAUDE.md` instrument-misreport
item (g) via rf2-jok0, so the next auditor is warned before running anything.

=== WHY — THE FOUR GROUNDS ===

(1) THE DOSSIER'S OWN SHOWCASE MARKER IS FACTUALLY WRONG. This is the single most decisive
fact in the file. Dossier section 4 Site 2 drafts a `;; PERF:` for
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/cascade.cljc:129` reading "one reduce over a whole
cascade's trace events per captured epoch, bounded at `sub-cap`/`view-cap`. Without transients
this rebuilds five persistent vectors per event." READ AT SOURCE, both cost claims are false.
The `cond` at `cascade.cljc:139-198` takes exactly ONE arm per event and falls through to
`:else acc` when nothing matches, so a persistent equivalent rebuilds ONE vector per event, not
five; the five result vectors are materialised once at the end, at `:207-211`. And the two flow
arms at `:179` and `:185` use bare `assoc!`/`conj!` with NO cap argument at all — only the sub
arms (`:166`, `:176`) and the view arm (`:196`) pass caps. So a three-line marker, written by a
careful analyst who had just read the file closely, carries two wrong cost implications. The
draft admits it needs confirming; the TAG SUPPLIES NONE. That is the convention failing in the
best case its own advocate could construct, and it is the answer to "what does the marker buy":
a claim of unverified accuracy, sitting where a grep will find it and be believed.

(2) THE RULE THE MARKER WOULD ENFORCE IS MISCATEGORISED. Dossier section 1.1 states imperative
constructs — `atom`, `volatile!`, `transient`, `set!`, `doseq` — are acceptable ONLY where they
buy performance in a hot zone. That is too broad, and the tree refutes it three ways:
  - `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/choice.cljc:315` uses `doseq` purely to
    throw on a self-targeting choice candidate. A validation effect. No speed content exists
    to state.
  - `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:75-81` holds the React root in an `atom`
    because loading a namespace must touch no DOM, so co-required example namespaces do not
    elbow each other onto the same `#app`. Six lines of excellent prose, zero performance
    content.
  - `spec/Conventions.md:1319-1328` — the `!`-suffix law — ALREADY RULES this exact question
    normatively for surface names, and rules it the other way: registrar-shaped mutation gets
    NO bang, because "adding a bang would tag every registration in the framework, which is
    the opposite of useful signal."
A `;; PERF:` obligation over these sites demands a performance claim where none exists, i.e.
it manufactures false explanations. The useful distinction is between externally observable
state/effects and local collection construction — not "is it imperative".

(3) `;; PERF:` IS NOT ABSENT FROM THE TREE, AND THE WAY THE DOSSIER MISSED IT PREVIEWS THE
CONVENTION'S OWN FAILURE MODE. `registrar.cljc:212` carries `;; PERF / coherence:`. The
dossier's section 5.1 census (`(?i);;+\s*perf(ormance)?\s*:`) returned zero-in-source because
` / coherence` sits between the word and the colon; the mayor's 2026-09-08 note caught a stray
`;; PERF ` = 1 and did not chase it. So the dossier produced a vocabulary-shaped false
negative WHILE MEASURING vocabulary-shaped false negatives. That is not a gotcha, it is the
mechanism: a marker makes prose greppable only if every author spells it identically forever,
and this tree's own capitalised-tag habit shows they will not — `;; COST:` and `;; ALWAYS-ON:`
(`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:98`, `:110`), `;; PURE:`
(11) and `;; CLJS-ONLY:` (14) in `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/`, and now
`;; PERF / coherence:`. The dossier reads that habit as evidence the convention is nearly
free ("standardise the tag you already reach for"); read honestly it is evidence that free-form
capitalised tags DRIFT, which is what would make the marker census untrustworthy in exactly
the way the prose census is untrustworthy today.

(4) THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS FALSE: THE HOT-ZONE RULE IS ALREADY AUDITABLE BY COMMAND. The
title says the rule "cannot be audited". It cannot be audited by a BADLY SPELLED command.
Measured this session, whole repo, all `.clj|.cljs|.cljc`, ripgrep-backed tool:
      `(transient `            ->  71 occurrences across  47 files
      `(volatile! |(vswap! `   -> 418 occurrences across 122 files
Both are ONE command, and both are COMPLETELY FREE of the contamination that motivated this
bead. Per file: `elision.cljc` 3, `trace/cascade.cljc` 5, `source_coords.cljc` 2,
`registrar.cljc` 1, `derivation/egress.cljc` ZERO, `machines/choice.cljc` ZERO — the two
false-positive files drop to zero the instant you match the spelling instead of the word.
That independently reproduces Codex's constructor table. And the results are FILE:LINE, i.e.
SITE-shaped, which is precisely the granularity the dossier's section 3.5 argues only a marker
can reach. `CLAUDE.md` item (g) already prescribes this exact remedy in these exact spellings
("Match the SPELLING you mean (`(transient `, `assoc!`, `persistent!`), never the bare word").
So the site-discovery half of any future audit costs one correct grep and zero authoring tax,
and it is already documented on main.

=== THE LOAD-BEARING ANALYSIS, PRESERVED ===

THE AUDIT'S FIGURES (rf2-5941, 2026-09-07, verdict PASS): 819 tracked production source files,
391,400 lines, 46 surfaces. 21 function-local scratch atoms tree-wide (later corrected to 19
after PR #9360 collapsed three into one factory) — that is the classic smell, and 19 in 391,400
lines is not a discipline problem. 169 production files use `transient`/`volatile!`/`vswap!`
and 136 of them (80%) carry prose explaining why. The audit found no systemic discipline
problem; it found at most an auditability problem, and ground (4) shows that problem was an
artefact of the query.

THE PROSE-CENSUS CONTAMINATION, WITH EVIDENCE AND CONTROLS. This is the most reusable thing in
the dossier. It is already on main as `CLAUDE.md` item (g); it is restated here because this
bead is where it was found and a future reader lands here first.
  FALSE NEGATIVES ON THE BEST-DOCUMENTED CODE. The synonym axis
  `(?i)perf|hot path|performance|allocation` rates `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc`
  at TWO hits (`:858`, `:896`) against roughly forty lines of exemplary justification, and
  rates `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/cascade.cljc` at ZERO while that file carries
  careful mutation-aware docstrings at `:94-115` ("O(1)", "in-place", "the `full?` guard is
  read BEFORE the conj so it never observes the post-mutation count"). POSITIVE CONTROL for
  that zero: same tool, same file, `persistent!|volatile!|vswap!|assoc!|conj!|dissoc!` returns
  13 and `transient` returns 11 on `cascade.cljc`. The zero is a property of the axis, not a
  broken search.
  FALSE POSITIVES ON THE MUTATION SIDE. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc`
  reads as the tree's largest concentration of undocumented transient use — 12 matching lines
  (13 occurrences; the dossier conflated the two) — and contains NO MUTATION AT ALL. Every hit
  is the domain term `:host-transient`, an in-flight HTTP handle address, at lines 14, 60, 233,
  234, 239, 240, 245, 246, 255, 278, 279 and 348. The mechanism is that `\b` MATCHES ACROSS A
  HYPHEN. Its only mutation-form hit is `(set! *warn-on-reflection* true)` boilerplate at `:72`;
  the narrow real-mutation pattern returns 0 (control: 13 on `cascade.cljc`).
  A THIRD FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS, found by the dossier and worth keeping:
  `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/choice.cljc` reads 8 on `\btransient\b`, zero
  mutation, and the collision needs no hyphen — it is the BARE WORD `transient` as the
  xstate/SCXML noun for an eventless state (lines 2, 9, 45, 71, 85, 158, 246, 252). Worse than
  `:host-transient` because any search for the word finds it, and because it is NOT renameable:
  "transient state" is the term of art in the domain this project targets for XState parity.
  WHY THIS IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY WRONG: the output is not an obvious error, it is a
  plausible RANKED WORKLIST that is wrong in the REASSURING direction — it manufactures
  findings against exactly the files that should be held up as the standard. An auditor who
  trusted the first census would have filed beads against exemplary code.
  THE GUARD, TWO PARTS: match the SPELLING you mean (`(transient `, `assoc!`, `persistent!`)
  so a hyphenated or homonymous domain term cannot answer for it; and READ THE RANKED FILE
  before believing its rank, because no synonym list is a census of INTENT.

A METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION THAT SURVIVES THIS BEAD (Codex, upheld): the "27 of 136 files"
and "11 of 13 host-transient files" figures are ratios of FILES under a particular detector.
They are not a measured false-positive RATE and not a claim about occurrences — a domain word
and real mutation can coexist in one file. Do not quote them as a precision figure.

EXEMPLAR FILES WORTH POINTING A FUTURE READER AT:
  - `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc` — `walk-states-tree` docstring
    `:890-903`, restated at `:866-870` and `:990-993`. Names what is hot (macro-expansion time,
    on every `reg-machine` form), what the functional shape would have cost (per-state
    allocation of intermediate persistent maps), the exit condition (benchmark against
    compile-time numbers before refactoring), AND a non-obvious correctness constraint that has
    nothing to do with performance: the accumulator must be a `volatile!` AROUND the transient,
    because a transient array-map promotes to a hash-map on its 9th distinct key and returns a
    NEW object, so `assoc!`'s return cannot be discarded. This is better than any marker would
    ask for and is the standard.
  - `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/cascade.cljc:94-115` — bounds and mutation-ordering
    documented without a single performance word. Correct, and correctly scores zero on a perf
    axis, because it was never making a performance argument.
  - `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:73-79` — an `atom` justified entirely on
    lifecycle/mount-isolation grounds. The counter-example to "imperative implies performance".
  - `spec/Conventions.md:1319-1328` — the `!`-suffix law, this repo's existing normative answer
    to "when do we mark mutation", and its reasoning ("the opposite of useful signal") is the
    reasoning that decided this bead.

WHAT A MACHINE-READABLE MARKER WOULD AND WOULD NOT BUY.
  WOULD: a partial index of authors' performance CLAIMS at sites where an author chose to write
  one. Nothing more.
  WOULD NOT: (i) site discovery — already one correct grep, ground (4); (ii) any assurance the
  claim is TRUE — ground (1) shows a careful author producing two false cost claims in three
  lines; (iii) any reduction in the false-positive half — the domain-word collisions are
  discharged by spelling, not by marking, and no marker shrinks them by one file; (iv) any
  answer to "does this optimisation earn its complexity", which is irreducibly a reading task
  that no tag and no form-parsing linter can perform.
  WHAT BREAKS IF NOBODY WRITES IT: nothing. The 47 constructor sites are one command away and
  80% already carry prose.
Under a posture that says TRUST THE PROGRAMMER and REJECT CEREMONY THAT EXISTS TO COVER A
TRUSTED PROGRAMMER, a standing obligation on every future author, read only by an occasional
auditor, enforced by nothing, and unreliable when written — is ceremony. Declined.

=== DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE — DO NOT ADD THESE LATER "TO FINISH THE JOB" ===
  1. NO CI GATE / LINT of any kind, including the changed-lines RATCHET variant. The dossier
     correctly notes a ratchet answers the day-one-redness objection; it is still refused, on
     the stronger ground that a correct gate needs a form-parsing detector of mutation sites
     (a text gate would demand markers above `project-host-transient` and the SCXML prose), and
     that is a disproportionate build for an audit that returned PASS — and it would still not
     grade whether the optimisation is warranted.
  2. NO SECTION IN `spec/Conventions.md`. No spec paragraph, no SHOULD, no MUST. The dossier's
     recommended one-small-PR is refused; that PR is not written.
  3. NO BACKFILL / RETROFIT — neither the 169-file sweep nor "opportunistic retrofit" as a
     standing instruction. Opportunistic retrofit is not free: it adds lines, decisions and
     conflicts, and yields uneven coverage that cannot be trusted as complete anyway.
  4. NO `:host-transient` RENAME, and no rename of the SCXML "transient state" vocabulary.
     `:host-transient` names an in-flight handle address clearly at `egress.cljc:233`; the
     collision is discharged by correct spelling; the term is load-bearing across `spec/`
     (`Derivations.md`, `Runtime-Subsystems.md`, `Spec-Schemas.md`, `002-Frames.md`,
     `016-Resources.md`, `009-Instrumentation.md`), six EPs, skills and the migration guide.
     Renaming away from a domain's own vocabulary to make a grep cleaner is the tail wagging
     the dog.
  5. NO FORM-PARSING MUTATION DETECTOR / reader-level tool.
  6. NO EDIT TO `CLAUDE.md` item (g) to add the SCXML sense. Item (g) already prescribes
     matching the spelling, which discharges BOTH domain senses at once (verified:
     `choice.cljc` reads 0 on `(transient `). Adding a second example is minutiae.

=== NEXT STEPS ===
NONE. There is no follow-on work and no dispatchable worker task. Item (1) of this bead
(the contamination finding) shipped via rf2-jok0 and is on main as `CLAUDE.md` item (g);
item (2) (the marker convention) is DECLINED here; item (3) (the rename) is DECLINED here.
No new bead is filed: the contamination finding already has a durable home in `CLAUDE.md`
and needs no work doing, so duplicating it into a bead would be pure redundancy.
THIS BEAD IS NOW EMPTY OF WORK and is left OPEN for the operator to close. Priority left at
P4 — raising it would signal work that no longer exists.

RECORDED BY: decision-closeout pass, mayor checkout, 2026-09-08. Read-only against the tree.
No tracked file was edited, no code, spec, `CLAUDE.md` or lint config touched, nothing staged,
committed or pushed, no build or test suite run. The measurements in grounds (1)-(4) were
taken with the ripgrep-backed search tool and by reading the cited source at the lines given.

title: docs(gate): doc_api_check's docstring names docs/core/api/**, a roster that does not exist — the code reads docs/api/
description:
Filed 2026-09-07 by the mayor from worker prose2-a's report on PR #9348, which found it while checking whether the gate's extractor would misfire on its edits.

THE DEFECT: `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/doc_api_check.clj`'s own docstring names a roster that does not exist.
  :7   "`docs/core/api/**` — the per-chapter human API reference"
  :91  "call-position references today (docs/core/api ~35, spec/Privacy ~22, ...)"
while the CODE's roster is `docs/api/` (:56, :58, and the roster itself around :84). Verified: `docs/core/api` is not a directory in this tree; `docs/api/` holds the per-namespace pages.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A TYPO: this gate is the FOURTH SURFACE obligation. Publishing or retiring a public name requires spec/API.md, the metadata sidecar, the regenerated manifest AND a member heading in `docs/api/<namespace>.md` — and that fourth is enforced by this gate and named by no bead. A PR in this session did the first three correctly and went red on the fourth. Anyone reading this file to understand what the gate covers is told to look in a directory that does not exist, and will conclude the gate does not cover the pages it actually grades.

ALSO WORTH CHECKING WHILE IN THERE, and this is what the worker was actually doing when it found the docstring: the extractor anchors on `\(rf/` before matching. That is why `(rf.machines/…)` call sites in `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md` do NOT redden it — there are four JVM-only tooling vars that would otherwise have failed. Whether that anchor is intentional or incidental is not established; the docstring should say which, since a reader cannot tell from the regex whether facade-only matching is the contract or an accident.

SCOPE: a docstring correction and, if the `\(rf/` anchor turns out to be contractual, one sentence saying so. Do NOT change the gate's behaviour — it is green across the tree and its roster is correct; only its self-description is wrong.

GATE: the `api-manifest` job's own steps (read the job's line range in `.github/workflows/lint.yml` and count `run:` steps — briefs have undercounted it twice, most recently as seven when it is eight).

NOT URGENT. P4: the gate works, only its description misleads.
notes:
WORKER gates-a, 2026-09-07. Implemented on worker/gates-a, PR #9364 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9364). Bead left OPEN for the mayor.

PREMISES VERIFIED AT SOURCE BEFORE EDITING (cited by construct, not line number, as the bead asked).
`git ls-files 'docs/core/api*'` returns 0 -- docs/core/api is not a directory. docs/api/ exists and
holds 22 tracked files (README + 21 per-namespace pages). The code's roster is the `dir-surfaces`
def: ["docs/api/" ["docs" "api"]] and ["docs/story/api/" ["docs" "story" "api"]]. Both of the bead's
cited constructs had NOT drifted and were found where described.

WHAT CHANGED -- DOCSTRING ONLY, in two places plus one addition.
  * The ns-docstring surface list: `docs/core/api/**` -> `docs/api/**`, and "per-chapter" ->
    "per-namespace", which is what the code actually reconciles (page-members builds
    docs/api/<namespace>.md; docs/api/README.md promises one page per public namespace).
    "Per-chapter" was true of docs/core/, the tree that does not exist at that path.
  * `min-references`: the same stale name carried a STALE COUNT, and the sentence already
    contradicted itself -- it claimed the three trees hold "~50" references and then itemised
    docs/core/api ~35 + spec/Privacy ~22 + docs/story/api ~15, which is 72. Measured at this tip:
    docs/api 285, spec/Privacy 22, docs/story/api 15 = 322. So Privacy and story were right and the
    docs/api figure was out by an order of magnitude. INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by the gate's own
    output when run: "spec/Privacy.md + docs/api/ + docs/story/api/ projection in sync (322
    public-var references checked against the manifest)". Per the house rule that a figure in a
    docstring goes stale silently, the replacement states NO per-tree count and says how to
    re-measure, rather than minting a fresh number.

THE `(rf/` ANCHOR QUESTION -- THE BEAD'S SUPPORTING CLAIM DOES NOT HOLD AT TIP.
The bead says the anchor is why "four JVM-only tooling vars" in docs/api/re-frame.machines.md do not
redden the gate. Measured: docs/api/ carries 35 non-facade alias call sites ((rf.machines/ 14,
(rf.http/ 14, (rf.routing/ 7), and EVERY ONE of their bare var names IS carried by the manifest's
bare-name set (checked against the 480 parsed :var names, with a two-way control -- a name known
present read true, a nonsense name read false). So widening the anchor would NOT redden the gate
today, and there are no four vars that would otherwise fail.
Because the anchor is therefore NOT established as contractual, it is documented as a DATED
MEASUREMENT rather than asserted as a contract: the docstring now says only two aliases are
extracted, that a sub-namespace-alias call is outside the check entirely, and that the narrowness is
not load-bearing at this tip. That answers the bead's "a reader cannot tell whether facade-only
matching is the contract or an accident" without inventing a contract nobody ruled.

GENERATOR OUTPUT UNCHANGED -- SHOWN, NOT ASSERTED.
  * Nothing `:require`s re-frame.api-manifest.doc-api-check anywhere in the directory (the other
    mentions in gen.clj, projection.clj and doc_guide_check.clj are COMMENTS), so `gen` cannot load
    it and a docstring in it cannot reach the generated file.
  * `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` -> "OK: spec/api-manifest.edn in sync (541
    public vars)", exit 0.
  * spec/api-manifest.edn git blob hash 47625d9d633c3b7bd05cb77904bfed903e5e254a before AND after;
    working tree clean afterwards. Byte-identical.
  * `clojure -M:test` in implementation/scripts/api-manifest: 98 tests, 194 assertions, 0 failures,
    0 errors, exit 0 -- which also proves the edited file still compiles.
No regeneration was needed and none was performed. No hot-zone file touched: spec/API.md and both
api-manifest sidecars are untouched.
close_reason: PR #9364 merged. doc_api_check.clj's docstring no longer names docs/core/api/**, a roster that does not exist; the code's roster is docs/api/. Worker gates-a showed rather than asserted that this was inert: spec/api-manifest.edn's blob hash is IDENTICAL before and after (47625d9d...), the tree stayed clean, 'gen --check' is green at 541 vars, and nothing :requires the edited namespace. CONTRADICTING THE BEAD: its claim that four JVM-only vars would otherwise fail does NOT hold — all 35 non-facade call sites resolve — so the worker documented the anchor as a dated measurement rather than inventing a contract to justify the citation. It also found the stale path carried a stale COUNT: '~50' itemised as 35+22+15=72, where the real total is 322, confirmed by the gate's own output.

title: docs(alias): RULED — decline the prose sweep; prose keeps its own example's alias. Decision + re-measured census recorded
description:
RULED 2026-09-08 23:42 AUSEST. This bead no longer asks a question — the decision is made and its
evidence is in the notes. Do NOT read the options below as a menu; they are settled.

THE RULING, three buckets:
  DELETE   nothing. Not one reference is removed. A blanket "remove all mentions" would destroy
           retirement bookkeeping, reserved-kind contracts and dated supersession notes.
  REWRITE  (R1) prose that contradicts a binding its OWN example makes — DELIVERED (8 sites,

THE "427" IN THE ORIGINAL TITLE AND TEXT IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BRIEF ANYONE. It is not a hit count
under any definition. Tracked .md under docs/ reads 429 today (427 when filed), which is suggestive
but does not prove what the original worker counted — treat the origin as unknown and the figure as

likewise not reproducible as stated and should not be used.

TRUE COUNTS, re-measured 2026-09-08 at HEAD 2da82eefc2 with a fresh instrument, 14/14 controls green
and a live-corpus assertion; full method, controls and the re-runnable queries are in the notes:
  code      : 2820 files, 11061 re-frame require edges, 0 non-canonical, all 27 surfaces at floor 0.
  prose     : tier 1 (alias-map keyed) 9327 hits / 1475 files; tier 2 (unambiguous) 3222 / 842;
              naive leaf grep 10343; canonical rf/ rf.<tail>/ in the same regions 14069.
  strata    : .md inline code 3854, .md fenced 1543, .md bare prose 569,
              .clj/.cljs/.cljc comments+docstrings 3361.

NOTHING HERE IS BLOCKED ON MIKE. Once the split bead lands, this one is empty of work — leave the
