notes:
========================================================================
PROSE ALIAS CENSUS (read-only measurement, 2026-09-07). Tip = main at the
time of measurement. NOTHING WAS EDITED; no PR.
RECOMMENDATION: (b), scoped to ~32 sites in 9 files. Then close. NOT (c).
========================================================================

WHAT I COUNTED — the operational definition, because no number means
anything without one.

PROSE REGION.
  * a git-tracked .md under docs/, skills/, migration/, spec/ or
    implementation/ (673 files); and
  * in a git-tracked .clj/.cljs/.cljc under implementation/, the COMPLEMENT
    of the ratchet's scan surface: line comments and string literals
    (docstrings). This is exactly what check_require_alias_dialect.py's
    reader-level mask blanks before it scans a bracket, so it is precisely
    "the part of the code corpus the ratchet cannot see".

ALIAS REFERENCE. A token `A/sym` where A is a symbol, sym is a symbol,
the token is not preceded by `:` (a literal or auto-resolved keyword is not
an alias reference — the ratchet's trap 1), is not followed by `/` (another
path segment), and sym does not end in a file extension (a repo-relative
doc path is not an alias reference — the ratchet's trap 3).

NON-CANONICAL. A is not the alias Conventions §Require-alias dialect allows
for the namespace it denotes: `rf` for re-frame.core / re-frame, and
`rf.<full dotted tail>` otherwise. This is canonical_alias() in the ratchet,
read at source, not paraphrased. NOTE that "bare-leaf" is too narrow a word
for what is actually out there: `h`, `ht`, `hm`, `ts`, `v`, `n`,
`reagent-adapter`, `uix-adapter` are ABBREVIATIONS, not leaves. The
population is "non-canonical", of which bare-leaf is a minority.

DENOTES. A is taken to denote namespace N when the prose region itself binds
`[N :as A]`; failing that, when the file's directory does; failing that,
when any tracked .md/.clj/.cljs/.cljc/.edn in the repo does.

THREE PASSES, as required, on both halves (bindings and use sites):
  A  line-oriented   B  whitespace collapsed   C  comment markers stripped,
  then collapsed.
Binding extraction is a BALANCED-BRACKET scan over each pass, not a regex to
end-of-line, because the ratchet's own trap 4 (a libspec vector that closes
on the next line) is real and silent.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE POPULATION — THREE-PASS COUNTS

Non-canonical alias references in prose regions:
    pass A (line)          7128
    pass B (flat)          7128
    pass C (strip+flat)    7128
Canonical (rf / rf.<tail>) references in the same regions, all three passes:
   10246.
Prose-region BINDINGS (distinct ns/alias pairs) DO move across passes:
    A 402   B 404   C 403
i.e. two libspec bindings in the corpus are line-broken and invisible to a
line-oriented scan, and one is reachable only with comment markers stripped.
That is the three-pass rule earning its keep on the bindings; the use-site
counts are pass-invariant here, which is a MEASUREMENT, not an assumption —
an `A/sym` token cannot be split by a newline, so collapsing whitespace
cannot create or destroy one.

By scope (pass A; docs/design counted SEPARATELY as asked):
    docs/design            2061      implementation/flows        55
    docs                   1531      implementation/http         53
    implementation/hicasso  733      migration                   55
    spec                    704      implementation/machines     49
    skills                  548      implementation/resources    43
    implementation/adapters 263      implementation/schemas      56
    implementation/core     387      implementation/routing      91
    implementation/ssr      300      everything else            <90 each

>>> THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS NOT USABLE AS A WORK ESTIMATE, and this is the
    most important instrument finding. Of 77 non-canonical aliases bound to
    a re-frame namespace anywhere in the repo, 25 are ALSO bound to a
    NON-re-frame namespace somewhere — and they are the high-volume ones:
    `h`, `n`, `r`, `reagent`, `machines`, `routing`, `epoch`, `db`,
    `events`, `mount`, `server`, `reg`. So a grep-shaped census over prose
    is systematically inflated by tokens that are not re-frame references at
    all. Hand-sampled false positives, all confirmed at source:
      - `uix/use-ref`, `uix/use-effect` in the UIx adapter README — that
        file binds `[uix.core :as uix :refer [defui $]]` at line 65. UIx the
        LIBRARY, not re-frame.adapter.uix.
      - `reagent/argv` in spec/Pattern-StatefulComponents.md — Reagent's own
        reagent.core/argv.
      - `reagent/reagent` in three skills pages — a MAVEN COORDINATE.
      - `server/client`, `story/test`, `epoch/replay`, `epoch/SSR`,
        `routing/navigation`, `alias/verb` — English slash-pairs and
        metavariables in running prose.
      - `routing/fragment-change` in spec/009 — a CONFORMANCE FIXTURE NAME.
    Restricting to the 52 UNAMBIGUOUS non-canonical aliases drops the
    population from 7128 to 2893 (2636 of them marked up as code); false
    positives survive even that filter.
    Two further honest splits: 797 of the 7128 sit in bare running prose
    with no code markup at all, and 635 name a namespace with no `(ns …)`
    declaration at tip — re-frame.freehand (removed 2026-08-16) and the v1
    archaeology in the migration corpus (re-frame.db, re-frame.subs,
    re-frame.router). Those CANNOT be walked to canonical: there is no
    `rf.db` to walk to.

>>> I DID NOT REPRODUCE 372 / 78 / 67 / 427. Nothing I measured lands on
    them under any definition I tried. One coincidence I report WITHOUT
    claiming causation, because it is one minute of the mayor's attention:
    `git ls-files 'docs/**/*.md' 'docs/*.md' | sort -u | wc -l` = 427
    EXACTLY. Also `implementation/flows` has ZERO bare `flows/` tokens in
    its markdown (its 55 hits are other aliases), which is hard to square
    with "flows 78 vs 4". Treat all four figures as unsupported.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. THE DISCRIMINATING QUESTION — HOW MANY SITES CONTRADICT THEIR OWN SAMPLE

This is the option-(b) census and it is the answer that matters.

Instrument 1 (alias-map keyed): 57 raw candidates — 33 where the SAME FILE's
prose binds the namespace to a different alias, 24 only at directory scope.

title: realworld: duplicate React key warning on the article-card tag list
description:
Seen 2026-09-04 in a development build of `:examples/realworld` once the feed actually
rendered (it was invisible before rf2-2xzc's fix because no cards were ever drawn, and it is
invisible in a release build because production React does not emit key warnings).

  Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop.
  Check the render method of `li`. It was passed a child from realworld-http.co...

A `li` list rendered from realworld-http code is missing `:key` on its children - most likely
the tag list on an article card, where several cards carry the same tag string, so a
value-derived key would collide across cards rather than within one. Reproduced on the home
feed after sign-in; zero page errors otherwise.

Small, cosmetic, and entirely inside examples/real-apps/realworld_http/. Filed rather than
folded into PR #9134 to keep that diff to the defect it explains.
close_reason: PR #9155. The bead's hypothesis is REFUTED: every tag list already carries ^{:key tag} (articles.cljs:443, comments.cljs:830), and all 7 seq-producing child sites across the 13 realworld_http files are keyed. The bead's 'entirely inside realworld_http' is also wrong - the unkeyed seq comes from realworld_shared/markdown.cljs and has no call-site fix. Mechanism verified link by link at source: markdown-it marks a TIGHT list item's paragraph hidden (measured: all 3 bullets of the demo article body return paragraph_open hidden=true); impl.cljs:70-73 maps hidden -> :plain; transform.cljc:79-80 has :plain return a bare (seq ...); transform.cljc:111 has :list-item = (partial into-markup [:li]) which conj's that seq in. Result [:li ("text " [:code ...])] - an ARRAY child, which is why React names the render method of li. Fixed by a :plain renderer emitting a fragment, so children are positional siblings not a list; keys would be wrong here since prose runs have no stable identity. Fixes both RealWorld apps (shared ns). NOT observed: the warning vanishing in a live dev build - no static gate sees a React key warning and no browser was driven.

DIRECTION OF FAILURE, both ways, because they need different responses. Over-reporting is the common
case and it fails CLOSED: a basename fence invents a collision, the mayor sequences two beads that never
conflicted, and the cost is throughput. It can also fail OPEN where two children spell the same file
differently -- one bare, one full -- and a matcher does not normalise, in which case a real collision is
missed and two workers land in one file. Stating the full path removes both at once.

This is the identity-field rule CLAUDE.md already gives for bead ids -- select on the identity, never on
a substring that merely mentions it -- reached through a file path instead of an id.

title: fix(pair-mcp): preload-missing hint still says :source-paths — the advice #10160 removed, and SKILL.md quotes it verbatim
description:
The MCP server's preload-missing hint still gives the advice PR #10160 REMOVED, and SKILL.md tells the agent to report that hint VERBATIM — so following it on a :deps app produces a build failure.

## The defect, measured at trunk f6e8628d10

`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/probe.cljs:99-104`, definition
`preload-missing-hint`, ends:

    "is on :source-paths. See skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md (§Setup)."

PR #10160 corrected exactly this advice across five documentation sites, because under `:deps` and
`:lein` shadow IGNORES a `shadow-cljs.edn` `:source-paths` key and warns that it did. This string was
missed.

## Why it is worse than an ordinary stale string

It is returned on the very rung this failure produces (`:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing`), and
`skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md` instructs the agent to **report the hint verbatim** — so the wrong
advice is not merely available, it is actively read out to the user at the exact moment they are
trying to fix the thing it is wrong about.

Following it on a `:deps` app was measured under rf2-7gz4c producing shadow's verbatim "were ignored!"
warning and then **compile exit 1**: `The required namespace "re-frame2-pair.runtime" is not available`.

## This is the same defect as errors.md:18, surviving one layer down

`skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md:18` WAS corrected by #10160 to say "the build's
**classpath**". The identical claim inside the MCP server's own hint string was not. So the corrected
documentation and the uncorrected runtime hint now disagree, and the runtime one is the one an agent
quotes.

## Shape of the fix

One definition, three use sites (`:365`, `:373`, `:391`), so the repair is in one place. Suggested
replacement for the final clause, from the rf2-7gz4c worker:

> "is on the build's CLASSPATH — for a `:deps` app an activated alias's `:extra-paths` in `deps.edn`,
> for `:lein` the `:source-paths` in `project.clj`, and only for a standalone shadow app
> `:source-paths` in `shadow-cljs.edn`."

## NO TEST PINS THE LITERAL TEXT — the search is live

Measured: **0** matches for the hint text across the server's test tree, against **1** in `src/`. So a
census for it is not returning a false zero; there genuinely is no pin. Whether to add one is open —
a literal-text pin on a hint string is the kind of thing that goes stale itself, so it may be right to
leave it unpinned and rely on the docs gate. That is a judgement for whoever takes this.

## Provenance

Found by the rf2-7gz4c worker while running the held end-to-end acceptance check of the #10160 recipe.
It NAMED the defect rather than editing, because the file lay outside its fence — the fence working as
designed. It is a third file beyond the two that item's fence named.
notes:
## Done — PR #10188 (branch worker/hintfix-2ezk3), 2026-09-22

The premise held at source and the defect was live at tip. `preload-missing-hint`
(`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/probe.cljs:99`) still ended
"is on :source-paths"; the shape was exactly as filed — one definition, three use
sites (`:365`, `:373`, `:391`), so one repair.

### Verified before acting, not assumed

* #10160 is `b1d638dc8f` (rf2-dpt9d). Its own message states the evidence: shadow-cljs
  3.4.10 `shadow/cljs/npm/cli.cljs` `run-clojure` warns "The configured :source-paths in
  shadow-cljs.edn were ignored! When using :deps they must be configured in deps.edn",
  `run-lein` the project.clj equivalent. It touched four files / five sites.
* `SKILL.md` §Setup does instruct "report the hint verbatim" — checked at source, so the
  item's central claim about why this string matters more than an ordinary stale one holds.
* `references/errors.md` is the corrected twin, and the new wording agrees with both it
  and SKILL.md §Setup's three-row classpath-owner table.
* NO TEST PINNED THE TEXT — confirmed independently. Zero matches for `source-paths`
  across the server's test tree, with the control taken FROM that tree rather than from
  `src/`: the same search returns many hits there for `:hint`, `preloads`,
  `shadow-cljs.edn` and `classpath`, so the zero is absence and not a dead instrument.

### The census: this was the last site

A three-pass census (line-oriented, whitespace-collapsed, and comment-markers-stripped-
then-collapsed, to reach a phrase wrapped across lines or sitting behind a comment marker)
over all 5571 tracked files finds `probe.cljs` the ONLY remaining file giving that advice
as an instruction. The other hits are legitimate and were each read: tracker prose; the
surface classifier; this repo's own `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, which is a
standalone shadow build where `:source-paths` IS correct; and SKILL.md's own standalone
branch. Control fires in the other direction — nine files carry the corrected "build's
classpath" wording, the #10160 sites among them.

Worth recording: the MCP server's own `shadow-cljs.edn` is `{:deps true}`. The advice the
server was handing out would have been wrong for the server's own repo.

### The fix

The hint now names the build's CLASSPATH and branches to all three owners, matching
SKILL.md §Setup: an activated alias's `:extra-paths` (or top-level `:paths`) in `deps.edn`
for `:deps`; `:source-paths` in `project.clj` for `:lein`; `:source-paths` in
`shadow-cljs.edn` only for a standalone shadow app. It also names the discriminator the
user must read (the top of their own `shadow-cljs.edn`) and states the ignore, so someone
who has already seen shadow's startup warning can connect the two and understand why they
keep landing back on this rung. The `:preloads` half is untouched — correct, and always a
`shadow-cljs.edn` line.

### THE OPEN QUESTION, ANSWERED: yes, pin it — as a PROPERTY, not as literal text

Argued rather than assumed, and the argument is the reason for the shape.

A literal-text pin COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS DEFECT. The string never changed, so an
equality assertion written when the hint was first authored would have stayed green for
precisely as long as the advice was wrong — it would have said nothing on the day #10160
landed, which is the one day it needed to speak. And it would then go stale on the next
rewording, which is this very item one layer up. So "add a pin" in its obvious form is not
merely unhelpful here; it fails in the reassuring direction.

What must hold is not the wording but the PROPERTY: the hint names the classpath and
BRANCHES to all three owning files rather than naming one. A revert to single-file advice
fails that; a rewording survives it. That is the invariant #10160 established, and it is
the thing worth defending.

Pinned at the RUNG rather than at the var, because the var has three call sites and what
matters is the text that reaches a caller. The new test drives `ensure-runtime!` through
the ladder to `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` and asserts on the `:hint` it finds in
the rejection's `ex-data`. `probe_test.cljs` already pinned this rung loosely at
`#"preload"`; this tightens the same rung without duplicating it.

### Control: the rung, not the string

The hint was READ OFF THE RUNG, not diffed in the source. Driving the ladder and printing
the delivered `:hint` returned the corrected text with the branch present.

Sabotage: reverting the clause produced a working file whose blob hash equals the pre-fix
blob byte-for-byte, so the plant reproduced the exact defect rather than an approximation.
The suite went to captured exit 1 with 4 failures, all inside the new test, each naming
the property lost, and the delivered hint printed as the old `:source-paths` text.
Namespace and assertion counts held at 1201 / 4415 across green and red, so no namespace
was crashed into a plausible-looking log. Restore verified by hashing the bytes against
the committed blob objects, with `git diff --quiet HEAD` as an independent second
instrument; the temporary print is gone from the final green log.

title: Links escaping docs/ into examples/ are validated by NO gate — measure the class, then decide gate vs one CLAUDE.md sentence
description:
Found by the rf2-cc1mb worker on 2026-09-22 while building a red-first control, and **reported rather
than repaired** — which is why it survives as a finding instead of evaporating into a fixed line.

## The defect

A relative link from a page under `docs/` that ESCAPES the docs tree into `examples/` — the
`](../../examples/…)` shape — is validated by **no gate in this repository**.

Measured at `docs/routing/examples.md:10`, in both directions on the same line, which is what makes it
a finding rather than a guess:

* A plant that broke an **in-tree** target on that line → `check_doc_slugs.py` **exit 1**, naming the
  file and line. So the gate reads the line.
* A plant that broke the **`](../../examples/…)`** target on that SAME line → `check_doc_slugs.py`
  **exit 0**. It reads the line and does not resolve a target escaping into `examples/`.
* `mkdocs build --strict` **exit 0** and never mentions it either.

`scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` does not cover `docs/` at all (`docs` is in its
`DOCS_GATE_ROOTS` exclusion set), so there is no third gate to catch it.

## Why it is dangerous rather than untidy

**It fails in the reassuring direction for the exact act a careful worker performs.** A worker
planting a sabotage control on such a link sees the gate exit 0 and has two readings available: *the
gate is broken* or *my plant did not apply*. The cc1mb worker took neither on trust — it planted on
the same line in the other direction, got a red, and so localised the blindness to the link CLASS.
A tireder reader concludes the plant failed, re-plants, and eventually decides the gate is fine.

And the green is indistinguishable from a real pass, so a genuinely broken `examples/` link in the
docs tree ships silently.

## What is NOT claimed

* The blast radius is unmeasured. Nobody has counted how many `](../../examples/…)` links exist under
  `docs/`, nor how many currently resolve. **Measure that first** — with the control taken from the
  target so a zero means absence rather than a broken instrument — because the answer decides whether
  this is worth a gate at all.
* Whether the skip is DELIBERATE is unknown. `check_doc_slugs.py` deliberately skips `http(s)` targets
  and every directory named `findings`, so a deliberate escape-hatch for paths leaving `docs_dir` is
  entirely plausible — read the resolver and its comments before treating this as a bug.
* No gate change is proposed here. If the skip turns out to be deliberate and correctly so, the right
  outcome is **one sentence in CLAUDE.md § Build & Test's link-validation paragraph naming the class
  as ungated**, next to the fence and no-links cases already recorded there — not a new mechanism.

## Sequencing

`rf2-dnx3r` is live in BOTH gate scripts right now (branch `worker/sitelinks-dnx3r`), teaching them to
resolve this project's own site URLs offline. **Do not dispatch this concurrently with it**, and
re-measure after that merges — its change may move the resolver this finding is about.

`rf2-3pwdo` already owns the CLAUDE.md link-validation paragraph and is ruled; if the outcome is one
sentence rather than a gate, it belongs there rather than in a PR of its own.
notes:
## VERDICT (worker, 2026-09-22, re-measured at merge base `99488a3c35` = the PR #10237 / rf2-dnx3r merge)

**THE PREMISE IS REFUTED AS STATED, AND THE REAL CLASS IS DIFFERENT AND LARGER.** The discriminator is
NOT "escapes `docs/` into `examples/`" — it is the `.md` EXTENSION. `check_doc_slugs.py` resolves a
relative target that leaves `docs/` perfectly well; `_resolve_target` returns None only when a target
escapes the REPO, and `examples/` is in the repo. What skips the link is an earlier, explicit guard in
`check()`'s link loop:

    # Only validate links to .md files — anchors and target-existence
    # on other file types (images, source files, asset links) aren't
    # part of the slug-index contract.  mkdocs' own link check is the
    # right gate for those.
    if not path_part.endswith(".md"):
        continue

**So the skip IS deliberate (item 2 of the brief): a comment, a stated rationale and a named delegate.**
It is not an absence-of-check inferred from silence.

### The control: four plants, ONE line, `docs/routing/examples.md:10`

That line carries both shapes at once — `[routing](../../examples/capabilities/routing/routing)` and
`[Tutorial](tutorial.md)`. Match count read as 1 before every plant; every restore verified against the
committed blob `f4b3e2120073369f15f497d73aee238efac0a24d` by the DEFAULT `git hash-object` form (the
file is `i/lf w/crlf`, so the default form is the right one) with `git diff --quiet HEAD` exit 0 beside
it, and `cr=13 crlf=13 bare_lf=0` after.

| plant | target | leaves `docs/`? | ends `.md`? | captured exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `tutorial-PLANT-P1-NO-SUCH.md` | no | yes | **1** — names `docs/routing/examples.md:10` |
| P2 | `../../examples/capabilities/routing/routing-PLANT-P2-NO-SUCH` | yes | no | 0 |
| P3 | `../../examples/capabilities/routing/PLANT-P3-NO-SUCH.md` | **yes** | **yes** | **1** — names `examples\capabilities\routing\PLANT-P3-NO-SUCH.md` |
| P4 | `PLANT-P4-NO-SUCH-asset` | no | no | 0 |

**P3 is the decisive plant and it is the one the original finding did not run.** The gate follows the
link out of `docs/` into `examples/` and reports the missing target by its `examples/` path. P4 closes
the square from the other side: a non-`.md` target that never leaves `docs/` is skipped just the same.
Perfect separation on the extension column, zero separation on the escape column. P1 and P2 reproduce
the original finding's two readings exactly at this merge base; the original localised the blindness to
the wrong axis because both of its plants varied extension and escape TOGETHER.

### The delegation in that comment does NOT hold for a target that leaves `docs_dir` — measured

The comment delegates non-`.md` targets to `mkdocs build --strict`. For a target that leaves `docs_dir`
MkDocs never sees a link at all: `mkdocs_hooks.py`'s `_REWRITES` turns `](../../examples/…)` into
`https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/main/examples/…` at build time, and MkDocs does not validate
external URLs. Measured end to end with P2 in place: `python -m mkdocs build --strict` exit **0**, the
log never mentions the plant (grep count 0), and the built page `site/routing/examples/index.html`
ships `https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/main/examples/capabilities/routing/routing-PLANT-P2-NO-SUCH`.
**A broken relative link is promoted into a broken ABSOLUTE URL on the published site.** Baseline
`mkdocs build --strict` exit 0 in 24s beside it, so the green is the instrument working.

The delegation is sound for the 24 non-`.md` links that stay inside `docs_dir`, and unsound for the 402
that leave it.

### BLAST RADIUS (item 1), measured with the GATE'S OWN extractor so fences are stripped identically

Across all roots `_iter_markdown` scans (768 pages: docs 429, skills 171, tools 109, spec 51, migration 8;
15,400 relative in-repo links):

* `.md` path-parts: **14,974**, of which **0 broken**. Corroborated independently by the live gate at
  exit 0.
* non-`.md` path-parts: **426**, of which **2 broken**. 402 leave `docs_dir` (2 broken), 24 stay inside (0).
* By source root, non-`.md`: docs 155 (2 broken), spec 119, tools 116, skills 33, migration 3.

**The bead's OWN named class — `](../../examples/…)` from a page under `docs/`, every depth — is 61
links: 60 non-`.md`, 1 `.md`, and ZERO broken today.** So the class the finding names is real, is larger
than "depth two", and is currently clean.

Control taken FROM the target, as asked: P3's red proves an escaping `.md` link is genuinely resolved
(so the 312 escaping `.md` links under `docs/` are gated, 277 of them into `spec/`), and spot-checks
confirm `examples/capabilities/routing/routing` and `examples/real-apps/realworld_http` exist while the
two reported-broken targets do not. A nonsense needle read 0 beside a live needle reading non-zero.

### The 2 live defects, and why they are worth an item of their own

Both on `docs/design/fresco/studio/the-clock-behind-the-published-rows.md`, lines 99 and 100:

* `../../../../implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_harness.cljs`
* `../../../../implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/fresco_narrow.cljs`

Both files exist, at `bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/`. `p0_harness.cljs` DID live at the cited
`implementation/core/test/...` path until `8a10915ed8` ("move the bench tree to bench/hicasso … move
only") relocated it. **The move broke the links AND the claim built on them**: the table calls these
rows "in a **different tree**" and "in a **third tree**", and after the move all the cited producers are
in one tree. So this is not a path typo to patch — repairing only the paths would leave the page
internally contradictory, links saying one tree and prose saying three. **Deliberately NOT repaired
here; filed separately.** Note these two are doubly invisible: non-`.md` to the slug gate, and
`design/fresco/` is in `mkdocs.yml`'s `exclude_docs` so the site build never sees the page either.
`check_provenance_pins.py` does not reach them — it grades commit permalinks, not file links.

### RECOMMENDATION — one sentence, not a gate (and the 2 links filed separately)

A gate is defensible and is NOT urged. The honest arguments, both ways:

* FOR: the mechanism is live and ships a dead URL to the published site; the comment's stated delegate
  provably cannot cover 402 of the 426; the machinery already exists (`_resolve_target`), so the check
  is existence-only and roughly six lines; and the project ALREADY validates these very destinations in
  the other spelling — `IN_REPO_GH_URL_RE` / `_in_repo_github_url_problems` (rf2-nvbz) unwraps
  `blob/main` URLs and checks existence and blob-vs-tree kind. The build converts the unvalidated
  spelling into the validated one.
* AGAINST, and decisive: the measured yield is **2**, both in a tree the site excludes, and the bead's
  named class is clean at 0. *We don't need to litigate every last fine detail.* A new mechanism to keep
  in sync is not earned by two stale links from one tree move.

**So: one sentence in CLAUDE.md § Build & Test's link-validation paragraph, which belongs to rf2-3pwdo
and is NOT written here.** The proposed text is in the worker's report to the operator. The gate
proposal is recorded there too, for the operator to take or drop; `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` is in any
case HELD by the rf2-co91r worker as of this writing.

### Side-finding: both gates' self-tests UNDER-REPORT their own pass counts

The printed total is a hand-maintained sum (`len(cases) + len(teeth_cases) + len(extraction_cases) +
len(fence_cases) + 4`) that does not include every block emitting a `self-test PASS` line.

| gate | pre-dnx3r PASS lines | pre printed total | post PASS lines | post printed total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `check_doc_slugs.py` | 155 | 151 | 159 | 155 |
| `check_readme_links.py` | 20 | 20 | 24 | 23 |

`check_doc_slugs.py` carries a constant −4 offset that PREDATES dnx3r; `check_readme_links.py` was exact
before and drifted by −1 with it. **The trap: doc_slugs' POST-dnx3r printed total (155) equals its
PRE-dnx3r PASS-line count (155)**, so quoting the PASS count before and the printed total after (or the
reverse) reads as "dnx3r added no self-tests" when it added four — a reassuring-direction misread of a
number this project's briefs routinely ask workers to quote before and after. Pre-dnx3r figures were
taken by exec'ing the parent blob with `__file__` pointed at the real script path, writing nothing into
the repo. Not repaired: both gate scripts are held.

### Not verified / out of scope

* rf2-co91r's dotted-final-segment regression was NOT exercised: this measurement skips all `http(s)`
  destinations and calls `_resolve_target` directly, so it never enters `_site_url_path`. The live gate
  read exit 0 at this merge base, so no such link is present in the tree today.
* No shadow-cljs lane entered at any depth.
* Nothing was edited in either gate script.
### ADDENDUM — re-derived at trunk `b3035950278b9883452e93ade6d4a158b4d3bb3c` (after rebase)

Trunk moved while this was being measured, and one of the landings — `2e929e7718` ("docs(examples): truth
three ruled examples-docs claims (rf2-cc1mb, rf2-cklff, rf2-j7w2u)") — edited the very page the control was
planted on, `docs/routing/examples.md`. It rewrote line 10's "What it shows" prose cell and left BOTH link
shapes on that line untouched, so the control site is structurally identical.

Every headline figure re-derived at the new base, and the verdict does not move:

* `.md` path-parts **14,974**, broken **0** (live gate exit 0 beside it, so two instruments agree).
* non-`.md` **427** (was 426 — one link added under `spec/`), broken **2**.
* Leaving `docs_dir` **403** (broken 2); staying inside **24** (broken 0).
* The two broken links are the SAME two, unchanged: `the-clock-behind-the-published-rows.md` lines 99 and
  100. Filed as rf2-319en.

So the recommendation stands as written above: one sentence rather than a gate, on a yield of two.
close_reason:
DONE — measured, premise REFUTED, recommendation recorded, no PR and no gate. Measured at trunk
`b303595027`. This item asked for a measurement before a repair, and the measurement changed what the
finding is.

## THE PREMISE IS WRONG AS STATED, AND THE ERROR IS INSTRUCTIVE

The discriminator is **NOT** "a link escaping `docs/` into `examples/`". It is the **`.md`
EXTENSION**. `check()`'s link loop in `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` carries an explicit guard
validating only targets whose path-part ends in `.md`, and its comment states the rationale and names

those."* `_resolve_target` returns `None` only when a target escapes the REPO, and `examples/` is in
the repo. **So question 2 is answered by comment and structure rather than inferred from an absent

match count read as 1 before each and every restore verified against the committed blob by the
default `git hash-object` form (`i/lf w/crlf`; `git diff --quiet` exit 0; cr=13 crlf=13 bare_lf=0):

| plant | leaves `docs/`? | ends `.md`? | exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 `tutorial-PLANT-P1-NO-SUCH.md` | no | yes | **1**, naming `…examples.md:10` |
| P2 `…/examples/…/routing-PLANT-P2-NO-SUCH` | yes | no | 0 |
| P3 `…/examples/…/PLANT-P3-NO-SUCH.md` | **yes** | **yes** | **1**, naming the escaping target |
| P4 `PLANT-P4-NO-SUCH-asset` | no | no | 0 |

**P3 is the plant the original finding never ran.** The original varied extension and escape
TOGETHER, so it had two readings that fitted two hypotheses equally and it took the wrong one —
exactly the confounded-variables shape CLAUDE.md records for instrument item (d). P1 and P2
reproduce the original's two readings precisely, so nothing it saw was wrong; only the axis it

## AND THE DELEGATION IN THAT COMMENT IS FALSE FOR ESCAPING LINKS — which is the better finding

The guard hands non-`.md` targets to `mkdocs build --strict`. Measured with P2 in place:

sync.** That is the stance's restraining half, applied to the item's own subject. The proposed

operator; the worker wrote it and deliberately did not land it. A costed gate sketch is on that note
too, should the answer ever change.

Both gates' `--self-test` UNDER-REPORT their own pass counts, the printed total being a

| gate | actual PASS / printed (pre-#10237) | actual PASS / printed (post) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check_doc_slugs.py` | 155 / **151** | 159 / **155** |
| `check_readme_links.py` | 20 / 20 | 24 / **23** |

title: machines-core: consumer attachment never ensures :rf.cofx/requires for a flat/compound machine's root :on candidates - a named root guard reads nil and is not selected
description:
## Defect

Consumer attachment (`:rf.cofx/requires` on a named `:guards` / `:actions` entry) never ensures the facts declared by candidates on a flat or compound machine's ROOT `:on`. The runtime DOES select from the root `:on` (spec 005 steps 7-8, `pick-transition`'s root fallback). So a named guard used there reads `nil` for its declared generator-backed fact, and the transition is wrongly NOT selected: silently, with no error. The same guard on a state's own `:on` works.

The spec defines the ensure-set as the union over "every guard/action any candidate transition for that event type can touch on the active state path (leaf→root)" (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:445`). The root `:on` is steps 7-8 of that walk (`:1555-1556`).

## Where

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc:606-700` (`ensure-set-in-scope`). It receives only the `:states` SCOPE, and its candidate walk `(doseq [i (range (count path))] …)` at `:650-675` visits prefixes of length 1..n. The machine map's own `:on` is structurally unreachable from there.
- `cofx_attach.cljc:783-830` (`ensure-set-for`). The parallel branch adds `parallel-root-diet` (`:731`) for the parallel root's `:on` / `:after`; the flat/compound branch (`:824-830`) has no root equivalent.
- The runtime side that DOES consult the root: `transition.cljc:1490-1493` (`pick-transition`), plus the root fallbacks inside `pick-done-transition` / `pick-spawn-error-transition` (`:1444-1447`).
- Public entry point: `rf/dispatch` to a registered machine whose root `:on` uses a named guard/action carrying `:rf.cofx/requires`.
- All citations are at `034d0c8fc8`.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-cofx :probe/roll {:recordable? true} (fn [] 6))
(rf/reg-machine :m
  {:initial :idle
   :guards  {:rolled-six? {:rf.cofx/requires [:probe/roll]
                           :fn (fn [{c :rf.cofx}] (= 6 (:probe/roll c)))}}
   :on      {:go {:target :done :guard :rolled-six?}}   ;; ROOT :on
   :states  {:idle {} :done {}}})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:m [:go]])   ;; stays :idle — the guard saw nil
```

## Evidence

EXECUTED. A scratch JVM probe (`make-reset-runtime-fixture`, plain-atom, real `dispatch-sync`), with no writes to the frozen tree:

| Case | `ensure-set-for` ids | guard saw | state after `[:go]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| CONTROL: guard on the LEAF `:idle`'s `:on` | `[:probe/roll]` | `6` | `:done` |
| CASE: identical guard on the ROOT `:on` | `[]` | `nil` | `:idle` |

INSPECTED, not executed. These are sibling gaps with the same shape: a slot the runtime selects from that the ensure-set does not walk.

- A parallel REGION body's own root `:on` is also unreached: the per-region call passes `(:states body)` only.
- `on-done-diet-for-event` (`:540-562`) looks up `node-at states done-path` without stripping a region-name head, so a region compound's `:on-done` diet is likely missed.
- The single-`:spawn` `[:spawn :on-error]` slot (resolved by `pick-spawn-error-transition`) has no diet clause.

Tracker: no existing bead. rf2-3oyn (closed) refactored these walks' accumulators and did not touch their coverage.

## Smallest fix

In `ensure-set-for`'s flat/compound branch, add the machine root's own `:on` candidates for `event-id`: the exact, `:ns/*` and `:*` tiers, their guard/action diets, and the target entry and `:always` closure. This mirrors what `parallel-root-diet` already does for the parallel root. Apply the same treatment to a region body's root `:on`, and decide whether the `:on-done` region-head and `:spawn :on-error` slots join the same change.

Fence: `cofx_attach.cljc` only, plus a JVM test beside `machine_cofx_attach_test.clj` pinning the CASE/CONTROL pair above. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines` (JVM; the change is in shared `.cljc` code, not a `#?(:cljs …)` branch).
- `npm run test:cljs` if any `*_cljs_test.cljc` cofx suite is extended.

## Decision needed

None on the root `:on` half, which the spec's leaf→root wording already covers. The implementer decides whether the three inspected sibling slots ship in the same change. Recommendation: yes. They are one "every selectable slot" audit of the same function, and each needs its own control-both-ways test.
notes:
== FIXED in PR #10296 (machines-tail worker, 2026-09-24 04:50 AUSEST), all three sibling slots included ==

Reproduced at trunk 27bc54ef87 by calling cofx-attach/ensure-set-for on an indexed machine, with a guard requiring :probe/roll. The ids came back EMPTY for all four slots:
- flat root :on;
- a region body's own root :on;
- a region compound's :on-done raised as [:rf.machine/done [:a :flow]];
- a single :spawn :on-error for [:rf.machine.spawn/error [:working] …].
Each control, placing the same guard where the walk already looked, returned [:probe/roll].

Fix (cofx_attach.cljc):
- ensure-set-in-scope now takes the scope's OWNING node (the machine, or the region body), and its candidate walk ends at that root's :on at decl-path []. A root :same-state resolves to the root's :initial path.
- on-done-diet-for-event strips a matching region head and declines a foreign one, as pick-done-transition does.
- A new spawn-error-diet-for-event adds the :spawn :on-error candidates.

Regressions, in machine_cofx_attach_test.clj:
- root-on-guard-fact-is-ensured-before-selection runs through the real router. The guard sees 6 and the machine reaches :done; the control is the leaf guard.
- region-body-root-on-guard-fact-is-ensured, region-compound-on-done-guard-fact-is-ensured (with a foreign-head negative control) and spawn-on-error-guard-fact-is-ensured are white-box ensure-set rows, each with a control.
- With the three fixes removed, 5 assertions fail across the 4 CASE deftests and every control stays green. The restore was verified by blob hash.
Merged-PR audit #10296: claim remains INCOMPLETE; new OPEN correction rf2-s2bda: INCOMPLETE: machine spawn-error ensure-set omits destination entry coeffects. See that separately trackable finding for evidence and acceptance. Existing status and closure metadata unchanged.
Merged-PR audit #10296 (779281870b7b8fbe5d5d7a83999d1815994287e7; merged 2026-09-23T18:50:03Z). Completeness: Root same-state initial descent and inline validation with explicit addresses are delivered. Two residual gaps have separate open findings: synthetic failure target-entry coeffects and unaddressed inline allocation. Correctness: Reviewed merged implementation, affected call sites, source claims and controls. Real-router probe proves the failure transition entry reads nil instead of the generated 42. A separate valid inline definition without either optional address crashes in format-spawn-id before spawn validation. Both linked discovered-from with appended source forward pointers; no existing statuses changed. Implementation quality: Focused merged-worktree JVM suites passed 40 tests/83 assertions (exit 0); actual loaded resource root verified. Diagnostic attempt 2 exited 1 exposing inline allocation; attempt 3 exited 0 confirming the CASE/CONTROL coeffect discrepancy. CI 65 SUCCESS/23 SKIPPED. Existing helpers suffice; corrections need no new API. Scanned all 66 open Beads for exact duplicates. Actionable findings: rf2-s2bda, rf2-j1ykz. Existing finding updates: none.
close_reason:
DONE — merged as PR #10296 (head e7a6792449), with its siblings in the same PR. CI 88/88 at band (CLJS node and browser lanes green). Local: implementation JVM sweep 21/21 (machines 1291 tests, 0 failures), 22 check_*.py invariants, mkdocs --strict, clj-kondo clean on changed lines; plants restored and blob-verified.

rf2-3x7nj.8.4 — FIXED, including all three optional sibling slots. Before: the :rf.cofx/requires ensure-set came back empty for a root :on, a region body's root :on, a region compound's :on-done and a single :spawn's :on-error. Fixed in cofx_attach.cljc; the root :on case through the real router (guard sees 6, machine reaches :done), the other three white-box with controls. title: story-execution: the unified run-result folds only :cannot-run refusals from the play run-state, so a failed wait-until / no-match click / settle error reads :pass
description:
## Defect

The unified run-result (`story/run`, `run-variant`, `story/is`, the canvas `data-run-status`) takes only the `:cannot-run` REFUSALS out of the play runner's per-step results and ignores every other failed step. A play step that fails without writing an `:rf.story/assertions` record therefore vanishes from the verdict: a `[:wait-until …]` that never becomes true, a `[:click …]` / `[:type …]` / `[:focus …]` that matches no node, a step whose preconditions never settle, and a settle or presence-host `:error` all mark the run-state `:fail`, while the unified result reads `:pass`, vacuously green when the script held no assertion. `run-state-refusals` says in its own docstring that it is "the SINGLE bridge from the run-state's refusal facts to the unified result, so the run-state and the unified `:status` cannot disagree", and on these steps they do disagree. The fold also reads only the LAST play's run-state, so a multi-play run drops even the refusals of every earlier auto-play.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:628-629`, in `record-result-map` (543): `run-state-unmet (rf.story.play.runner/run-state-refusals (rf.story.play.runner-events/current-state variant-id))`. This is the only run-state input to `rf.story.result/run-result`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner.cljc:587-618`, `run-state-refusals`: it filters `cannot-run-step?` (`:cannot-run?` / `:skipped?`) and drops every other `:passed? false` result.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner_events.cljc`:
  - 1043-1063, `exec-wait-until!`: an unmet predicate is `step-fail` with `:cannot-run? false` and records no assertion. Its docstring and spec 017:1071-1072 both say "NEVER a silent pass".
  - 690-703, `exec-click!`: "click failed — no node matched" is a `step-fail`. `exec-type!` and `exec-focus!` do the same.
  - 1799-1811: the precondition budget runs out and the step fails.
  - 1071-1076, `presence-step-result`: `:error` becomes a `step-exception`.
- `runner_events.cljc:155-158` / `313-318`: `current-state` reads `run-state` keyed by frame alone, and `set-state!` overwrites it on every play, so it holds only the last play driven. `executed-play-keys` is already in scope at `runtime.cljc:568`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/result.cljc:1070-1071`: a `:pass` with no records reports `{:type :pass :message "run :pass — no assertions (vacuously green)"}` to clojure.test.

Public entry points: `re-frame.story/run`, `run-variant`, `story/is`, and the canvas run owner (`runtime/resume-run!`).

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-event :p/set (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ k v]] {:db (assoc db k v)}))
(rf.story/reg-variant :story.p/wait-until
  {:script {:script [[:dispatch [:p/set :n 1]]
                     [:wait-until [:db [:n] 99]]]}})
@(rf.story/run :story.p/wait-until)
;; => {:status :pass :assertions [] …}
;; (runner-events/current-state :story.p/wait-until) => {:status :fail :failures 1 …}
```

`story/is` over that variant emits one `:pass` report, so a JVM CI gate goes green on a script whose own step failed. In the browser, the canvas `data-run-status` reads `pass` while the toolbar play chip reads FAIL for the same run. A recorded or hand-written `[:click "[data-test=\"save\"]"]` against a renamed hook fails the step and still reads `:pass` on every unified surface.

## Evidence

- EXECUTED. A process-local JVM probe against the frozen tree used `:local/root` deps on `tools/story` and `implementation/epoch`, with `re-frame.epoch` loaded, the plain-atom adapter, and `install-canonical-vocabulary!`:
  - the `:wait-until` variant above read unified `:status :pass`, 0 assertions, while run-state read `:status :fail :failures 1`;
  - CONTROL, the same script with `[:assert [:rf.assert/path-equals [:n] 99]]` in place of the wait-until: unified `:status :fail`, 1 assertion.
- INSPECTED, CLJS-only or browser-only paths:
  - the click / type / focus no-match, the precondition timeout, and the presence `:error` produce the same `step-fail` / `step-exception` shape with no assertion record, and take the same fold;
  - the multi-play last-state read follows from `set-state!` / `current-state`.
- Tracker: `run-state-refusals`, run-state plus unified, and wait-until each return no bead that covers this. The same instrument does find other beads, e.g. `canonicalize` returns 18.

## Smallest fix

Beside `run-state-refusals`, add a projection of the GENUINE step failures in a settled run-state into the unified verdict:

- a `step-exception` becomes an `:error` unit;
- any other `:passed? false` result that is not a refusal becomes a `:fail` unit;
- an `[:assert …]` step's failure is excluded, because its record is already on `:rf.story/assertions` and must not count twice.

Fold these into `:unmet`, or into synthetic records, in `record-result-map`. Read EVERY executed play's state through `current-state-for-play` over `executed-play-keys`, not `current-state`.

Fence: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner.cljc`, `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc`, and possibly `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/result.cljc` if `:unmet` cannot carry a `:fail` unit. One sentence in `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` §Unified run result. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`cd tools/story && clojure -M:test` (JVM lane), with a regression beside the existing run-state-refusals tests in the shape of the probe above. The CLJS-only branches (DOM no-match, presence, the precondition timeout in the `js/setTimeout` loop) are graded only by `npm run test:cljs` / `npm run test:browser`.

## Decision needed

No. Spec 017 already says it: a wait-until that never holds is "NEVER a silent pass" (017:1071-1072), and the unified result is "the single boundary every runner / Test mode / CI / clojure.test / MCP consumes so they cannot disagree" (`re-frame.story/run-result` docstring). The fix brings the unified result into line with the run-state, which already reports `:fail`.
notes: Merged-PR audit #10310 (2b16d6683ee3e3bded162c5f88a1b488d807596b; merged 2026-09-23T21:49:55Z). Completeness: Fresh reruns/replays, compiled play selection, failed-step folding across executed plays and decorator refusal are implemented. Canvas verdict integration was explicitly omitted by the fence; independently tracked in rf2-iftxj. Correctness: Reviewed runtime phase/refusal paths, assertion de-duplication, trigger rewiring and canvas generation guard. Accepted reported JVM 2058/7722 and five negative controls; CI 38 successful checks. Canvas gap confirmed by source and the implementer report, without a rerun. Implementation quality: One owner and retained run options reduce divergent behavior; avoid a second run or parallel status store when connecting the canvas to its new generation. Actionable findings: rf2-iftxj. Existing finding updates: none.
close_reason:
DONE — merged as PR #10310 (head 733f3dc7c5), with its siblings in the same PR. CI 88/88 settled (38 pass, 50 skipped). CLJS was graded by CI only (node lane, browser lane, examples compile sweep, Story play-scripts harness), and the harness drove two on-demand plays through rerun! with the expected pass and fail. Local: tools/story clojure -M:test exit 0, 2058 tests; 20 static checks exit 0; clj-kondo warnings 12 before and after, all pre-existing. Each defect was reproduced at trunk; controls were restored and hash-verified.

rf2-3x7nj.30.1 — FIXED. The unified run result now counts failed play steps that did not already record an assertion, and it reads every play that ran, not just the last. At trunk a never-holding wait-until read :pass with 0 assertions. Now it reads :fail with exactly one :rf.error/story-play-step-failed. A failing path-equals still yields exactly one record, so nothing is double-counted. Spec 017 §Unified run result is updated. CONTROLS: fix removed -> 5 failures; reading only the last play -> 2 failures.

title: machines-lifecycle: a queued single-:spawn completion folds :on-done after the parent left or re-entered the spawning state (stale carrier attributed to the new attempt)
description:
## Defect

A single-`:spawn` child's completion carrier is QUEUED, not delivered synchronously (`dispatch-carrier!` → `child-dispatch!`). If parent events are already in the queue ahead of it, the parent can leave its `:spawn`-bearing state, or leave and RE-ENTER it with a fresh child, before the carrier arrives. When it arrives, `apply-spawn-on-done` folds the dead child's result into the parent's `:data` unconditionally. It resolves `:on-done` from the parent's spec at the carried invoke-id "whether or not the parent still rests on the spawning state", and the carrier carries no child identity to check against the slot. On re-entry the old child's result is therefore attributed to the NEW attempt while the new child is still running: the parent's `:always` guards and `:on` clauses see it in the same macrostep, and the new child's real completion later folds a second time. Spec 005:4002 names exactly this: a late completion whose spawn correlation no longer names a live actor ("the actor was already destroyed, or the spawn slot was reused") is stale, and its `:on-done` routing MUST NOT run. The `:spawn-all` path already fences the identical race with its exact-attempt coordinate (join.cljc:710). Single `:spawn` has no equivalent fence. finalize.cljc's stale gate (:507) only asks whether the parent INSTANCE is alive at mint time.

## Where

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:656-688` `apply-spawn-on-done`, reached from `:993-1007` for every `[:rf.machine.spawn/done invoke-id completion]` that is not a join child's.
- `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:808-818`: the single-`:spawn` completion map is `{:result :error? :completed-at}`, with no spawned-id or attempt identity.
- Public entry: a declarative `:spawn` with `:on-done`, where the parent's own exit/re-entry event sits in the queue ahead of the carrier (e.g. a user "retry"/"cancel" arriving in the same drain as the child's finishing HTTP reply).

## Failure scenario

Parent `:idle {:on {:start :loading}}`, `:loading {:spawn {:machine-id :pc/child :on-done (fn [{:keys [data result]}] (update data :results conj result))} :on {:cancel :idle}}`. The child is `:running {:on {:go :done}}`, `:done {:final? true :output-key :id}`, `:data {:id "first"}`. After `[:pc/parent [:start]]`, one handler queues `[child#1 [:go]]`, `[:pc/parent [:cancel]]`, `[:pc/parent [:start]]`. The queue is then `[cancel, start, carrier#1]`. The parent leaves `:loading`, re-enters it (`:rf/spawned` → `:pc/child#2`, live), and only then folds carrier#1: `:results ["first"]`, while child#2 has produced nothing. With just `:cancel` queued, the fold runs with the parent resting in `:idle`.

## Evidence

Executed with a bounded JVM probe (`probe_c.clj`, frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`):
- RE-ENTRY: parent state `:loading`, `:rf/spawned` names `:pc/child#2 live? true`, registry `{[:loading] :pc/child#2}`, `:results [first]`. Trace order: child#1 done → parent transition (cancel) → parent transition (start) → spawned child#2 → parent event-received (carrier#1).
- EXIT: parent state `:idle`, `:results [first]`.
- CONTROL (nothing queued ahead): `:results [first]`, the legitimate fold.

The fold is right in the control and wrong in the other two. No test pins either queue ordering. The single-`:spawn` stale tests (`machine_reply_lowering_test.clj:244`) cover only the destroyed-parent case.

## Smallest fix

Carry the finishing child's spawned-id on the single-`:spawn` completion map, as the join child's already does. At the parent boundary, suppress the fold and the engine step (stale reply, no `:data` mutation) when the parent's current configuration no longer contains the `:spawn`-bearing node at `invoke-id`, or when `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned parent invoke-id]` names a different live actor. Fence: `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc`, `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc`, plus one test. No hot-zone file, since the 005:4002 wording already demands it.

## Gates

`.cljc` shared code, no reader conditional: `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` (`implementation/machines`) and `npm run test:cljs`.

## Decision needed

Mostly no. The re-entry case is spec-stale by 005:4002. The one call is the EXIT case: should a completion that finished while the parent was in the state, but is delivered after the parent left, still fold? `apply-spawn-on-done`'s docstring currently says yes. title: story-ui-evidence: share dialog text-copy failures (Share URL / Copy EDN / Static build) are recorded via mark-error! but never rendered, so a failed Copy EDN is silent with no manual fallback (rf2-jgn8 half-landed)
description:
## Defect

rf2-jgn8 made the share dialog's text copies honest at the state level: `copy-text!` now routes a failed or absent clipboard write through `mark-error!` with a human reason. But `command-block` renders an error only when its caller passes `:error`, and only the Screenshot row does. The Share URL, Copy EDN and Static build rows never pass it.

So a failed text copy shows nothing at all: no false "copied ✓", which was the rf2-jgn8 bug, but also no failure. Copy EDN has no on-screen body either, so there is no manual-copy fallback, despite `copy-text!`'s docstring saying "the dialog keeps the snippet / URL field on screen as the manual-copy fallback". The rf2-jgn8 acceptance ("usable feedback/manual-copy affordance") is therefore only half met. Its tests assert the state atom and never the rendered row, so they cannot catch this.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs:555-575`: `copy-text!` (docstring and `mark-error!` call).
- `:689-719`: `command-block` renders `story-egress-error-<test>` only when `error` is non-nil.
- The rows:
  - `:773-787` Share URL: no `:error`, though its URL input is a fallback;
  - `:790-798` Copy EDN: no `:error` and no `:body`;
  - `:812` Screenshot: passes `:error (when (= :screenshot (:cmd error)) (:reason error))`;
  - `:817-827` Static build: no `:error`.
- Tests: `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/share_egress_cljs_test.cljs:530-563` check `(:error (dialog-state-snapshot))` only.
- Entry point: the Share / export dialog ("Copy EDN", "copy URL", "copy command").

## Failure scenario

The Story UI is served from an insecure dev host (no `navigator.clipboard`), or clipboard permission is denied. The user clicks "copy EDN". The state records `{:cmd :copy-edn :reason "clipboard write did not complete — copy it by hand"}`, but the row renders nothing, and the EDN is nowhere on screen to copy by hand. The user believes the copy happened, or cannot tell that it did not, and pastes stale clipboard content.

## Evidence

INSPECTED only. This is a `.cljs` file, and the brief allows no browser.

- A search for `story-egress-error` over `tools/story/test` returns 0 hits. The control is the same pattern matching `share.cljs:714` in src, so no test ever checks the rendered error row.
- rf2-jgn8's close reason records that its tests are state-level and were not run locally.

## Smallest fix

1. Pass `:error (when (= <cmd> (:cmd error)) (:reason error))` on the three text rows, mirroring the Screenshot row.
2. For Copy EDN, show the EDN in a read-only field on failure (or always), so the manual fallback the docstring promises exists.

Fence: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs` (plus its cljs test). No hot-zone file.

## Gates

This is a `.cljs` file, compiled only by the CLJS lane: `npm run test:cljs`, with a render-level assertion on `story-egress-error-copy-edn`. A JVM green says nothing about it.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Worker verdict (story-ui2-3x7nj, PR #10335): FIXED

The bead's two-point smallest fix is applied, in `ui/share.cljs`.

1. The Share URL, Copy EDN and Static build rows each pass `:error (when (= <cmd> (:cmd error)) (:reason error))`, mirroring the Screenshot row. A failed text copy therefore renders `story-egress-error-<test>` on its own row, with the reason "clipboard write did not complete — copy it by hand" and no copied flash.

- `failed-copy-edn-shows-the-snippet-to-copy-by-hand` checks the field is read-only and holds the `(rf.story/reg-variant …)` snippet extending the focused variant. Its control: no fallback field shows before any copy fails.

title: examples-capabilities: linearlite mints each optimistic card's tmp id by swap!-ing a global atom inside the :linearlite/create-issue event handler - the impure mid-handler minting the coeffects guide's minting ladder rules out
description:
## Defect

Linearlite, the write-side flagship for optimistic mutations, mints each new card's placeholder id INSIDE the `:linearlite/create-issue` event handler by `swap!`-ing a process-global `defonce` atom. That is the exact move the coeffects guide rules out: "A handler that secretly reads the clock or mints a random id mid-fold smuggles in a value the ledger never recorded, and replay diverges" (docs/core/coeffects.md, §The ledger), with the preferred remedy spelled out as the minting ladder — derive it from recorded state, or mint at the dispatch site and ride the event (§Fresh ids: the minting ladder). The minted id is not throwaway: it becomes the mutation's `:params :id`, its instance key `[:create tmp-N]` (a durable mutation-instance record in runtime-db) and the optimistic card's id in the resource cache. Two sibling examples go out of their way to teach the opposite (seven_guis `crud` and `circle_drawer` both explain why an id that lands in state must be a function of prior state), so the example a programmer or an AI copies for "optimistic create" teaches an impure handler.

## Where

- `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs:188` — `(defonce ^:private optimistic-id-seq (atom 0))`
- `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs:190-193` — `next-issue-id` does `(swap! optimistic-id-seq inc)`
- `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs:520-528` — the `:linearlite/create-issue` handler calls `(next-issue-id)` and puts the result in `:params` and `:instance [:create tmp-id]`
- Entry point: the new-issue form's submit, `core.cljs:578-581`, dispatching `[:linearlite/create-issue title]`.
- Contract: docs/core/coeffects.md §Fresh ids: the minting ladder and §The ledger; docs/core/glossary.md §Recordable vs ambient coeffects ("fresh id … captured onto the event envelope before the handler runs so durable results replay identically").

## Failure scenario

Dispatch `[:linearlite/create-issue "Gamma"]`, then replay that same recorded event into a fresh frame in the same process (a pair-tool or story replay, a second test in one bundle, a re-totalled ledger). The handler's effects differ for identical `(db, event)`: the first run executes mutation instance `[:create "tmp-1"]` with `:params {:id "tmp-1" …}`, the replay executes `[:create "tmp-2"]` with `:params {:id "tmp-2" …}`, so the resulting runtime-db (mutation instances, and the optimistic card while the write is pending) is not the one the recording produced. The replay promise ("two fresh apps fed the same sequence of events finish in identical states") fails for the one event the example exists to show.

## Evidence

INSPECTED only (`.cljs`; the CLJS lane is not available to this review). The handler reads nothing but the atom to choose the id, and the atom is outside every partition the ledger records, so divergence under replay in one process follows by construction. Controls: the two sibling examples that do this correctly, `examples/core/seven_guis/crud/core.cljs:36-42` and `examples/core/seven_guis/circle_drawer/core.cljs:40-50`, each with a `:next-id` counter in app-db; and this very slice's other minting site, `resources/core.cljs:332` (`(str "reader-" slug)`), which is a pure function of the event. Tracker: `bd search optimistic-id-seq` returns 0; the eight linearlite beads (rf2-9man, rf2-mmos, rf2-chl2, rf2-k4oe, rf2-pqt5f, rf2-zw6nf, rf2-wuten, rf2-fn0kx.4) concern write ordering, conflict policy, tests and decode, not id minting.

## Smallest fix

Take rung 1 of the ladder: keep a `:next-tmp-id` counter in app-db and allocate from it in `:linearlite/create-issue` (`tmp-id (str "tmp-" (:next-tmp-id db 1))`, then bump it in the returned `:db`), deleting the `defonce` atom and `next-issue-id`. That keeps the event shape `[:linearlite/create-issue title]`, so `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs`, which dispatches exactly that and finds cards by title, needs no change. (Rung 2, minting at the dispatch site, changes the event shape and that test with it.) Reword the comment at `core.cljs:182-187` to say why the id comes from app-db. Fence: `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

The file is `.cljs`, so only the CLJS lane grades it: `npm run test:cljs` (the node lane loads `linearlite_example_cljs_test`, whose name ends `-cljs-test`) and the examples compile sweep for the `examples/linearlite` build. A JVM green says nothing about it. Both take the machine-wide shadow-cljs lane.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:

Premise verified at trunk b0973944f9: the `defonce` atom was at :188, `swap!` at :193, and the handler at :520-528.

The `defonce` atom and `next-issue-id` are deleted. The comment now says why the id comes from app-db, and the app-db section comment names the counter. The event shape `[:linearlite/create-issue title]` is unchanged. `linearlite_example_cljs_test` needed no change: it dispatches that shape and reads the id off the card, and nothing in it references the atom.

Control, a JVM probe. It evaluates the handler form read from `core.cljs` and replays one recorded event into two fresh app-dbs:

title: examples-patterns: boot's failure seam hangs at :loading-deps in the dev build - the :spawn-all per-child :on-done folds a failed child's error map into a typed slot and the schema rollback swallows :on-any-failed
description:
## Defect

The boot example's failure seam (tick "Fail the next boot", click "Re-run boot") HANGS the boot at `:loading-deps` in the dev build instead of reaching the `:failed` screen. The runtime runs a `:spawn-all` child's per-child `:on-done` for an `:error? true` finality too, so the failed `/user.json` loader's 503 error map is folded into the boot machine's `:data :user`. The example's own `BootData` schema types that slot `[:maybe User]`, so the candidate runtime-db is rejected (`:rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :machine-data :rollback? true`). The rollback discards the whole carrier macrostep: the join never records the failure and `:boot/deps-failed` is never dispatched. The user child is already torn down and the one-shot seam already disarmed, so nothing can ever finish the join. The page sits on "Booting... Loading dependencies" with no Retry button. This is the failure branch PR #10178 made reachable (rf2-fn0kx.5 finding 1), and it does not work in the build `npm run dev:example -- examples/boot` serves.

The root cause is runtime, not the example. Spec 005 says `:on-done` "fires when the child enters a (non-error) `:final?` state" (005:3000), that an `:error?` finish "SKIPS `:on-done`" (005:3390), and that a `:spawn-all` child's `:on-done` is "the same ... fold a single `:spawn` declares" (005:3812). The single-`:spawn` path honours that. The join path does not: it folds `:on-done` for both kinds. The fold context is only `{:data :result}`, so a per-child `:on-done` cannot even tell a failure from a success. No runtime bead owns this; searched all statuses (see Evidence).

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc:613` derives `kind` (`:failed` when `:error?`). `:786-799` then calls `apply-child-on-done` with `result` unconditionally, before `intercept-fold` ever looks at `kind`. `:555-586` is `apply-child-on-done`, which has no kind check.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc:203-233`: `apply-on-done` hands the callback `{:data data :result result}`, with no error flag.
- Example: `examples/patterns/boot/boot.cljs:296-301` has the `:user` child's `:on-done` `(assoc data :user result)`. `:161-162` has the loader's `:failed {:final? true :error? true :output-key :error}`. `:307-311` has `:on-any-failed [:boot/deps-failed]`.
- `examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs:57-64` defines `User`, and `:91-97` has `BootData [:user [:maybe User]]`.
- `examples/patterns/boot/core.cljs:136-155` is the failure seam, which answers `/user.json` with a 503. `views.cljs:131-139` renders `boot-progress` for every non-terminal state, and `:37-54` shows that screen carries no retry.
- Spec: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3000`, `:3390`, `:3812`, and `:3882` step 1. Step 1 reads literally as "always", and the join code implements that literal reading. `spec/010-Schemas.md:186` is row 7, a machine-data candidate rejection with a full rollback.
- Public entry: the example's own UI. More generally, any `:spawn-all` child spec with an `:on-done`, a child that can reach an `:error? true` leaf, and a typed `[:schemas :data]`.

## Failure scenario

In `npm run dev:example -- examples/boot`: the boot reaches `:ready`, the user ticks "Fail the next boot" and clicks "Re-run boot".
1. `:configuring` completes.
2. `:loading-deps` spawns routes, flags and user.
3. routes and flags complete.
4. The user loader reaches `:failed` with the 503 map.
5. Its carrier folds `:on-done`, and `:data :user` becomes `{:status 503 :message "Simulated /user.json outage ..." :kind :rf.http/http-5xx}`.
6. `BootData` rejects the candidate and the macrostep rolls back.

Result: the boot stays at `:loading-deps` for ever. Expected: `:failed`, the error screen, and Retry.

## Evidence

**Executed** (bounded JVM probe, output in the review scratch dir `probe2/boot2.out`):
- The probe loaded `examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs` and `boot.cljs` VERBATIM with `load-file`. It read `core.cljs`'s demo-stub forms from the frozen file and eval'd them verbatim; only `ns`, `defonce app-root`, `mount!` and `run` were skipped.
- It used frame `:rf/default` with the example's `:fx-overrides`, on the core, machines, http and schemas artefacts.
- Control, with the seam disarmed: `state=:ready`, `:user` the demo user, no error trace.
- With the seam armed and "Re-run boot": `state=:loading-deps`, one trace `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure {:where :machine-data, :machine-id :app/boot, :phase :macrostep, :rollback? true}`. Still `:loading-deps` 3 s later, with `fail-next-boot? = false`.

**Executed, without the schemas artefact** (`probe/boot.out`): the same armed boot reaches `:failed`, but `:data :user` holds the 503 map (`{:status 503, :message "Simulated /user.json outage (the demo's failure seam).", :kind :rf.http/http-5xx}`). That demonstrates the per-child `:on-done` ran on the `:error?` finality. It is also why the prior wave's schema-less probe saw the branch work.

**Inspected**:
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/boot_cljs_test.cljs` reaches `:failed` only through a blanket canned-failure override. That fails the single-`:spawn` config loader, which routes through `:on-error` and skips `:on-done`, so no test drives a join-child failure.
- `:on-done` has 0 matches in `implementation/machines/test/*spawn_all*`. Control: the same pattern matches 18 other machines test files.

**Tracker**:
- An all-status search over title, description, notes and close_reason found 0 hits for `apply-child-on-done` and for `per-child :on-done` near fail/error.
- The one near hit, rf2-3x7nj.9.3, is about single-`:spawn` completions after exit, a different defect.

## Smallest fix

Runtime. In `join.cljc` run `apply-child-on-done` only when `kind` is `:done`, matching the single-`:spawn` rule. Reword `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3882` step 1, and optionally `:3812`, to say "for a non-error completion". spec/005 is a **HOT-ZONE** file.

Add a JVM regression in `implementation/machines/test` covering a join child with `:on-done` that reaches an `:error?` leaf, asserting that `:data` is untouched and `:on-any-failed` fires. The example then needs no change.

An optional witness is a join-failure case in `boot_cljs_test.cljs`: fail `/user.json` only, with schemas loaded, and assert `:failed`.

## Gates

- The machines JVM artefact (`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines`, or `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`).
- `npm run test:cljs`. The join code is `.cljc` outside any reader conditional, and the boot witness is a CLJS test.

## Decision needed

Yes. (A) Per-child `:on-done` is success-only, the reading 005:3000/3390/3812 support: fix `join.cljc` and clarify 005:3882. (B) Keep folding failures: document that in 005, add `:error?` to the `:on-done` context, and make boot's folds ignore failures. A is recommended.

== RULING (mayor's ruling agent, 2026-09-24 13:20:56 AUSEST, under the project stance; dossier + Codex Recommendation weighed) ==

QUESTION: Does a child's failure ever reach a SUCCESS route — the `:on-done` fold, or the `:rf.machine.spawn/done` event — in either spawn form?

OPTIONS AS PRESENTED (sizes):
- A (the bead's): the `:spawn-all` per-child `:on-done` is success-only. One guard in join.cljc plus one spec sentence. Leaves single `:spawn` folding failures.
- A+ (dossier and Codex): A plus an `(:error? completion)` guard in registration.cljc `apply-spawn-on-done`. Two guards plus 005 :3287/:3888 sentences. Leaves a single-`:spawn` failure with no `:on-error` riding the DONE carrier.
- B: keep folding failures; add `:error?` to the fold context; reverse 005 :3003/:3341/:3396/:3469 and Spec-Schemas :2647; rewrite boot's three folds and the docs/skills pages. Large.

RULING — "A failure never reaches a success route, in either spawn form." A+ in intent, with the single-`:spawn` half fixed at the ROUTING instead of at the fold:
1. `:spawn-all`: the per-child `:on-done` runs only for a `:done` completion (the join.cljc guard). As both reviewers said.
2. Single `:spawn`: EVERY failure — an `:error?` leaf AND an uncaught child action exception — rides the FAILURE carrier `[:rf.machine.spawn/error <invoke-id> <error> <attempt>]` whether or not `:spawn :on-error` is declared. Resolution then follows spec 005 §`:on-error`'s two arms exactly as already written: `:on-error`, else an explicit `:on {:rf.machine.spawn/error …}` walked leaf to root then the root `:on`, else nothing. The done carrier therefore only ever carries a success, so the `:on-done` fold AND any explicit `:on {:rf.machine.spawn/done …}` are success-only with no guard at the fold.
This supersedes A+'s registration-side `:error?` guard, which is dead under this ruling. Do not add it.

WHY — where I agreed and disagreed:
- AGREE with both on the principle, on rejecting B, and on the join guard. B keeps a silently failing trap in every fold, contradicts four spec sentences, every doc and skill page, and XState. The stance rules it out.
- AGREE with the dossier, against the bead, that single `:spawn` does NOT honour success-only unless `:on-error` is declared. Confirmed at source and by probe P1 below.
- DISAGREE with both on HOW single `:spawn` is fixed. A fold guard fixes the fold only. Measured (probe P2): a parent using the documented sibling idiom `:on {:rf.machine.spawn/done {:target …}}` takes its SUCCESS transition on a child FAILURE today, and would still do so under A+ (fold skipped, transition taken). The idiom is taught as "works too" (docs/machines/actors.md:280), "works equally well" (skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/spawn.md:89) and in docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:281. Same trap class, one idiom over. And spec 005 §`:on-error` arm 2 (:3392 — an explicit `:on {:rf.machine.spawn/error …}` catching a failure when no `:on-error` is declared) is unreachable today for BOTH triggers; A+ leaves it unreachable.
- DISAGREE with Codex that carrier routing is "a separate question". The tracker already assigned it to THIS bead: rf2-3x7nj.9.3's close reason says "`:on-error` arm 2 was deliberately not reworded, because rf2-3x7nj.41.1 is pending there", and rf2-3x7nj.8.2's addendum says "Coordinate it with whatever rf2-3x7nj.41.1 rules." Punting again would orphan it.
- The ruled fix is SMALLER code than A+: two conjuncts deleted rather than a guard added, and the parent-spec resolution that existed only to answer "did the parent declare `:on-error`?" becomes dead and is deleted. It makes the spec's existing arm 2 true rather than rewording it, and it matches XState's shape: a failed invoke raises the error event, which onError handles, and onDone is never taken for it.
- AGREE with Codex, against the dossier, that "land after PR #10296" is stale. The 9.3/8.2 currency fence landed in PR #10311 (merged 2026-09-23T21:53:50Z; commits 795d4f8830 and 5b1bc6ea87). #10296 was a different PR (rf2-gdne8, 8.4, 9.6). No open PR touches this fence: 4 open PRs, 19 files, 0 of them in spec/005, Spec-Schemas, API.md, machines src, examples/patterns/boot or boot_cljs_test.

PRESERVED ANALYSIS
Line numbers are at trunk 4c70b35a41 (= origin/main). The fence files are byte-unchanged since b15785613b: `git diff --stat b15785613b HEAD` over implementation/machines, spec/005 and examples/patterns/boot printed nothing.

The defect (bead reviewer and dossier, measured independently):
- Boot example failure seam (tick "Fail the next boot", click "Re-run boot"). The `/user.json` loader reaches `:failed {:final? true :error? true :output-key :error}` (boot.cljs:162). The `:spawn-all` per-child `:on-done` `(assoc data :user result)` (boot.cljs:300; routes :288, flags :294) folds the 503 map into `:data :user`. `BootData` types that slot `[:maybe User]` (schema.cljs), so the candidate is rejected with `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure {:where :machine-data :phase :macrostep :rollback? true}`. The rollback discards the whole carrier macrostep: the join never records the failure and `:on-any-failed [:boot/deps-failed]` (boot.cljs:308) never fires, while the child is already destroyed and the one-shot seam disarmed. The boot stays at `:loading-deps` for ever — still after 3 s and after `:boot/restart` — and the page has no Retry. Control: the happy boot reaches `:ready` with the demo user.
- Dossier's in-JVM simulation of the join guard (alter-var-root, no tree edit): `:failed` with `{:status 503 :kind :rf.http/http-5xx}`, and `:boot/restart` then reaches `:ready`. Without the schemas artefact the unfixed boot does reach `:failed`, but `:data :user` holds the 503 map — which is why the prior wave's schema-less probe saw the branch "work".
- Codex's independent synthetic probe agrees: a typed join failure is stuck (one schema failure, child already destroyed); an untyped join failure reaches `:failed` with the error map in the success slot; a single-spawn failure with no `:on-error` pollutes the slot (or rolls back under a schema); with `:on-error` the fold is skipped.
- Mechanism, join: join.cljc:644 derives `kind` (`:failed` when `:error?`). :827-830 then calls `apply-child-on-done` UNCONDITIONALLY on the verified path, before `intercept-fold` reads `kind` (:843-846). `apply-child-on-done` (:586-618) has no kind check. resolver.cljc:204 `apply-on-done` hands the callback `{:data :result}` only, with no error flag, so a fold cannot tell. A `:spawn-all` child may not declare `:on-error` (validation.cljc:1528 `known-spawn-all-child-spec-keys`; rejected as `:rf.error/machine-unknown-spawn-key`). The only failure hook is the block's `:on-any-failed`; without it, failures go to the join's `:failed` set and `:rf.warning/spawn-all-join-unsatisfiable` fires once (join.cljc:860-876).
- Mechanism, single `:spawn`: finalize.cljc:459-461 is `on-error? (and error-leaf? parent-id (some? (:on-error spawn-spec)))`. Without `:on-error` the failure rides the DONE carrier with `:error? true` (finalize.cljc:821-838), and the parent boundary folds it through `apply-spawn-on-done` (registration.cljc:658-691, called at :1069-1071) with no `:error?` check. The action-exception trigger dispatches the failure carrier only when `parent-declares-on-error?` (registration.cljc:224-225; spawn_error.cljc:99-111), so without `:on-error` nothing reaches the parent at all. The engine side of arm 2 already exists: transition.cljc:1381-1482 `pick-spawn-error-transition` tries `:on-error`, then walks leaf to root, then the root `:on`. A test comment states the gap outright — machines_on_error_cljs_test.cljc:502-506: "The synthetic spawn-error event is only DISPATCHED when the spawning parent declares `:spawn :on-error`" — which is why that arm-2 test reaches it through a guard-failing `:on-error`.
- Spec. Success-only is the dominant reading: 005:3003 key table "(non-error) `:final?`"; :3341 "`:on-done` is the *success* notification"; :3396 "Success vs failure are mutually exclusive per finish … SKIPS `:on-done`"; :3469 "instead of `:on-done`"; :3818 per-child `:on-done` is "the same … fold a single `:spawn` declares"; :3835-3836 `:done` = plain final, `:failed` = error final; Spec-Schemas.md:2647 "INSTEAD OF the `:data`-only `:on-done` callback"; docs/machines/actors.md:144 "successful final state"; skills spawn.md:30 "non-error", with :157 restating :3396. The contrary text: 005:3888 join step 1 (unconditional, and implemented literally); :3894 "as they land"; :3287 and Spec-Schemas.md:2647 "an error leaf with no parent `:on-error` behaves exactly like any other `:final?` leaf"; and the D-list bullet at :3284 (no qualifier).
- History: never ruled. The single-spawn gate came from 93ac6ccd8f (rf2-5hlsh, first-class `:on-error`, "existing behaviour unchanged") — residue of the pre-`:on-error` workaround "error leaf + parent `:on-done` stashes it". Per-child `:on-done` came from 8bf9545b89 (rf2-kuky.14), whose target API labels `:done` "success"; its commit message never discusses a failure reaching the fold.
- Exposure: the framework's own `:rf.http/managed` wrapper has an `:error? true` `:failed` leaf with `:output-key :rf/result` (implementation/http machine_wrapper.cljc:120-124), and spec/014 suggests fanning it out under `:spawn-all`. Any natural fold `(assoc data :k result)` on a failable join child is hit.
- Parity: 005:4653 and :4676 make the XState v6 direction the reference ("align unless substrate-constrained"). Mike's machines rulings have gone ALIGN every time (rf2-127ff, rf2-eicq0, rf2-3x7nj.8.1).

This ruling's probe.
