"Ruled" is an in-process simulation by alter-var-root only: `finalize/dispatch-spawn-done!` re-routed to `spawn-error/dispatch-spawn-error!` when the completion is `:error?` and carries no `:child-id`; `spawn-error/parent-declares-on-error?` answering "is a single-`:spawn` child"; the join's `apply-child-on-done` skipped for an `:error?` carrier. Each row uses a fresh fixture. The child's `:ok` ends on a plain leaf with `:the-value`, `:fail` on an `:error?` leaf with `{:status 503}`, and `:throw` raises an action exception.

Today such a wildcard already catches error-leaf failures via the done carrier. Under the ruling it also catches an action-exception failure carrier from a single-`:spawn` child whose parent declared no `:on-error`. (2) The standing XState RECORDS in re-frame2's own tree — `docs/EP/EP-0029-xstate-v6-machine-parity.md` (written against alpha.1/alpha.2; every A/B/C premise graded still-true / moved / reversed), `spec/005-StateMachines.md` §Lessons from xstate (§Parity re-validation, §Four non-substrate divergences, §Deliberate name divergence), `spec/CP-5-MachineGuide.md` §Lessons table, `docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md`, `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md`, and the five items rf2-2qfi assessed and deliberately did not file — each sentence about XState or about re-frame2 graded against the installed alpha.59 package and the alpha.59 docs, with the measured truth recorded where it has moved.

Method: the XState side is executed, not recalled — `xstate@6.0.0-alpha.59` is installed in the session scratchpad and driven with node through the pure `initialTransition` / `transition` / `getMicrosteps` API and `createActor`, with the v6 `next`-branch docs (`xstate-v5-to-v6.md`, `cheatsheet.md`, `glossary.md` and the topic pages) and the changelog as the documentary sources. The re-frame2 side is driven on the JVM through `reg-machine` + `dispatch-sync` and the pure `machine-transition`, with `spec/005` line citations at the sha read and the pinning test named where one exists. Changelog rows whose topic belongs to another dimension (A structure, B semantics, C interpretation, E tooling) are still classified here but handed off in the findings doc rather than filed; only stale RECORDS (one bead per document, max eight) and dimension-owned gaps become beads. Deliverables: the changelog matrix, the records audit, stale-record beads, handoffs, and the one-page "state of parity at alpha.59" summary including the posture sentence on periodic re-validation, at `ai/findings/xstate-v6-parity/D-changelog-and-records.md`.

title: Xray Views resolves subscription topology outside the observed frame
description:
The Views panel classifies an observed app's subscription runs using ambient registration metadata, rather than the observed frame's image generation. For an app whose subscriptions live only in its image, derived subscriptions are displayed as direct app-db readers and their declared dependency edges disappear. This makes the tool misleading during ordinary image-isolated app debugging.

Evidence: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs:697-724 builds :rf.xray/reactive-data from the observed focus/history, but line 716 calls the zero-argument re-frame.subs.tooling/sub-topology without resolving the observed frame. The tooling function reads ambient registrar registrations (implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/tooling.cljc:59-123). Xray itself seats a separate image generation (panels/image_view_reads.cljs:343-356). partition-subs-by-level at reactive_panel_subs.cljs:487-519 treats absent topology entries as Level 1 with no dependency/source metadata.

Reproduced through the current JVM subscription runtime: create a host image with :review/base and :review/derived (inputs [[:review/base]]), and a distinct inspector image containing the actual :rf.xray/reactive-data callback and its four inputs. Supply a focused host epoch with both sub-runs, then subscribe-once to the inspector composite. Result: Level 1 = [:review/base :review/derived], Level 2 = []. Control wrapping the same callback in the host's frame resolution returns Level 1 = [:review/base], Level 2 = [{:sub-id :review/derived :inputs [:review/base]}]. Both results select the same host epoch. The callback and pure helpers are extracted from current source; the only JVM adaptation is catch :default -> catch Throwable. Browser rendering was not executed.

Local reproduction: ai/findings/codex-xray-review-re-frame2-1/jvm/reactive-live-probe-re-frame2-1.clj; successful attempt reactive-live-probe-re-frame2-2.log/.exit (exit 0). The first invocation used the wrong dependency cwd and failed before evaluating the code; attempt 2 uses the recorded jvm/deps.edn.

Small fix: resolve static topology against the observed frame using the existing frame-resolution/tooling seam before projecting the record. Keep this a consumer correction; do not expand the public subscription API. Add a focused regression with disjoint host/inspector images, and ideally a same-ID metadata collision to prove the target wins.

Deduplication: rf2-zimh fixed frame-targeted LIVE cache metadata readers inside subs.tooling; it does not scope this separate static sub-topology consumer. rf2-3x7nj.24.3 fixed per-instance graph identities, a separate problem. Review posture: pre-alpha, trust the programmer, accurate tools and small fixes; no extra validation framework.
acceptance_criteria: An image-isolated host displays its base and derived subscriptions in the correct levels with host input edges/source metadata, regardless of inspector or global registrations. A regression exercises the actual composite subscription with disjoint images.
notes:

Regression: `reactive-data-resolves-topology-through-the-observed-frame` in tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels_e2e/reactive_data_e2e_cljs_test.cljs. It uses disjoint images:

description:

The PR admits ISO-8601 :after keys and round-trips them through SCXML, but chart/layout.cljc event-segment:660 still renders every after value using (str "clock " after "ms"). Thus a valid "PT1S" appears as "PT1Sms", a malformed unit label on the user-visible chart. Format an ISO duration correctly, either as its valid duration spelling or using the existing duration resolver and milliseconds. Keep this a local formatter correction.
acceptance_criteria: A chart label for {:after "PT1S"} shows a correct duration without the invalid PT1Sms spelling. Preserve the existing integer-millisecond label and other edge kinds; cover the ISO case with a small formatter assertion.
notes:
== FIXED (worker, 2026-09-25, PR #10393) ==
I reproduced this at trunk cdf978feb8: (layout/event-segment {:after "PT1S"}) returned "⌚ PT1Sms". There was also a second render site the description does not name. projection.cljc passes the raw :after key as the event node's :afterMs, and event_node.cljs builds the visible chart header from :afterMs as (str "⌚ " after-ms "ms"). Integer keys return the same value, and subscription-vector and fn keys come back as-is, so every other label is unchanged. Milliseconds also agree with how the chart already renders a lowered :timeout "PT2S", as ⌚ 2000ms.

title: FALSE: a history restore declared above its owner leaves the owner standing
description:

title: core-instrumentation: offset reads below a :large declaration now return a size marker - confirm against spec 009's get-path index-range pagination
description:
Discovered from rf2-3x7nj.4.1 (merged as PR #10279, 2026-09-23). Offset-rooted egress now applies ancestor declarations. For the :sensitive axis that is the fix. For the :large axis it is a behaviour change nobody has ruled on: a get-path / project-egress read BELOW a :large declaration now returns a size marker for the value that was read, where before it shipped raw. The large opt-in (elision false on the pair tools) still fetches the raw value, which is how a fetch of the handle path itself already behaved.

The tension: spec/009-Instrumentation.md says a :vector marker is "paginatable via get-path with an index range". If paging a large vector by index now returns markers for each element that is itself large, or for the slice, the pagination path may be defeated for the ordinary (non-opt-in) caller. The worker followed the bead and did not measure the pagination case.

## Decision needed

Yes. Should a descendant read under a :large declaration (a) return a size marker for the value read (as merged), with pagination served only through the explicit large opt-in, or (b) ship raw below the declaration, so the declaration marks only the handle path itself? First measure what get-path with an index range returns today for a :large vector, since the answer may make this moot. spec/009 is hot-zone.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #10279 independently measured the exact existing pagination question at 950a0cba74f4ba056b1ae5b0a523cf4e7d6a702a. A bounded JVM public project-egress probe with {:items ["a" "b"]}, :large [[:items]], off-box profile, and paths [:items 0]/[:items 1] returns two size markers with the correct element handles by default; include-large? true returns ["a" "b"]. Probe 1 test/3 assertions, zero failures/errors (worker gate root and exact merged resource verified). Inspected get_path.cljs: singular and batch forms use this same get-in plus absolute :path projection; no index-range operator exists there. This confirms the existing need to reconcile spec/009 pagination wording and the chosen descendant-large policy; no policy choice inferred by this audit and no live MCP/browser run claimed.
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 00:22:39 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==
Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-ealv5.descendant-reads-under-large.md (ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot; the findings below stand on their own). Read at trunk 8e65232c40 (= origin/main; elision.cljc / projection.cljc / get_path.cljs unchanged since the fix commit 950a0cba74).

RECOMMENDATION: (a) keep as merged — a declaration governs its whole subtree on both axes, raw only via the per-call large opt-in. No core change. Follow-ups: a no-decision wording repair (spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3021 hot zone; pair-mcp Principles.md:653-658 and :682-686, 003-Tool-Catalogue.md:117-119, get-path descriptor descriptors_data.cljs:1011-1018, skill wire-size-budget.md:84-86), plus an optional separate ruling on un-gating the size override from --allow-sensitive-reads.

DECISIVE FINDINGS:
1. The promised "index range" pagination exists nowhere. get-path is plain get-in in both forms (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_path.cljs:107 singular, :147 batch); parse-path-arg (args.cljs:324-349) has no range syntax; get-in [:rows [0 50]] reads missing. Repo-wide, only spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3021 claims it, so that sentence is stale under either ruling.
2. The old raw-below result was an accident of the same bare-offset seed that leaked secrets, not a mechanism. The walker keeps a matched declaration live through every map key and index below it (fork-decl-paths elision.cljc:859-896, fork-index-paths :898-933): probe fork-decl-paths #{[:rows]} :name -> #{[:rows]}, fork-index-paths #{[:rows]} 0 -> #{[:rows]}, and a naive (b) walk of [:rows 0] with #{[:rows]} still returns a marker. So (b) needs a new "fresh match" coverage rule for :large only, asymmetric with :sensitive; walker-wide it would also ship large content raw into rf2-fc84b's focused-slice traces.
3. Measured (bounded JVM probe, exact get-path eval opts, off-box-tool, 5,000 rows under :large [[:rows]]): batch paths [:rows 0]..[:rows 49] returns 50 markers / 11,320 B with zero row content at trunk, versus 50 rows / 4,022 B with :rf.egress/include-large? true, which is also exactly what pre-fix 950a0cba74^ returned by default. A 2 MB element under :large [[:attachments]] pre-fix shipped 2,000,028 B raw; at trunk it is a 231 B marker carrying :bytes. BEAD CORRECTION: "elision false still fetches the raw value" holds only under --allow-sensitive-reads; on a default launch get_path.cljs:173-175 forces elision true (same pattern in 7 pair tools), and the get-path descriptor does not say so, so a default-install agent has no structured route under the declaration (eval-cljs remains).
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 01:08:41 AUSEST) ==

Reproduced on the JVM with the real Story recorder:

- make every one of these say the truth;

### 3. Static-build tests that guard local copies

Some tools/story static-build tests call LOCAL COPIES of the predicates they claim to guard, so a regression in the real predicate cannot turn them red. Point each test at the real predicate. Show one going red on a planted regression in the real code.

title: Xray UI truths: add-pill test cannot fail, mutes-only filtered count hidden, unused relative-time subscription

  - If it is not real, "the premise does not hold", with the evidence, is a complete deliverable.
- **Item 3.** If the rows really ignore the value, drop the subscription and the argument. If some row does use it, say which and leave it.
- No new UI vocabulary and no new API. Each fix needs a regression that is red with the fix removed.

tools/xray/src (the filters/pills view, the events ribbon and the event list) and tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/filters/. Put new tests in new files where possible.

title: FALSE: resource :data-schema is still documented as runtime validation and validation-failure redaction
description:
Audit of PR #10459 at 5bc04c8aef928ddb494623c7bd901077ebf38e84. New independent audit finding for the data-validation claim reported under rf2-opsfb.

spec/015-Data-Classification.md:194 groups a resource :data-schema with machine [:schemas :data] and resource :params-schema as schemas that validate the data and redact their validation-failure traces. Privacy.md:113 likewise includes resource :data-schema among schemas driving validation-failure redaction. The new spec/015:364 correctly says the opposite: resource :data-schema has no runtime validator and drives neither route.

Code evidence: the complete :data-schema reference census in implementation/resources/src finds declaration examples/docs, the explicit non-consumer comments in classification.cljc:350-364 and ssr.cljc, and tooling.cljc:229-238 exposing the shape as process metadata; it finds no runtime validation call. By contrast registry.cljc:696 onward validates resource params through :params-schema and the registered schemas hook. Response shape validation belongs to the request :decode schema. Thus an author can incorrectly rely on :data-schema to reject malformed fetched data, and the docs promise failure redaction for a validator that does not run.

Required correction: make the affected prose distinguish resource data-schema reflection metadata, actual params-schema validation, machine data validation, and request decode validation. Point to the existing contract rather than inventing another validator. Include the Privacy table in the small consistency correction so it does not retain the same false claim. This issue requests accurate documentation, not new runtime validation behavior. The existing worker has already reported this distinction; implementer tests are accepted and no extra suite was rerun.

title: machines (JVM): machine-source-unstamped warning fires on a literal definition with no :guards or :actions
description:
On the JVM, defmachine or an inline reg-machine on a map literal that carries no :guards and no :actions still emits :rf.warning/machine-source-unstamped. The same literal with a single guard does not warn. Both cases were measured at c456e717e9 by the correctness pass of rf2-ahrss.

Likely cause, not verified: the Clojure reader attaches no line metadata to map literals, so a definition with no fn forms has nothing for the source-coords stamp to read. The CLJS reader is believed unaffected, but shadow-cljs was not run to confirm it.

Low priority. It is a spurious warning on a JVM-only path, and the fix is either to stamp from the defining form's own coordinates or to suppress the warning when no fn form exists to stamp.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT: FIXED (branch worker/machwarn-hefqg, PR #10474, commit a8e4e0d713 after rebase onto 02d3c89fea)

REPRODUCED at trunk 016e3cc7dd on the JVM. A new namespace registered a fn-free inline literal, a fn-free defmachine value and a fn-free plain def. It failed 3 of 5 assertions, with the actuals [:fn-free/inline], [:fn-free/defm] and [:fn-free/def] where [] was expected.

CAUSE (verified; the bead's "likely cause" holds):
- The JVM LispReader attaches :line/:column only to list forms, never to map literals.
- So on the JVM the reg-machine / defmachine literal walk (re-frame.source-coords walk-machine-spec, walk-element-source and walk-machine-inline-source) can stamp only fns: :guards / :actions entries, and inline :entry / :exit / :guard / :action fn literals.
- For a fn-free spec, stamp-machine-spec-expr returns the spec unchanged, so defmachine expands to a plain def.
- The advisory keyed only on "the spec carries no source metadata", so it fired where its own fix could change nothing.

FIX (the bead's "suppress" route). The "stamp from the defining form's coordinates" route would edit core's core_reg_macros.cljc / source_coords.cljc, which were outside this dispatch's fence.
- In implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc, maybe-warn-source-unstamped! now ALSO requires, on the JVM only, that the spec carries a fn. That test is the new :clj-only spec-carries-fn?, a tree-seq fn? walk.
- CLJS is unchanged. cljs tools.reader positions every map literal, so the walk stamps the root of any literal spec there.
- The existing CI test reg-machine-co-locates-state-node-coords-cljs already pins fn-free map-node stamping on CLJS.

REGRESSION: implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_source_unstamped_fn_free_cljs_test.cljc, which runs on both the JVM and the CLJS :node-test lane.
- A fn-free inline literal and a fn-free defmachine value are silent on both platforms.
- A fn-free plain def warns on CLJS only.
- A plain def whose only fn is an inline :entry warns on both platforms.
- A plain def with :guards / :actions fns warns on both platforms.

SABOTAGE: I deleted the #?(:clj (spec-carries-fn? machine)) line. The regression ns plus re-frame.machine-source-unstamped-warning-test went to 3 failures of 16 assertions, exit 1. After the restore, the blob hash matched the committed blob.

JVM gate, clojure -M:test in implementation/machines:
- Before: 1513 tests, 6467 assertions, 0 failures.
- After, on the final base (with rf2-izlpl included): 1519 tests, 6474 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0.
- This item accounts for exactly +5 tests / +5 assertions of that.

CLJS: I relied on CI; no local shadow-cljs run.

RESIDUAL, inherent to the suppress route. On the JVM, a literal whose only fn sits in an inline slot as a SYMBOL naming a fn (e.g. :entry log-entry) still warns spuriously: the walk captures only fn LITERALS, and a runtime fn does not say how it was written. Only the stamp-from-form route in core removes that.

SPEC FOLLOW-UP (not edited; spec/** was held). The :rf.warning/machine-source-unstamped row of spec/009-Instrumentation.md says an inline literal and a defmachine value "both arrive source-bearing and do not warn". On the JVM a fn-free one now arrives source-blind and is exempt, so the row could gain that clause.

1. `:always-depth-limit` is read only from the machine spec root: `(get machine :always-depth-limit always-depth-limit-default)` in transition.cljc `drain-to-fixed-point` and in parallel.cljc. Nothing under implementation/core reads it. §Bounded depth now says "per machine, with `:always-depth-limit` at the machine spec's root".
2. Both engines tag the depth-exceeded error `:actor-id`, not `:machine-id`. §Bounded depth is fixed.
3. The raise counter counts raised events dequeued across the whole macrostep: seeded 0 at the public entry, `(inc raise-depth)` passed into each nested settle, and parallel's `depth` works the same way. The "compose" sentence now says 16 per macrostep, not 16 per microstep.
4. The top-level keys table gained `:sensitive`/`:large` (linked to §Privacy), `:always-depth-limit` and `:raise-depth-limit`, all in validation.cljc `known-machine-root-extra-keys`.
5. The spec/009 `:rf.warning/machine-source-unstamped` row now says that on the JVM only a spec carrying a fn qualifies, so a fn-free spec does not warn. This is registration.cljc `maybe-warn-source-unstamped!`, gated `#?(:clj (spec-carries-fn? machine))`.
OPEN, NOT DECIDED HERE: the old sentence also claimed "the macrostep can include up to 16 microsteps". That is true of the parallel engine (`(>= acc-micro always-limit)`, counted across the macrostep) and FALSE for flat/compound machines, where each dequeued raise's nested settle starts its own `:always` count (transition.cljc: "They stay out of `always-depth`: the nested settle bounds its own iterations"). Measured on the JVM with re-frame.machines/machine-transition on a flat machine that takes b->c->d, raises, then e->f->g: `:always-depth-limit 2` returns :ok at :g after four `:always` microsteps, and limit 1 returns :rf.error/machine-always-depth-exceeded. The spec now says only that the limit bounds the `:always` microsteps. Whether it should be per settle run or per macrostep is a design question for whoever owns the machines engine.

description:

title: Require-alias convention in docs: allow the short aliases
description:
MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): option 2. Amend spec/Conventions.md §Require-alias dialect to say that DOCUMENTATION samples may use the short aliases the corpus already uses (ssr, ts, th, schemas, flows, epoch, head, ssr.ring), while rf.<tail> stays canonical in framework SOURCE, where collisions matter. The reasons: reader ergonomics under the stance, and a one-sweep conversion of the whole corpus is churn for no user benefit. No ratchet extension to docs. HELD with #10504 (Conventions.md is a hot zone): cluster into that dispatch. Mike may overrule.

From GitHub issue #10507 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** decision · **Priority:** P3 · **Surface:** `spec/Conventions.md` §Require-alias dialect (hot-zone), and every `docs/` corpus page

## Description
`spec/Conventions.md` makes `rf.<tail>` the canonical alias for every framework namespace other than `re-frame.core`, reserving bare leaf aliases for application namespaces. The docs corpus, guides and API reference alike, uses short aliases: `ssr`, `ts`, `th`, `schemas`, `flows`, `epoch`, `head`, `ssr.ring`/`ssr-ring`. Only machines and routing use `rf.machines` / `rf.routing`. The ratchet `check_require_alias_dialect.py` does not grade docs.

## Options
1. Convert the whole docs corpus to `rf.<tail>` in one sweep, and optionally extend the ratchet to docs fences.
2. Amend the convention to allow the short aliases in documentation.

## Acceptance
- A ruling is recorded, and the corpus is consistent with it.

Discovered by: day8/re-frame2#10468.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor)
HELD with #10504 (rf2-kusgs): the kusgs cluster is now HELD — SEQUENCED BEHIND worker/regfx-gzepz (spec/Conventions.md edit). Dispatch together with rf2-kusgs once that PR MERGES.

== VERDICT (worker/specrec-kusgs, PR #10528, 2026-09-26)
FIXED per the ruling (option 2). Partly already at tip: the section's scope paragraph (landed 2026-09-09, before the issue) already bound only repository Clojure source and let documentation establish an application-local alias. The amendment makes the ruling explicit: rf.<leaf> is canonical in framework source, because a bare leaf alias collides there with an application namespace's, and documentation samples may use the short aliases the corpus uses (ssr, ssr.ring, head, schemas, flows, epoch, ts, th). No ratchet change; check_require_alias_dialect.py still grades source only.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #10528 (merged, trunk e8178657ac; CI 88/88), per the ruling. Part was already at tip: a scope paragraph from 2026-09-09 already let docs use their own aliases. The amendment names the short aliases and says rf.<leaf> stays canonical in framework source. No ratchet change.

title: xray spec: navigation glyphs and the per-tab icon table don't match the shipped UI
description:
From GitHub issue #10542 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** spec/implementation disagreement · **Priority:** P4 · **Needs a ruling:** update the spec or the UI

## Gap
Found during the `re-frame2-xray` skill review (day8/re-frame2#10535), which corrected the skill but not the spec.

1. **Navigation glyphs.** The spec shows a `[◀ ▶ ⏭]` cluster at `tools/xray/spec/000-Vision.md:271,380`, `003-Machine-Inspector.md:1765,1774` and `007-UX-IA.md:87`. The shipped buttons render `‹ › »` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:890-906`).
2. **Tab icons.** `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §17.1.5 calls its per-tab icon and stripe table (⚡ ◐ ◉ …) binding. Nothing renders it: tab buttons show the label only, with the mnemonic in `title` (`shell.cljs:2581-2627`).
3. **Also check:** whether the `configure!` example in `tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md` puts `:theme` at the top level. `configure!` reads only `:rf.xray/*` keys, so a top-level `:theme` is silently ignored (`config.cljc:1905-1920`). The skill had exactly this mistake.

## What to do
For 1 and 2, either update the spec to match the shipped UI or change the UI, and mark the icon table as future work if it stays unshipped. For 3, check the example and fix it if needed.

## Acceptance
The Xray spec describes what ships, or clearly marks what is planned.

MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): the SPEC FOLLOWS THE SHIPPED UI.
(1) The navigation glyphs become the shipped ‹ › » at every cited site.
(2) The §17.1.5 per-tab icon/stripe table is no longer described as binding. Tab buttons render the label, with the mnemonic in title; say so. Remove the icon table, or mark it plainly as an unshipped design; the worker picks whichever reads more cleanly.
(3) Check the configure! example in tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md, and fix it if :theme sits at the top level, since configure! reads only :rf.xray/* keys.
No UI change.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #10555 (merged, trunk b94afcc1c0; CI 88/88 at head c688030aed), per the ruling that the spec follows the shipped UI. The Xray spec (000, 003, 007, 018 and 021) now shows the ribbon glyphs ‹ › » at every site that cited the old cluster. The §17.1.5 icon/stripe table is no longer binding, and the spec states that no tab or panel header carries an icon. The configure! premise did not hold: the only literal example was already correct. The precedence prose in 015 now shows the nested :rf.xray/settings {:theme ...} form. No UI change. Residue (a shell.cljs docstring glyph, a trace_state.cljs comment, and the 003 mini-scrubber prose) is filed separately.

title: Core/epoch/flows/test-support defects: destroy-adapter! loses the first failure, :dispatch-later with a bad :ms fires at once, reg-flow bad metadata throws raw, epoch facade rejects frame values, :clear-app-schemas? inert
description:
Found by the docs/api review, steps 1-2 (rf2-elnoo, PR #10549, merged 2026-09-26 at trunk a55df1a1e3). Each item is a CLAIM measured by that review; re-verify it at tip before acting.

1. destroy-adapter! loses the first failure when both the Fresco drain and the disposer throw, against spec/006:337.
2. A :dispatch-later with a missing or bad :ms dispatches immediately.
3. :rf.fx/reg-flow with non-map metadata throws a raw exception.
4. The epoch facade rejects frame VALUES; only ids work.
5. The test fixture's :clear-app-schemas? option does nothing.

MAYOR RULINGS (2026-09-26):
(1) Keep the first failure, per spec/006.
(2) Refuse a missing or non-numeric :ms loudly with a named error, preferring an existing :rf.error/* id. A silent immediate dispatch is a surprise the caller never asked for.
(3) Give it a named :rf.error/* with the offending value, like the other reg-* metadata guards.
(4) Normalise frame values through frame-target->id, exactly as rf2-zkks7 did for ssr hydrate!.
(5) Make it work if that is small, otherwise remove the option.
Each gets a regression, shown red with the fix removed.

title: skills: structural follow-ups from the per-skill reviews (leaf size ceilings, split recipes, duplicated facts, design-record provenance)
description:
From GitHub issue #10547 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** task (umbrella) · **Priority:** P4 · Each item is independent and can be closed with the reasoning recorded.

The nine skill-review PRs (#10529–#10531, #10533–#10537, #10539) deliberately left these, as restructures beyond a proportionate editing pass.

1. **re-frame2-setup: leaves at the size ceiling.** `references/deps-versions.md` (16,382 B) and `entry-namespace.md` (16,352 B) sit right at the 16 KB limit that `tests/setup_drift_test.clj` enforces, so any correction trips it. Move the `:local/root` table or the post-publish section into its own leaf.
2. **re-frame2-setup: generator command lives in the README.** The exact generator command and the `-Tnew` prerequisite live in `skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md`, a human-facing file, but `SKILL.md` rule 4 sends the agent there. Move it into a reference, and update `tests/generator_route_test.clj`, which reads it from the README.
3. **re-frame2-setup: no troubleshooting row for a missing `:shadow` alias.** `SKILL.md` calls this the most common first-watch failure, but gives no error string. Capture the real message from a run and add a row.
4. **re-frame2-pair: Story recipes are split.** They are split across `references/recipes.md` and `references/stories.md` ("Diffing two variants" appears in both). Merging them means updating `tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj`, which pins headings in `recipes.md`.
5. **re-frame2-pair: file contents don't match their names.** `mcp-transport.md` holds op semantics ("When to use snapshot vs the per-op reads"), and `vocabulary.md` holds the privacy and launch-flag rules. Both are misnamed or misplaced. Moving them touches inbound anchors and test pins.
6. **re-frame-migration: facts restated across leaves.** The M-8 and effect-map facts are restated in 4–5 leaves, and the voice leans on bold and all-caps. A dedup pass could cut 15–20%, but it must keep the three migration drift gates green. The "silent-fail register" title now also holds loud-at-load rows.
7. **re-frame2: observability routing explained twice.** `references/…/privacy-and-elision.md` §Choosing where observations go restates `production-observability.md`. Shrink it to the privacy clauses plus a pointer.
8. **Design records still carry bead ids, dates and history.** These are `skills/*/spec/design.md`, `spec/inputs.md` and `authoring-prompt.md` (improver, pair-retro, reagent-migration, re-frame-migration), plus the reagent-migration `evals/evals.json` `notes` field (~7 KB). Decide whether the present-tense rule covers skill-internal design records, and strip them if so.
9. **Bundled-script candidates**, only if they pay for themselves. Each is deterministic work the agent currently does by hand:
   - setup: materialise the scaffold files from `first-counter.md`;
   - implementor: an EDN-aware conformance-corpus summary;
   - reagent-migration: print each census class beside its MIG route.
10. **Eval re-runs.** After the description rewrites, re-run each skill's trigger and behaviour evals. They were not run because they need the eval harness and live model runs. Priorities: re-frame2-implementor entries 1–22, re-frame2-xray eval 26, and pair-retro's new "earlier-conversation session" route, which needs a manual replay line in `evals/README.md`.

MAYOR RULINGS per item (2026-09-26), under the stance:
1. APPROVED: split re-frame2-setup's deps-versions.md / entry-namespace.md, moving the :local/root table or the post-publish section into its own leaf, so corrections stop tripping the 16 KB ceiling.
2. APPROVED: move the generator command and the -Tnew prerequisite from skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md into a reference, and update tests/generator_route_test.clj.
3. APPROVED, only if the real error string can be captured. The Clojure CLI's missing-alias message needs no shadow-cljs compile. Otherwise drop it and say why.
4. APPROVED: merge re-frame2-pair's Story recipes into one home, and update the prompt_regression_test.clj heading pins.
5. DECLINED: renaming or moving mcp-transport.md / vocabulary.md content touches inbound anchors and test pins for a naming nicety.
6. PARTLY: DECLINED the 15-20% dedup pass (it risks the three drift gates for modest gain). APPROVED retitling the "silent-fail register" so it covers its loud-at-load rows.
7. APPROVED: shrink privacy-and-elision.md §Choosing where observations go to the privacy clauses plus a pointer to production-observability.md.
8. DECLINED: skill-internal design records (spec/design.md, spec/inputs.md, authoring-prompt.md, evals notes) are working design records, like docs/design, and the present-tense rule does not reach them.
9. DECLINED: no bundled script has shown it pays for itself.
10. NOT DISPATCHABLE: eval re-runs need a live-model harness. Recorded here, and not worked.
Do items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 (retitle) and 7.
close_reason: Done in PR #10557, merged 2026-09-27 at trunk 6d0a87809c (closure from the PR body; the worker was stopped by operator decision after its PR went green). (1) Done in part: re-frame2-setup's post-publish :mvn/version section moved to references/post-publish.md (deps-versions.md 16,382 -> 15,497 LF bytes; a 100-byte correction trips the 16 KB ceiling test before and passes after). entry-namespace.md (16,297 B) is NOT split: it already fits under the ceiling, and two held readers (tools/template emitted_test_run_test.clj and scripts/check_skill_setup_counter_drift.py) read its regions, so under the stance no follow-up is filed. (2) Done: the generator route moved to references/generator-route.md, pinned by tests/generator_route_test.clj. (3) Done: a troubleshooting row carries the captured missing-shadow-alias error string. (4) Done: re-frame2-pair's Story procedures live in references/stories.md. (5) Declined by ruling. (6) Retitle only: "compile-clean register". (7) Done: privacy-and-elision.md points to production-observability.md. (8), (9) declined, (10) not dispatchable, by ruling. bb structural suites 0 failures; PR CI 88 of 88 green.

title: Dev build: a malformed :carriers block rethrows from the trace and kills the router thread
description:
Found by the docs/api steps 3-4 worker (PR #10562, merged 2026-09-27). A CLAIM; reproduce at tip first.
In a dev build, a malformed :rf.http/managed :carriers block raises :rf.error/bad-classification on first use (privacy.cljc validates it when a request is traced, not at reg-fx; spec/009 now says 'refused at the next request', rf2-3mfdf). The claim is that the raise happens INSIDE trace emission and rethrows out of it, so the throw escapes the router's drain and kills the router thread. Earlier measurement (the docs/api correctness step) also recorded that when it fires it makes the whole dispatch-sync throw.
MAYOR RULING (2026-09-27): a misconfiguration must be LOUD but must never take the runtime down. The refusal of the bad :carriers block stays a named :rf.error/bad-classification, reported through the normal error channel for that request, and that request is refused. It must not escape trace emission, kill the router, or poison later dispatches. Add a regression that shows the router still processes a following event after the refusal, red with the fix removed.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT (PR #10567, branch worker/httpfix-g5zil, commit 5999c07c39) — FIXED
Reproduced at trunk 072b57fd62 (JVM, :carriers {:headers [:X-Team-Key]}): managed-handler raised :rf.error/bad-classification; core's fx walk reported it as :rf.error/fx-handler-exception; that error trace's projection reached the :http/project-managed-fx-args hook, which re-read the block and threw again inside trace/emit-error!; trace emission rethrew (stack: privacy/managed-carriers -> classification/project-fx-tags -> trace/emit-error! -> fx/emit-fx-error! -> fx/do-fx -> router/run-one-pass!). Effects: dispatch-sync threw; no error trace reached listeners; a sibling [:dispatch ...] in the same :fx vector was dropped; an async drain threw to the host. NOT reproduced: "kills the router thread" — on the JVM the drain's emergency re-arm still processed the next queued event and later dispatches.
Fix, http only (no core change): privacy/project-managed-fx-args never throws on a malformed block and projects :request fail-closed to :rf/redacted (reply addresses still project); handlers/managed-handler refuses the request up front (before the middleware chain, debug-gated like the trace) with the named :rf.error/bad-classification, reported as that effect's :rf.error/fx-handler-exception.
Regression implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_carriers_refusal_test.clj (async drain driven by hand): drain does not throw; refused effect's sibling AND the next queued event processed; one fx-handler-exception naming :rf.error/bad-classification; header value absent from the trace; later dispatch-sync not poisoned. With the fix removed: exit 1, 7 of 11 assertions fail (drain throws :rf.error/bad-classification, log [:fetch :next] without :sibling, 0 error traces). Restore verified by blob hash. http JVM suite 541/4212 -> 543/4239 (both beads), exit 0.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10567, merged 2026-09-27 at trunk 78a7d58c13, in implementation/http only.
Reproduced at 072b57fd62: the handler raised :rf.error/bad-classification, and the error trace for it re-read the :carriers block through the :http/project-managed-fx-args hook and threw again inside trace emission. So dispatch-sync threw, no error trace reached listeners, a sibling [:dispatch …] in the same :fx vector was dropped, and an async drain threw to the host. "Kills the router thread" did NOT reproduce: on the JVM the drain re-arms and later events still run.
Fix: the projection hook never throws; with unreadable carrier names it redacts the whole :request. managed-handler refuses the request up front with :rf.error/bad-classification, reported as the effect's :rf.error/fx-handler-exception. The check still runs in dev builds only, so production is unchanged.
Regression: http_managed_carriers_refusal_test.clj; with the fix removed it exits 1 with 7 of 11 assertions failing (restore verified by blob hash). http JVM 541 tests / 4212 assertions -> 543 / 4239. PR CI 88 of 88 green.

title: spec/016: promises a dev/Xray warning for over-broad :cross-scope? invalidation that nothing implements
description:
MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): option A. Drop or reword the spec/016 bullet (~986) to say what exists: Xray MARKS cross-scope invalidations in its resources panel. Do not build the warning. Re-verify its absence first, using the existing Xray cross-scope marking as the positive control, and check that docs/api/re-frame.resources.md does not repeat the promise.

From GitHub issue #10493 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** spec/implementation disagreement · **Priority:** P3 · **Needs a ruling:** remove the promise, or build the warning

## Gap

`spec/016-Resources.md` ~line 986 (at `92c6b29960`), in the list of what makes `:cross-scope? true` an audited operation:

> - dev/Xray **warns** when a descriptor would be more precise than a broad `:cross-scope?` sweep.

The `docs/resources` correctness pass (day8/re-frame2#10480) found no such warning in `implementation/resources/src` or `tools/xray`. What does exist is Xray *marking* an invalidation as cross-scope (`tools/xray/.../panels/resources.cljs` ~line 859). The guide docs used to promise the warning and were corrected to describe the marking instead, so the spec is now the only place that still promises it.

## Options

- **A (recommended): drop the bullet**, or reword it to say what Xray does: it marks cross-scope invalidations in its resources panel. That is the smallest change, and it keeps the spec as the source of truth for behaviour that exists.
- **B: implement the warning.** This needs a working definition of "a descriptor would be more precise". For example, every scope the sweep actually touched was enumerable at the call site. That is new analysis in Xray, with its own tests.

## What to do (for option A)

1. Re-verify there is no implementation. Search `implementation/` and `tools/` for the warning's likely spellings (`more precise`, `cross-scope` near `warn`). Use a pattern that finds the existing Xray cross-scope *marking* as a positive control, so a zero means the warning really is absent.
2. Edit the bullet in `spec/016-Resources.md`.
3. Check whether `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md` repeats the promise.

## Acceptance

- The spec and the implementation agree, and no guide or reference page promises a warning that does not exist.
- The doc gates exit 0. `spec/` is staged into the MkDocs build, so `mkdocs build --strict` covers it.

spec/016-Resources.md about :678 still lists :rf.resource.internal/aborted. No such event exists: the resources artefact registers 11 :rf.resource.internal/* events (see spec/Conventions.md after #10528), and an abort arrives on failed. Correct the spec/016 list to match; re-verify the line at tip.

The same search finds the phrase in spec/016 (control 1). The only :rf.warning/* id containing "scope" is mutation-scope-mismatch. The bullet now says Xray marks cross-scope invalidations in its resources panel.

The roster row is reclassified from "error (registration)" to "error (use-time)".

title: Gate follow-ups after rf2-11zc2 / rf2-wbx0q: README gate's site-URL anchors, CLAUDE.md's "path-only" sentence, mcp-transport.md optional markers, a test.yml comment
description:
Found by the gate worker (PR #10576, merged 2026-09-27 at trunk b66ff71e51). Each is a CLAIM; verify at tip.
1. scripts/check_readme_links.py is still path-only for day8.github.io site URLs, while check_doc_slugs.py now checks their #anchors (MkDocs _N slug model, in _site_url_problems). Three root-markdown site anchors depend on it: one in README.md and two in SKILL-REDIRECT.md, all of which resolve today. MAYOR RULING: give the README gate the same anchor check by REUSING the docs gate's code, not by writing a second one. Add a self-test plant that goes red.
2. CLAUDE.md, § Build & Test, the link-validation paragraph, says site URLs are resolved "path-only, in BOTH gates". After item 1 that is false for both gates. Correct that sentence to the gates as they are, and change nothing else in the paragraph.
3. skills/re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md: the ? optional markers disagree with each tool's :required list in tool-descriptors.edn. describe-image's frame and trace-window's ms are written as required but aren't, and all three snapshot keys are written as required though none is. Correct the markers to the descriptors. The drift gate checks argument NAMES only; do not extend it to optionality (not gold plating).
4. .github/workflows/test.yml: the comment on the drift self-test step lists the axes it checks and omits the new argument-signature axis. Add it. It is a comment-only edit to a HOT ZONE file, so nothing else in .github may change.

title: HTTP bad-return diagnostic echoes sensitive interceptor data into trace tags
description:
PR #10522 makes :rf.error/http-interceptor-bad-return observable, but its new diagnostic publishes the invalid return in :returned and interpolates it into :reason before calling prepare-emit-failure. That composer redacts :body, :body-text, :decoded, :detail and string :cause; it does not redact :returned or :reason. A malformed interceptor return containing request data therefore escapes into the trace even when the request is explicitly :sensitive? true.

Reproduced on CURRENT origin/main fc45d9978c2d23bad1bc69e3a109c8299dfc1f17, isolated committed core/http sources, JVM plain-atom fixture. Register a trace listener, then call run-interceptor-chain! with ctx {:sensitive? true :request {:url "https://example.invalid/x" :headers {"Authorization" "BAD_RETURN_SECRET"}}} and a :before fn returning [(get-in ctx [:request :headers "Authorization"])]. Catch the intended bad-return exception. The emitted bad-return event has top-level :sensitive? true, but both [:tags :returned] and [:tags :reason] contain BAD_RETURN_SECRET. Probe exit 0; BAD_RETURN_TRACE_PRESENT=true, SENSITIVE_STAMP=true, RETURNED_SLOT_LEAKS=true, REASON_LEAKS=true. This report is about the trace listener/recording boundary; it does not claim a separately verified off-box sink escape.

Code: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc:410-425 (bad-return construction/emission in shared run-chain*); implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy.cljc:371-411 (redact-failure-with-flag). The shared branch serves :before and :after. Existing regression uses nil only, so it proves the id without exercising data-bearing invalid returns. The surrounding implementation already treats author-controlled error text as sensitive because it can echo tokens.

Keep the useful bad-return id and interceptor identity, but project the data-bearing return and its textual echo through the established effective-sensitivity policy. Do not add another privacy mechanism or broaden registration APIs. Verify both phases and an earlier interceptor marking the request sensitive.

Evidence: ai/probe-10511-current/probe-10522-top-flag.clj and ai/probe-10522-audit-sep23-monitor-2.log/.exit in audit-sep23-monitor. Source rf2-n1w8n remains closed; this is a new separately trackable finding.
acceptance_criteria: For a sensitive request, data-bearing non-map returns from before/after interceptors cannot leave a secret in any recorded bad-return trace field, including returned and reason. The diagnostic still identifies bad-return and the interceptor; a genuine throw still identifies failed. Test effective sensitivity inherited from an earlier before interceptor and preserve useful non-sensitive diagnostics.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #10606 (worker/httpbadret-sdeze), reproduced first at trunk c19d2c4d74.

Reproduced on the JVM with a trace listener, using an Authorization header value as the secret and an interceptor returning [(get-in ctx [:request :headers "Authorization"])]. At base the bad-return row was stamped :sensitive? true while [:tags :returned] and [:tags :reason] both carried the secret. That held for all three cases: :before with top-level sensitivity, :after on a sensitive request, and :before where an EARLIER :before set [:request :sensitive?] true. Control: on a NON-sensitive request the row shows :returned and :reason raw and is not stamped. That is the tip policy and it is kept.

Siblings with the same cause on the same surface were fixed too. :rf.error/http-interceptor-failed redacted :cause but repeated it in :reason (" Cause: <message>"). :rf.error/http-reply-tail-failed carried the caught throw's message raw in :cause, and for an :after bad return that message echoes the returned value.

Fix, all under implementation/http:
- privacy/redact-failure-with-flag redacts a non-nil :returned under the effective sensitivity, beside :body/:detail/string :cause. A nil return stays visible.
- middleware/run-chain* renders each chain-error row's :reason from the slot value the composer PROJECTED (:returned or :cause), so the sentence never shows more than the slot.
- transport/emit-reply-tail-error! composes through prepare-emit-failure, whose string-:cause rule covers the throw message.
The id, the interceptor id and :reply-error-id stay on every row. The thrown ex-info is unchanged (on-box app data).

title: A denylisted query param (e.g. ?api_key=) on a NON-sensitive request leaks raw through the chain error's URL on core's fx row, while the HTTP row and :rf.fx/args redact it
description:
Found by rf2-ksdtl's worker (PR #10609, merged at trunk d69d0285b8), and recorded in that bead's close reason. It is a CLAIM; reproduce it first.

REPORTED: on a request NOT marked sensitive, a denylisted query parameter such as `?api_key=...` is redacted on the HTTP layer's own row and in `:rf.fx/args`. But when an interceptor fails, the chain error's data carries the request URL raw, so core's `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception` row (`:exception`, on both the trace and the always-on error record) shows the value.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT: denylist redaction applies to every request, sensitive or not, which is exactly why the HTTP row and `:rf.fx/args` already apply it. #10609 routed the chain error through the HTTP redaction only when the request is sensitive. The URL's denylisted query values need the same always-on treatment in the thrown error.

FIX at the producer, `raise-chain-error!` in `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc`, which #10609 added: apply the always-on URL denylist redaction to the chain error's data on EVERY request, reusing the existing denylist projection. Add no new mechanism, and change nothing in core.

Keep everything else about a non-sensitive request's error exactly as #10609 left it: the returned value and the thrown message stay as-is. Do not redact the in-process request.

A regression goes red at base, with a denylisted param on a non-sensitive request and a failing `:before`, on core's row and on the always-on record. Controls: a non-denylisted param rides verbatim, and #10606's and #10609's regressions stay green.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10614 (commit "fix(http): a chain error's URL redacts denylisted query values on every request").

REPRODUCED on the JVM at d69d0285b8 before any change. The request was not sensitive, the URL was ?api_key=DENYLISTED_QUERY_SECRET&user_id=42, and a :before threw. The chain error's own row already read api_key=:rf/redacted with :sensitive? stamped. But core's :rf.error/fx-handler-exception row carried the raw value in :exception's ex-data :url, on the dev trace and on the always-on record: 4 of the new regression's 9 assertions failed. SIBLING, same producer: a failing :after on a non-sensitive request leaked the value through the :rf.error/http-reply-tail-failed always-on record's :exception (2 of 4 assertions failed).

FIX at the producer only. In raise-chain-error! (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc):
  (cond-> extra sensitive? (rf.http.privacy/redact-failure true))
became
  (rf.http.privacy/redact-failure extra sensitive? (rf.http.privacy/managed-carriers))
This is the existing projection, now applied on every request and given the registration's carriers so the thrown :url matches the chain error's own row. Nothing in core changed. A non-sensitive chain error's other slots, its message and the in-process request are as #10609 left them. Spec 014's Failure mode item 2, the Privacy "thrown value carries the same projection" paragraph and Production elision now say the thrown value redacts denylisted query values on every request. Spec 009's reply-tail row speaks only of the sensitive case and stays true.

CONTROLS:
- user_id=42 rides verbatim.
- The throw's message rides verbatim.
- An app carrier {:include ["shop_token"] :except ["sig"]} redacts shop_token and leaves sig verbatim, on core's row and on the always-on record.
- #10606's and #10609's regressions stay green: the http suite read 549 tests / 4314 assertions at base, and 551 / 4329 with the fix, 0 failures. The +2 / +15 is exactly the two new deftests.

SABOTAGE:
- Restoring the base form of that line turned the two regressions red: 8 of 15 assertions failed.
- Passing nil carriers instead failed the carrier control 2 of 11: sig was redacted and shop_token rode raw.
- Each restore matched the committed blob 32d72b52ef.

title: spec/014-HTTPRequests.md's reg-http-interceptor examples register without a frame, which raises :rf.error/no-frame-context at namespace load
description:
Found by rf2-md9qk's worker (PR #10610, merged at trunk 43e118fbcf). That PR fixed the same defect in the shipped skill recipe (`skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md`), but the spec was outside its fence. It is a CLAIM; verify it first.

`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` §Shape and §Example (Bearer auth) show `reg-http-interceptor` with no `:frame`, and the example's comment says requests "on `:rf/default`" carry the header. As #10610 measured, registration resolves the frame with `require-current-frame!` when `:frame` is absent, so the form as printed raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` outside a frame scope, and installs nothing.

Align the spec's examples with the runtime and with #10610's recipe: an explicit `:frame`, or `with-frame` around a block of registrations. State that the frame need not exist yet at registration time, because the chain is looked up by frame id per request. Correct the "on `:rf/default`" comment to match. If the spec deliberately describes a `:rf/default` fallback that the runtime lacks, report it rather than editing the spec to match either side. `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` is not a hot zone.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10614 (commit "docs(spec): the HTTP interceptor examples name their frame").

VERIFIED at source. When :frame is absent, reg-http-interceptor resolves the frame with rf.frame/require-current-frame! (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc, the frame-id binding in reg-http-interceptor). The chain is keyed by frame id with no frame-existence check, and it is read at issue time. Spec 014's Shape prose already said a registration under no scope raises :rf.error/no-frame-context, "never :rf/default", and Spec 002 makes :rf/default an ordinary id. So the spec describes no :rf/default fallback; only the examples and the comment disagreed.

FIX in spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:
- Shape: the example registers with :frame :app. A paragraph now says a registration names its frame, with :frame or with an enclosing rf/with-frame, and that the frame need not exist yet, because the chain is keyed by frame id and read each time a request is issued.
- Example (Bearer auth): :frame :app, and the comment now says requests "on :app".
- SIBLING in the same block: the example request had no reply target. The runtime refuses an unaddressed request with :rf.error/http-no-reply-target before it reaches the wire, so the request now carries :reply-to [:articles/listed].

EVIDENCE: a scratch JVM project read the fenced blocks out of the base spec (d69d0285b8) and the edited spec and evaluated them as printed, 13 checks.
- Base Shape and base Example at namespace load: both raised :rf.error/no-frame-context, and the interceptor registry stayed {}.
- Edited forms: both installed, with the chain keyed on :app ([:auth-header :app/bearer-auth]) while frame :app did not yet exist. After make-frame :app, a request on :app carried "Bearer tok-123" and its reply landed.
- with-frame registered on a frame that did not exist yet.
- The base example's request was refused with :rf.error/http-no-reply-target, with 0 new requests on the wire.
- PLANTED: the edited Example registered on :frame :wrong (plant match count 1), and the header read nil. The check failed as intended. It was the only failing check of the 13, and the run exited 0 by design.

DOCS GATES: both were shown red on a planted broken link in the new paragraph.
- check_doc_slugs.py exited 1, naming spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:845.
- python -m mkdocs build --strict exited 1, "Aborted with 1 warnings".
- The restore matched the committed blob b85b8fe0ed.
- On the final base 19d524206e both exit 0.
- The examples themselves are fenced code, which neither gate inspects, so the JVM run is their evidence.

title: Gate-efficiency trial: re-run only the suites a rebase can reach, one build-lane window per worker, planted faults scoped to the namespace; then consider amending docs/the-mayor-method
description:
Mike, 2026-09-29 14:09 AUSEST: "In 60 mins, after you have trialed the new method, consider modifying /docs/the-mayor-method". Review is due about 15:11 AUSEST.

WHY. Measured on worker/subprivacy-2p7fo (rf2-ajpcr + rf2-2p7fo, PR #10611), 66 minutes in at 13:59:
- It ran its six JVM suites one after another (routing, routing-prod, resources, core ~3 min, core-prod ~3 min, machines) about 4.5 times: baseline, then final passes 1-4. That is roughly 35 minutes of wall time.
- The fourth pass (13:52-13:58) followed a trunk move by PR #10612, which changed only docs/ and spec/. It could not have reached core or resources, but core, core-prod and resources were re-run anyway, for about 6 minutes.
- About 10 planted-fault runs each ran a whole suite when one namespace would have done.
- One CI round trip (~15 min) came from the public-API manifest drift check, which the brief did not nominate for a late-bind directory change.
- CI waiting accounted for about 20 minutes, and model time for a minority, roughly 15 minutes.

Current rule: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, "Before you push": "Re-run the gates on the final base after every rebase."

THE TRIAL RULES, sent to all six live workers at 14:1x:
1. After a rebase, list what landed: `git diff --name-only <old-base> <new-base>`.
   - Re-run only the suites that diff can reach: the artefact whose files changed, plus every artefact whose deps.edn `:local/root` chain includes it. implementation/core reaches nearly everything.
   - Where the diff reaches none of your suites (docs/, spec/ prose, .beads/, or an artefact off your chain), skip the re-run. Instead, quote the diff's file list in the PR body and name PR CI as the final-base gate, since it tests your branch merged onto the current trunk.
2. Scope each planted-fault run to the namespace under test, not the whole suite.
3. Take ONE shadow-cljs lane window per worker, at the end: base counts from a detached base checkout in the worker's own worktree, then head counts, then scoped plants.
4. The mayor nominates the public-API manifest check in any brief touching late-bind rows or public names.

EVIDENCE TO COLLECT from each worker's report: how many rebases, which suites were re-run and which skipped (with the diff that justified each skip), lane windows taken, and an estimate of minutes saved. Also record any case where a skipped re-run would have caught something CI later caught, since that is the failure this trial could introduce.

Close this bead with the verdict and, if the method changes, the PR that changed it.
notes:
== TRIAL EVIDENCE 1: worker/subprivacy-2p7fo (PR #10611, merged at 940f8334f1), 2026-09-29 14:2x AUSEST ==
Both of its rebases happened before the trial started, but the worker applied the reach test anyway and reported it.

Rebase 1 (6c698873a3 -> 98facb7f83): no path under implementation/, spec/, examples/, scripts/ or .github/. Only the doc gates were re-run.

Rebase 2 (-> b712ee8269): the only source change was implementation/http/src (rf2-ksdtl).
- Re-run, because http is on their test classpaths: core, the core production gate and resources. Their counts were unchanged.
- Skipped, because http is not in their :local/root chain, directly or transitively (checked): routing, the routing production gate and machines.

Other measurements:
- Minutes saved: about 10-12.
- Lane windows: 0. CI's node lane graded the :cljs arm.
- MISSED CATCHES: none. CI caught nothing a skipped re-run would have caught.
- The public-API manifest drift check was the one CI round that local gates did not predict, because the brief did not nominate it. The trial's rule 4 (the mayor nominates it) addresses that.

The whole task ran 81 minutes (4853 s), 305 tool uses.
== TRIAL EVIDENCE 2: worker/httpdeny-qfw1n (PR #10614, merged at 0cdc51f202), 2026-09-29 14:4x AUSEST ==
One rebase, d69d0285b8 -> b712ee8269, done before the trial rules arrived. The worker re-ran all five JVM suites (http, resources, reply-conformance, ssr-ring, core) and both docs gates by reflex.

Under the trial rule:
- The diff was 84 files: .beads/, docs/ssr, spec/011, adapter tests and story-ui tests. None of them reaches those five suites, so all five would have been skipped and only the docs gates re-run.
- Estimated saving: about 10 minutes.

A NUANCE the trial rule does not address: four commits from #10611 (core classification, resources, routing) landed AFTER this PR's final base and CI run. This PR's CI graded a merge ref that did not contain them, and the mayor merged on the five-clause criterion: mergetree clean, no textual overlap. Neither the old rule nor the trial rule covers a sibling landing between a PR's last CI run and its merge. The old rule would only catch it if the worker rebased again. Record this as a known residual when writing the method change; it is not a reason against the trial.

Lane-window note, same tick: storyfix-w3s0g asked for 7 compile+run cycles (est 45-75 min). The mayor dropped the clean-final step in favour of PR CI's node and browser counts, which saves 2 cycles.
== MAYOR VERDICT 2026-09-29 15:1x AUSEST: ADOPT, amend the method ==

EVIDENCE, from 14:10 to 15:10. Three completed reports and three in-flight workers.

Rebase re-run by reach:
- subprivacy (#10611): at rebase 2, re-ran the three suites http reaches and skipped routing, routing-prod and machines, which it does not. Saved ~10-12 min. 0 missed.
- httpdeny (#10614): re-ran all five suites by reflex. Its rebase diff (84 files: .beads, docs/ssr, spec/011, adapter and story-ui tests) reached none of them. Would have saved ~10 min. 0 missed.

TWO FINDINGS THE TRIAL SURFACED, which belong in the text:
(a) PR CI grades the change MERGED onto the trunk as of its push (the merge ref), not the branch's merge base. title: compile-node-test.cjs with --config-merge clears .shadow-cljs/builds/node-test AFTER compiling, so a focused dev-mode node bundle cannot run (ENOENT on its cljs-runtime files)
description:
Found by rf2-3h7v2.6's worker (prune-xraytop6) on 2026-09-29 while taking a scoped base count in a lane window. `implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs`, invoked with `--config-merge` (the route `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`'s own comment recommends for a focused compile), removes `.shadow-cljs/builds/node-test` after the compile finishes. title: Claim false: keyword feed-reply translation leaks vector-page declarations
description:
Merged-PR audit #10631, merge c323e3ed3ebfe50736fd912dc6fe201f41ba89e4, run 7c8a9165-023d-421f-98ce-3e92f6303aef.

The approved route and Spec 016 say a vector page keeps its declaration as written. feed-reply-spec instead strips the keyword accessor key from every matching data declaration, even when the actual page was a vector and the merge never used the accessor.

Reproduction: register an infinite feed with :page->items :items and :sensitive [[:data :items :ssn]], then settle page [{:items {:ssn "probe-secret"} :name "public"}]. The app and BOTH off-box continuation reply :value slots carry [{:items {:ssn "probe-secret"} :name "public"}]. Control: exactly the same vector page and declaration without :page->items redacts :ssn. The ordinary enveloped keyword page {:items [{:ssn "probe-secret" :name "public"}]} also redacts as intended.

Cause: trace_egress.cljc:847-858 drops :items to produce [:data :ssn]. state.cljc:1517-1522 merges vector pages by identity before considering the accessor, so the reply still has the :items nesting. Registration permits this valid combination; egress cannot infer the page shape from the accessor alone.

Required correction: preserve vector-page declarations as well as the translated envelope reading when projecting keyword-accessor replies, without adding reply-shape machinery. Keep the existing envelope behavior and raw app/trusted-local delivery. Add a regression for a vector page with an accessor configured and a declared nested field whose first key equals that accessor; prove the secret leaves neither fx carrier.

Measured through the real public registration/ensure/reply flow and project-fx-args-egress, using the PR's capturing transport and helpers, against sources exported from the exact merge. Each case produced two off-box reply carriers; app delivery stayed raw. Evidence: ai/probe-10631/review-probe.clj and ai/probe-10631-audit-sep23-monitor-1.log / .exit in audit-sep23-monitor. JVM probe exit 0; this is a targeted reproduction, not a broad suite rerun.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10641 (commit 87db48a56f on worker/egress3-dagjo). feed-reply-spec in trace_egress.cljc now reads a declared data path that runs through a keyword accessor's key BOTH without that key (the enveloped reading) and as written (the vector-page reading, since state.cljc merge-pages->items merges a vector page by identity without reaching the accessor). This PR adds no reply-shape machinery. The enveloped behaviour, the raw in-process delivery and the callable fallback are unchanged. The Spec 016 feed-reply sentence was updated to match.

Decisive measurement (JVM, real reg-resource / ensure :reply-to / on-success reply flow, carriers projected by project-fx-args-egress): the new test a-keyword-accessor-feeds-vector-page-reply-redacts-the-declaration-as-written covers :page->items :items with :sensitive [[:data :items :ssn]] on the vector page [{:items {:ssn SECRET} :name "zero"}].
- At base: 3 failures. Both reply :value slots carried the SECRET, and the carrier string check fired.
- With the fix: green.
- With the fix planted back out: 3 failures again, only in that test. The restore was verified by blob hash (default-form hash-object equals the committed blob).
- Controls green throughout: the same vector page with no :page->items redacts, and the enveloped keyword page redacts.
- Resources JVM suite: base 867/8122/0, final 871/8147/0.

title: Correct PerformanceObserver delivery explanation in source and instrumentation spec
description: Docs four-pass review found implementation/core/src/re_frame/performance.cljc docstrings and inline comments claim PerformanceObserver callbacks run at measure time before clearMeasures. W3C Performance Timeline queueing algorithm enqueues entries into observer-specific buffers and delivers callbacks asynchronously; clearMeasures only clears timeline entries. Node perf_hooks probe confirms synchronous=false, observed=1, retained=0 after immediate clear. Docs API reference is corrected in campaign PR. Reconcile source docstrings and matching spec/009-Instrumentation.md prose without changing runtime behavior. Primary source https://www.w3.org/TR/performance-timeline/#queue-the-performanceobserver-task .
notes:
== RESULT (worker perfobs-x8ghp, 2026-10-01 AUSEST): PR #10678, head 7952cab390 (rebased on origin/main 6fd206430d). Prose only.

Mechanism, verified at the source: the W3C Performance Timeline "queue a PerformanceEntry" algorithm (https://www.w3.org/TR/performance-timeline/#queue-a-performanceentry) appends the entry to each registered observer's own buffer, then queues the PerformanceObserver task. clearMeasures empties only the timeline buffer. Node v24 perf_hooks probe: synchronous=false, observed=1, retained=0, and a late observer using buffered:true saw 0. The callback ran only after a 200-deep microtask chain had drained, so it is a task, not a microtask.

Sites fixed:
- performance.cljc: the ns docstring Observer-first contract (top level, not in a reader conditional), the mark-and-measure docstring and the macro inline comment (both in the #?(:clj) branch).
- spec/009: the "Clear after emit" bullet and the Consumer access lead-in plus its JS example comment.
- Delta beyond the brief's list:
  - performance_cljs_test.cljs: a testing string carried the same false claim.
  - performance_emit_nightly_test.cljs: a comment called the delivery "a microtask".
  - spec/009 production surface #3 and posture-table row #5: both said observers read via performance.getEntriesByType('measure'), which returns [] under the default retain-entries? false.

Not changed: spec/009 line 1374 and the other "delivered to observers then cleared" shorthands. They are true at the buffer level, since the entry is in each observer's buffer before the clear. docs/api/re-frame.performance.md was already correct and the new wording matches it.

Gates, each exit code captured from the runner:
- present_tense.py verify against 954e86a4fe: exit 0, so only comments and string contents differ.
- clj-kondo without --fail-level: base and head finding sets identical.
- JVM require of re-frame.performance: exit 0.
- check_doc_slugs: exit 0. A planted broken anchor at 009:1507 gave exit 1; after restore the blob hash matched HEAD and the re-run gave exit 0.
- mkdocs build --strict: exit 0.
- Twelve ratchet scripts: all exit 0.

Finding filed: rf2-yq9ak covers spec/Tool-Pair.md (hot zone), whose Performance API consumption section leads with getEntriesByType, which is empty by default, and says the observer "fires per emitted entry".

title: RealWorld restore-reply comments say canned replies carry no :correlation; false once rf2-nhz44 lands
description:
Owning item: rf2-nahcr (RealWorld JWT examples; its PR #10680 merged as a4f1afb008). Discovered while fixing rf2-nhz44.

Once rf2-nhz44 (PR #10685) merges, canned managed-HTTP replies carry `:correlation {:request-id <id>}` whenever the request args carry a `:request-id`, as the live reply does. The RealWorld demo backend (examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs, the `transition` stub near line 570) forwards the app's args map to `:rf.http/managed-canned-success` / `-failure` with only `:after-ms`, `:value`, `:kind` and `:tags` assoc'd on, so an app `:request-id` survives into the reply.

Two comments on trunk then state something false. Verified at origin/main 9c36507278:
- examples/real-apps/realworld_http/auth.cljs, in `:auth/session-restored` (about lines 544-545): "The window, not a generation in the reply, is the test because replies from the demo backend's canned stubs carry no `:correlation` to hold one."
- examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs, about line 580: the same sentence.

The window guard (`restoring-session?`) still works, so nothing is broken. What is open is a choice for the owner:
(a) adopt the tutorial's guard. Issue the restore `GET /user` with `:request-id [:auth/restore (:auth-generation db)]` and drop the reply when `(second (:request-id correlation))` is not the current `:auth-generation`, which matches docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md; or
(b) keep the window guard and rewrite the comment so it gives the window's own reason instead of the canned-stub gap.

Either way, the sentence about canned stubs carrying no `:correlation` goes. This must not land before rf2-nhz44 merges.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor, 2026-10-02 00:44 AUSEST): dispatch only after PR #10685 (rf2-nhz44) MERGES == This bead corrects comments that become false only once the canned replies carry :correlation. Clears when #10685 is merged into main.
== FENCE LIFTED (mayor, 2026-10-02 00:50 AUSEST): PR #10685 MERGED (2026-10-01T14:50:21Z, trunk f53d3285a2). Dispatchable. ==
== MAYOR RULING (2026-10-02 00:54 AUSEST): option (a) == The comment's only stated reason for guarding the restore reply by the window rather than a generation in the reply was the canned-stub :correlation gap, which PR #10685 closed; so the examples teach the one guard the tutorial (docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md) teaches: restore GET /user carries :request-id [:auth/restore (:auth-generation db)] and the reply is dropped when its generation is not current. restoring-session? keeps its other jobs. Fallback to (b) only if (a) needs more than the request args and the reply guard per file, or the demo backend drops the id; the worker reports why. Dispatched to rwcorrelation-9f4em.
== WORKER RESULT (rwcorrelation-9f4em, 2026-10-02): FELL BACK TO (b) PER THE RULING'S OWN CONDITION; PR #10692 ==
Option (a) needs more than the restore request's args and the reply guard in each file. In both apps the restore GET /user is fired by the `:auth/flow` machine's `:begin-restore` action. Its context map carries `:data :event :state :meta :rf.cofx` and never app-db (spec/005-StateMachines.md §Actions), so the action cannot read `:auth-generation`. The tutorial avoids this because its `:auth/session-read` event handler issues the request and holds `db`. Adopting (a) would therefore also mean threading the generation through the `[:auth/flow [:auth/restore (some? token)]]` dispatch in `:auth/session-read` and through the action's destructure: a third site per file. The other routes are a `{:rf/sub ...}` recordable-cofx entry or moving the request out of the machine.
Demo backend premise verified: `respond` in examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs passes the app's whole args map to `:rf.http/managed-canned-success` / `-failure`, with only `:after-ms`, `:value`, `:kind` and `:tags` added. So an app `:request-id` survives into `:correlation`.
Done under (b): in both examples/real-apps/realworld_http/auth.cljs and examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs, the false sentence ("replies from the demo backend's canned stubs carry no `:correlation`") is replaced. The new text gives the window's present-tense reason: the request comes from `:begin-restore`, which never sees app-db and so has no `:auth-generation` to put in a `:request-id`, and the window answers the same question from app-db alone. Comment-only, no behaviour change.
Gates: check-examples-compile.cjs --list exit 0, listing examples/realworld and examples/realworld-resources. check_retired_spellings exit 0; a fault planted in the edited line made it exit 1, and after restore the blob hash matched HEAD. check_ambient_durable_reads exit 0. check_keyword_catalogue_drift exit 0. A git grep for the false sentence finds 2 files at f53d3285a2 and 0 at the PR head. Final-base evidence is PR CI: the CLJS example compile job.
If the owner still wants (a), the smallest version is the one-value threading through the `:auth/restore` event payload described above. That is the minting ladder's rung 2 ("ride the event payload").
== MAYOR (2026-10-02 01:02 AUSEST): worker's fallback to option (b) ACCEPTED == The restore GET /user is issued from the :auth/flow machine's :begin-restore action, which never sees app-db (Spec 005 §Actions), so (a) needed a third change per file; the ruling's own fallback applied. PR #10692 rewrites the comment to give the window's present-tense reason.

title: pair-mcp set-operating-frame success replies select-frame!'s {:ok? true :frame id}, not the documented frames-list envelope
description:
Found while pinning the operating-frame wire-vocab fixtures to production (rf2-vopnk). Owner: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp operating_frame.cljs + the skills/re-frame2-pair preload runtime.

set-operating-frame's SUCCESS reply is not the envelope its descriptor and its own comments promise.

- `re-frame2-pair.runtime/select-frame!` (skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs) returns `{:ok? true :frame frame-id}`.
- `set-form` in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/operating_frame.cljs evaluates `(if (some #{f} (:frames (frames-list))) (select-frame! f) {:ok? false :reason :no-such-frame ...})`, so on success the eval value IS select-frame!'s map, and `set-operating-frame-tool` passes it straight through `wire/ok-text`.
- So a real successful pin replies `{:ok? true :frame :stories}`. The descriptor (set-operating-frame description: "On success returns the resolved map {:ok? true :frames [...] :app-frames [...] :selected <pinned> :operating <resolved>}", and its example 1) and the comment in set-operating-frame-tool ("success: frames-list's {:ok? true :frames :app-frames :selected :operating ...} map") both say otherwise.
- No test sees the real shape: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/conformance_test.cljs fixture `:set-operating-frame/happy` STUBS the `select-frame!` eval as returning the full triple, and the mcp-conformance end-to-end harness calls set-operating-frame only in degraded mode (:nrepl-port-not-found).

Measured by reading source at trunk 128a3cc076; not run live.

Fix is one of: make set-form re-read `(frames-list)` after `select-frame!` (as reset-form already does), or correct the descriptor and comment to the `{:ok? true :frame id}` reply. The first matches what an agent is told it can use to "confirm the pin took". Either way the conformance_test stub should return what the runtime returns.
notes:
== MAYOR RULING (2026-10-02 04:36 AUSEST): option one - make the reply match the descriptor == set-form re-reads (frames-list) after select-frame!, as reset-form already does, so a successful set-operating-frame replies with the documented {:ok? true :frames :app-frames :selected :operating} envelope an agent uses to confirm the pin took. The descriptor stays. The conformance_test.cljs :set-operating-frame/happy stub must return what the runtime actually returns for the eval set-form sends, so the test would have caught the old mismatch. Dispatched to pair-setframe.

title: check_doc_slugs.py does not resolve relative links from docs/ into the source tree, so a renamed source file breaks docs links unseen
description:
No gate checks a relative link from docs/ into the source tree. So when a source file a docs page links to is renamed or deleted, the docs link breaks with no gate noticing. The AGENTS.md "Which Gate Covers Which Edit" table has no row for this case either.

TASK. Make scripts/check_doc_slugs.py resolve relative links that leave the docs tree (docs/, spec/, migration/ and the other roots it grades) against the repo root, and report a missing target the same way it reports a missing in-docs target. Smallest change. No new script, no new CI job (the gate already runs in CI). Census the existing such links first, and fix or report any that are already broken. CONTROL. A planted broken implementation/ target must turn the gate red. Restore, and blob-hash the restore. Every currently valid link must stay green.

LESSONS FROM the implementation/core children (rf2-zbnoc.9-.13):
- Census for name citations before cutting. A docstring in another file citing a test by name was the one thing that forced a restore in rf2-zbnoc.13.
- Read-only review subagents can surface candidates fast, but every candidate still needs reading against its cover before acting.
- The compile wrapper treats any warning as fatal, and a scoped compile can warn on code the branch never touched (a namespace using cljs.reader or clojure.set without requiring it passes in the full build only on load order). Compare warnings against the base copy before treating them as yours.
- A base copy that calls a helper the branch deleted needs its own base copy of that helper.
- The JVM per-test counter must load every namespace before running any of them. A per-test assertion counter (test-vars with a counting reporter) gives an exact per-test baseline to predict each batch against.
- A source-grep test can be satisfied by the function's own docstring, so plant the behaviour, not the text.
- The Bash tool halves runs of backslashes even inside quoted heredocs (CLAUDE.md instrument hazard (o)): write scripts and plant patches with the Write tool.
- Fast scoped node verification: node implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs node-test out/<name>.js --config-merge '{:ns-regexp "^<re>" :output-to "out/<name>.js"}' compiles in seconds; then node out/<name>.js --test=<ns,ns>. - scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh and scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh fail closed without a base ref; pass origin/main.
