title: docs(xray): the manual-boot example in api/mount-control.md mounts with reagent.dom/render, which throws under React 19
description:
docs/xray/api/mount-control.md, section "A manual boot", shows an app boot that requires `[reagent.dom :as rdom]` and mounts with `(rdom/render [views/root] (js/document.getElementById "app"))`. Under React 19, stock Reagent's reagent.dom/render warns and then calls the removed react-dom/render, which throws a TypeError (Reagent 2.0.1 src/reagent/dom.cljs lines 17-21; the corrected diagnosis landed in PR #10790 and PR #10795). A reader who copies the snippet gets a broken boot.

Found by rf2-6yb5c's worker (PR #10795), outside that fence. title: O-16 async-flow guide: lifecycle-aware forwarding of a shared completion; never start or restart an inactive singleton (GH #10930)
description:
GitHub #10930. migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md (worked example about L145-166) appends addressed dispatches to both :app/boot and :wizard/setup on every public completion, and generalises this to one append per awaiting machine. implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc (about L501-528) creates an initial snapshot and marks bootstrap pending when no singleton snapshot exists, so the forward can start a never-started consumer or restart one whose flow has halted. spec/005-StateMachines.md (about L91) specifies final-state auto-destruction. Mayor verified the worked example at trunk 1c9bf4739e. skills/re-frame-migration/references/async-flow-to-machines.md requires the complete O-16 companion before proposing a conversion.

Ask: qualify the worked example and the producer-retargeting instructions with lifecycle-aware delivery. Keep the original completion handler's db writes and effects exactly once, and route only to the intended active run using supported APIs. Explain never-started consumers, completed flows, repeated starts and stale completions. Distinguish an enqueue-time presence check from delivery-time validity: a flow can halt before a queued addressed notification runs. Never suggest registrar membership alone as a guard, or an unconditional broadcast to every registered singleton. Acceptance: the example and its checks cover an unstarted consumer, a completed consumer, two independently active consumers, a queued completion after halt, and a completion from a superseded run; no unrelated consumer is created or restarted. Docs only, unless the supported API cannot express it (then report).

Mayor triage 2026-10-05 at trunk 1c9bf4739e: valid, filed by Mike; actioned. Read the issue in full (`gh issue view 10930 --json body,comments`). The PR carries 'Fixes #10930' on its own line; the mayor closes this bead at merge and verifies the issue reads CLOSED.
notes:
== RESULT 2026-10-05 AUSEST (worker o16life) — PR #10936 (draft until marked ready; Fixes #10930)

Passages changed (docs only):
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md, section Retarget the producers. The Re-address bullet is qualified: a producer that can fire with no run awaiting it goes through a handler that reads the run. The Append and Forward bullets drop the unconditional per-machine dispatch. The child-actor bullet notes that the runtime stale-suppresses that completion itself. A new rule paragraph, "Deliver only to a live, awaiting run", sits before the rewritten worked example (producer, consumer, and a case walk). The :halt? mapping note gains the exception that a forwarded-to consumer keeps its terminal states without :final?.
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md section 2 (Awaited event-ids) and section 3 (both bullets and the closing paragraph) drop the unconditional recipe, including the Wave-0 row.
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/async-flow-to-machines.md (router leaf): one clause names the lifecycle rule.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md does not repeat the recipe and is unchanged.

The guard and the API it uses:
- At enqueue, the producer's plain reg-event body calls rf/subscribe-once [:rf/machine id] (spec/API.md calls it the one-shot read for handler bodies). It forwards only when the snapshot's :tags carry the consumer's awaiting tag, and stamps the forward with the run token from (:data snap).
- At delivery, the consumer decides. It keeps its terminal states without :final? (Spec 005 D7 footgun note), so a queued forward lands on a live snapshot and is an unhandled no-op. A :guards entry compares the run token in :data with the token the forward carries.
- Registrar membership is explicitly ruled out as a guard, and so is broadcast to every registered machine.

Supported-API limit: an authored dispatch to a singleton cannot be fenced at delivery. Spec 005 D5 births a fresh run on any event to a definition-bearing address with no snapshot. 005 L3410 says the runtime fences only its own carriers ("never the author's dispatch"). 002 L1924 says a plain handler's :dispatch joins the back of the queue. The closest supported shape is the documented one: consumer stays live, and the guard runs in the consumer. The existing child-actor route also qualifies. No new API was invented.

Five walks, executed on the JVM. A scratch namespace outside the tree evals the guide's own fenced code; the exit code was 0.
- OLD (unconditional forward, :final? consumers):
  - unstarted: both consumers are created.
  - completed: :app/boot restarts (kicks 2) and :wizard/setup is re-created.
  - two active: OK.
  - queued after halt: both are re-born.
  - superseded run: run 2 takes run 1's payload.
- Enqueue-time read alone (:final? consumers): queued after halt still re-births. This is the enqueue-versus-delivery distinction, executed.
- NEW: no consumer is created or restarted in any case. The public handler ran once and :theme/apply ran once in every case.
- Planted controls:
  - Removing the tag read: NEW unstarted creates both consumers.
  - Removing the :this-run? guard: NEW superseded case hands run 2 run 1's forward.
  - Both restores were verified by blob hash.

Gates, all exit 0:
- check_doc_slugs (sabotage red)
- check_skill_migration_cites and its self-test
- o1617 router drift and its self-test (sabotage red)
- contract drift and its self-test
- mkdocs build --strict
- the 43 other check_*.py scripts
- the 4 check-*.sh scripts (boundary and attribution run with origin/main)
- PR CI: 25 pass, 63 skipped, 0 fail
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #10936 (merged at c6728dd1de; GitHub #10930 reads CLOSED). The O-16 shared-completion forward is now lifecycle-aware.
- Enqueue time: the producer's plain reg-event body reads each consumer with rf/subscribe-once [:rf/machine id]. It forwards only when the snapshot's :tags carry the consumer's awaiting tag, and it stamps the forward with the run token from that snapshot's :data.
- Delivery time: the consumer decides. Its end states drop :final? (spec 005 D7's own advice), so a late forward lands on a live snapshot and is inert. A token guard refuses a forward from a superseded run.
- Why both checks: spec 002 L1924 queues a plain handler's :dispatch FIFO, so the run can halt before the forward is delivered.
- The original public handler's db write and effects still run exactly once. Registrar membership and an unconditional broadcast are both ruled out.
- Stated limit: the supported API cannot stop a queued, app-written dispatch from starting a singleton whose run has ended. Spec 005 D5 creates a fresh run before any app code at that address can check, and 005 L3410 says the runtime fences only its own carriers, never the author's dispatch. So the guide documents the closest supported shape and invents no API.
Sites changed: migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md (new "Deliver only to a live, awaiting run" rule, a rewritten worked example with a per-case walk, four producer bullets, and a :halt? exception); skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md (sections 2 and 3, including the Wave-0 contract row); skills/re-frame-migration/references/async-flow-to-machines.md (one clause). migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md did not repeat the recipe and was not touched.
Control: a scratch JVM namespace evaluated the guide's own code blocks, exit 0. OLD guide: the unstarted case created both consumers, the completed case restarted or re-created both, the after-halt case re-created both, and the superseded case took the predecessor's payload. NEW guide: nothing created or restarted, the two active consumers each got one forward with their own token, the after-halt forward was inert, and the superseded forward was refused. With the enqueue check alone and :final? kept, the after-halt case still re-created both. title: re-frame2-pair: give each tool behaviour one prose home, fix the surviving can't-reload claim, and slim first-contact guidance
description:
## Problem

The re-frame2-pair MCP server's tool **behaviour** is restated by hand across up to nine surfaces, and nothing checks any of those copies against what the server actually does: output shapes, defaults, redaction channels, freshness verdicts, hint advice.

The surfaces:
- the skill (`SKILL.md` and `references/`);
- `docs/skills/re-frame2-pair.md` and `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/capabilities.md`;
- the server's `README.md`, `003-Tool-Catalogue.md` (3,812 lines) and `DESIGN-RATIONALE.md`;
- the descriptors (`descriptors_data.cljs`) and the generated manifest;
- hint strings in server code;
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md`.

The existing gates pin **names** only. `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py` checks tool names, table rows and argument keys. `tool_contract_test` checks the `SKILL.md` contract string against a fingerprint of names plus argument keys. Both stay green while behaviour prose drifts.

## Evidence (2026-10-02..09)

- **4 of 5 behaviour fixes needed a second sweep commit:**
  - 9671842e28 (#10917 freshness), a773ff2241 (#10916 orient overflow) and ac883bc438 (#10921 reload) were followed by faf4f6f202, which fixed `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, the docs page, `DESIGN-RATIONALE.md` and a preload comment still carrying the old claims.
  - ed389393cf (#10985 dry-run effect args) was followed by b2254343ba, which found two more wrong facts no issue had reported (the wrong opt-in named for epoch effects; the server README claiming gate-off forces `elision false` back to true).
- **c9e120b2e7 (#10923):** the claim "Reagent/UIx apps always get `:evidence-tier-unavailable`" was false, and lived in 9 files.
- **`include-fx-args`** shipped 2026-06-12 (765f9d306d) and went undescribed for about four months, until #10985. The argument was already in the name-checked transport table, so the gate was green throughout.
- **The sweeps still missed one (verified at trunk 9e84689562):** `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md:17` says "**You can't reload a browser yourself — relay the `:hint` to the user.**" That is the exact claim #10921 asked to remove.
- **First-contact cost is growing.** `SKILL.md` grew 4,060 → 4,711 words (+16%) this week, and the always-read "Connect first" section grew 628 → 974 words (+55%). Part of that growth is a restated `:unknown-reason` list that the docs page also carries (~L131), along with orient's 20-example cap (~L11).

## Why it is structural

No layer owns a behaviour description, so every fix has to rediscover where the copies are. Behaviour claims can't be compared mechanically, so the remedy is fewer copies, not another gate.

## Direction (minimal)

1. Fix `references/errors.md:17`: reload is conditional on capability and ownership, per ac883bc438.
2. Make `docs/skills/re-frame2-pair.md` human-level plus a link: drop wire detail such as the `:unknown-reason` values and the orient cap number.

title: Image assembly exempts :rf.interceptor/* refs from the existence check, so a misspelt standard seals and fails at dispatch
description:
## Bug

Image assembly's missing-reference check skips every interceptor id in the `:rf.interceptor` namespace. So an inline image event that misspells the one framework standard, `[:rf.interceptor/ptha [:cart]]` for example, seals cleanly at `make-frame` and fails only when the event is first dispatched. An application interceptor with the same typo is refused at construction.

The people affected are authors of inline image events (stories and test doubles), who get the error late.

## Evidence

**Where (trunk 475bdcaacf):**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/image_assembly.cljc:1125-1133` (`application-interceptor-ref?`): returns false for any keyword whose namespace is `"rf.interceptor"`.
- `image_assembly.cljc:1182-1188`: the interceptor leg of `check-references!` filters references through that predicate.
- `image_assembly.cljc:1432-1438`: `check-references!` runs against the sealed resolver, which already merges the protected standards. So a published standard would pass the check anyway; the exemption only lets misspellings through.

The gap is narrow. A namespace `reg-event` resolves every reference against the registrar at registration (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:169-187`). A frame's own `:interceptors` resolve at `make-frame` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:460-474`). Only inline image events, whose existence check is deliberately left to `check-references!` (`events.cljc:1647-1670`), and explicit-pool assembly rely on the exempted check.

**Repro (*probed*):** JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/core`, plain-atom adapter. Run at HEAD 9b20bf0093, whose `implementation/core` is byte-identical to 475bdcaacf.

```clojure
(defn h [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :ran true)})
(rf/make-frame {:id :probe/typo
                :images [(rf/image {:id :test/typo
                                    :registrations {:reg-event [[:app/ev {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/ptha [:cart]]]} h]]}})]})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:app/ev] {:frame :probe/typo})
```

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| B1: misspelt standard `:rf.interceptor/ptha` | `make-frame` seals; the dispatch throws `:rf.error/unregistered-interceptor` |
| B2: control, misspelt app interceptor `:app/ptha` | `make-frame` throws `:rf.error/image-missing-reference` |
| B3: control, real `:rf.interceptor/path` | `make-frame` seals |

**Contract:** `spec/002-Frames.md:2579`: "Image values … validate refs during assembly of the resolved image generation". `spec/002-Frames.md:2645`: the generation "validates the refs at assembly". The same section says v2 keeps exactly one standard interceptor, `:rf.interceptor/path`.

## Expected

A reference to an interceptor id that the sealed generation does not provide fails assembly with `:rf.error/image-missing-reference`, whatever its namespace.

## Fix direction

- Delete the namespace exemption and check every authored reference against the sealed resolver.
- Keep factories unexecuted during sealing: this is a presence check only.
- An explicit-pool fixture that references a standard must then have that standard published, which better represents a runnable generation.

## Acceptance

- New test: B1's image fails at `make-frame` with `:rf.error/image-missing-reference`. It fails at trunk.
- B3, a published `:rf.interceptor/path`, still seals.
- `framework-standard-interceptor-reference-skipped` (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/image_assembly_cljs_test.cljc:88-94`), which pins the exemption, is rewritten to assert both of the above.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (sol/02 §7, read); reproduced by JVM probe at trunk.
- Related: rf2-mn2ht.18 also edits `image_assembly.cljc`. Sequence the two or give them to one worker.
- Hot zones: none.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-frames-registration.md` Insight 13 and A11(c); `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/02-core-registration-images.md` §7.

That worker is the only toucher of spec/002-Frames.md for now. Do not dispatch a second worker onto it until that worker reports.

Premise held at base 02018bf667: check-references! filtered interceptor refs through application-interceptor-ref?, which skipped every :rf.interceptor/* id, so [:rf.interceptor/ptha ...] sealed.

Knock-on: the test runtime fixture (test_support.cljc reset-runtime!) now re-seeds the :rf.interceptor/path standard beside :rf/set-db and :rf/install-frame-state, as init! does. Without it a sibling namespace whose fixture clears the standard registry left an explicit-pool assembly unable to resolve a path ref; the exemption had been masking that.

title: Resource subs re-validate and re-canonicalise unchanged params on every frame-state commit; memoise per payload
description:
## Bug

Every live resource subscription re-validates and re-canonicalises its params on every commit that changes the frame-state, even when its payload and the resource registration are unchanged. Typing one character into an unrelated form re-runs the EDN walk, the Malli `:params-schema` validation and canonicalisation once for every resource read on screen.

## Evidence

Code at 475bdcaacf:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:463-534`: all `:rf.resource/*` and `:rf/resource` subs are `reg-frame-state-sub`. Their single input is the whole frame-state, so any app-db commit is a changed input.
- `subs.cljc:82-119` (`resolve-scoped-key`) runs on every recompute. It looks up the spec, resolves the scope, and calls `registry/validate+canonicalize-params`. The code's own comment says so: "a resource sub re-runs this on every frame-state change" (`:116-118`).
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/params.cljc:65-85`: that pipeline runs `reject-non-edn!` (a full EDN walk), the late-bound Malli validator when the schemas artefact is loaded, then `canonicalize`.

Repro (*probed*: JVM, plain-atom substrate, schemas artefact loaded, run at 989a1c6d53, whose core and resources trees are identical to 475bdcaacf). The probe holds three subs on one unchanged payload, wraps `re-frame.resources.params/validate+canonicalize` in a counter, and dispatches ten keystroke events that write only `:form/text` in app-db:

```clojure
(def q {:resource :probe/article :scope :rf.scope/global :params {:slug "w"}})
(def subs* [(rf/subscribe [:rf/resource q]) (rf/subscribe [:rf.resource/stale? q])
            (rf/subscribe [:rf.resource/data q])])
(dotimes [i 10] (rf/dispatch-sync [:probe/keystroke (str "text-" i)]) (run! deref subs*))
```

Observed:

```
malli validator late-bound? true
held resource subs: 3  unrelated app-db commits: 10  params validate+canonicalize calls during them: 30
```

Contract:
- No spec clause requires per-commit re-validation.
- Per-commit scope re-resolution is required, because spec 016's `{:from-db}` re-keying contract (`spec/016-Resources.md:226-235`) says a sub must follow a principal change. The fix keeps that.
- No latency was measured. This is repeated work on the hottest read path, not a measured slowdown.

## Expected

An unrelated commit runs no params validation for a resource sub whose payload and registration are unchanged. Scope re-resolution still runs on every pass.

## Fix direction

- Memoise validate-plus-canonicalise per (params payload, params presence, resource spec identity). Re-registering the resource, which changes the spec identity, invalidates the entry.
- Keep scope resolution per pass.
- Keep the memo small and owned: one slot per live sub, or a bounded cache. A process-global, never-evicted map is the leak rf2-3x7nj.10.2 fixed for the items merge memo.
- Do not move validation to `ensure` alone. An invalid passive read must still raise `:rf.error/resource-invalid-params` the first time it is read, rather than sitting `:idle` silently.

## Acceptance

- New JVM counting test, failing before the fix (it reads 30 today):
  1. Hold three resource subs on one payload.
  2. Dispatch ten events that change only an unrelated app-db key, dereferencing after each.
  3. Assert zero `validate+canonicalize` calls.
- Re-registering the resource, or changing the payload, triggers exactly one validation per sub.
- An invalid payload still throws `:rf.error/resource-invalid-params` on first read.
- `sub-re-keys-on-mid-session-account-switch` (`resources_from_db_scope_cljs_test.cljc:173`) stays green.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (resources decision 12). Sol 15 supplied the "memoise, don't move to ensure" correction.
- Prior art: rf2-3x7nj.10 ("Considered and rejected") called the re-validation deliberate, but the deliberate part is the `{:from-db}` re-keying, which this fix keeps.
- Hot zones: none.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/resources.md` decision 12 and action 2.
notes:

Premise verified at tip 72c951f102 with the bead's own repro: JVM, plain-atom substrate, schemas loaded, 3 subs ([:rf/resource] / [:rf.resource/stale?] / [:rf.resource/data]) held on one payload, 10 keystroke events writing only :form/text, every sub deref'd after each. validate+canonicalize calls: 30. The bead's count holds.

MEASUREMENT, JVM, warm, per unrelated app-db commit with every sub deref'd. "Memoised" means params/validate+canonicalize was replaced by a perfect per-payload memo, so the difference is the most any memo could save. The subs alternate between a one-key schema [:map [:slug :string]] and a four-key nested schema. Each figure is the median of 4 interleaved runs of 1000 commits:
- 10 resource subs: 630 us per commit as shipped, 387 us memoised; validation is 38.5%, about 24 us per sub per commit.
- 30 resource subs: 1061 us shipped, 709 us memoised; 33.1%, about 11.7 us per sub per commit.
- 60 resource subs: 2143 us shipped, 1372 us memoised; 36.0%, about 12.9 us per sub per commit.
- No resource subs: the per-commit baseline is about 135-165 us. Run-to-run noise is about +/-30 us.
Microbenchmarks, ns per call, warm: validate+canonicalize-params took about 6.3 us on the one-key schema and about 20 us on the four-key one. And the only memo the brief allows, one slot per live sub owned and released with the sub, cannot be built from resources:
- a reg-frame-state-sub body is one handler fn shared by every instance;
- the only per-instance state in the sub machinery is the memo cell that core's re-frame.subs.memo/make-layer-1-memoised-body closes over (last input, last result), and nothing in it is exposed to the body;
- the other route, memoising through the signal graph, would re-register all 19 resource subs as parametric layer-2 subs over two new internal subs (a frame-state identity sub and a per-payload params sub). That changes every resource sub's input kind as tooling sees it, adds two framework sub ids, and still needs a re-registration signal.
If Mike wants the third back, the clean place is a core facility, a per-instance cell offered to single-source sub bodies. That is a core change (implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc), not a resources one.
No code, test or spec changed for this bead. The scope re-resolution per pass, which the {:from-db} re-keying contract requires, is untouched.

title: Xray width reset in a narrow viewport persists an override instead of restoring host CSS
description: Merged-PR audit #10981, correctness lens. The new canonical width contract says resetting removes the html override and returns to the host stylesheet. Source inspection of both merge 4ba53943ca and current origin/main shows a reachable exception: :rf.xray/reset-panel-width dispatches :rf.xray/set-panel-width-px with default 560; that handler clamps before persistence. At a 600px viewport, clamp-panel-width-px yields 540, stores 540, and apply-panel-width! writes --rf-xray-inline-width:540px because it compares the clamped number with default 560. The baseline is therefore still masked after reset, and the stored override survives a later wider viewport. The direct effect calls also disagree: numeric default 560 at viewport 600 writes 540px, while nil at viewport 600 clears, since the nonnumeric clamp path returns 560. Existing default-clear DOM tests run only against the ambient roomy viewport. This is a source-derived reproduction; no local shadow-cljs run is claimed. Proposed action: make the existing reset event restore the documented baseline consistently without manufacturing a persisted numeric override, while retaining the clamp for an actual user-resized width. Add a focused 600px reset/default regression through the real handler/effect and a wide-viewport control; keep the one CSS property and existing public API.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor, 2026-10-11 12:44 AUSEST): DISPATCHED ==
Dispatched with its sibling (rf2-ogkk7 + rf2-eflcr) to worktree xray-fixes: one worker, two PRs (worker/xray-fixes for rf2-ogkk7 first, then worker/xray-cascade for rf2-eflcr). It owns the tools/xray files these two fixes need. Build-lane windows are granted by the mayor on request. Do not dispatch it again.
== RESULT (worker xray-fixes, 2026-10-11 13:10 AUSEST): PR #11132, branch worker/xray-fixes, 2 commits (test first, then fix) ==
FIX. settings/effects.cljs apply-panel-width! decides clear-vs-write on the INPUT: the default 560 (or nil) clears the <html> override at every viewport, and a stored default is never rewritten to its clamp. A real user width still clamps, writes and repairs storage. registry.cljs :rf.xray/reset-panel-width no longer re-dispatches set-panel-width-px. It writes a nil override (nil reads as absent in storage and in the merge), sets the live width to the inherited one (the configure! seed width, else the default), applies that through apply-panel-width!, and puts the resulting live value in the db slot. No new API, event or CSS property.
FAILING-FIRST, narrowed shadow builds in one granted lane window. Pre-fix source: browser (resize-handle.*-dom-cljs-test$) exit 1, 3 failures in 7 tests / 27 assertions; node exit 1, 1 failure in 31 / 50. HEAD (blob hashes verified): both exit 0 at the same counts. At 600px the pre-fix reset gave [drag "480px", after reset "540px", stored true]. At 1600px it gave ["480px" "" true]: the html clear is the wide control, but the old reset ALSO persisted 560 at wide viewports, a numeric override that outranks a later host configure! width. Direct apply-panel-width! with 560 at a 600px viewport wrote "540px" pre-fix. The node row (configure! 640, drag 720, reset) gave [560 true] pre-fix and [640 false] fixed.
CLAIMS. Every description claim held at source or by measurement. The survives-a-wider-viewport claim follows from the stored width and was not separately measured. tools/xray/spec states the reset behaviour correctly, so it is unedited. clj-kondo exit 0 with 0 findings. No .cljc touched, so no JVM lane. The final-base gate is the PR's CI.

Resetting Xray's panel width now restores the host stylesheet baseline at any viewport: the reset no longer routes the default 560 through the clamp-then-persist path, so a narrow viewport no longer stores a clamped 540 or writes --rf-xray-inline-width; the clamp still applies to a real user-resized width. Same CSS property, same public API. Changes in tools/xray: registry.cljs, settings/effects.cljs, and the resize_handle tests (a focused 600px reset/default regression through the real handler and effect, plus a wide-viewport control). Failing-first, narrowed lane window: pre-fix source went red (browser exit 1, 3 failures in 7 tests/27 assertions; node exit 1, 1 failure in 31/50); HEAD green (browser 0, node 0, same counts). title: K2: take the next bulk ensemble against Fresco's 1.5x architecture kill, in a quiet-box window
description:
OWNER OF EP-0038's K2 ERRATA ROW: the 1.5x bulk architecture kill. Filed by rf2-ouf09 (merged-PR audit #10968), which found the row unowned and docs/design/fresco/validation.md pointing at rf2-8a746, a bead gc'd from the live tracker on 2026-09-02 (present by identity at checkpoint 5365011d5a, absent at 42ea359b1e "gc - decay 851 closed issues"). The protocol below is recovered from that record and carried here inline so nobody needs the history.

WHAT K2 IS. validation.md, Kill criteria table, verbatim: "K2 | Bulk (>= ~100 boundaries, one commit) > 1.5x Reagent view work after those iterations". The P2 graduation ruling (HD-029, 2026-08-13) left it NOT WAIVED; validation.md "The kill table at graduation" says a later red result bites exactly as registered. EP-0038's 2026-10-06 ruling (d) carries it as the errata row "K2 under its own protocol".

THE PROTOCOL. Source: rf2-8a746's comment "DELEGATED DECISION ... WHAT ADJUDICATES BULK ROWS" (2026-08-07, operator-overturnable), parts 1-4. Implemented by commit 8a2bd66cc9 (the run-preserving effect-size interval), commit 5e1d0b936f (the check standard's out-of-sample limits, rf2-c1974) and commit 44581c63dc (complete evidence before pooling, PR #7738). Amended once, by commit ea8414eddf (rf2-vp0j7 and rf2-vh0e3, 2026-08-08): the bulk bar gates only the pair it names, and the cross-run band is no longer a veto. That amendment left the gated verdict byte-identical on both ensembles. All of it now lives in bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/.
- SCENARIO. The clock lane's bulk rows in clock_app.cljs: bulk300 ({:kind :bulk :k 300}, one frame/replace-app-db! changing all 300 of the 300 mounted boundaries) and bulk100 ({:kind :bulk :k 100}). These are K2's ">= ~100 boundaries, one commit". narrow ({:kind :bulk :k 1}) shares the bulk class and its rule but is not K2's scenario.
- INSTRUMENT. clock_run.cjs: playwright Chromium, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false. It reads Chromium's renderer counters over CDP (Performance.getMetrics) on either side of one operation. The operation resolves only after the frame it causes, so raw TaskDuration is the clock of record. Canonical design: 6 rounds x (4 warmup + 10 samples), tare on, 3 segments, no narrowing knob (no --no-build, no HCLOCK_ONLY). A narrowed run writes canonical:false, and the readjudicator's first gate refuses it.
- RUN CONTROL (ruling part 3). This is the level-denominated check standard clock_check_standard.json, id fresco-clock/ctl-2x-level v4. Its bulk class has centre 1.7207. A run is in control when its 18-block median lies inside the frozen location limits and its robust scale is at or under the frozen dispersion limit. It was calibrated at Chromium 147.0.7727.15. Its recalibrateOn list includes any Chromium change, any change to the harness, door, tare, settle or counts, any floor-page change, and any change of published clock. Any of those requires a FRESH baseline before the standard may judge new runs.
- VERDICT (ruling part 4). This is PUBLICATION.bulk in clock_readjudicate.cjs. Only the pair fresco / reagent-subs is gated. The estimand is the paired same-round LEVEL ratio at fixed witness and fixed K, taken as paired log-ratios with a hierarchical percentile bootstrap that resamples outer runs before inner rounds (Kalibera & Jones 2013). A row publishes ONLY when its WHOLE 95% interval lies below 1.0 (the bar: a magnitude publishes) or wholly above 1.5 (ARCHITECTURE-KILL). Anything else is INSTRUMENT-LIMITED and publishes no magnitude. Part 4 also required the effect to clear the same-run noise band; under the 2026-08-08 amendment that band is printed as a diagnostic and decides nothing (crossRunBandVeto: false).
- HARD REFUSALS, which the ruling left unchanged: read-back, canonical-DOM, page-error, arm-order, quiet-box and band-ceiling (35%).

WHERE K2 STANDS. Re-adjudicated by rf2-ouf09 at trunk 591b6d306d, running node clock_readjudicate.cjs over the restored clock-emvod run1-8 and clock-w3yxd run1-6 corpus (exit 0). For fresco / reagent-subs:
- bulk300: point 1.0051x, 95% CI [0.9724 - 1.0425].
- bulk100: point 1.0292x, 95% CI [0.9940 - 1.0643].
Each is over 12 reportable runs x 6 rounds, and both read INSTRUMENT-LIMITED. Neither interval reaches the 1.5 line, so the kill has not fired on the retained evidence, and the 1.0 bar is unresolved. The decision brief's scoreboard says the same thing: "all gated intervals straddle 1.0".

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES. Take ONE canonical clock_run.cjs ensemble on the then-current trunk, in a granted window, and adjudicate it with clock_readjudicate.cjs under the rule above. Record the bulk300 and bulk100 verdicts on this bead. If either publishes, also record it in validation.md's kill-table K2 bullet. No threshold moves, no row is added, and no ruling reopens.

BLOCKED ON a concrete prerequisite rather than a bead: an EXCLUSIVE quiet-box window that the mayor or Mike grants. Quiet-box is a hard refusal. The retained ensembles were taken with \System\Processor Queue Length 0 before and after, and with no other worker dispatched. The window also needs the shadow-cljs build lane for its duration, because a canonical run builds. Each run takes about 6-7 minutes; the 8-run clock-emvod ensemble took 51 minutes on 2026-08-07. NOT blocked on a published artefact: the bench builds from source, so rf2-kmqx3 is not a prerequisite.

BEFORE THE WINDOW OPENS:
1. Write the run count on this bead. The retained ensembles were 8 runs and 6.
2. Restore the corpus with node bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/data_archive.cjs --restore, and confirm the readjudicator reproduces the standing above.

title: INCOMPLETE reserved-content contract: Fresco native props accept children and raw HTML
description:
At PR #10400 (edcf24321890811f06b43d8ddd20f6ab5e633334), spec/004B:475-476 says both emitters refuse children and dangerouslySetInnerHTML in an attribute map. SSR now does, but the Fresco native path does not enforce that contract: codec.cljs native-element:1392-1402 passes the map to convert-props; convert-entry:393-423 writes both canonical names; reserved-name?:69-81 guards only __proto__, prototype and constructor. With no positional children, make-element:1368-1372 forwards those props directly to React createElement. Thus content can enter through props instead of the structural child/trusted-markup grammar, and a void tag can fail only at the React render boundary.

Required correction: enforce the documented reserved-content refusal on the native attribute path using canonical-slot and an existing appropriate structured-error convention. Keep legitimate boundary/component and raw React escape-hatch contracts distinct, and preserve React-space key/ref routing. Add a direct Fresco regression demonstrating the bypass before the fix and refused children/raw-HTML props after, with ordinary attrs and legitimate child/trusted-markup controls. This audit establishes the source path; a Fresco runtime probe was not run, and the implementation task already requires that proof before changing behavior.

The corresponding implementation is already in rf2-wt2wy, currently in_progress. This separate OPEN finding tracks the exact correction under the audit policy; coordinate that implementation, do not duplicate edits. Existing status/closure fields remain unchanged.
close_reason:
RULED, NO CODE CHANGE (mayor, 2026-09-25). This finding asked Fresco's native attribute path to refuse :children and dangerouslySetInnerHTML because spec/004B:475 says both emitters do. Worker rkeytail-wt2wy verified the premise by running it (PR #10404): Fresco passes both through, and that pass-through is a documented, CI-tested use.

RULING on item 2 (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance): Fresco keeps passing React's content props through. NO Fresco code change.
- Fresco's native attribute map is a React props map, and React owns its content slots. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is Fresco's one trusted-markup door: skills/reagent-migration MIG-34 prescribes it as the migration of r/unsafe-html, the codemod flags those sites, and CI's MIG-23 SSR cold-start node test (mig34-preserve-working-unsafe-html) renders it. `v/html`, which spec/004B names as the one trusted-markup spelling, exists nowhere under implementation/. Refusing the prop would leave Fresco with NO way to render trusted markup, which is a lost capability rather than hardening. Trust the programmer: the prop's own name is the warning.
- `:children` on a native tag is likewise left to React, whose own semantics apply (a void element throws in React).
- The SPEC is what is wrong here. 004B and 011 must state the split the code already has:
  - the UI-tree tier (re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree) refuses `:children`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and every spelling that canonicalises onto them, and its trusted-markup spelling is the `:html` node variant;
  - Fresco's React emitter passes React props, content props included, through to React, and its trusted-markup spelling is React's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
  That prose goes to rf2-kgtn0, which already carries "v/html ... make each row describe what the shipped code does".

So the correction this finding asked for is not made in Fresco. The contradiction it found is real and is corrected in the spec under rf2-kgtn0.

- What: the editing flag every cell reads is a single global value that changes on every click-to-edit and again on every commit, so all 2,600 components re-run on both transitions — and the commit is exactly the moment the cell map changes, so the per-cell `=`-dedup on `:cells/value` cannot prevent a single render on the propagation path the example exists to demonstrate.
- Evidence: traced end to end. Click -> `:cells/start-editing` -> `[:cells :editing-id]` nil -> "A1" -> `:cells/editing-id` yields a new value -> every mounted `cell-view` deref'd it -> all 2,600 re-render. Enter/blur -> `:cells/commit` (:364-379) sets editing-id back to nil AND replaces the cell map in the same `:db` -> all 2,600 re-render again whether or not their `:cells/value` moved. Contrast todomvc, which does this right: examples/core/todomvc/subs.cljs:71-74 `:todo.ui/editing?` is parameterised by id so a row re-renders only when ITS flag flips, and views.cljs:68 derefs that. Control: `:cells/value` really is per-id and `=`-deduped (subs.cljc:274-331), so the claim is true of the value sub in isolation; the defeat is the sibling deref in the same component. (Reagent re-runs a component when any reaction it deref'd changes value; a render-count probe on `cell-view` would show 2,600 per click, and 2,600 per commit rather than "cells whose value changed".)
- Action: add `(rf/reg-sub :cells/editing? {:inputs [[:cells/editing-id]]} (fn [[eid] [_ id]] (= eid id)))` and deref `[:cells/editing? id]` in `cell-view` — the todomvc shape, one sub and one line. The README and docs sentences then become true as written; M only because the worker should re-read seven_guis/README.md:31 and docs/core/subscriptions.md:234-237 afterwards and confirm no wording needs to move.

### 2. Flight Booker registers the unqualified fx id `:notify` — the one example that breaks the "prefix every registered id" convention, and it is the custom-fx exemplar spec/Construction-Prompts.md points at  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: examples/core/seven_guis/flight_booker/core.cljs:100 (`rf/reg-fx :notify`), :90 (`[:notify {...}]`); examples/TESTING.md:69-74 (the convention: "each example prefixes every id with its own stem"); spec/Construction-Prompts.md:1430 (cites Flight Booker as the CP-3 "custom `:notify` fx" exemplar); implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:120-124 (reg-fx's own docstring example is `:my/notify`).
- What: a bare, generic fx id in the shared `:node-test` registry — the exact collision shape TESTING.md exists to prevent — taught by the example a reader is sent to for "how to register an fx".
- Evidence: Grep `reg-fx :[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\s` over examples/ -> 1 hit (this one). Control: the namespaced form `reg-fx :[a-z][a-z0-9.-]*/` -> 18 hits across 15 files, so every other example fx is stem-prefixed. No live collision today (`reg-fx :notify` -> 1 file tree-wide), so this is teaching cost only.
- Action: rename to `:flight/notify` (two lines) and update the mention at spec/Construction-Prompts.md:1430. S.

### 3. Temperature: a non-numeric entry blanks the other field; the 7GUIs task says the other field is left unchanged  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: examples/core/seven_guis/temperature/core.cljs:88-105 (both edit handlers store `(parse-num raw)`, nil on junk, as the canonical value), :136-156 (the `-text` subs render `(when c ...)` for the passive field), :174 and :179 (`(or c-text "")`).
- What: typing "12x" into the C box sets `:celsius nil` and the F box goes blank; the published task reads "When the user enters a non-numerical string into TC the value in TF is not updated and vice versa" — F should keep showing its last value.
- Evidence: traced: `[:temp/edit-celsius "12x"]` -> `{:celsius nil :input-source :celsius :typing "12x"}` -> `:temp/fahrenheit-text` -> `(when nil ...)` -> nil -> view renders "". (The task also starts both fields empty where the example seeds 0 C; harmless, noted only.)
- Action: keep the last canonical value on a failed parse — in each edit handler `:celsius (if-some [n (parse-num raw)] <n / converted n> (get-in db [:temp :celsius]))`. The passive field then holds its last conversion, which is the task's rule; schema unchanged. S.

### 4. TodoMVC: the header input commits on blur (a todo appears when you tab or click away) and is not autofocused on load; both depart from the TodoMVC app-spec the README says it follows  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: examples/core/todomvc/views.cljs:59 (`:on-blur (fn [_] (on-commit))`, unconditional inside the shared `todo-input`), :103-112 (`task-entry` passes `:on-commit #(dispatch [:todo.ui/commit-new])` and no `:autofocus?`); README.md:3 ("follows the current TodoMVC app spec"), :22.
- What: (a) type "buy milk" in the new-todo box and click the "Active" filter link — a todo is created by the blur, where the spec's New-todo section says Enter creates; (b) that section also asks for the new-todo input to be focused on page load (`autofocus`), which the example gives only to the edit box.
- Evidence: traced: blur -> `on-commit` -> `:todo.ui/commit-new` (events.cljs:150-157) -> `[:todo/add title]`; nothing distinguishes the header from the edit box. The edit box's blur-commit IS spec ("When the edit input is blurred, the changes are saved"), and the `id` guard in `:todo.ui/commit-edit` (events.cljs:169) correctly makes the post-Escape/Enter unmount blur a no-op — so only the header is off. Inherited from the v1 example, whose `todo-input` also saves on blur, which is why it reads as intended. Everything else the spec names is right: filters as routes, toggle-all inversion, clear-completed hidden at zero, Escape discards, blank save deletes, `todos-reframe2` key (all pinned by implementation/core/test/re_frame/todomvc_cljs_test.cljs).
- Action: give `todo-input` a `:commit-on-blur?` prop (default true) and pass `false` from `task-entry`; add `:autofocus? true` to the header input (the ref already exists). About four lines. S.

### 5. Timer: `:tick-active?` is written `true` twice and never `false`, so the schema field documented as "is a tick chain currently running?" is dead state a copier will trust  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: examples/core/seven_guis/timer/core.cljs:67 (schema row and its comment), :121 and :204 (the only writes, both `true`), :159 and :179 (the reads).
- What: after the chain finishes (`done?` at :152) the flag still reads `true`, and the real "has it stopped?" predicate is `was-stopped? (>= elapsed-ms duration-ms)` at :176 — two answers to one question, one of them wrong, in the example whose lesson is the generation token.
- Evidence: Grep `tick-active\?` in the file -> 7 hits: 1 schema row, 2 writes (both `true`), 2 destructures, 2 reads; control: `tick-gen` in the same file is written with `inc` at :180 and :201, so the grep does see writes. Neither the docstring's rules (:20-25) nor the README's timer row names a stop/pause path. The timer's actual semantics are right and match the task: retarget below elapsed stops with the bar full, retarget above elapsed re-arms under a bumped generation, Reset re-anchors and retires in-flight ticks (traced for the drag-down-then-up-inside-one-tick race: one chain survives).
- Action: delete the field (schema row, the two seeds, the two `and`s): `rearm?` becomes `(and was-stopped? (> ms elapsed-ms))`, the tick guard becomes `(not done?)`. S.

### 6. Circle Drawer: a left-click inside an existing circle drops a new circle; the task creates one only in an empty area  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: examples/core/seven_guis/circle_drawer/core.cljs:268-280 (`:on-click` on the `<svg>` dispatches `:drawer/add-circle` for every click; the `:circle`s carry `:fill "transparent"`, which is hit-testable under SVG's default `pointer-events: visiblePainted`, so a click on a circle's interior bubbles to the svg), docstring :4-6.
- What: clicking a circle to look at it stacks a fresh circle on top of it; the published task says "Left-clicking inside an empty area inside the canvas will create an unfilled circle" (and greys the nearest circle under the pointer, which the example drops without saying so).
- Evidence: read; the transparent fill is what makes right-click-on-the-interior open the dialog (:278-280), so it is deliberate and the left-click consequence is its side effect. The engine is right: one undo step per add, a whole drag collapsing to one step, undo/redo round-trip, redo cleared by a new action, `:next-id` outside the snapshot, and the no-change guard are all pinned green by implementation/core/test/re_frame/circle_drawer_undo_cljs_test.cljs, and the interceptor is byte-for-byte the one docs/core/interceptors.md:318-333 teaches.
- Action: keep the handler pure and make `:drawer/add-circle` a no-op when the point lies inside any existing circle (`(some (fn [{:keys [x y radius]}] (<= (js/Math.hypot (- cx x) (- cy y)) radius)) circles)`), and add one docstring line saying hover-select and the popup menu are elided. S.

### 7. TodoMVC README and the boot how-to send the reader to core.cljs for a URL-change listener that is not there  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: readme-drift] [size: S]
- Where: examples/core/todomvc/README.md:14 ("`core.cljs` — entry point, frame setup (with the hash `:url-strategy`), and the URL-change listener"); docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:283-284 ("adds URL routing, a `hashchange` listener, and `:url-bound? true`"); examples/core/todomvc/core.cljs:67-82 (the comment: "Wiring up the URL-change listener is NOT a separate step").
- What: both pages describe the file as containing listener code; it contains none — `:url-bound? true` plus the hash `:url-strategy` on the `frame-root` (core.cljs:59-63) makes the frame install it — and the file's own comment says exactly that.
- Evidence: Grep `hashchange|addEventListener|popstate` over examples/core/todomvc -> 4 hits in core.cljs, every one inside a comment (:56, :75, :76, :81), plus README.md:23 prose; control: `"hashchange"` as a string literal in implementation/routing/src -> 2 hits in routing/strategy.cljc, the real installer.
- Action: README.md:14 -> "entry point and frame setup (hash `:url-strategy` + `:url-bound?`, which is what installs the URL listener)"; how-to:284 -> "adds URL routing via `:url-bound? true` and a hash `:url-strategy` (the frame installs the `hashchange` listener)". S.

## Per-example census
examples/temperature (examples/core/seven_guis/temperature): 1 finding above (#3); README MATCHES; roster: listed
examples/flight-booker (examples/core/seven_guis/flight_booker): 1 finding above (#2); README MATCHES; roster: listed

> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every

## Worker rules

- Every path:line below was read at the FROZEN review tree named in the report header. Re-verify each cite at the current trunk before editing; the review wave's earlier beads found premises that had moved.
- Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing.
- Fences are full repo-relative paths. Hot-zone files (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) are sequential; if a finding lands in one, say so and wait for the mayor's sequencing.

DO NOT START until child .1 records a PROCEED verdict.

ONE WORKER, ONE BRANCH, ONE PR. This is not negotiable and the epic says why: the change
touches nearly every sequential-never-parallel hot-zone file in CLAUDE.md at once, including
the api-manifest trio and the report-changed-surfaces.sh / _changed-surfaces.test.cjs mirror
pair that must move in a single commit. Split across two PRs, the tree does not build.
Before starting, check no worker worktrees are in flight; this is the largest conflict
generator the repo can produce.

== WHAT TO RENAME ==

Hicasso -> Fresco, everywhere, in all four case forms, across tracked files EXCLUDING
.beads/. Per the epic:
  hicasso 24,312 / Hicasso 2,995 / HICASSO 391 / hicasso_ 174, plus 741 PATHS.
A lowercase-only sweep leaves 3,386 occurrences standing. Re-measure first; do not trust
these figures, they are a 2026-09-09 snapshot.

                                 — the epic explains why this differs from ui/freehand)
  ALIAS `h` DOES NOT CHANGE. Every `h/defview`, `h/sub`, `:as h` stays exactly as it is.

USE `git mv` FOR PATHS so history follows the files.

The epic lists these; treat that list as the checklist, not as background. In particular:
  * shadow-cljs build ids (9 of them) — verify with
    `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list`, which reads its roster
    out of implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. The count must not drop.
  * npm scripts in implementation/package.json — several name hicasso in the SCRIPT FILENAME
    as well as the key, so the file rename and the script text move together.
  * 9 files under .github/ (six workflows + three scripts).
  * ~45 files under scripts/ and implementation/scripts/, including check_provenance_pins.py
    (docs.yml validates docs/design/hicasso/ BY PATH — that path is moving) and
    require-alias-baseline.edn.
  * implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2-hicasso — an exports
    directory whose NAME is the coordinate.
  * scripts/_test_fixtures/ holds hicasso-named fixtures for check_doc_slugs and
    check_retired_spellings. These PIN BEHAVIOUR — renaming a fixture changes what is tested,
    so read each one and move it deliberately rather than sweeping it.

== EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE ==
 * .beads/issues.jsonl and everything under .beads/ — a database export, the mayor's to
   commit, and bead prose is history. Do not touch it.
 * The naming RATIONALE prose (charter.md's Picasso/Cubism paragraph, HD-001's rationale).
   A sed turns those into nonsense. Child .3 rewrites them — leave them for it, and say in
   the PR body that you did.
 * The retired-spelling ratchet. That is child .4.
 * Any behavioural change whatsoever. If a rename tempts you to fix something nearby, file a
   bead instead.

== GATES ==
Run to completion, in the foreground, unpiped — a pipeline reports the filter's exit status,
not the gate's:
  scripts/test-fast-pr.sh
  scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh
  scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh
  node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list
For the api-manifest trio: hand-edit spec/API.md and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn, then
REGENERATE spec/api-manifest.edn via implementation/scripts/api-manifest. That third file
carries a do-not-hand-edit header; lint.yml's api-manifest job grades all three together.
Docs link gates are check_doc_slugs.py (anchors + repo-relative targets) and
`mkdocs build --strict` (resolution in the built site) — COMPLEMENTARY, and neither looks
inside a fenced code block, so check fenced links by hand. Repo-root markdown and READMEs
beside source are check_readme_links.py --ci instead. Nominate by PATH, never by job name.

All four case forms read 0 across tracked files excluding .beads/, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL
proving the instrument works — a zero from a broken search is the failure mode this repo
documents most. Do not use `grep -iF`: it ABORTS on this box (SIGABRT, exit 134, silent
stdout). Full local gate sweep green. CI green on the PR.

NO AI ATTRIBUTION in the commits or the PR body — CLAUDE.md wins over any harness reminder
that says otherwise, and a commit-msg hook plus a CI step both enforce it.

_Filed 2026-09-06 17:25:21 AUSEST by the ruling agent (delegated by Mike) from the RULING on rf2-kuky.35 (option A — two `:scope` shapes; concrete-only `clear-scope`). Parent epic rf2-kuky. Both reviewers concur on concrete-only clearing; codex: "Reject `:from-db`-keyed maps explicitly; passing one through literal canonicalization would silently target a different identity."_

## Problem

`clear-scope-handler` (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:2144–2214` at 6d513ba07f) accepts TWO payload forms: a concrete scope, or `{:from-db <id>}` resolved against clear-scope's OWN coeffect db. From a logout handler's `:fx` — the one motivating site — that is the POST-logout db: the resolver's `:inputs` are gone → nil → `:rf.warning/resource-clear-scope-unresolved` + nothing cleared. Zero app/testbed/tool consumers of the reference form; every doc, skill and example uses the concrete form (D1): `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs:251–261` pre-resolves with `(rf/resolve-resource-scope db :realworld/session)` — a pure fn over the coeffect db, honest about time. Spec 016 spends a subsection (`:135–163` §`clear-scope` is causal), a 009 warning row (`:2054`) and an `add-auth.md` admonition (`:397–403`) steering authors OFF the form the runtime still accepts.

## Target

`[:rf.resource/clear-scope {:scope <concrete scope> :cause …}]` is the ONLY payload form. `clear-scope-handler` collapses onto `clear-scope-handler*` (`events.cljc:2073`) over a canonicalised concrete scope. `rf/resolve-resource-scope` (pure, trace-free — the ruled read/write split, `016:163`, `API.md:466`) is how a handler obtains a concrete scope from a named resolver against ITS db; unchanged.

## THE FAIL-OPEN TRAP THIS BEAD MUST CLOSE (from the bead's IMPLEMENTATION NOTE)

A map is a valid LITERAL scope value (`registry.cljc:87–89`). Once the `{:from-db …}` arm is deleted, a `{:from-db :x}` payload reaching `clear-scope` would canonicalise as a literal map scope, key nothing, and no-op silently — the exact fail-open `events.cljc:2182–2184` was written to prevent. Required: extend the `state.cljc:456–531` policy-vs-value guard (`canonicalize-scope`, which already refuses a policy keyword at a concrete boundary) to refuse a `:from-db`-keyed map at a concrete boundary with a LOUD error — reuse that guard's existing error shape/id (do not mint a new warning id; if a new error id is unavoidable, add its `009` row — hot-zone). The rejection happens BEFORE any cache state changes. Pin it with the replacement test (below). This refusal also serves the route-entry and payload override sites once (iii)/(iv) land — keep it in the shared guard, not in `clear-scope` alone.

## Keep — do not touch

- `resolve-scope-input` (`scope_registry.cljc:650`) STAYS: `:rf.resource/invalidate-tags` and `:rf.mutation/execute` keep their `{:from-db}` arms — they resolve against the SAME event's db (the right world).
- The pure/traced split between `resolve-resource-scope` and the causal `resolve-scope*`.
- The D1 leak-boundary tests (`resources_scope_leak_boundary_cljs_test.cljc:145,159`) must pass unchanged.
- rf2-kuky.34's surface (`reg-resource-scope` arity, `016` §Named resolvers `:165–239`) — not this bead's.

## Deletions (re-measure: `git grep -n resource-clear-scope-unresolved -- ':!.beads'` = 20 lines / 11 files at a36952cfce)

- The `{:from-db …}` arm in `clear-scope-handler` + its nil-resolution branch.
- `:rf.warning/resource-clear-scope-unresolved`: `late_bind/directory.cljc` (1), `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` (1), `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc` (1), `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj` (4 lines naming the warning), `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2054` row, `016` prose, docs (below), any `tools/` catalogue entry, any core error-catalogue conformance test (grep `implementation/core/test` for the id).
- Manifest: n/a (no var).

## Tests

- `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_from_db_scope_cljs_test.cljc:272–333`: the `record-clear-scope-warnings!` recorder and the two deftests `clear-scope-from-db-resolves-and-clears-the-resolved-scope` and `clear-scope-from-db-nil-warns-and-clears-nothing` (NOTE — codex's correction to the dossier: the SECOND test dispatches `[:t/logout]` first and then clears with `{:from-db}` after logout, demonstrating the form failing at its one motivating site) → replace with ONE deftest asserting a `{:from-db …}` clear-scope payload is REJECTED loud (error surfaced through the frame's error path, not a warning) and clears NOTHING (jake's entry untouched, `entries` unchanged).
- Codex acceptance, cite the existing tests that prove it in the PR body: logout / account-switch clears the departing scope, leaves the replacement and global scopes intact, and suppresses late replies (`resources_scope_leak_boundary_cljs_test.cljc` + the RealWorld logout idiom).

title: api(views): one value-hook name — uix use-subscribe → use-sub; delete the frame-first arity, public use-current-frame and wrap-view
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from views.md (ref views.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

"Read a subscription's value from a React function component" is one operation with two names: `re-frame.adapter.uix/use-subscribe` (`implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:140`) and `re-frame.hicasso.native/use-sub` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:46`). Both are value-returning hooks over `useSyncExternalStore`; their tracking machinery differs (the spine acquires/releases the subscription itself; Hicasso's joins the collector's cells) and that difference stays — the NAME is what drifted. The rule that fixes it: the verb returns a subscription (`subscribe`, Reagent's reaction — unchanged), the noun returns its value (`h/sub` in a Hicasso body — unchanged; `use-sub` in any function component — the one hook name). Two more UIx surfaces fail the demand bar: the frame-first 2-arity `(use-subscribe frame-kw query-v)` (`uix.cljs:144-146`, `spine.cljs:3374`) is exactly the positional frame-first shape API-shrink #1 (rf2-csbbwu) deleted from `subscribe` / `subscribe-once` / `dispatch` for misbinding, surviving in the adapter because the shrink stopped at the facade, with zero consumers outside the adapter's own tests; and `use-current-frame` (`uix.cljs:66-78`, spine `:2868-2870`) is the raw `useContext` read that `use-subscribe` calls internally to stay context-subscribed (`spine.cljs:3346-3367`), published as adapter API, returning a sentinel (`:rf.frame/no-provider`) as if it were an answer — zero consumers outside `spine.cljs`, `uix.cljs` and their tests. Finally `uix/wrap-view` (`uix.cljs:183-190`) is the payload of the `:adapter/wrap-view` late-bind hook that `reg-view*` already consumes (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:433-474`): zero consumers outside tests; the hook stays internal, the public var goes.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b)

- `use-subscribe` 1-arity, app-authored: 12 sites in 3 files — `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:63`, `login/core.cljs:52,53,55,56,57,93,95`, `dashboard/core.cljs:237,280,321,322`; tool-authored: `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_uix/views.cljs:9` (1); adapter testbed `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs:31` (1).
- `use-subscribe` 2-arity: ZERO app or tool sites. Test sites (more than the fable doc's "3"): `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:71,122,148,173,179,189,194,207,260,306` (a `target` frame threaded positionally to avoid mounting a provider) and `:462-463` (`use-subscribe-2-arg-pins-explicit-frame`, calling `react_shared_suite.cljs:4088 assert-use-subscribe-2-arg-pins-explicit-frame`); `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/three_way_parity_cljs_test.cljs:478` (UIx arm of the parity test). Every one is a test OF the arity or a convenience; none is a consumer.
- `use-current-frame`: zero sites outside `spine.cljs` (13, internal) and `uix.cljs`; tests `uix_use_current_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (12), `react_shared_suite.cljs` (5), `substrate_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs` (3), `uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs` (2).
- `wrap-view`: zero sites in examples/, tools/, testbeds/; tests 89 occurrences / 10 files, 59 of them in `react_shared_suite.cljs` reached through the suite's `cfg` key `:wrap-view` (:38, :509, :6734), plus `uix_source_coord_dom_elision_prod_test.cljs` (10), `uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs` (4), `uix_boot_order_source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (3), `view_alias_registry_cljs_test.cljs` (3), `substrate_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs` (3), `react_shared_suite_tests.clj` (4), `routing_arity_cljs_test.cljc` (1), `ssr_source_coord_test.clj` (1), `uix_reg_view_devtools_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (1).
- Spec teaches the deleted shape: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2105` shows `(use-subscribe frame-id [:q …])` AND a Reagent `@(rf/subscribe frame-id [:q …])` 2-arg form that does not exist — `re-frame.subs/subscribe` has arities `[query-v]` / `[query-v opts]` only (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1756,1785`); `spec/API.md:242` rows both arities; `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:119,125,269` and `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:94` teach the 2-arg form.

## Target API

```clojure
;; any React function component — UIx, or an island under Hicasso — ONE hook name, 1-arity only
(uix-adapter/use-sub [:q …])            ;=> current value; re-renders on change (was uix/use-subscribe)
(n/use-sub [:q …])                      ;=> unchanged (re-frame.hicasso.native)

;; explicit-frame read from a hook consumer: scope the subtree — a captured frame is NOT a hook
($ uix-adapter/frame-provider {:frame :tenant-b}
   ($ price-cell))                      ;; price-cell calls (use-sub [:quote/price sym])
;; NOT (:subscribe (rf/capture-frame :tenant-b)) inside render — that reads once and never re-renders (codex correction)

;; "which frame am I in", from a hook
(:frame (uix-adapter/use-frame))        ;; or (rf/current-frame-id) — use-current-frame is gone

;; Reagent (verb → reaction) and Hicasso body (noun → value) — unchanged
@(subscribe [:q …])   (h/sub [:q …])
```

`wrap-view`: the `:adapter/wrap-view` late-bind hook (`spec/Conventions.md:1765`) and the spine's `wrap-view-fn` (`spine.cljs:3413`, routed at `spine.cljs:3554`) stay exactly as they are — `reg-view*` consumes them. Only the public `re-frame.adapter.uix/wrap-view` var, its manifest row, its API.md row and its docs go. Tests that call `uix-adapter/wrap-view` directly (the elision prod test, boot-order test, the shared suite's `:wrap-view` cfg key) reach the same fn through `(:wrap-view spine-fns)` — the adapter's private `spine-fns` at `uix.cljs:48` — or through `reg-view*`; keep every assertion, move only the door.

Internal names: the spine's let-bound `use-subscribe` / `use-subscribe-2` / `use-current-frame` and the return-map keys (`spine.cljs:3406-3407`) may keep their names or follow the rename — the worker picks one and says so; what is public is `re-frame.adapter.uix/use-sub`. `use-current-frame` remains an internal call inside the 1-arity hook (it is what keeps the component context-subscribed, `spine.cljs:3346-3350`) — make it private, do not delete the mechanism.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer. Codex: "For hook-based reads, use `use-sub` consistently: a value-returning hook. Retain `subscribe` for the dereferenceable subscription and Hicasso's collector `sub` for its render-body read. Keep `use-frame` as the hook-shaped way to capture frame operations. A captured subscription is not a replacement for a React subscription hook; removing an explicit-frame hook arity must use a scoped subtree, not silently lose re-rendering." Codex Thoughts also note the alternative of keeping explicit targeting as `(use-sub query {:frame f})` if a real hook consumer ever needs to compare frames without restructuring its tree — prefer removal on the current evidence (zero consumers); if a consumer appears, that opts-map form (never frame-first positional) is the shape to add. Codex on `use-current-frame`: "Making the unused raw `use-current-frame` export internal is reasonable without inventing a replacement reader." Fable withdrew its `(:subscribe (rf/capture-frame :f))` suggestion after codex's correction.

## Deletion list

- `re-frame.adapter.uix/use-subscribe` (renamed to `use-sub`; the old name is not kept — no shim).
- The 2-arity `[frame-kw query-v]` of the hook (`uix.cljs:144-146` docstring sentence, `spine.cljs:3374`); `react_shared_suite.cljs:4088 assert-use-subscribe-2-arg-pins-explicit-frame` and its caller `uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:462-463`.
- `re-frame.adapter.uix/use-current-frame` public var (`uix.cljs:66-78`); `uix_use_current_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs` — delete, or rewrite to pin the internal behaviour (the 1-arity hook re-renders on a provider swap) through `use-sub`.
- `re-frame.adapter.uix/wrap-view` public var (`uix.cljs:183-190`).
- `spec/api-manifest.edn` rows 83 (`use-current-frame`), 85 (`use-subscribe` → `use-sub`), 86 (`wrap-view`); `spec/API.md:242` (rewrite as `use-sub`, 1-arity), `:244` (delete), `:247` (delete); `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md` §`use-current-frame` (:131-) and §`wrap-view` (:188-201), and the `:5,:10,:240` mentions.

description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from subscription-inputs.md (ref subscription-inputs.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Per the ruling on `@subscription-inputs.1`: `reg-sub` declares its dependencies positionally (`:<-` chain or a two-fn tail, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:87-170`) and hands a single input to the body as a bare value for `:<-` but as `[v]` for an `input-fn` (`subs.cljc:1284-1309`, `subs/memo.cljc:267-282`, `subs.cljc:2068-2098`). This bead lands the regular grammar and delivery; it does NOT yet delete the old grammar (that is `.6`, after the consumer sweeps `.3`–`.5`).

## Target API

```clojure
(reg-sub id ?metadata computation-fn)
;; metadata :inputs
;;   absent          → :input-kind :db          body (fn [db query-v] …)                      ;; unchanged
;;   [query-vector*] → :input-kind :static      body (fn [inputs query-v] …) — inputs a VECTOR
;;   fn-or-Var       → :input-kind :parametric  same body shape; inputs realized per concrete query-v
;; {:inputs []} → body receives [] (no dependencies); absent → app-db. Distinct by design.

(rf/reg-sub :cart/by-price {:inputs [[:cart/items]]}            (fn [[items] _] (sort-by :price items)))
(rf/reg-sub :cart/visible  {:inputs [[:cart/by-price] [:cart/filter]]} (fn [[items f] _] …))
(rf/reg-sub :article/page  {:doc "…" :inputs (fn [[_ id]] [[:article/by-id id] [:viewer]])} (fn [[a v] q] …))
```

title: research(story): measure the advantage thesis — run the three falsification journeys (explore->retain->strengthen; failure->cause->regression; human state->agent->verified revision) on Story and on Storybook 10.6 against the same planted defect, and report re-entry, diagnosis time and host switches
description:
== WHY ==
The Story-parity research (ai/findings/Story/fable/report.md section 4; astra's report and grok's agree) concludes that Story's surplus over Storybook-class workshops is STRUCTURAL and not yet PROVEN ERGONOMIC: a variant is a named application plan, every cell is a frame of the real machine, effects stub at the reg-fx seam, every run carries an epoch tape, fidelity is computed and labelled — and none of that has been shown to save a programmer re-entry, diagnosis time or context switches on a realistic task. Astra's critique (ai/findings/Story/astra/critique-for-fable.md point 5) is the sharpest statement: "Demonstrate less re-entry, easier diagnosis and fewer host/context switches on the same realistic task before calling them an ergonomic win." The report adopted astra's three falsifiable workflows as the next experiment. This bead runs them. A result of "no ergonomic win yet" is a valid and useful outcome.

== THE THREE JOURNEYS (report section 4.4; run each on BOTH sides, same defect, by someone who built neither) ==
1. EXPLORE -> RETAIN -> STRENGTHEN. A cheap pinned state gets a name; its pin is replaced by real setup events; a behaviour check is added. MEASURE manual re-entry and lost inputs across the three steps; the stronger case must DETECT a handler defect the pinned picture could not (plant one: e.g. the login machine's :submit transition drops the email). FAIR COMPARISON: Histoire's live source that follows controls; Storybook args + provider decorator + MSW. STOP RULE: if no work is saved, stop adding transformation UI.
   Story side: Controls on /idle (schema-derived, landed at #9800) -> save-as-variant -> the fidelity-upgrade snippet (view_state.cljc upgrade-snippet; parses and sheds the pin since #9803; NOTE rf2-yt6ak, held: pins composed from fragments may survive) -> add an :assert step -> run.
2. FAILURE -> CAUSE -> REGRESSION. A failed retry; the responsible event/effect/machine transition; a minimal repro that KEEPS the expectation; the fix. MEASURE time and wrong turns from the failed row to the evidence, inside the one-gesture budget of tools/story/spec/018-Story-UI-North-Star.md section 10.1; then fail/pass/fail without weakening any expectation. FAIR COMPARISON: Storybook Interactions plus the framework's DevTools. STOP RULE: better-structured evidence without a faster diagnosis is not yet an ergonomic win.
   Story side: Test mode on the login_form testbed -> the evidence row (rf2-v5p6l says the link does not render at trunk — if still true, measure the diagnosis WITH the link absent and say so) -> Xray on the assertion's epoch -> promote from Test mode (needs the dialog-capture fix filed beside this bead, which BLOCKS this journey for the testbed's shape; the API route works today) -> fix -> fail/pass/fail. The JVM version of this leg is already executed (evidence.md P6); the browser version with a human is the measurement.
3. HUMAN STATE -> AGENT -> VERIFIED REVISION. The human names a state; the assistant reads its resolved inputs and run evidence, edits the ordinary declaration, re-runs in the right host. MEASURE host switches, translations and manual steps; both surfaces must report the same inputs and the same failure. FAIR COMPARISON: Storybook's MCP addon (preview) plus its Vitest tests. STOP RULE: two host transports are acceptable if choosing the right one is easy (chapter 09 now names the two hosts on its first screen — #9801).
   Story side: story-mcp over stdio (tools/story-mcp; prelude and requests in ai/findings/Story/fable/probes/) for the headless loop, re-frame2-pair for the live browser; count every switch. The research's earlier MCP transcript proved TRANSPORT only — its "fix" edited the expected value, not the app (astra and grok both flagged this); this time the agent must repair the APPLICATION and the requirement must be preserved.

== SET-UP ==
Storybook side: astra's executed fixture ai/findings/Story/astra/evidence/storybook-fixture/src/Login.stories.tsx (Storybook 10.6.0, addon-vitest, Interactions; fail/retry/success in play()) — reuse it; `npm create storybook@latest` in a fresh Vite app if it must be rebuilt (record the version). Story side: `npx shadow-cljs watch :examples/login-form` from implementation/, http://localhost:8043/index.html#/stories. Same planted defect on both sides (name it in the deliverable; the login machine is the shared subject).

== DELIVERABLE ==
ai/findings/Story/fable/advantage-measured-<date>.md: per journey, per side — steps, re-entries, lost inputs, wall time, wrong turns, host switches, whether the defect was detected, and the stop-rule verdict; then one paragraph per journey saying whether the structural surplus produced an ergonomic one, and what single change would most improve the Story side (an IDEA for Mike, not a bead). Preserve raw transcripts and screenshots under ai/findings/Story/fable/evidence/journeys/. Nothing is built; no tracked file is edited; no bead is filed from this bead.

_Filed 2026-09-06 17:19:30 AUSEST from the RULING on rf2-kuky.38 (option A — collapse — ruled on Mike's behalf; the full dossier and both reviewers' analysis are attached to that bead's notes). Bead 2 of 2 — the hot-zone sweep; blocked by bead 1 (rf2-kuky.66). Parent epic rf2-kuky._

## Problem

Bead 1 (rf2-kuky.66) deletes `:rf.route/transitioned` from the runtime, tests, conformance fixtures, Xray and the non-hot-zone spec/docs. Four hot-zone spec files, the hot-zone migration README and its three skills mirrors still name it afterwards — and until this bead lands, the migration guide recommends an event the runtime no longer registers. Keep that interval short: this bead goes to the HEAD of the hot-zone queue the tick bead 1 merges.

## Target

Every remaining mention of `:rf.route/transitioned` in the five hot-zone files and the three skills mirrors is retargeted to `:rf.route/handle-url-change` dispatched with `{:rf.route/cause :link}`, with a dated pre-alpha "removed, no shim" note in the migration README. No alias, no shim, and NO rename of the survivor.

## Files (line numbers at ruling tip 13884f326f — re-measure with the ripgrep tool: `rg -n ':rf\.route/transitioned'`)

- `spec/API.md:281-282` — collapse the two events rows into one: `:rf.route/handle-url-change` | URL-change handler for link / popstate / initial load / SSR; the cause rides `:rf.route/cause` (`:link`, `:popstate`, `:initial`, `:ssr` are the framework's own feeds); default scroll `:top` for `:link`, else `:restore`. | 012. `api_md_check` is unaffected (keyword rows carry no tier); `spec/api-manifest.edn` does not name the id.
- `spec/Conventions.md:76` (reserved `:rf.route/*` namespace row — drop the name from the parenthetical list) and `:1823` (packaging table, `day8/re-frame2-routing` row — drop the name). NOTE: rf2-kuky.38's description cites :1813; that line is blank at tip, the second mention is :1823.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:554` (framework-authority stamp list).
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:236` (fragment-changed / navigation-blocked bullet).
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md`: M-20 `:1028` (v1 `:route/url-changed` → `:rf.route/handle-url-change` + `{:rf.route/cause :link}`); M-60 `:2433-2454` (the section STAYS as the dated history of the rename that did happen — `:rf/url-changed` → `:rf.route/transitioned`, `:rf.route/url-changed` → `:rf.route/fragment-changed` — and gains a dated note: `:rf.route/transitioned` itself is removed under rf2-kuky.38, pre-alpha, no shim; the replacement is `:rf.route/handle-url-change` dispatched with `{:rf.route/cause :link}`; the `(rf/reg-event :rf.route/transitioned …)` sample at :2454 is retargeted); plus the mentions at `:1368`, `:1373`, `:1610`, `:2989`.
  MUST include the override-widening sentence (Codex refinement, adopted in the ruling): a v1 app that had re-registered `:rf.route/transitioned` must re-register `:rf.route/handle-url-change` AND branch on `:rf.route/cause`, because that handler also receives Back/Forward (`:popstate`), initial load (`:initial`) and the SSR request URL (`:ssr`) — a blind registration rename would intercept all four.
  Do NOT rename anything to `:rf.route/url-changed`: M-60 records that keyword as the former FRAGMENT TRACE OP (now `:rf.route/fragment-changed`); reusing it collides with the migration record.
- Skills mirrors of M-60 — ride with the README so the migration story is one-touch: `skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-cross-cutting.md:38`, `skills/re-frame-migration/references/pre-rename-upgrades.md:19`, `skills/re-frame-migration/references/sequencing.md:94`.

## Hot-zone

ALL of `spec/API.md`, `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` are hot-zone one-touchers: serialise with every other wave-3 (and any other) toucher of those files. One PR.

## Sequencing

Blocked by bead 1 (rf2-kuky.66) MERGING on main (beads close on PR-open, so closed is not on main). Then head of the hot-zone queue.

## Acceptance

- `rg -n ':rf\.route/transitioned'` repo-wide (excluding `.beads/` and `ai/`) returns only: the migration README's M-60 history row(s) plus its dated removal note, the three skills mirrors' M-60 history cells, and bead 1's single dated retirement sentence in `spec/012-Routing.md` (if bead 1 kept one). Nothing in `spec/API.md`, `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` names it.
- `spec/API.md` events table has ONE URL-change row; table column counts verified by hand and stated in the PR body (nothing validates table shape).
- Gates, run FOREGROUND to completion and never piped: `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` AND `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` (both run unguarded in `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job on every PR; the two gates model different anchor suffixes and different roots — nominate by path, run both, cite CI), `mkdocs build --strict` (its hook stages `spec/` and `migration/` into the build — no manual staging step), and the `skills-structural` job in `.github/workflows/test.yml` for the skills mirrors.

## Traps

- Use the ripgrep-backed search tool, never Bash `grep -iF` (aborts silently here). Line numbers above will have drifted by dispatch time — ask `rg`.
- Run `sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh` before editing and report WORKTREE_ROOT; never `git stash` (commit first, then `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main`); do not commit anything under `.beads/` from the worker branch; remove any `implementation/node_modules` junction as the last act.
