title: Fan an always-on hydration-recovery record to production error sinks from both the spine and Fresco mount paths
description:
## Ruling

Hydration mismatches will be reported by React adoption alone. The render hash and the head hash are deleted in a follow-on bead. This bead lands FIRST and is additive: every hydrating root, on both mount paths, puts an always-on, structural-only record into the production error sinks. Without it, the deletion would quietly reverse rf2-tildz, because the hash path is today the only framework path that puts a hydration mismatch into a production error sink.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned, with the instruction:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both recommendations chose option A ("adoption alone"). Both put this production record first, before any deletion. The Codex review added Fresco's separate mount path to the scope, and that is folded in here.

Decisive facts, all at trunk 89517e8f54:
- The hash path is the only always-on mismatch record. `verify-hydration!` fans `{:error :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch :where rf/verify-hydration! :frame :failing-id :server-hash :client-hash :recovery :time}` through `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:674-703`). The 009 catalogue row says "The **adoption tier** rides the dev trace alone" (`spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2023`).
- The spine adoption reporter is debug-only. Its emit sits inside `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...)` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1178`). Its installation on `hydrateRoot` happens only when the host authored `:on-recoverable-error` or debug is on (`spine.cljs:1211-1225`, gate at `:1224`). The mount call site is `spine.cljs:4094-4111`.
- Fresco has its own mount path, and it is also debug-only. `hydrate-root-options` installs `hydration-reporter` only `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...)` (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs:350-359`). The emit is at `mount.cljs:312-323` and the reporter at `mount.cljs:325-348`.
- React 19.3's production build does pass recoverable hydration errors to `onRecoverableError`. It builds the minified #418 error at `implementation/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.production.js:2966-2974` and hands each queued recoverable error to `root.onRecoverableError` at `:13171-13176`. So the record is buildable.

Rejected options:
- B (keep a repaired body hash): it still misses every divergence below the root view's own markup, and it keeps the authoring surface: `:render-tree-fn`, the root-spelling traps and three knobs.
- C (leave as is): it keeps a false `:warned-and-replaced` label on the hash arm, a head hash with no reader, and the spelling traps.
- A deep hash (render every view to hash it): it doubles hydration work, cannot evaluate form-2/form-3 local state before mount, and still misses emitter-side differences.
- Updating the spine alone: Fresco would then be the one React-family root with no production signal.

Supersedes: nothing. rf2-tildz's guarantee (production must see mismatches) is RE-HOMED onto the adoption channel, not reversed. It changes the "adoption tier rides the dev trace alone" sentence of the 009 row and the "both the reporter installation and the emit are debug-gated + DCE'd, so ... production builds pay zero cost" clause of `spec/011-SSR.md:693`.

## Work

Code:
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs`:
  - Install the composed `onRecoverableError` on EVERY hydrating root, in every build. That means dropping the `(or (fn? authored) rf.interop/debug-enabled?)` gate at `:1224`. `:identifier-prefix` handling is unchanged.
  - Inside the adoption window only (the same `(.-adopting adoption-ref)` gate the dev trace uses, `:1204`), fan an always-on record through the `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record` late-bind hook, the way `hydrate.cljc:693-703` does today.
  - Then keep the dev trace (`emit-native-hydration-mismatch!`, still debug-gated and DCE'd).
  - Then keep delegating to the host callback or React's default report (`report-recoverable-default!`). Installing any callback turns React's default off, so the delegation is what keeps the fail-open behaviour.
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs`: make the same change. Install `hydration-reporter` on every hydrating root, and fan the same record within that root's own window (`rf.fresco.impl.roots/adopting?`). Keep its per-root scoping and its delegation to the default report.
- Record shape, STRUCTURAL ONLY: `{:error :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch :where <the door symbol each path already uses> :recovery :warned-and-replaced :time (rf.interop/now-ms)}`, plus `:frame` when the mount knows it. `:frame nil` is allowed (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:1056-1084`). React's message is NOT included: in development it carries app text, and production sinks receive the record raw, with no privacy gate. React's rich message stays on the dev trace only.
- Keep it small: about 30 lines across the two paths. Factor a shared helper only if it falls out naturally. Fresco must not `:require` anything new from the spine if that creates a cycle.

Spec:
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2023` (the `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` row): the adoption tier now ALSO fans a structural-only always-on record (`:where`, `:recovery`, `:time`, `:frame` when known). The rest of the row (the hash arm) stays until the deletion bead.
- `spec/011-SSR.md` §Hydration-mismatch detection (`:693`): the reporter is installed on every hydrating root, and only the dev trace is DCE'd. Note that `spec/011-SSR.md` is the one i/crlf file: edit it with the Edit tool or Python bytes, never `sed -i`.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`: touch it only if the general non-event always-on record schema enumerates categories and needs the adoption arm. Check, don't assume.

Tests:
- Add a production-posture test on each path, the spine (via an adapter, e.g. beside `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/adapter_hydrate_root_options_dom_cljs_test.cljs:101-153`) and Fresco. A hydrating root with a nested text mismatch must deliver exactly one record to a corpus error-emit listener, and that record must carry no React message text.
- Run it with debug off where the harness allows. Otherwise assert directly that the record path does not depend on `debug-enabled?`.
- A recoverable error AFTER the window closes must produce no record.

Deliberately stays:
- The dev trace and its React message.
- Host `:on-recoverable-error` composition (compose, never clobber).
- The window closers.
- The whole hash channel. The follow-on bead deletes it.

## Sequencing

- Hot zones touched: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, and possibly `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`. `spec/011-SSR.md` is touched too, and it is the one i/crlf file.
- Depends on: nothing. It lands first. rf2-qyjv2 (the hash-channel deletion) depends on it, and rf2-9kbu2 (the `emit-ui-tree` deletion) follows rf2-qyjv2.
- Cross-dossier: it shares `spec/011-SSR.md` §Hydration-mismatch detection with the work from `ssr-server-init-reserved-name.md` and `node-ssr-allowlist-and-html-string.md`, so sequence edits to 011 with theirs. `reagent-slim-keep-or-retire.md` changes which adapters the spine path serves, but not this change.

## Evidence

Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:
- the hash-path always-on record;
- both debug gates on the spine and both gates on the Fresco path;
- the error-emit record shape;
- the 009 row text.

Read but not run: React's production #418 routing to `onRecoverableError`, from the installed react-dom 19.3.0 production build.

Still needs a run: everything. No build or test was run for this ruling.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Both `spine.cljs` `hydrate-root-options` and Fresco `mount.cljs` `hydrate-root-options` install an `onRecoverableError` on every hydrating root, whatever `rf.interop/debug-enabled?` reads. Non-hydrating roots are unchanged.
2. Inside the adoption window, each path fans exactly one record per recoverable error through `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record`. Each record holds only `:error :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`, `:where`, `:recovery`, `:time` and (when known) `:frame`, and no React message text.
3. After the window closes, a recoverable error produces no record. It is still delegated to the host callback or React's default report.
4. A test on the spine path (through an adapter) and a test on the Fresco path each pin items 2 and 3. Both run green in `npm run test:cljs` or the browser lane that owns the file.
5. The `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` row of `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` and `spec/011-SSR.md` §Hydration-mismatch detection both state that the adoption tier fans a structural-only always-on record, and that only the dev trace is DCE'd. `spec/011-SSR.md` keeps CRLF line endings: CR count == CRLF count, and bare LF == 0.
6. The hash channel is untouched by this bead.

title: Remove subscription-vector :after delays and their live watch; teach config-driven delays as :data plus a delay fn
description:
## Ruling

Remove the subscription-vector form of a machine `:after` delay key (`{[:settings/idle-warning-ms] :warning}`), together with its live watch-and-restart machinery, its two error ids (`:rf.error/machine-after-sub-threw`, `:rf.error/machine-after-watch-failed`) and its `:on-resolution` cancel reason. A config-driven delay becomes a value in the machine's `:data` read by a `(fn [{:keys [snapshot]}] ms)` delay. The value reaches `:data` through the spawn `:data`, through a named event, or by sampling a subscription on entry through the existing recorded `{:rf/sub query-v :as fact-id}` coeffect source. A mid-wait restart is an explicit named event the author writes, such as `[:configure ms]` handled with `:reenter? true`. Inline fn delay keys and the current delay-fn signature stay. Delay evaluation stays exactly where it is today, in the timer fx against the committed snapshot. This is part 1 of option C. Machine-scoped named delays (part 2) are a separate bead that depends on this one.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

The dossier's recommendation and the independent Codex review both chose option C: remove live subscription-vector delays, add machine-local named delays, keep inline fns and the current fn signature.

**Decisive facts (at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. **The form is a live, unrecorded read of app-db from outside the machine's snapshot.** The vector branch of `resolve-delay-ms` subscribes in the machine's frame and derefs (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc:147-163`). The timer then activates the reaction and adds a watch (`timer.cljc:914-968`). On any unequal value, `on-sub-changed!` (`timer.cljc:476-564`) cancels the timer with `:reason :on-resolution` and re-arms it for the full new delay measured from now, with no machine event. Every other machine callback is held to the opposite rule: "actions and guards cannot see `app-db` at all" (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:827`). The native in-machine subscription read already exists as the recorded `{:rf/sub query-v :as fact-id}` source, sampled once and replayed verbatim (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:465`; `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_cofx_sub_source_test.clj:45-59`).
2. **Nothing uses it except the machines tests.** No example, testbed or tool testbed declares a sub-vector delay. The repo's two real dynamic delays are fn delays over `:data`: `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:719-723` (backoff) and `examples/patterns/long_running_work/worker.cljs:186-188` (work tick).
3. **It is the most defect-prone corner of `:after`.** Since the form landed in `b379557213`, four commits fixed defects specific to the subscription path, and none of those defects raised an error: `b347bda149` (rf2-fva6c.1, a bad resolved value leaked the sub ref-count), `aa29b187c1` (rf2-8cndln, a fired one-shot was re-armed by a later sub change), `6b65e11156` (rf2-wmpte, on Reagent the delay never re-resolved after its first arming) and `d05345f99b` (a parallel-root timeout was cancelled permanently the first time its delay changed). A subscription that changes faster than the delay also postpones the timer indefinitely, because each unequal change restarts the window.

**What is given up, stated plainly.** Sub re-resolution re-times one timer without re-entering its state. The replacement, a config event handled with `:reenter? true`, runs exit and entry again, restarts the state's other timers and spawned work, and can reset descendants. A parallel root cannot be re-entered at all (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:263-274`; `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/parallel_root_after_dynamic_delay_cljs_test.cljc:39-82`). Both recommendations accept this bounded loss because no consumer exists. The docs must say so plainly rather than claim the rewrite is equivalent. If a real application later needs independent live re-timing while preserving the rest of its state, that is the trigger to revisit.

**Rejected options:**
- **A, keep the form as it is:** it keeps the one live encapsulation crossing, roughly 210 lines of watch code in `timer.cljc`, and a substrate-sensitive live-watch obligation on every port, all for a capability nothing in the repo uses.
- **Keep the subscription spelling but sample it once at entry:** it keeps the crossing while dropping live tracking, the one thing the crossing paid for. An `:entry` action declaring the recorded `{:rf/sub}` source already samples a subscription at entry, recorded and visible in `:data`.
- **B alone, with no named delays:** rejected by both recommendations in favour of C. Named delays are the dependent bead filed alongside this one.

**Not part of this bead.** Moving delay resolution into the pure engine (`build-after-fx`) is a sub-decision on which the two recommendations differ, and it is still open for Mike. Keep resolution where it is.

**Supersedes:** Spec 005's teaching of the sub-vector form as "the **canonical** answer for 'the delay should track an app-level configuration'" (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:2368`). This closes the item that rf2-29hkz's close reason left open ("the sub-vector `:after` delays"). rf2-29hkz itself is not superseded. No EP is involved.

title: Skills: teach :rf/default as the conventional single-app frame id instead of :app/main
description:
## Ruling

**`:rf/default` is the conventional, documented frame id for a single-frame app, and every teaching surface converges on it.** Today the repo teaches three ids for the same thing: `:rf/default` (examples, scaffold, getting-started, test fixture, migration, pair MCP), `:app` (the guide) and `:app/main` (the skills and parts of the spec). After this ruling the scaffold, examples, guide, skills and spec boot templates all write `:rf/default` for a single-app frame.

It is a NAMING CONVENTION ONLY:

- `frame-root` keeps its REQUIRED `:id`, written out on the page. A missing `:id` still raises `:rf.error/frame-root-missing-id`.
- The runtime still never creates, infers or falls back to `:rf/default`: it is not created by `init!`, not the React-context default, not a lookup tier. A rootless `dispatch` still raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.
- Apps stay free to choose any other id. Descriptive ids stay wherever a passage teaches genuinely independent frames (two roots, per-request SSR frames, stories, embedded widgets).
- Wording constraint: describe it as a shared TEACHING convention, never as an address the REPL or tools secretly expect. Tool-Pair tier 3 resolves any sole app frame whatever its id (`spec/Tool-Pair.md:498`), and the pair guard merely exempts `:rf/default` from reserved-tool classification.
- Matching the app's id and the test fixture's id helps orientation, not test fidelity: the fixture builds `:preset :test` and does not mount the production root, so its `:fx-overrides` / `:interceptors` are not reproduced. Do not claim otherwise.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both the original dossier recommendation and the independent Codex review chose option A (bless the name, keep `:id` required, align the guide and skills) and both deferred B.

**Decisive facts (at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. **The newcomer path fails silently today.** `docs/core/getting-started.md:97` builds the counter with `(def app-frame :rf/default)`. The next guide page, `docs/core/app-db.md:109`, says "call `(rf/app-db-value :app)`", and `app-db-value` returns `nil` for an unknown frame (`spec/API.md:692`). So the instruction returns `nil` on the app the reader just built. Census: `:rf/default` in 41 example files and the template (`tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/core.cljs:17`); `:app` as a frame id across about 67 files under `docs/` (e.g. `docs/core/introduction.md:51`, `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:46` `(def app-frame :app)`); `:app/main` in the skills and spec (e.g. `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/project-structure.md:106`, which tells readers to pick a "descriptively-named" id and calls `:rf/default` "worth picking only for a tiny app or v1 migration").
2. **The spec still calls the id merely ordinary**, at `spec/002-Frames.md:234-249` and `:900-911`, following EP-0002 resolved open issue 4 (`docs/EP/EP-0002-frame-target-resolution.md:1278-1283`). That issue's premise was that "the reservation buys neither migration nor docs clarity", and it no longer holds. Migration rule M-20 rewrites `:re-frame/default` to `:rf/default` (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1022`, row at `:1034`), and the guide calls a single-frame app "Type A — only `:rf/default` in play" (`:696`). The test fixture ensures "the conventional `:rf/default` app frame" (`spec/008-Testing.md:196`, `:216`). The pair guard exempts it as "the canonical app frame" (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/reserved_frame_guard.cljs:60-71`).
3. **`frame-root` requires `:id` and fails loud without it** (`spec/002-Frames.md:1696`, `:1746` "There is no `:rf/default` floor"; the shared validator `require-frame-root-id!` is at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/frame_boundary.cljs:143-166`). That stays, so this ruling needs no code change.

**Rejected options:**

- **B (an id-less `frame-root` defaults to `:rf/default`): deferred, not taken.** It hides the REPL address from the source. It also gives `frame-root {}` and `make-frame {}` different meanings for "no id": the conventional frame against a private gensym. And it makes silently joining a shared frame the easy path: a second id-less root replaces the first root's `:fx-overrides`/`:interceptors` and never replays its `:initial-events`. Revisit only with evidence that `:rf.error/frame-root-missing-id` is a recurring stumble.
- **C (examples move to app-chosen ids):** the REPL address varies per app, new apps diverge permanently from M-20-migrated apps and from the fixture default, and the guide would still have to pick one id.
- **D (leave as is):** keeps the three-way split and the silent `(rf/app-db-value :app)` failure.
- **Renaming to a non-"default" `:rf/*` id:** about 2,600 occurrences in about 800 files for a wording nuance, and it loses the v1 echo of `:re-frame/default`.
- **Rootless calls resolving to the sole live frame:** stays closed. A callback captured in a destroyed frame would land in its sole successor.

**Supersedes:** the framing of EP-0002 resolved open issue 4 that `:rf/default` is merely an "ordinary" id. Its substance stands: no privilege, no inference, no floor. This ruling does NOT reopen rf2-78wg or rf2-mhpo; their "there is no `:rf/default` floor" corrections stay true and must survive every rewrite.

**Filed as four beads** (label `dossier-ruling`): the spec bead first, then the guide sweep, the examples comment sweep and the skills sweep, which can run in parallel once the spec bead has merged.

## Work (this bead: the skills sweep)

**The main acceptance case is convergence.** An AI pair loading the re-frame2 skills must be taught the same single-app id the scaffold writes, `:rf/default`. Today `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/project-structure.md:106` tells it to pick a "descriptively-named" id such as `:app/main` and calls `:rf/default` "worth picking only for a tiny app or v1 migration". Meanwhile `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/entry-namespace.md:122` scaffolds `(def app-frame :rf/default)`.

- **Scope:** `skills/**` and `docs/skills/**`, EXCEPT `skills/**/tests/**` fixtures and `skills/**/evals/*.json` prompts that describe a user's own app, where any legal id is fine. Shadow-cljs build ids (`{:builds {:app …}}`) are not frame ids and stay.

title: Route every shadow-cljs entry through one launcher that takes a machine-wide build-lane lock, owns the compiler process tree and clears stale test output
description:
## Ruling

Every shadow-cljs entry goes through ONE launcher, which does three things:

1. takes a machine-wide build-lane lock;
2. owns the compiler child and its whole process tree;
3. deletes a one-shot compile's declared disposable output before compiling.

The lock replaces the social announce-and-take protocol with a step that can refuse. A run that finds the lane busy prints who holds it and waits, instead of two runs wedging silently.

Build the launcher by extracting the stale-output and compiler-result handling that `implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` already has. Do not write a second launcher beside it.

Long-lived `watch` and server entries must not hold the global lock for their whole lifetime. Establish their ownership and cancellation behaviour, and keep the protocol prose as the fallback for any entry the lock cannot cover. Retire the AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md protocol prose only once a spawn-policy test shows that every entry goes through the launcher.

This is the third bead of the tooling dossier's option (C), which moves each test invariant into the tool that every invocation reads.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

**Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:**

1. **Exclusivity lives only in prose.** It is AGENTS.md § "The shadow-cljs Build Lane Is Machine-Wide Exclusive", CLAUDE.md's "granting the shadow-cljs build lane" rules, and the memory `claude-md-shadow-cljs-build-lane`. Two concurrent runs "wedge silently": no error, no exit file and no output. CLAUDE.md's own conclusion is that an announcement notifies and does not ask, so two correct announcements compose into a collision. Only something that sees every holder can refuse, and a lockfile is that thing.
2. **Stale-bundle deletion lives in one launcher.** `implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs:129-132` deletes the output before compiling, and resets the lane cache for `--config-merge` compiles (`:119-127`). `implementation/scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs:178-181` compiles `node-test` through a bare `spawnSync(process.execPath, [runner, 'compile', 'node-test'])` that skips the delete. About ten other launchers in `implementation/scripts/` compile the same way.
3. **Watches are long-lived.** `implementation/scripts/dev-testbed.cjs:247` spawns `shadow-cljs watch`, which runs indefinitely, so a lock held for its lifetime would block every other worker. Upstream shadow-cljs supports parallel watches with project-relative caches. Exclusivity is therefore this machine's measured operational constraint, not a documented shadow-cljs requirement.

**Rejected:**

- *Keep the prose protocol.* Nothing in it can refuse. Every worker has to remember the grant, kill by ancestry when told to yield, and report overlaps.
- *Diagnose the wedge before building the lock* (an earlier review's position). Serialising is already the protocol's remedy, so a lock helps whatever the cause. Diagnose once, alongside the work.
- *A brand-new launcher beside `compile-node-test.cjs`.* It would duplicate the stale-output and compiler-result handling that already exists.
- *Delete every build's output or cache before any compile.* Only a one-shot compile's declared disposable output carries the stale-bundle risk. Wiping watch outputs or the shadow-cljs cache is collateral damage.

**Supersedes,** only once the spawn-policy test proves coverage (until then they stay):
- the announce-and-take build-lane protocol in AGENTS.md § "The shadow-cljs Build Lane Is Machine-Wide Exclusive";
- CLAUDE.md's "Mayor only — granting the shadow-cljs build lane";
- the memory `claude-md-shadow-cljs-build-lane`.

No bead ruling is overturned.

## Work

- **One helper**, for example `implementation/scripts/lib/shadow.cjs` (`lib/` already exists). Extract it from `compile-node-test.cjs`'s existing handling (`:112-188`). It resolves `shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js`, spawns it under `process.execPath`, streams its output and returns the compiler result.
- **The lock.**
  - It is a machine-wide lockfile outside any worktree, taken atomically, recording `{pid, worktree, command, started}`.
  - A dead holder's lock is reclaimed.
  - A waiting run prints a line such as `waiting for build lane held by <pid> (<worktree>, <command>)`.
  - It is released on every exit path, the tree-kill path included.
  - It is cancellable: Ctrl-C while waiting or while running reaps the whole child tree and releases the lock.
  - On CI, with one build per runner, it must be harmless.
- **Delete before compile:** remove only the declared disposable output of a one-shot compile.
- **Route through it:**
  - the roughly ten compile launchers in `implementation/scripts/` (census: `git grep -l "shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js" -- implementation/scripts`);
  - the literal `shadow-cljs` npm scripts in `implementation/package.json`;
  - machines-viz's JVM `shadow.cljs.devtools.cli` call.
- **Watch and server entries** (`dev-testbed.cjs`, the `serve-and-run-*` launchers): decide and document their ownership and cancellation. For example, hold the lock only around the initial compile, or give them a separate mode. Do not hold it for the process lifetime.
- **Spawn-policy test:** it fails if any script or npm script reaches the shadow-cljs runner other than through the helper. Give it a planted-violation control.
- **Diagnose one wedge** along the way, with a thread dump and a memory reading, and record what it was on this bead.
- **Retire the prose last.** Only after the spawn-policy test is green AND the watch and server behaviour is settled, retire or shrink AGENTS.md's Build Lane section and CLAUDE.md's grant rules to the fallback for any uncovered entry, and update the memory. CLAUDE.md is the mayor's file, so propose that edit for the coordinator to make.
- **Deliberately stays:** the build definitions in `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones:** none of the listed ones by default. The edits land in `implementation/package.json` and many `implementation/scripts/*.cjs` files. If routing an entry forces a change to `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` or `.github/workflows/*`, those are hot zones.
- **Depends on:** nothing.
- **Within this dossier:** its "resize the local loop" question (Q1, still open for Mike in `ai/decisions/tooling-invariants-and-lane-registry.md`) would land after this bead if it is ruled, so that the opt-in CLJS tier is locked.
- **Cross-dossier:** the beads from `test-react-retire.md` (rf2-f00gs) and `reagent-slim-keep-or-retire.md` (rf2-47zrp) delete launchers and builds, `serve-and-run-reagent-slim-smoke.cjs` among them. Land those first if both are ready, so there are fewer launchers to route. Otherwise whichever lands second rebases.
- **The build lane:** running this bead's own tests enters shadow-cljs, so it needs a build-lane grant from the coordinator like any other run, until this bead lands.

## Evidence

**Read in source** at trunk 89517e8f54: every line cited above.

**Not measured:**
- the wedge's cause;
- the lock's behaviour on Windows (file-locking semantics, PID liveness checks).

The acceptance runs are the measurement.
acceptance_criteria:
1. One helper module is the only code path that spawns the shadow-cljs runner or the JVM shadow.cljs.devtools.cli. A spawn-policy test enforces this and goes red on a planted direct spawn.
2. Two worktrees running `npm run test:cljs` at the same time serialise. The second prints a waiting line naming the holder's pid, worktree and command, then proceeds when the first finishes, and both runs are green.
3. A lock left by a killed process (dead pid) is reclaimed by the next run with no manual step.
4. Ctrl-C or a kill during a locked run reaps the whole compiler process tree and releases the lock. Ctrl-C while waiting exits without taking the lock.
5. A one-shot compile deletes its declared output before compiling. Watch outputs and the shadow-cljs cache are not wiped.
6. A long-lived watch does not block other workers' compiles for its whole lifetime, and the helper documents its ownership and cancellation rule.
7. The existing _compile-node-test-*.test.cjs tests stay green. compile-node-test.cjs's stale-output and compiler-result handling lives in the helper and is not duplicated.
8. One wedge diagnosis (thread dump and memory reading) is recorded on the bead.
9. The AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md protocol prose is retired, or reduced to the fallback for uncovered entries, only after criteria 1 and 6 hold. The PR says which was done.

WHAT LANDED ON THE BRANCH
- implementation/scripts/lib/shadow.cjs is the one helper, usable as a library (runShadow, acquireLane) or as a CLI (node scripts/lib/shadow.cjs [--clean p]... [--cwd d] [--clojure aliases] [--hold-lane] <command> ...).

description:
Once the Fresco scaffold path works (rf2-ezmzk), teach Fresco as the default view layer. Align the entry docs, the Views chapter and the AI skills with that working path, and convert only the central teaching examples.

## Ruling

Mike decided on 2026-10-17: "take Codex's side on all five". For the Fresco dossier, that means the following.

**What is decided:**
- Fresco is the taught path for new applications.
- Reagent and UIx stay explicit, supported, first-class choices.
- The advertised default switches only through one working greenfield path. That path is the template's `:fresco` scaffold, whose default flips in rf2-ezmzk at the first tag. rf2-k33yt has already put Fresco's test kit on its `:paths`.
- Do not advertise a default that would require a newcomer to migrate the generated application straight away.

**Explicitly NOT part of this work:**
- **No portable `spec/004-Views.md`.** `spec/Ownership.md` (~69) classifies Fresco's package contract as a CLJS-reference binding. A teaching default does not make a React-based implementation a portable framework requirement.
- No wholesale example migration.
- No expansion or retirement of optional modules.
- No `reg-state` relocation.

**The costs to teach honestly.** Teaching them means a clear selection paragraph, not new machinery:
- `h/event` behaves differently according to its prop position.
- Foreign components can need callback and slot declarations.
- Fresco has no component-local reactive cell; app-db and React islands are deliberate.
- Hook-heavy products may stay simpler on UIx.
- SSR: Fresco renders on Node only (`re-frame.fresco.server` calls `react-dom/server`). A JVM backend that renders Fresco needs the Node crossing. The JVM-renderable route is Reagent, and that choice must be visible BEFORE installation.

## Work (after rf2-ezmzk lands)

1. **Entry docs.** Cover the pages the README and the mkdocs nav lead a newcomer through first, plus the README's view-layer paragraph (~`README.md:184`). Fresco is the default in the scaffold. Add the selection paragraph:
   - Fresco by default;
   - Reagent for JVM SSR without Node, and for v1 migration;
   - UIx for hook-heavy, React-first apps.
2. **The Views chapter** (`docs/core/views.md`).
3. **SSR guide.** The opening model section of `docs/ssr/concepts.md` (~30-57) names both routes: Fresco via the Node renderer, and Reagent on the JVM.
4. **AI skills:**
   - `skills/re-frame2` (its views reference and `SKILL.md` ~59);
   - `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md` (~54), which today follows the template's Reagent/UIx-only limitation.
5. **Examples.** Convert only the central teaching examples, meaning the ones the entry docs and the Views chapter point a newcomer at. Keep the adapter witness examples on their adapters.

## Sequencing

This bead depends on rf2-ezmzk. No CLAUDE.md hot-zone files are touched unless `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` prose must change; if so, that change goes in its own hot-zone PR. Gates: `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, plus the examples compile sweep for any converted example.

3. `docs/core/views.md`, `docs/ssr/concepts.md`, `skills/re-frame2` and `skills/re-frame2-setup` all teach the same default.
4. No `spec/004-Views.md` is added. Adapter witness examples are unchanged. Converted examples compile.

title: SSR emitter: the invalid-hiccup-head errors copy the whole element (children included) into message and ex-data
description:
## Defect

Two SSR emitter errors carry the whole offending hiccup element, children included, in both the thrown message and its ex-data:

- the reserved `:rf/*` head arm (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:651-667`): `(pr-str safe-element)` in the message, and `:extra {:element safe-element}`;
- `reject-invalid-hiccup-head!` (`emit.cljc:669-705`): the same pattern.

`rf.error/safe-form` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/error.cljc:540-552`) only replaces cyclic JS values. On the JVM it returns the form unchanged. So whatever the element's children hold reaches the error: rendered app-db values, including ones classified `:sensitive`, and a subtree of any size.

Verified by reading at trunk 3fa88920c8.

## Change

Have these errors identify the element without copying its contents. Roughly: keep `:head` in ex-data, and replace `:element` and the message's `(in element …)` with a bounded description, such as the tag, the attribute keys and the child count. Check whether any other emitter error copies a whole element the same way, and treat it alike.

Spec 011 and Spec 015 govern what may reach an off-box channel. Check where these errors egress (server logs, error traces, any dev payload) before you pick the bound. Related: rf2-2fn0u, the pending decision on redacting handler exception text under `:sensitive`. This bead does not depend on that ruling, because a hiccup element is not a handler's exception.

## Acceptance

- A test for each arm: an element whose child holds a sentinel string throws `:rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head`, and the sentinel appears in neither `ex-message` nor `(pr-str (ex-data e))`. The message still names the head.
- The existing tests that pin these errors still pass, or are updated to the new shape.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (PR #11455, branch worker/ssr-fresco-hydration, commit 4c1c1c77dc) ==
Done. The bound is Spec 015's: a framework render diagnostic carries a content-free shape summary, never the value, and explicitly no map :keys (spec/015-Data-Classification.md, Author guidance for the exception-path residual). So the attribute keys the bead suggested are left out. All three arms that copied the element now describe it as re-frame.error/diag-value-summary's {:type :vector :count n} under the existing :element key, and the message says "(in a hiccup vector of n forms)":
- the reserved :rf/* head arm and the malformed-head arm of :rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head (:head kept; on the malformed arm the head still crosses error/safe-form);
- the :> arm, :rf.error/ssr-reagent-native-head, which had the same pattern.
The :element key name stays so Spec 009's :rf.error/ssr-reagent-native-head row (outside the fence) still names the ex-data correctly; the :rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head row now says what :element holds. Other emitter errors checked: :rf.error/invalid-tag-name carries the tag keyword and :rf.error/ssr-nonrenderable-component the component fn. re-frame.ssr.ui-tree's malformed-node errors carry node values in ex-data, but that file is outside the fence and emit-ui-tree is deleted by rf2-9kbu2.
Regression: ssr_emit_test.clj head-errors-describe-the-element-without-its-contents, one row per arm with a child sentinel: the sentinel is in neither ex-message nor (pr-str (ex-data e)), the message names the head, and :element is the shape. Red on tip: exit 1, 9 failures (message, ex-data and :element on each arm). Green: ssr JVM exit 0, 328 tests / 1608 assertions against a tip baseline of 327 / 1593 (+1 test, +15 assertions, predicted).
Merged-PR audit #11455: follow-up rf2-g7kqt — Summarize malformed SSR heads instead of copying their app content. This is a separate open finding; the source status and ruling are preserved.
close_reason: Merged in #11455 (087f52b0f9; commit 4c1c1c77dc). The SSR emitter's head errors (the reserved :rf/* head arm, reject-invalid-hiccup-head!, and the :> arm :rf.error/ssr-reagent-native-head, which had the same leak) carry a shape summary {:type :vector :count n} in place of the element, and the message reads "(in a hiccup vector of n forms)"; :head is kept. Attribute keys are left out because Spec 015 rules a map's keys out of such a summary. The ex-data key stays :element so Spec 009's :> row stays accurate. Evidence: the new sentinel test went red on tip (exit 1, 9 failures) and green after; ssr JVM lane exit 0 at 328/1608 against a 327/1593 baseline, as predicted; CI green. ssr/ui_tree.cljc's malformed-node errors also put node values into ex-data; that code goes with rf2-9kbu2.

title: Frame destruction resolves machine exits outside the destroyed frame's image
description:
PR #11488 correctly clears the ambient event owner for A's destruction, but the eventless machine-exit walker still resolves the machine definition without A's registration view. With two image-isolated frames selecting different definitions of the same machine ID, destroying A executes B's :exit against A's snapshot. A's own cleanup is skipped and the other application's cleanup runs. This is a separate observable isolation failure from the duplicate-exit write refusal fixed by #11488.

Exact-merge public-API JVM probe at ef868172260149f8275df0833c29d387ca48f5f2:
1. Register :audit/type twice through re-frame.machines/reg-machine*, metadata :rf.provenance/ns audit.a and audit.b, with distinct :entry/:exit log callbacks.
2. Make A and B with rf/image :select-ns selecting their respective namespace plus a shared boot/destroy event namespace. Spawn one :audit/type actor in each frame using dispatch-sync.
3. The entry log is [[:a :entry] [:b :entry]], proving each image resolves its own definition, and both snapshots exist.
4. Destroy A cold, from A's event, or from B's event. In all three modes the exit log is [[:b :exit]], expected [[:a :exit]]. A disappears and B's actor remains live.
Result: 3 tests, 12 assertions, 3 failures, 0 errors; all entry, actor-presence and frame-lifecycle checks pass. Probe/log/exit: ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11488-registration-view-1.{clj,log,exit}. No shadow-cljs lane used.

Owning path: core frame.cljc run-destroy-recipe! calls notify-machine-destruction! without binding the target frame's resolution; machines lifecycle_fx/frame_destroy.cljc walks actors and exit_cascade.cljc run-child-exit! resolves through lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc spec-from-id-or-snapshot. That calls registrar/lookup, which uses whichever generation/live view is ambient, or the latest registration when none is bound. The :on-destroy event's own view ends before the subsequent machine walk; clearing *event-owner* supplies write authority but no registration view. Spec 002's image-isolation contract and registrar/lookup's documented per-frame resolution require A's definitions.

Small correction: run the eventless teardown/exit resolution through the existing target-frame resolution seam while A's claimed record is still available, preserving #11488's no-event-owner write behavior. Add a regression with two distinct images sharing one machine ID, covering cold and cross-frame destruction and checking that only A's exit runs. No new public API or ownership machinery is needed.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (2026-10-18 00:00 AUSEST): draft PR #11492, commit 84303dc165 on worker/destroy-image (base ba719742da) ==

Reproduced at tip. A new regression, machines/test/re_frame/frame_destroy_image_exit_cljs_test.cljc, uses two image-isolated frames. Each selects its own registration of :fdix/type plus an :fdix/note effect emitted by :exit, and both also select a shared boot/destroy namespace. Every destroy mode logged [[:b :exit]] where [[:a :exit]] was expected: top level, A's own event, B's effect, and pending inside B. The entry-log, actor-presence and frame-gone controls held.

Fix: notify-machine-destruction! in core frame.cljc runs the :machines/teardown-on-frame-destroy! hook inside (:live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution id ...). That is live_frame/call-with-frame-resolution, which delegates to call-with-record-resolution, the seam the router's per-event resolution shares (router process-event!). It is reached through the existing late-bind key, as error_emit/executed-coord already does. No directory row changes, no new API, and *event-owner* stays nil, so #11488's write behaviour is kept. At step 3 the id resolves to the claimed incarnation, because the reservation is held and the record stays registered until step 9. One binding covers the whole step-3 walk: actor-live?, the spec resolution, the :exit cascade and its do-fx, reaping of tracked children, the classification drop, and resource release.

Sibling steps:
- Step 2 (:on-destroy) already binds the frame's own view, via router run-frame-destroy-event! -> run-one-pass! -> process-event!.
- Steps 5-6 (sub-cache disposal; the flows, routing, resources, machines-timer, http, fx, fresco, live-frame and ssr hooks) resolve no registrations. They only release id-keyed host state, so none has the gap.
- Epoch steps 7a and 10 are out of fence and were not examined in depth.

Evidence, from namespace-scoped JVM runs of the new test:
- Red at tip: exit 1, 4 failures.
- Fix planted out (match count 1): exit 1, 4 failures, each row logging [[:b :exit] [:b :exit-fx]].
- Restored: exit 0, 1 test, 4 assertions. The restore matched the committed blob by default-form blob hash f5e5868eb3, and git diff --quiet exited 0.

Gates (exit codes captured to files):
- test-jvm-implementation: exit 0. Machines went from 647/1517 to 648/1521, as predicted.

title: Flows prose still describes a vacation queue and drain: router.cljc flows-interceptor comment and Spec 013 :140, :299
description:
## Defect

Prose still describes flow output-path vacations as a queue that is drained later. In the code, a vacation happens in place: `vacate-path-in-db` (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc` ~512) is applied directly to the pending db inside the flow pass (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc` ~345-397). Nothing queues a vacation, and nothing drains one.

The stale sites at trunk 5ae3ed2c81:

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` ~1642-1649: the flows interceptor's `:after` guard comment says the flow pass "loses a queued vacation", and lists "no vacation drain" among what the guard skips. The reference to the "output-path vacations its rows record" (~1642) and the comment near ~1286 should be checked against the same model.
- `spec/013-Flows.md:140`: `destroy-frame!` drops the memo, "its pending path vacations included".
- `spec/013-Flows.md:299`: the restored bookkeeping is "`last-inputs` + the in-drain abandoned-path vacations".

Verified by reading at trunk 5ae3ed2c81.

## Change

Restate each site as the code works now, in the present tense. Vacations happen in the pending db during the flow pass, so an aborted event discards them with that db. Keep only what the memo really holds, and do not invent a queue to explain it. Comments and spec prose only; no behaviour change.

title: HTTP: the wire status is :http-status in the failure map and :meta, ending :status at two levels
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20: rename the HTTP wire status to `:http-status` in the failure map and in `:meta`. The alternative was to keep `:status` at two levels as the accepted cost of one envelope.

## Problem

Measured at trunk 8fc6369484.

A managed-HTTP reply has a closed top-level `:status` (`:ok` / `:error` / `:cancelled`). The wire status code is also called `:status`, in two places:
- inside the classified failure map at `:error` (`:rf.http/http-4xx` and `:rf.http/http-5xx`, `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` around line 511);
- inside a successful reply's `:meta` (around line 567).

Spec 014 calls this "The priced wrinkle — `:status` at two levels" (around line 560). The teaching pays for it twice:
- `docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md:184`: "Note the two `:status` levels…";
- `docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md:564`: "Mind the **two `:status` levels**…".

The code that reads it is `(get-in reply [:error :status])`, beside a top-level `(:status reply)` meaning something else.

The writers are in `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/`:
- `transport.cljc:137`, `:1083` and `:1207`;
- `transport_cljs.cljc:182`;
- `transport_jvm.cljc:304`.

## Change

- The wire status is `:http-status` wherever it rides the reply: the failure map under `:error` and the success `:meta`.
- `:status-text` keeps its name, since it is not ambiguous.
- The reply's top-level `:status` is unchanged.
- No alias, no transition period.
- Census every reader before editing, on two token axes: the `get-in` / `[:error :status]` / `[:meta :status]` paths, and destructuring of the failure map (`{:keys [status …]}` over an `:error` value). Readers live in:
  - `implementation/http` (including `:retry` and `:after`);
  - `implementation/resources` (which lowers onto managed HTTP);
  - Xray (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc:921`);
  - the pair MCP;
  - tests, docs, skills and examples.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`: the failure-category table, §Reply payload shape, §Successful-response metadata, the 401 refresh recipe (around line 887), and delete the "priced wrinkle" paragraph.
- `spec/Managed-Effects.md`, if it shows the HTTP `:meta` shape.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`: the HTTP failure and `:meta` schemas. **Hot zone.**
- `docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md` and `docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md`: the code moves to `[:error :http-status]` and both "two levels" notes go.
- `docs/async/http.md` and any skill that teaches the failure shape.

## Acceptance

- A 503 reply carries `{:status :error :error {:kind :rf.http/http-5xx :http-status 503 …}}`.
- A 200 reply carries `{:status :ok :meta {:http-status 200 :status-text … …}}`.
- No reader of the wire status still says `:status`. Show the census in the PR body, on both token axes, with a control hit.
- HTTP, resources, Xray and pair-MCP suites green, plus `npm run test:cljs`.

## Sequencing

Hot zone: `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`. `implementation/http/` is otherwise isolated.

Breaking: every app reading the wire status changes one key. Effort S–M.

title: Fresco test kit: a supported reset bracket and render-to-commit helper, so tests stop reaching into impl.collector
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 8fc6369484.

Every Fresco runtime test needs two things: a reset before and after, and a way to render a body then commit it. The test kit publishes neither, so consumers reach into implementation namespaces:
- 36 files under `tools/xray` call `re-frame.fresco.impl.collector/reset-runtime!` (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/collector.cljs:1310`);
- three Xray panel tests drive `render-body`, `commit-boundary!` or `last-reads` directly (`tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/fresco_cljs_test.cljs`, `fresco_causal_cljs_test.cljs`, `fresco_live_panel_dom_cljs_test.cljs`);
- 54 files under `tools/xray` require some `re-frame.fresco.impl.*` namespace;
- 84 of Fresco's own test files require `re-frame.fresco.impl.collector`.

`re-frame.fresco.test.runtime` (`implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test/runtime.cljs`, 203 lines) exposes census reads and witnesses (`stats`, `residue`, `quiesced!`, `cell-reaction`, `cell-readers`, `boundary-reads`, `reads-of`, `snapshot-of`, `body-runs`, `reset-body-runs!`) but no bracket.

A test that resets first and checks afterwards can also manufacture a clean result: the reset erases the residue the check was meant to see.

## Change

Add two things to `re-frame.fresco.test.runtime`:
- **A reset bracket.** A fixture-shaped fn, or a macro if the test framework needs one. It reads quiescent residue **before** it calls `reset-runtime!` and fails on residue, so cleanup cannot hide a leak. It then resets, so the next test starts clean.
- **A render→commit helper** over the existing body, commit and read operations. It returns what a test asserts on (the markup or tree, and the reads).

Reuse the L2 and L3 operations the kit already has. Add no production lifecycle and no second graph. If the bracket only multiplies aliases of the current doors, narrow those doors instead and say so.

Then move one Xray suite onto them, `fresco_cljs_test.cljs` or whichever reads most clearly.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `docs/core/fresco/15-testing.md`: document the bracket and the helper as the supported runtime seam.
- The test-kit reference page, if one lists `test.runtime`'s fns.

## Acceptance

- The migrated Xray suite requires no `re-frame.fresco.impl.*` namespace.
- A planted leak, meaning a reaction left alive, makes the bracket fail. Removing the plant makes it pass.
- Production erasure still excludes the test kit (the bundle-isolation and erasure gates stay green).
- Fresco and Xray suites green, plus `npm run test:cljs`.

## Sequencing

Isolated to `implementation/fresco/test_kit/` and one Xray test file. It is a good first consumer of rf2-l9bij's authoring contract, but it does not wait on it.

Effort S–M, low risk.
notes:
== DISPATCH (mayor), 2026-10-20 08:32:30 AUSEST: fresco-testkit-presence, clustered with rf2-ohau2 and rf2-sekvu.
== WORKER SUMMARY (fresco-testkit-presence), branch worker/fresco-testkit-presence

DISPOSITION: done.

ADDED to re-frame.fresco.test.runtime:
- render-and-commit! frame-kw body [props]. It renders a body function or a defview head (the head goes through codec/retained-body, as ht/tree does), then commits through collector/commit-boundary! with a no-op notifier. It answers {:element :reads :release}.
- reset-bracket, a map :each fixture. :before resets. :after waits on quiesced!, reads residue, and reports a :fail through cljs.test/do-report if any counter is above zero (a :pass otherwise). Only then does it call reset-runtime!. It is a map because the check is async, and cljs.test runs only map fixtures asynchronously.
- Both are compositions of existing collector doors. There is no production lifecycle and no second graph, and the bracket is not an alias: its check-before-reset order is new behaviour.

WITNESS: test_kit/test/.../test_kit_runtime_bracket_cljs_test. The plant is a committed boundary that nobody releases, so its reaction stays alive. The test runs the bracket's own :after with cljs.test's reporter swapped for a recorder. The result is one :fail whose :actual names {:cells 1 :cell-refs 1 :boundaries 1 :edges 1}, and the residue is zero afterwards. With the plant removed (released), it records one :pass.

XRAY: tools/xray/test/.../panels/fresco_cljs_test.cljs moves onto both, and now requires no re-frame.fresco.impl.* namespace (it previously required codec and collector). Its fixtures are map-form: the xray runtime fixture with :async? true, then reset-bracket, so the bracket's check runs before the frame teardown. The redaction row a-sensitive-query-argument-... mounted a boundary it never released, and the bracket would fail it, so it now releases.

DOCS: 15-testing.md gains "Boundaries without React: re-frame.fresco.test.runtime" as the supported runtime seam. api-reference.md gains a test.runtime section listing the two doors.

title: [MIKE DECISION] Should a handler's exception text be redacted off-box when its registration declares :sensitive?
description:
[MIKE DECISION] Should an event handler's exception text be redacted off-box when that handler declares :sensitive?

What changed. Before rf2-ot1aa (PR #11384, merged as 7add3bd9b0), the db-focus heuristic stamped every trace in a [:rf.interceptor/path P] handler's scope :sensitive? true, and that stamp incidentally covered the :rf.error/handler-exception row. The heuristic is gone, and the ruling's exception-text sibling (rf2-5kw8f, then rf2-1bign) redacts :exception-message, :exception and :reason only on machine- and flow-owned rows, under its own words "and no wider". So no framework emitter now stamps :rf.error/handler-exception as sensitive, and its text slots leave the box raw even when the handler's registration declares :sensitive paths.

Concrete consequence, reported by rf2-ot1aa's worker: in a sensitive Story variant, a handler's exception text reaches the variant's refusal payload unredacted. Story's stepper_start_cljs_test was reworked to use a caller-supplied stamp, because the framework no longer supplies one.

Options:
- (A) Redact :exception-message and the raw :exception on :rf.error/handler-exception when the handler's registration declares any :sensitive path, or its frame does: the same condition the machine and flow projectors use, keyed by the registration instead of a guessed slice. A small projector in classification.cljc plus Spec 009's row.
- (B) Leave it. Exception text is the author's own code's output, and an author who throws secrets can redact them in the throw. Document in Spec 009 and the privacy docs that handler exception text is not redacted, and point Story's sensitive variants at that.

Recommendation: (A). It matches the machine and flow rule already ruled, keeps the off-box guarantee for a handler that explicitly declared itself sensitive, and costs one projector. (B) is defensible under trust-the-programmer, but it leaves the declared-:sensitive handler as the one owner whose exception text ships raw.

Not decided by anyone yet: this bead holds no worker until Mike rules.
close_reason:
RULING (Mike, 2026-10-20 13:41 AUSEST): closed as minutiae; not actioned.
A handler's exception text keeps its current off-box treatment whether or not the registration declares :sensitive. No code, spec or doc change follows. Per the posture, we trust the programmer and do not litigate every fine detail.
The bead had no dependents.

title: Xray: describe sub schema failures as pass-through
description:

title: Trial: generate the tier, kind, owner and status cells of one spec/API.md table from the manifest
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 a trial: generate the tier, kind, owner and status cells of one shipped-var table in `spec/API.md` from the curated metadata, keeping signatures, notes, examples and planned-API rows authored. Adopt it for the rest only if an ordinary export change then needs fewer hand edits and the diff stays readable.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

- `spec/API.md` has 24 tables with both a Status and a Tier column, and 147 var-rows in them that resolve to a `spec/api-manifest.edn` row. Every such row restates four facts the manifest already holds: M/Fn (`:kind`), Tier (`:tier`), Spec (`:owner`) and Status (`:status`). Those three axes are curated in `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` (`:tier`/`:owner`/`:status`, documented at `:11-22`).
- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/api_md_check.clj` parses the rows back (`parse-var-rows`, `:196`) and grades two of the four: Tier, and the leading M/Fn marker (`reconcile`, `:300`). Status and Spec are not graded, and they have drifted:
  - 11 Status cells differ from `:status`. Most add prose (`spec/API.md:187-190`), but `reg-resource`, `reg-mutation` and `reg-resource-scope` (`:455-459`) say `post-v1 lib (optional capability)` where the manifest says `v1 (optional capability)` (`spec/api-manifest.edn:119-121`).
  - 17 Spec cells differ from `:owner`, nearly all by listing a second spec (`006, 011` at `:248`; `002, 006` at `:263-265`). Yet `spec/API.md:23` says the Spec column names exactly the canonical owner, and that other cross-references go in Notes.
- The M/Fn cell also carries authored detail after the marker: `Var (map)` (`:247`), `Fn (UIx hook)` (`:262`).
- So adding a public var means a metadata entry, a regenerated manifest, and an API.md row restating the same four values by hand.

## Change

- **Trial.** Pick one shipped-var table; the UIx adapter table (`spec/API.md:259-269`, 9 rows) has every case above.
  - Mark the table so `generate!` (`gen.clj:1181`) rewrites its four cells from the manifest, and the drift check fails when the committed table differs.
  - Signature and Notes cells stay authored. An extra spec in a Spec cell moves to Notes, per `spec/API.md:23`.
  - Decide whether a kind parenthetical stays as authored text after the generated marker, or moves into the signature.
  - `api_md_check` keeps grading every table that is not generated.
- **Exit.** Make one ordinary export change against the trial table, such as adding a var, and count the hand edits before and after.
  - If it needs fewer and the diff reads cleanly, adopt the rest in a follow-on bead.
  - If not, keep today's design, revert the trial and record why on the bead.
- Planned-API rows (`post-v1 (planned, …)`) stay authored either way.
- Fix the three resources Status cells in passing, whichever way the trial goes. Check which value is right against Spec 016 first.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/API.md` (the trial table, and `:23` if the Spec-column rule changes) with `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` and the generated `spec/api-manifest.edn`. **Hot zone**: these three are one holding, graded together by the `api-manifest` job (`.github/workflows/lint.yml:624`, the API.md step at `:663`).
- `api_md_check.clj`'s docstring (`:1-70`), if generated tables are skipped.

## Acceptance

- `generate!` rewrites the trial table's four cells, and running it twice changes nothing.
- A planted wrong Tier or Status in the generated table turns the drift check red (planted-fault control; revert).
- `api_md_check` still grades the other tables, and its 50-row floor (`api_md_check.clj:94`) still holds.
- The bead records the before and after hand-edit counts, and the adopt or revert decision.
- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest` green, and the `api-manifest` CI job green.
notes:
== DISPATCHED (mayor), 2026-10-21 18:51:42 AUSEST: worktree api-table-trial, branch worker/api-table-trial, solo. The trial adopts or reverts on the hand-edit count; an adopt means the mayor files the follow-on for the remaining tables. Nobody holds the classifier pair this wave.
== TRIAL RESULT, 2026-10-21 19:20:04 AUSEST (worker api-table-trial, PR #11608): ADOPT.

Premises verified at tip e877a30afe: 24 tables with Status+Tier, 147 var-rows resolving to a manifest row, 11 Status drifts, 17 Spec drifts. Citation shifts: the Spec-column rule is spec/API.md:20 (not :23). The resources Status drift is FOUR cells — resolve-resource-scope (:461) has it too.

Decision: ADOPT — fewer hand edits, and the diff reads cleanly.

FOLLOW-ON (mayor to file): generate the remaining 23 tables. Items the generator refuses today and the follow-on must decide:
(1) Mixed-namespace tables (Resources) need a default namespace plus qualifier resolution — move adapter-aliases into api-md-cells.
(2) Non-var rows inside Tier tables (`— | — | (rf/clear …)`, keyword, configure-key and planned-API rows) must be skipped by the api-md-check rule.
(3) The `M/Fn (CLJS)` dual-kind cell.
(4) 7 Status drifts carrying prose (dispatch, dispatch-sync, subscribe, subscribe-once, reg-sub, register-listener!, unregister-listener!).
(5) 12 Spec drifts: move second specs to Notes; init! (006 vs 002) and configure!/current-config/features (— vs Conventions) need a ruling.
(6) Whether api-md-check stops grading generated tables: its tier and kind checks become redundant, its qualifier check does not.

The UIx adapter table is the trial: it gained a Notes column, and its five second-spec citations moved there as links; the kind parenthetical stays authored after the generated marker. api_md_check is unchanged and still grades every table. title: App-db validation failures redact by the schema-wide rule; the leaf-precise walker grammar retires
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that the app-db leaf in a validation failure trace takes the coarse rule every whole-value slot already uses, `(or schema-has-sensitive? schema-has-opaque-child?)`. That retires the precise per-slot route (`redact-tags-per-slot`) and most of `walker.cljc`'s re-implementation of Malli grammar.

Transient and rejected-value privacy stay, and so do safe path summaries. `:path` stays visible only through declared `:map` keys.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e. The precise route still exists beside the `:schemas/check!` seam and the classification read (`project-through-registry`).

**Two decisions for one trace.** `validate-app-schema!`'s failure arm (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:1018-1224`) computes:
- `leaf-sensitive?`, which is `schema-sensitive-at?` on the failing `:in` (`:1123`). It governs the narrowed `:value` only (`app-db-narrowed-slots`, `:174-179`).
- `whole-sensitive?`, which is `schema-sensitive-at?` with a nil path (`:1124`), i.e. the coarse rule. It governs `:explain`, `:explain-humanized` and the `:sensitive?` stamp.
- `redact-tags-per-slot` (`:237-269`) applies the pair (call at `:1195`). The size arm splits the same way (`leaf-large?` / `whole-large?`, `:1136-1138`).

Every other surface already redacts whole: `redact-tags` (`:190-235`) under the coarse rule (`:717-718`), and the hot-reload violation path (`storage.cljc:527-528`).

**What the precision costs.** `walker.cljc:758-1318` (561 lines) serves only this route:
- `prefix?` (`:758`);
- `align-in-path` (`:796-975`), which aligns Malli's `:in` through collections, regex-sequence widths and ambiguous branch tails;
- `sanitize-sensitive-path` (`:978-1206`), the `:path` scrubber;
- `schema-sensitive-at?` (`:1207-1318`).

Their only callers outside `walker.cljc` are `validate.cljc:1123-1124` and `:1164`, a facade re-export of `schema-sensitive-at?` (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc:63`; `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1431`) and one test (`schemas_failure_paths_test.clj:67`).

**Untouched:** `project-through-registry` (`validate.cljc:275-318`) walks `:value` through the frame's elision registry with `re-frame.elision`'s walker, not this grammar.

## Change

- **One decision.** `:value` takes `whole-sensitive?`, computed as `(or (schema-has-sensitive? schema) (schema-has-opaque-child? schema))`. Replace `redact-tags-per-slot` with `redact-tags`. The size arm takes `whole-large?` for every slot, so a large leaf beside a sensitive sibling redacts (sensitive wins).
- **`:path` summary.** When `whole-sensitive?`, `:path` is the registered path plus the longest prefix of `:in` made of declared `:map` keys (looking through `:maybe`). Every segment after that prefix is `:rf/redacted`. A `:set` element, a `:map-of` key, a closed-map extra key, an index and a branch tail are all covered by that one rule. A non-sensitive failure keeps its raw `:path`, as today.
- **Delete** `align-in-path`, `sanitize-sensitive-path`, `schema-sensitive-at?`, `prefix?`, `index-bearing-ops` and `app-db-narrowed-slots`, plus the per-slot commentary at `validate.cljc:1036-1160`. Keep any helper the extractors (`walk-flags`) still call.
- **Retire** the `re-frame.schemas/schema-sensitive-at?` re-export, with no alias.
- **Stays:** the registry projection, the `:explain` / `:explain-humanized` handling, transient payload redaction on every other `:where`, and the opaque fail-closed posture.
- **`:rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque`** stays, with a narrower reason. It is emitted only from `reg-app-schema` / `reg-app-schemas` (`storage.cljc:645`), and its row names the cost of opacity as "precision and the `:large?` arm". After this change no app-db failure has leaf precision, and sensitive already subsumes large. One cost remains: an opaque schema's failures always redact, even when nothing in it is sensitive. The reason is cut to that.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/010-Schemas.md`:
  - `:383` (the per-slot size decision on app-db);
  - `:420` ("then narrows `:value` to the failing leaf");
  - `:422` (the `:set`-element carve-out becomes the declared-`:map`-key rule);
  - `:171` (`:path` on a sensitive failure).
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2076`, the `:rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque` row: drop the leaf-precise sentence and the precision claim. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1431`: delete the row, then regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn`. **Hot zone** (with `spec/API.md`, which needs no edit).
- `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md`: `:307` (which slots redact) and the `schema-sensitive-at?` entry (`:418-428`).

## Acceptance

Flip or replace these tests in `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/`:
- `schemas_sensitive_test.clj`:
  - `app-db-validation-collection-sibling-narrowed-value-verbatim-whole-explain-redacted` (`:310`): `:value` is `:rf/redacted`, and `:path` keeps only declared map keys.
  - `app-db-validation-scrubs-value-bearing-path-segments` (`:222`): expected paths under the new rule.
  - `app-db-validation-large-leaf-beside-sensitive-sibling-elides` (`:554`): `:value` is `:rf/redacted`.
  - `sanitize-sensitive-path-transparent-through-maybe` (`:90`): rewrite against the new summary.
- `schemas_failure_paths_test.clj`: delete `schema-sensitive-at?-flags-the-leaf-its-ancestors-and-descendants` (`:67`).

Still passing unchanged: `schemas_sensitive_test.clj:344` (non-sensitive closed-map extra key), `:353` (opaque fails closed), `:388` (variable-width sequence) and the registry tests (`:154-221`).

New row: a failing non-sensitive leaf inside a schema that marks a sibling `:sensitive?` shows `:value :rf/redacted`.

Gates green: the security tier's `validation_redaction_invariant_security_cljs_test.cljc`, the JVM schemas suite, `npm run test:cljs`, the `api-manifest` check, `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py`.

title: Epoch: the off-box trace-events projection becomes an allow-list, so an unknown tag ships redacted
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 8fc6369484.

Off-box, an epoch record's `:trace-events` are projected by `elide-trace-events-slot` (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:2288`). It is a chain of carrier-specific passes:
- re-root the `:rf.event/db` slots;
- omit event args (`:rf.event/v` / `:event`);
- omit HTTP response bodies;
- omit resource scope values;
- omit resource trace keys;
- omit resource keys inside fx args;
- omit fx args;
- elide large sub values;
- the bulk `project-egress` walk.

That is a deny-list. A new trace tag that carries a payload ships raw off-box until someone adds an arm for it. The chain has grown one arm per discovered carrier, and the standing rule for gates is the opposite: fail on input you cannot classify.

`:trigger-event` and `:effects` already work the safe way, redacting by default.

rf2-42gpe (in progress) makes the pair MCP ship these projected records instead of dropping flagged ones. So the projection becomes the only thing between a trace tag and an off-box reader.

## Change

- **Allow-list.** Off-box, keep a closed allow-list of tag keys. A value passes only if it also meets a structural shape rule (keywords, numbers, booleans, and collections of those). Redact every other tag value to `:rf/redacted`.
- **Trusted-local is unchanged.**
- **Ids and query vectors carry user values** (`[:user/by-email "a@b"]`), so their args redact: keep the head id, redact the args.
- **Operation-specific entries** go in only where a named consumer needs a structured value. The pair MCP re-derives `:render-events` from projected render tags (`project-dispatch-result-src`, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs:250`), which is the concrete check.
- **Keep the existing egress opt-ins and owner classification:**
  - `:rf.egress/include-sensitive?`;
  - `:rf.egress/include-large?`;
  - `:rf.egress/include-event-args?`;
  - `:rf.egress/include-fx-args?`.
- **Delete the carrier arms the allow-list subsumes.**
- **The rule lives with projection and security** (`re-frame.projection`), not in a second epoch-only privacy API.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` "Redacted slot values". **Hot zone.**
- `spec/Security.md` §Epoch privacy posture.
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, where it describes the off-box trace-events shape. **Hot zone.**

## Acceptance

- An unknown tag carrying a string ships as `:rf/redacted` off-box.
- Query-vector args redact, and their ids survive.
- The pair MCP's `:render-events` derivation is unchanged on a fixture.
- Trusted-local output is byte-identical to today.
- Each existing per-carrier off-box test still passes, or is subsumed by an allow-list test that names the carrier.
- Epoch, security-tier and pair-MCP suites green, plus `npm run test:cljs`.

## Sequencing

Hot zones: `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, `spec/Tool-Pair.md`. Start after rf2-42gpe merges, since both change what the pair MCP ships from epoch records.

Effort M, risk medium: it changes the off-box shape only, and fail-closed is the safe direction.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): Phase 0a census instruments (parsed census, graph walk, duplicate census) are not required to be committed, so per-unit checks and the post-sweep reconciliation cannot re-run the plan's counts
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md §Step 5, The per-rule completeness gate, item 4 (around line 131).
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md §5, first consequence (line 101).

## What it says

- inventory-and-plan Step 5 item 4: "A raw zero is not evidence (item 2); the search record on the rule's line is". A disposition "names the surfaces the rule lists, the searches that covered them". The leaf never says to keep the instrument that produced a count.
- orchestrating §5: "Judge a unit on whether it applied every rule its files trip (the inventory says which)".

## What happened (generic)

Several Phase 0a counts come from an instrument, not from a one-line `rg`:

- a parsed census that tells a render-time read from a callback read (rf2-q84e5);
- a loaded require-graph walk (rf2-9v16x);
- a duplicate-registration census (rf2-soqmk);
- a reconciled codemod or lexical count.

The plan records the instrument's output, and nothing asks for the instrument itself to be kept.

Two later checks need to re-run exactly that instrument:

- the per-unit judgement in orchestrating §5, where a unit's files should drop to zero for its rules;
- the post-sweep reconciliation.

When the instrument lived only in the planning session, both checks get rebuilt by hand. A rebuilt instrument counts differently, so a residual site and an instrument difference look the same. The boot unit of a ~170-file migration reported exactly this: the per-unit gates written against the plan's census sections could not be run as written, because the census instruments had not been committed.

## Evidence

- `grep -n -i 'census\|script\|instrument\|re-run' skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md` gives three hits, and none asks for an instrument to be kept. :64 and :125 are about a migration re-run's stale build output, and :79 matches "subscription". Control: `grep -c -i registration` on the same file gives 10.
- `grep -rn -i 'census' skills/re-frame-migration/` finds only:
  - auto-call-site-rewrites.md:544 and :548, and breaking-changes.md:170. These are the M-73 codemod, which ships with the corpus and so can be re-run.
  - causal-world-inputs.md:54.

## Suggested change

Add one rule to Step 5's record, and point to it from orchestrating §5:

> Every count in the plan must be reproducible. Record a search as its exact command. Commit any instrument that is not a single command (a parsed census, a graph walk, a duplicate census) with the plan, at a tracked path, together with the count it produced. Per-unit checks and the post-sweep reconciliation re-run that same instrument, scoped to the unit's files, and compare against the plan's count.

title: docs(migration): corpus M-59 and the M-19 unwrap note omit v1 unwrap's version-dependent shape check and the :after restore a project unwrap needs
description:
The migration skill's M-59 row (skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md) now teaches two points about v1 `unwrap` that the corpus does not carry.

## Where

migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:
- "M-59. `at-boundary` / `unwrap` interceptor values -> ..." (its "`unwrap` -> handler destructuring" part).
- The M-19 note "v1 prior art — `unwrap` and `trim-v`", whose item 1 says every dispatch for an `unwrap` id "has to be" `[<id> <map>]` because "v1 `unwrap` would have thrown otherwise".

## The two points, verified at source

1. The shape check depends on the v1 version. In the published re-frame jars, `re_frame/std_interceptors.cljc` `unwrap` `:before` behaves as follows. 1.4.3 throws `ex-info` when `(and (= 2 (count event)) (map? payload))` is false. 1.2.0 and 1.3.0 run the same test, call `(console :warn ...)`, and return the context unchanged, so the handler gets the event without the reshape. re-frame's own 1.4.0 release note (PR 763) records the switch from warning to throwing, and `git show v1.1.2:src/re_frame/std_interceptors.cljc` (the release that introduced `unwrap`) warns. So the M-19 note's "would have thrown otherwise" holds from 1.4.0 only. On 1.1.2 to 1.3.x, a malformed dispatch only warned. Plain destructuring drops the check either way: `[:id]` and `[:id "x"]` bind nils, and `[:id {...} :extra]` drops the extra.
2. A project-authored `:app/unwrap` must restore `:event`. v1's `unwrap` `:after` restores `:event` from `:original-event`, which v1 seeds when it builds the context. re-frame2 keeps no original event: `original-event` gets 0 hits under implementation/. The v2 router also reads `:event` from the finished context to attribute the event's trace (router.cljc, `emit-event (rf.interceptor/get-coeffect ctx :event)` followed by `(some-> emit-event first)`). So an interceptor that reshapes `:event` in its `:before` and has no `:after` leaves outer interceptors and the trace seeing the payload map.

## Suggested change

In M-59's `unwrap` part, add the per-site question the skill row now asks: does every dispatcher send `[id map]`? Where one may not, keep the check as an event `:schema` on the registration, with `:boundary? true` for production. Also state that a project `:app/unwrap` restores `:event` in its own `:after`. Correct the M-19 note's "would have thrown otherwise" to name 1.4.0. This is the corpus half of rf2-u71i2's suggested change. That bead's write scope was the skill only, and this file is a hot-zone file.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): the smoke-test done-bar demands a clean boot trace and :rf.warning scan with no rule for expected diagnostics: a preserved v1 bug v2 makes loud, or a dev advisory the app triggers by design
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/runtime-smoke-test.md: loop step 7 (line 36) and the done line (line 39).

## What it says

- :36: "**Scan the dev trace** for any `:rf.error/*` / `:rf.warning/*` emitted during boot".
- :39: "This loop is done when it comes back clean: … a clean boot trace".
- The leaf has no rule for an expected diagnostic. A search for allowlist, "expected warning" and baseline finds only :9 ("re-baselines counts (M-12)").

## What happened (generic)

Two classes of diagnostic make "clean" unreachable in a behaviour-preserving migration.

1. **A v1 bug the migration must keep, which v2 reports.** Example: an event id written as an `:fx` row key. v1 warned on the console and skipped the row. v2 emits `:rf.error/no-such-fx` when the row runs (MIGRATION.md §M-8 :398: "An unregistered fx id inside `:fx` is not silent — it emits `:rf.error/no-such-fx` when the entry runs"). Fixing the bug changes behaviour, and keeping it fails the done-bar.
2. **A dev-only advisory the app triggers by design.** `:rf.warning/non-serialisable-event-payload` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/router/diagnostics.cljc:275-297: "Advisory: the dispatch proceeds. Dev-only, gated wholesale") fires for every dispatch whose payload carries a host value. A `js/File` from a file input, a Blob, or an atom all trigger it, and upload and import flows carry those legitimately.

With no rule for these, a migrator does one of three wrong things: fixes the kept bug (a silent behaviour change), restructures the payload (a redesign), or calls the scan clean anyway.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- Observed on a ~170-file app's convergence smoke checklist, which had to carry both classes.

## Suggested change

Add a named-exceptions rule to the done line. An expected diagnostic passes only when it is listed with:

- its id;
- the site that triggers it;
- the reason: either preserved v1 behaviour, naming the item that owns that decision, or an advisory the design accepts;
- a deliberate trigger in the smoke, so the entry is shown to be the only cause.

Anything not on the list still fails the scan. A listed entry is never counted as a regression, and never passes silently.
