title: skill(re-frame-migration, re-frame2 testing): neither leaf says the reset fixture's ambient frame mints :live (no preset), so after M-72 adds a recordable generator a migrator cannot tell whether existing tests break; only :preset :test frames are strict
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective. This is a suggestion, not a work order. Verified at origin/main bafbe4028e.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/causal-world-inputs.md, the "Generated identity (UUID)" bullet (line 127).
- skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md §Pinning recordable coeffects: `:rf.cofx` in dispatch opts (lines 108-128).

## What it says

- causal-world-inputs.md:127: "In live mode an absent declared fact is generated at processing-start and recorded in `:rf.cofx` … Strict mode (including the `:test` frame preset) rejects an absent fact with `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx`, so deterministic tests supply it."
- testing.md:110: "a test pins those inputs by passing `:rf.cofx` in the dispatch opts". The only unpinned behaviour it describes is for `:rf/time-ms` (:128: "omit it and the runtime stamps the wall clock at dispatch").

Neither leaf says which policy the standard test frame uses.

## What happened (generic)

When M-72 moves a handler's `random-uuid` into a recordable generator, the migrator has to know what the change does to the existing tests that dispatch that event. :127 names only strict mode and the `:test` preset, which suggests that tests run strict and will now fail with `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx`.

The standard test frame is not strict. The reset fixture seats `:rf/default` with no preset and no mint policy, so the router's `:live` default applies and the generator mints a fresh value on each run. Existing tests keep passing unchanged. A test that asserts the exact value has to pin it in `:rf.cofx`. Only a test on a frame made with `:preset :test` fails with `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx`.

Neither leaf says this, so the migrator has to read the source to find out. Observed on a ~170-file app, in a unit that moved handler-minted ids to recordable generators.

## Evidence

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:4572-4583, `ensure-default-frame!`: `(upsert-frame! :rf/default {:doc "Test-fixture app frame …"})`. It sets no `:preset` and no `:rf.cofx/mint-policy`. test_support.cljc:413 calls it.
- "mint" and "preset" each have 0 hits in test_support.cljc. Control: `ensure-default-frame!` has 1 hit.
- cofx.cljc:953-963: `default-mint-policy` is `:live`. cofx.cljc:965-984: `resolve-mint-policy` takes the per-call opt, then the frame config, then `:live`.
- frame.cljc:2276-2292: only the `:test` preset sets `:rf.cofx/mint-policy :strict`.
- `grep -rn -i mint` over both skills finds only the generic ladder (causal-world-inputs.md:110/:113/:127, re-frame2 fundamentals/cofx.md:62/:84/:109/:140/:212). `grep -n -i "strict|:live|missing-required-cofx|:preset"` over testing.md finds 0 hits.

## Suggested change

In causal-world-inputs.md:127 and testing.md §Pinning, add: "The reset fixture's ambient frame (`:rf/default`) has no preset, so it mints `:live`: a declared-absent generator fact is generated fresh on each run, and existing tests that dispatch the event keep passing. A test that asserts the value must pin it in `:rf.cofx`. A frame made with `:preset :test` is `:strict`. There, a test fails with `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx` until it supplies the fact, or until it opts back in with `{:rf.cofx/mint-policy :live}`."

Add a step to M-72's per-handler checklist: after converting a handler, check its tests for exact-value assertions and for frames made with `:preset :test`.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): the M-72 index row and the corpus's What-to-look-for list only cofx-shaped triggers, so a Step-5 census misses direct random-uuid / js/Date.now reads in handler bodies and their callees

comments.text:
From a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (pass 7). This is a suggestion, not a work order. Verified at origin/main bafbe4028e.

There is further evidence for the callee half of this item's trigger text ("in a reg-event* body or in a fn it calls … its callee walk").

causal-world-inputs.md:54 says: "The patterns match direct calls only." :67 says: "So follow the calls each handler, reducer, machine action and guard makes back to their source." That describes a top-down walk with no procedure. On the same ~170-file app, a unit worker grepping its own files counted zero, because the mint sat behind a helper in another namespace.

Suggestion: make the walk mechanical and bottom-up, and name it where this item's new trigger text points:

1. Run the §Identify greps project-wide.
2. For each accepted hit, name the top-level fn that encloses it.
3. Grep that fn's call sites, resolving aliases through each ns form, and repeat until no new fn appears.
4. Every reg-event* body, machine action or guard that the walk reaches is a site. It belongs to the unit that owns the handler.

Record the walk's output in the census, so per-unit gates can re-run it (see rf2-unsl1). A hit inside a recordable `reg-cofx` supplier is the recorded generator, not a site (rf2-bo73l).

title: Windows Store-alias python: test:scripts reds on four files that launch a bare python/python3 (check_modules_compile.cjs, preflight-story/xray-package.sh, rewrite-local-root-coord.sh)
description:
On a Windows host whose `python` and `python3` are the Microsoft Store app-execution aliases (exit 9009 to a spawning process, 49 through a shell), `npm run test:scripts` goes red on four files. The fast-PR spine runs that lane on any diff touching a `.cjs`/`.mjs`/`.js` file or a package manifest, so it reds there before it reaches its fresco steps. All four have the same cause rf2-syytn fixed for the fresco npm scripts: a bare interpreter name.

Measured 2026-10-29 on `worker/fresco-python` (rf2-syytn, PR #11716), `test:scripts` tests 85 / pass 81 / fail 4:

- npm run test:scripts: 85/81/4, exit 1 before (9009 from the roster spawn; "rewrite of '../../core' aborted (exit 49)"). 85/85/0, exit 0 after.
- npm run test:fresco-compile: exit 0 (11 namespaces, both passes).
- scripts/test-fast-pr.sh: exit 0, PASS fast PR spine. Its --repo-root was a scratch repo whose diff adds implementation/package.json, so the plan read "scripts cljs". It reached the fresco invariants and fresco lint export gates, both green, with no PATH shim.

title: senior review: core: public API facade, classification, privacy and test support
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/ — core, every core_* facade namespace, classification, elision, privacy, recordable, path, spec, features, conformance, test_support, test_helpers
- implementation/core/resources/, implementation/core/deps.edn, and the tests for the above

FOCUS: The re-frame.core surface as a programmer meets it (spec/API.md), static data classification and egress elision (Spec 015, Privacy), and the test-support API (Spec 008).

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.
notes:
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 10:22:49 AUSEST, trunk 9657b27a5d)

Slice read at 795c61b924; the only commit since is a beads checkpoint (no implementation/core or spec change). Ten findings, most important first. Behaviour claims were confirmed in ONE JVM probe on core's :test classpath (clojure -M:test plus a script alias, exit 0); each probe line below has a control beside it.

1. implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:856-869 — `assert-path-equals` passes on a frame that does not exist.
   Quote: `actual   (get-in (rf.frame/frame-app-db-value frame-id) path)`
   What: `frame-app-db-value` returns nil for an unknown or destroyed frame id, and nil when no scope is established (`resolve-frame` -> nil). So `(= expected nil)` reports :pass whenever the expectation is nil.
   Cost: the common "token was cleared" / "error is gone" assertion `(ts/assert-path-equals [:session :token] nil {:frame :test/autth})` stays green on a typo'd frame id, a destroyed frame or a missing fixture scope. It is a test that cannot go red, in the helper Spec 008 names as the state-assertion surface.
   Fix: when `frame-id` names no live frame (`(rf.frame/frame frame-id)` is nil), report :fail with a message naming the frame and return false. Add a deftest beside `assert-path-equals-frame-opt` in test_support_test.clj.
   Size S. verified: probe 1a, a typo frame with a nil expectation, reports [:pass]. Controls: 1b, the live frame with a wrong value, reports [:fail]; 1c, the live frame with the right value, reports [:pass]. Lens: test rigour / correctness.

2. implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:620 (the `reg-mutation` macro docstring) and :361 (its CLJS fn-alias docstring) — both list `:retry` as an optional metadata key.
   Quote: "`:populates` / `:scope` / `:invalidate-timing` / `:retry`"
   What: `:retry` is not a mutation metadata key. resources/mutation_registry.cljc `mutation-metadata-keys` leaves it out on purpose ("it rides the managed-HTTP args"). core_resources.cljc:65-66 and API.md (the request-decoration row) both say the request fn returns `:retry`.
   Cost: a programmer, or the AI they use, reads `rf/reg-mutation`'s docstring, puts `:retry` in metadata, gets one dev warning and no retries.
   Fix: drop `:retry` from both lists and add the core_resources sentence ("write retries are opt-in: the request fn returns `:retry` in its managed-HTTP args").
   Size S. verified: probe 4a, `reg-mutation` with `{:params-schema [:map] :retry {…}}`, emits `:rf.warning/unknown-registration-key` with `:unknown-keys [:retry]`. Control 4b, the same call with `:doc` only, emits 0 such warnings. Lens: ergonomics / docstrings.

3. implementation/core/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2/config.edn:80-85 — there is no hook for `re-frame.test-support/with-emit-recorder!`.
   Quote: `re-frame.test-support/with-trace-recorder!   hooks.re-frame.core/with-trace-recorder!` (the only test-support entry)
   What: `with-emit-recorder!` has exactly `with-trace-recorder!`'s shape, `[recs-sym opts?] body+`, and is on Spec 008's normative test-support list. Without a hook, every consumer, this repo included, sees "Unresolved symbol" for the recorder binding.
   Fix: add `re-frame.test-support/with-emit-recorder! hooks.re-frame.core/with-trace-recorder!`. The existing hook names no macro and rewrites to `(let [sym (atom [])] opts? body+)`, which fits as-is. Then extend kondo_export_test.clj so every let-shaped test-support bracket must have a hook.
   Size S. verified: `clj-kondo --cache false --lint` on install_frame_state_cljs_test.cljc and emit_recorder_bracket_cljs_test.cljc exits 2 with exactly two warnings, "Unresolved symbol: errs" (line 81) and "raw" (line 45). Control: the same file's `(with-trace-recorder! [traces …])` at lines 123/126 is not flagged. Lens: ergonomics.

title: senior review: schemas and spec-resource
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- implementation/schemas/**
- implementation/spec-resource/**

FOCUS: Schema validation boundaries and their production elision (Spec 010), and the build-time spec-resource dependency recorder.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.

== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 15:34:30 AUSEST, trunk 317d064e9c)

Slice: implementation/schemas/** and implementation/spec-resource/**. Read in full: all seven schemas source namespaces, spec_resource.clj, both deps.edn, and the tests listed under "looked at and sound", against Spec 010 (whole), the Spec 009 :rf.schema/violation row and core's re-frame.classification/project-trace-event. The slice's files are byte-identical between ac07b2bc19 (review start) and 317d064e9c, so every path:line below holds at 317d064e9c.

Six findings: 2 correctness (privacy egress), 1 simplicity/test-rigour, 3 docs. All size S, all verified.

--- 1. :rf.schema/violation ships a reg-classification-sensitive live value verbatim (correctness / privacy; S; verified)

Place: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:523-534, in maybe-emit-schema-violation!: `(let [sensitive? (or (rf.schemas.walker/schema-has-sensitive? new-schema) ...` and then `:mismatching-value (if sensitive? redacted-sentinel live-value)`.

Defect: the violation trace decides redaction from the schema's own :sensitive? marks only. It never projects the live value through the frame's classification. Core's trace chokepoint (re-frame.classification/project-trace-event) has no arm for this op or for the :mismatching-value slot either. Spec 010 §`:sensitive?` says an app-db path is declared sensitive once, by classification, and that the one declaration covers the path's validation-failure traces as well as its egress. The dispatch-time failure honours that (validate.cljc project-through-classification). The registration-time violation does not.

Measured with a JVM probe on the schemas :test classpath, exit 0 at both ac07b2bc19 and 317d064e9c:
  (rf/reg-classification :auth {:sensitive [[:auth :token]]})
  (rf/reg-app-schema [:auth] [:map [:token :string]])
  ;; live app-db {:auth {:token "SECRET-1"}}, then
  (rf/reg-app-schema [:auth] [:map [:token :int]])
  => one :rf.schema/violation, :mismatching-value {:token "SECRET-1"}, top-level :sensitive? nil
  Control, same frame and path: an event writing "SECRET-2" there gives :rf.error/schema-validation-failure with :value :rf/redacted and :explain :rf/redacted, and "SECRET-2" appears nowhere in the trace.

Cost: hot-reloading or first-registering a schema over live state puts a classified credential or PII value onto the dev trace bus verbatim. That bus feeds Xray, epochs and the pair/MCP tools.

Fix: in maybe-emit-schema-violation!, walk the live value the way project-through-classification walks :value: `(rf.elision/elide-wire-value live-value {:frame frame-id :path path})`. Stamp :sensitive? true when the walk changed the value, and let a :large classification produce its size marker. The schema-side `(or schema-has-sensitive? schema-has-opaque-child?)` arm stays. Add a classification case beside violation-redacts-mismatching-value-when-new-schema-sensitive (schemas_reg_side_effects_test.clj). While there, fix the comment block at storage.cljc:461-473. It names the validate posture as `(or schema-has-sensitive? schema-opaque?)`, but the code (and validate.cljc) use schema-has-opaque-child?. (Alternative home for the projection: a :rf.schema/violation arm in core's project-trace-event, owned by rf2-r5cc2.5. The in-slice fix is smaller and keeps the decision next to the schema-side one.)

--- 2. Under classification-only sensitivity, an app-db failure's :path and :reason carry :map-of keys and :set elements verbatim (correctness / privacy; S; verified)

Place: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:967-981 in validate-app-schema!. `trace-in-path (if (and in-path sensitive?) ... declared-key-prefix ...)`, where `sensitive?` is the schema-side decision only. project-through-classification (validate.cljc:218-255) then redacts :value / :explain and stamps :sensitive? true, but never touches :path, and :reason was already built from the raw trace-path.

Defect: Spec 010 §`:sensitive?` "One carve-out — :path past the declared keys" exists because Malli's :in carries caller data (a :set element, a :map-of key, a closed map's extra key). The carve-out runs only when the SCHEMA marks the slot sensitive. The same Spec makes classification the primary way an app-db path is declared sensitive.

Measured (JVM probe, exit 0 at both shas):
  (rf/reg-classification :users {:sensitive [[:users]]})
  (rf/reg-app-schema [:users] [:map-of :keyword :int]) ; event writes {:users {"alice-SECRET@example.com" 1}}
  => :sensitive? true, :value :rf/redacted, :explain :rf/redacted, but
     :path [:users "alice-SECRET@example.com"] and
     :reason "App-db at path [:users \"alice-SECRET@example.com\"] failed schema [:map-of :keyword :int], got string."
  The same with a :set: classification [[:auth :codes]], schema [:map [:codes [:set :int]]], write #{"SECRET-CODE"} => :path [:auth :codes "SECRET-CODE"], and :reason carries it too.
  Control: the same :map-of with a schema-side {:sensitive? true} gives :path [:users :rf/redacted], with no leak.

Cost: the trace says :sensitive? true, so consumers trust it, but the email or token still rides in :path and :reason to every listener.

Fix: decide classification sensitivity before building the path. Lift the `sensitive?` computation out of project-through-classification into a helper. Build trace-in-path, and so :reason, under `(or schema-sensitive? classification-sensitive?)`, keeping the declared-key-prefix rule unchanged. Add the two classification shapes above to app-db-validation-sensitive-path-keeps-declared-map-keys (schemas_sensitive_test.clj). Its existing classification test (:145) uses a declared :map key, so it cannot see this.

--- 3. The validator-call path has a dead entry point and tests named for a seam they do not reach (simplicity + test rigour; S; verified)

Place: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:610-622 `(defn validate-with-registered-fn` and implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:374-382 `(defn run-validator`.

Defect: neither has a production caller. Census over implementation/ and tools/: validate-with-registered-fn appears only at its definition and in 6 test call sites; run-validator's only caller is validate-with-registered-fn. Control: the same census found those 6 test hits. The three real validation sites each deref the atom and catch the throw themselves: storage.cljc:498 `(when-let [validate-fn @rf.schemas.validator/validator-fn]`, validate.cljc:763 (check!) and validate.cljc:887 (validate-app-schema!). That makes four spellings of "call the validator". Two tests pin the dead fn under names that claim the boundary seam: schemas_test.clj:261 `validate-with-registered-fn-bypasses-debug-gate` ("the boundary seam routes through the registered validator even with debug-enabled? false") and schemas_fail_open_test.clj:79 `boundary-seam-malformed-schema-returns-false`. The :boundary? true check goes through check! (the :schemas/check! hook), so these two cannot go red on a boundary regression and read as coverage that is not there. Relatedly, the facade comment at schemas.cljc:29 says "Validator atoms stay private to their owning namespace", but they are public defonce vars read from storage and validate. Spec 010 §Test-support says they are private.

Fix: delete validate-with-registered-fn and run-validator. Route the three derefs through one validator.cljc accessor (or validate-entry-result), and mark the atoms ^:private so the comment and Spec become true. Re-point the two tests at check!: one JVM case of check! under `(with-redefs [rf.interop/debug-enabled? false] ...)`, asserting the verdict is returned without tags, and the malformed case through check!'s :rf.error/malformed-schema category. Existing check! coverage: schemas_check_seam_test.clj, plus schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs for the :advanced arm.

--- 4. set-schema-fns! tells port authors the validator never runs in production (docs, misleads a programmer; S; verified)

Place: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:301-306: "every call site is already gated on `debug-enabled?`, so the validator's body is unreachable in `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false` builds."

Defect: false. check! (validate.cljc:762-774) calls the validator with no debug gate. Spec 010 §Production builds says the :boundary? true check "is ungated", and recordable-coeffect and route/resource-param checks also validate in release builds.

Cost: a port author who believes this may write a validator that leans on dev-only code (malli.error, a dev registry, a debug-gated helper). It then breaks only in production, and only on boundary or cofx traffic.

Fix: state the real contract. The validator is pure, and it runs in production for the always-on checks (boundary, recordable cofx, route/resource params), so it must be production-safe. Every other site elides. This is Spec 010 §Locked rules with its "subject to the boundary-validation override" clause kept.

--- 5. Stale spec line-number pointers and two mislabels in docstrings (docs; S; verified)

Place and defect:
- "Spec 010 §Schema digest line 491" appears 4 times: digest.cljc:9, validator.cljc:38, validator.cljc:256 and validator.cljc:415. Line 491 of spec/010-Schemas.md is inside the §Schemas resolve through the frame's images code block. The schema-print contract is §Schema digest / §Digest algorithm step 1.
- "per Spec 010 L145" at schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs:44. Line 145 is the open-vs-closed-maps paragraph.
- digest.cljc:11 sends the reader to "re-frame.schemas.validator/printer-fn", the atom Spec 010 calls private, instead of set-schema-fns!'s :print.
- schemas.cljc:8 calls :boundary? true "the boundary interceptor". Spec 010 §Boundary-validation interceptor naming rules that it is not an interceptor.

How the census was run: a regex for `line NNN` / `LNNN` over both slice trees. Control: it found the known "line 491" occurrences. It found exactly these five.

Fix: replace each line number with the section name (§Digest algorithm, §Production builds). Point digest.cljc at set-schema-fns! :print. Say "the :boundary? true check".

--- 6. spec-resource's :test alias claims a naive-shape control the test does not run (docs / test rigour; S; verified)

Place: implementation/spec-resource/deps.edn:23-26: "It drives the shipped resolver and the naive `requiring-resolve` shape from two threads". The test (spec_resource_test.clj:119-123) drives only resolve-after-require.

Defect: the shipped-fn assertion is sound. It requires :during-load ::blocked, which a regression to the naive shape never reaches. But nothing proves the fixture still reproduces the race, so a fixture change that closed the window would leave the test green and the comment wrong. Measured, by running the test namespace's own :once fixture around its observe-resolver-during-load (exit 0):
  requiring-resolve => {:during-load {:state :unbound}, :observer-result {:state :unbound}, :loader-result {:state :bound}}
  resolve-after-require => {:during-load ::blocked, :observer-result {:state :bound}, :loader-result {:state :bound}}
So the control is one assertion away.

Fix: add `(is (= {:state :unbound} (:during-load (observe-resolver-during-load requiring-resolve))))` beside the shipped-fn test, which makes the comment true. Or, failing that, reword the comment.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): no way to see past a mid-sweep compile's first missing namespace; a test build's :ns-regexp can be narrowed with --config-merge, and requires checked against the resolved classpath
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md §5 "The all-or-nothing single compile gate" (lines 95-104).
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md, the opening "whack-a-mole" paragraph (line 7).

## What it says

- inventory-and-plan.md:7: "A compile reaches those breakages **one namespace at a time** — so a 'swap the coord, compile, fix the first error, recompile, fix the next' loop turns into whack-a-mole". The remedy offered is the up-front inventory scan.
- §5 :102: "Errors surface together; trace each to its unit, fix, recompile the whole tree."

## What happened (generic)

Mid-sweep errors do not surface together. shadow-cljs stops at the first namespace it cannot resolve, so an early or consolidated compile shows one missing namespace per run. In a fan-out, the owner of the next error can only be found after the first error is fixed, and that fix is an edit to somebody's source.

Two source-free instruments got past this on a ~170-file app:

1. **Narrow a test build with `--config-merge`.** Test targets (`:browser-test`, `:node-test`, `:karma`) select their namespaces by `:ns-regexp`. Running `shadow-cljs compile <build> --config-merge <file.edn>`, with the file holding `{:ns-regexp "<a regexp that excludes the failing test ns>"}`, compiles the rest and shows the next error. Unlike the vector `:entries` in rf2-irzfr, a string survives shadow's deep-merge: it replaces the old value.
2. **Check every require against the resolved classpath before compiling.** Resolve each `:require` of the migrated tree against the build's classpath: the tools.deps classpath file under `.cpcache/`, or `clojure -Spath`. That lists every missing namespace in one pass, with its requiring file and so its owning unit.

Gotchas seen while doing it:

- On Windows the shadow-cljs CLI started clojure through PowerShell, so the EDN had to be passed as a file, not inline.
- EDN strings reject the escape `\.`, so the regexp needs `[.]` for a literal dot.
- shadow exited 0 on an option-parse error, so check the output for "Build completed", not the exit code.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- shadow-cljs 3.4.12, shadow/build/api.clj `deep-merge`: two vectors are `(->> (concat a b) (distinct) (into []))`, but `(string? b) b`, so a string is replaced.
- `git grep -n -i -E "config-merge|ns-regexp|cpcache"` over skills/re-frame-migration finds nothing. The control `shadow-cljs` finds hits in the same tree (SKILL.md, floor-gate.md and others).
- Observed on a ~170-file app during an early combined compile (see rf2-yk4lx).

## Suggested change

Add a short "Seeing past the first missing namespace" note to §5, and cross-link it from inventory-and-plan.md:7. It should give the two instruments above with their gotchas, and say that, without one of them, the consolidated gate is a series of compiles, one missing namespace at a time.

Related: rf2-irzfr (--config-merge cannot swap :entries) and rf2-yk4lx (early convergence probe).

title: senior review: machines-viz
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- tools/machines-viz/**

FOCUS: The state-machine visualiser: model extraction, layout, rendering.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.

== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 18:49:17 AUSEST, trunk 735d02394f)

Slice: tools/machines-viz/** (src, page, test, spec, README, deps/shadow config, public/viewer.html, scripts). Read-only review against tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md and spec/Principles.md. 7 findings. By lens: 2 correctness (1, 2), 2 ergonomics (3, 5), 2 simplicity (4, 6), 1 comments/docs (7). By size: 2 M (1, 7), 5 S.

1. Click payloads lose their keywords crossing clj->js, so the Xray on-chart simulator's click-to-send cannot step. [Lens 1 correctness · M · verified at source, not run end-to-end]
   Place: chart/projection.cljc:1854 `:eventId     event-id` (a keyword) and :1458-1459 `:path (:path n)`, then chart.cljs:1167 `:js-nodes (clj->js nodes)`. The renderers read the converted values back: chart/edges.cljs:524 and chart/nodes/event_node.cljs:279 `(on-click #js {:eventId  event-id ...})`, chart/nodes.cljs:425 `(on-click (js->clj path))`.
   Defect: cljs.core/clj->js turns every keyword VALUE into `(keyword-fn x)`, default `name` (read in clojurescript-1.12.145.jar cljs/core.cljs `defn clj->js`). So `:on-edge-click` gets `eventId "login"` for `:auth/login`, and `fromPath` / `toPath` and the `:on-state-click` path arrive as vectors of bare strings. The namespace is gone and the type has changed. The DOM suite pins the string form: chart/chart_dom_cljs_test.cljs:538 expects `[["authenticated"] ["unauth"] ["authenticated" "browsing"]]`.
   Cost: Xray's sim reads `(aget payload "eventId")` (tools/xray/.../static/machines/sim.cljs:888) and hands it to `edge-click->event`, which returns nil unless the value is `(keyword? event-id)` (sim_helpers.cljc:685). So every on-chart edge click is a no-op. Xray's own test (sim_cljs_test.cljs:291) dispatches `:event-id :start` directly, which skips the chart, and no machines-viz DOM test clicks an event node. That is why it is green. A third-party host also gets an ambiguous path for namespaced state ids.
   Fix: build the payload from CLJS values at projection time, so nothing renderer-facing goes through clj->js. One way is for the projector to thread `:onClick (when on-edge-click (fn [] (on-edge-click #js {:eventId event-id :fromPath from-path :toPath to-path})))` (and the same for the state path), with the renderers calling `(on-click)`. This keeps the documented JS-object shape with keyword values. It also drops the callbacks out of `cache-key` (chart.cljs:1552-1555), so an inline host fn no longer re-projects and re-marshals the graph. Then add a DOM test that clicks an event node of a machine with a namespaced event and asserts the keyword. Update API.md :63 if the payload shape changes.

2. Context-band redaction fails OPEN when the classification is not a set. [Lens 1 correctness, privacy boundary · S · verified by JVM REPL]
   Place: chart/context_redaction.cljc:95-98 `(defn- classifies? [ks k] (or (contains? ks k) (contains? ks whole-data)))`.
   Defect: `contains?` on a vector tests INDEX membership. So `:context-band-sensitive [:token]` redacts nothing, and the live value is painted and then serialised into the SVG / PNG / clipboard export. In CLJS a list fails open the same way. On the JVM a list throws.
   Evidence (REPL from a scratch dir, src on :paths): `{:sensitive #{:token}}` -> `{:token :rf/redacted, :n 1}` (control); `{:sensitive [:token]}` -> `{:token "s3cret", :n 1}`; `{:sensitive '(:token)}` -> IllegalArgumentException "contains? not supported on type: clojure.lang.PersistentList".
   Cost: a host that hand-writes the prop as a vector (the natural EDN spelling of "these keys") leaks exactly the slots it marked sensitive, and nothing warns it.
   Fix: coerce once at the boundary, e.g. `(set sensitive)` / `(set large)` in `redact-value`'s destructure or in `redact-context`. Then any collection classifies, and the `derive-classification` sets are unchanged. Add the vector case to chart/context_redaction_cljs_test.cljc.

3. The viewer page renders only the hash it loaded with. [Lens 3 ergonomics · S · verified at source]
   Place: page/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/viewer.cljs:169 `(defn ^:export run ...)` decodes `location.href` once. Nothing in tools/machines-viz registers `hashchange`: a search for hashchange|onhashchange|popstate returned zero hits, with `location` in viewer.cljs (7 hits) as the control.
   Cost: pasting a second share-URL for the same viewer into an open viewer tab is a same-document fragment navigation. The browser does not reload, so the tab keeps showing the PREVIOUS machine under the new URL, which is a silently wrong chart. API.md:1622 says "On page load", so the code matches the spec. The edge is in the spec too.
   Fix: in `run`, add `(.addEventListener js/window "hashchange" run)` once (guarded the way `app-root` already is). `run` re-renders the root idempotently. Note it in API.md §Read-only viewer.

4. `share/value-free-summary` is a byte-for-byte re-implementation of core's `re-frame.error/diag-value-summary`, and `grammar/definition-summary` repeats the same arms a third time. [Lens 2 simplicity · S · verified at source]
   Place: share.cljs:500-565 (`defn- value-free-summary`, 13 arms in the same order as implementation/core/src/re_frame/error.cljc:341-354), and grammar.cljc:391-410 (the non-map arms of `definition-summary`).

The share docstring calls itself "an INDEPENDENT implementation rather than a mirror", and that independence buys nothing. share.cljs already requires `re-frame.error :as rf.error`, and core is a declared dep of this artefact.
   Fix: share calls `rf.error/diag-value-summary`. grammar's map arm becomes `(merge (rf.error/diag-value-summary d) {:parallel … :state-count … :region-count …})`, with its other arms deleted. grammar's "requires only clojure.string" note is about staying off the machines ENGINE, and requiring core's error ns does not change that. Keep the existing summary-shape tests as the pin.

5. The three placeholder states ignore `:theme`. [Lens 3 ergonomics · S · verified at source]
   Place: chart.cljs:1427-1496. The no-definition, invalid-definition and empty divs style off `tokens/tokens` (lines 1438-1440, 1474-1476, 1495), which is the dark-palette alias (theme/tokens.cljc:179). The resolved `theme-palette` is only computed later, in the `:else` branch (:1518).

   Fix: resolve `theme-palette` before the `cond` and render all three through one `(placeholder testid-suffix aria-label text palette)` helper.

6. The React bridge hand-feeds Reagent's internal `argv` prop when `r/as-element` is the public API for the same element. [Lens 2 simplicity · S · probable]

title: resources: should the coarse :sensitive? claim cover a cache entry's :error, :refresh-error, :page-error and cursors, not only :data?
description:
Spec 015 §Subsystem projection-relative classification (the `reg-resource` row) and Spec 016 §Resource registration spec both say a resource's coarse `:sensitive?` / `:large?` claim lowers onto the cache entry's whole `:data` ("a coarse `:sensitive?` / `:large?` claim as the entry's whole `:data`"), and implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/classification.cljc `instance-declaration-paths` does exactly that. So the entry's other value-bearing slots — `:error`, `:refresh-error`, `:page-error`, `:next-page-param`, `:page-params` — stay unclassified for every runtime-db reader even when the resource claims the whole entry sensitive. Measured: a `:sensitive? true` resource's 4xx `:error` body echoing a submitted value, and its `:next-page-param` cursor, project raw through the frame classification (`local-render-value-at` at the entry's absolute slot path), while `:data` redacts.

Xray's Resources panel no longer depends on this: rf2-r5cc2.20 gates every payload of a `:sensitive?` resource's instance row on the registry's coarse claim. The question for the spec owner is whether the coarse "whole-entry" claim should cover the entry's other value slots at the runtime-db classification too, so every reader (an MCP trusted-local read with `:rf.egress/include-runtime-db? true`, the SSR projection, a future panel) gets it. If yes: extend `instance-declaration-paths` to conj each of those slots beside `data-prefix` under the same sensitive-wins rule, amend the two spec sentences, and add a resources-artefact test with an `:error` body and a cursor beside the `:data` control.

Decline condition: if the answer is that only `:data` is classified and error envelopes / cursors are the app's to keep clean (as params are), close this with that reason recorded in Spec 016.
notes:
== COORDINATOR RULING (2026-10-29, under the project stance) ==
YES: extend it. A coarse `:sensitive? true` on a resource claims the WHOLE cache entry sensitive, so every value-bearing slot of the entry is classified, not only `:data`: `:error`, `:refresh-error`, `:page-error`, `:next-page-param`, `:page-params` beside `:data`, under the same sensitive-wins rule (and `:large?` likewise for the slots it can apply to). Reason: an error body routinely echoes the submitted value and a cursor routinely carries a token; a claim that reads "this resource is sensitive" but leaves those raw at every runtime-db reader (MCP trusted-local reads, SSR projection, future panels) fails open, and the panel-side gate in rf2-r5cc2.20 already treats the claim as whole-entry. title: M-1 write migration must contribute a dispatch effect from interceptors instead of calling dispatch
description:
Audit of merged PR #11682 (ab783ec4ce4290144321b39e303cfa634fea8d32), correctness and implementation-quality lenses. The sentence remains at current HEAD.

skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md, M-1 edge case (line 117 at merge), says: "A handler returns the event in :fx instead, and an interceptor or fx body calls rf/dispatch". The interceptor arm moves a write into the pure chain as an immediate scheduling side effect, bypassing :fx-overrides for :dispatch. It conflicts with docs/core/interceptors.md, Contribute, don't perform: replay/tests re-run the chain; an interceptor contributes effect rows.

Independent JVM probe against current core, exit 0: an :after interceptor directly called (rf/dispatch [::write]); the source event was dispatched with {:fx-overrides {:dispatch recorder}}. The write handler ran once and the override ran zero times. Control: the interceptor appended [:dispatch [::write]] to [:effects :fx]; the write handler ran zero times and the override ran once. Audit scratch: .git/codex-pr-audit-01a18603/11682-probe.clj and 11682-probe.log.

This matters when the migration runs under Story or a test that replaces dispatch: following the new recipe still mutates state, and re-running an interceptor performs scheduling again instead of merely describing the effect.

Small repair: distinguish the interceptor from the fx body. Have the interceptor return (update-in ctx [:effects :fx] (fnil conj []) [:dispatch ev]); retain rf/dispatch for an effect body. Keep the existing warning that the write is deferred until after the current event, and keep Type B author review for the timing change. No new API or general migration machinery is needed.

close_reason:
FIXED in PR #11806 (head de2cb884d5, CI green: 77 checks, 54 success / 23 skipped, All required checks passed). Finding 1 (P3): worker.cjs called the render module's boot hook without awaiting it. A promise-returning boot let an isolate report ready and render before boot finished, and a rejecting boot got past the boot-time refusal and looped isolate replacement.

Fix: the worker's boot is async and awaits renderModule.boot() inside its existing try, before posting ready. A rejection now takes the same boot-error refusal path as a synchronous throw, and isolate.cjs's existing boot deadline bounds the wait. Both worker.cjs copies (ssr-node src and ssr-ring resources) moved in one commit and are byte-identical; absence.test.cjs's copy pin is green. The README render-module contract says that a promise boot returns is awaited and that a rejection refuses the boot as a throw does.

Witness: fixture test/fixtures/async-boot.cjs, with modes throw, reject and slow, plus two protocol.test.cjs rows. First, a rejecting boot refuses at boot exactly as a throwing one does, with :rf.ssr-node/malformed-render-module and the module's message; throw is the control. Second, a boot that resolves 200 ms later has finished before the first render. Plant: with the await removed, protocol.test.cjs went red (exit 1, 17 pass, 2 fail). The throw control passed, the reject half failed with "the service must not come up", and the slow row read data-booted="false". Restored, and the blob hash matched the committed blob.

Gates, local, pre-rebase: node ssr-node test/run.cjs exit 0, 78 to 81 tests (protocol 17 to 19, serve 7 to 8, as predicted). CI node-ssr-node green.

The operator collapses the root's `:profile`, which stores `[panel site [:profile]] {:expanded? false}`. Zooming into `[:user]` then renders the zoomed `:profile` (really `[:user :profile]`) collapsed, a node they never touched. The reverse also holds: toggles made while zoomed re-apply to whatever sits at that relative path after zoom-out. Spec 021's zoom section says only that depth knobs restart at the zoom root (:5062-5065), not that overrides are positional.
- Evidence: INSPECTED; every call site is cited above.
- Smallest fix: key the expansion slot by the absolute path, `(into (vec zoom-path-prefix) path)`, at the four sites, since zoom-path-prefix is already threaded into render-container. Testids and depth stay relative. Fence: views/edn_inspector.cljs.
- Gate: node lane. Toggle a node at root, zoom, and assert the same relative path under the zoom root is not overridden.
- Decision needed: no.

4. P4. The zoom gesture on a removed-container ghost is dead, and it arms a latent zoom that fires on a later epoch.
- Where: views/edn_inspector.cljs:3406-3413. zoom-trigger-attrs is attached to every non-empty non-root container, including the `:removed-ancestor?` ghosts render-node builds at :4093-4110 (a dissoc'd map key) and the `[removed-key-tag bi]` rows of sequential-diff-children (:2070). Its target is an absent key or a synthetic segment, so zoom-resolves? (:515-521, used at :4920-4921) is false: nothing happens, while `:zoom-to` (:435-443) stores the path. With a stable `:site-id` that entry outlives the epoch.
- Failure scenario: a diff-mode mount with `:zoomable? true`. The operator double-clicks (or presses Enter on) the struck-through `:error {…}` ghost and nothing visible happens. Epochs later `:error` is set again, the stored path now resolves, and the inspector re-roots onto `:error` with breadcrumbs, unprompted. A ghost's tab-index 0, aria-label "Zoom into …" and title "Zoom in (Enter)" also promise a gesture that does nothing.
- Evidence: INSPECTED.
- Smallest fix: omit zoom-attrs when `removed-ancestor?` is true. Inside a ghost there is nothing in `value` to re-root onto. Fence: views/edn_inspector.cljs.
- Gate: node lane. Assert a ghost container carries no `data-rf-zoom-target`.
- Decision needed: no.

5. P4. A modal closes when a text selection that started inside it is released over the backdrop. This applies to all six modal-chrome modals, including the EDN popup and the filter edit popup.
- Where: theme/modal_chrome.cljs:161-163. The backdrop `:on-click` dismisses with no check that the press began on the backdrop. The dialog's stopPropagation (:171) only covers clicks whose target is inside the dialog.
- Failure scenario: when mousedown and mouseup land on different elements, the browser fires click on their nearest common ancestor, here the backdrop. Drag-selecting a value in the EDN popup (it has no copy affordance, so selection is how a value is copied out) or the pattern text in the filter edit popup, and releasing just outside the dialog, dismisses the modal. An unsaved edit-popup pattern is lost.
- Evidence: INSPECTED (browser event semantics, plus the handler at :161-163).
- Smallest fix: record on the backdrop's `:on-pointer-down` (or `:on-mouse-down`) whether `(identical? (.-target e) (.-currentTarget e))`, and dismiss on click only when that press and the click target are both the backdrop itself. Fence: theme/modal_chrome.cljs (+ its test).
- Gate: node lane. A modal_chrome row where a mousedown targets a dialog child and the click targets the backdrop, asserting on-dismiss is not called.
- Decision needed: no.

CROSS-SLICE
- `load-theme!` with the `:root { --rf-xray-* … }` override its own test uses (global_styles_cljs_test.cljs:218) stops reaching the INLINE shell once `settings/effects/apply-theme!` writes a theme class onto `#rf-xray-root`. The CSS sits correctly as the last head child (global_styles.cljs:1643-1661). The cause is the class write in settings/effects.cljs, so the finding is recorded on rf2-lgzco.17, which owns settings/effects.cljs and core.cljs.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED
- shell.cljs:295-342 `row-tooltip-text` pr-strs the full event vector unbounded for every L2 row on every paint. Large payloads cost time only, and an endless lazy seq in an event vector is not a normal path. Performance, not correctness.
- views/resizable_table.cljs:182-191 writes BOTH columns of a dragged pair as px, so once every column has been dragged the table stops tracking its container. That is UX and the design as written, not a defect.
- views/edn_inspector.cljs:4484-4488 cites a `data-rf-affordance="popup"` hover rule in the global stylesheet that does not exist (grep over tools/xray: only the attribute and its tests). Cosmetic: the button stays at opacity 0.6.
- edn_widget.cljs:94 builds `(keyword (str "rf.xray.inspect/" node-key))` from node-keys containing "/" (static/flows/panel.cljs:260). In CLJS the name then reads "rf.xray.inspect", but keyword equality is by fqn, so expansion keys stay distinct and testids stay distinct through the mount-id. No wrong output.
- edn_inspector_default_formatters.cljs:150-176 renders an invalid Date as `#inst "NaN-NaN-NaN"`. Not a normal path.
- A lazy seq in app-db that throws when realised would throw out of bounded-vec (edn_inspector.cljs:1008-1010) during render. Rejected: the host app is already broken by that value. Whether the panels' display projections realise it before the widget does was not traced.
- views/edn_inspector_popup.cljs: :site-id is dropped and :panel-id re-derived (:521-526), so a popup does not share expansion or zoom with its opener. Sound.

NOT VERIFIED
- Every finding is on a CLJS-only path read without a build. Finding 5 depends on browser click-target semantics that no unit lane can exercise as a real drag.
- global_styles.cljs motion-css (371-876) and react-flow-base-css (931-1536) were scanned for selectors, not read rule by rule.

title: Spec 010 and Spec-Schemas still say the validation site reads only the schema's :sensitive? for an event, fx or sub payload
description:
Since PR #11805 (rf2-lgzco.30), a registration's own `:sensitive` / `:large` paths on `reg-event`, `reg-fx` and `reg-sub` cover that registration's `:schema` failure trace. Event paths re-root at `[1 …]`, and fx and sub paths stay payload-rooted. Spec 010 §Composition with the complementary privacy sites already says so. The rf2-gq11q census of `skills/`, `docs/` and `spec/` found two spec sentences that still describe the older model. Both were outside rf2-gq11q's write scope, so they were left as they are.

1. `spec/010-Schemas.md` ~:384, the cross-reference blockquote under §`:sensitive?` — privacy in schema-validation error traces. It ends "the validation site consults the per-slot schema declaration only." That is no longer true for an event, effect or sub: the check also applies the registering handler's own paths after the schema's decision. Keep the "no handler-meta `:sensitive?` coarse fallback" clause, which is still true, and replace "only" with a pointer to the registration's paths (§Composition with the complementary privacy sites, same page).

2. `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` ~:343, a comment inside the registration-metadata schema block. It says a transient value's slot is declared sensitive "by its schema (`{:sensitive? true}` Malli props)". The owner for a transient payload is the registration's `:sensitive` paths (Spec 015 §Registration-owned transient classification). The schema prop is the owner only for an HTTP `:decode` body, and for the failure trace of a coeffect or a machine's `:data`. Reword the comment to say that.

Gates: `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`. Prose only, no behaviour change. Mind any live fences on spec/010 and Spec-Schemas.md, which are hot-zone.
